GNL-induced nonlinear spatial encoding causes geometric distortions that compromise image-guided radiotherapy. Diffusion models require extensive sampling and rarely account for GNL. Flow matching shortens sampling, but velocity matching does not directly minimize the reconstruction error. We propose ReCoFlow-MRI, a conditional flow-matching framework for few-step GNL-corrected reconstruction. Methods: The calibrated GNL displacement field is integrated into the nonlinear encoding model to construct a distortion-corrected zero-filled image, which conditions a velocity field learned along a linear path from Gaussian noise to fully sampled images. The pretrained network is fine-tuned with a pixel-supervised endpoint loss on its five-step reconstruction. Results: On simulated fastMRI brain data, five-step ReCoFlow-MRI achieved the highest PSNR and SSIM among compared methods, including 128-step diffusion sampling. On MRI-Linac phantom and volunteer data, it achieved effective reconstruction and reduced the maximal geometric error from 24.95 to 2.12 mm, with 98.39% of the 3718 fiducial markers below 1 mm. Conclusion: ReCoFlow-MRI jointly addresses undersampling artifacts and geometric distortions within a few-step generative reconstruction. Significance: It provides a potential solution for fast and geometrically accurate imaging in image-guided radiotherapy.

authors.name: Qidi Luo, Hongli Chen, Jialiang Zhang, Yuting He, Yang Gao, Chunyi Liu, Yaohui Wang, Feng Liu, Shanshan Shan

papers.title: Atomic interferometry based on a phase-jump error signal with suppression of the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift
papers.summary: We develop a method for forming Ramsey fringes in atomic interferometers as a difference error signal using the phase-jump technique for Ramsey pulses (phase-jump error signal). In this case, the measurement procedure can be implemented as stabilization (locking) of the frequency chirp rate at the central zero of the error signal. We show analytically that this approach allows suppressing the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift (LACS). This shift was recently theoretically predicted and experimentally identified in the papers [V. I. Yudin et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{122}, 737 (2025); D. N. Kapusta et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{123}, 388 (2026)]. A characteristic feature of the LACS is an inverse cubic dependence $\propto 1/T^3$ (where $T$ is the time between adjacent Ramsey pulses), and it can become dominant for interferometers with a short baseline. Therefore, the developed measurement algorithm with a phase-jump error signal will enable significant improvement in the metrological performance of compact quantum sensors for various purposes (atomic gravimeters, accelerometers, gyroscopes).

authors.name: V. I. Yudin, O. N. Prudnikov, A. V. Taichenachev, M. Yu. Basalaev, M. D. Radchenko, D. N. Kapusta, A. N. Goncharov, A. E. Bonert, V. G. Pal'chikov, T. Zanon-Willette, L. Zhoug, M. S. Zhan

papers.title: A new restitution model for wet particle collisions using fully resolved numerical simulations
papers.summary: Particle collisions play a central role in wet particle processes such as granulation, drying, and chemical reactors, yet the influence of the liquid on the collision dynamics remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the influence of liquid viscosity, liquid density, liquid content, impact velocity, solid density, and surface tension on the wet restitution coefficient using numerical simulations. In this study, a Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) framework is used that has been validated against dedicated experiments of wet-wet particle collisions, showing a good agreement for both liquid-bridge evolution and rebound dynamics. The restitution coefficient decreases with increasing liquid viscosity, liquid density, and liquid-to-solid density ratio, whereas increasing impact velocity increases rebound. The negligible influence of surface tension indicates that viscous dissipation is the dominant source of energy loss under the investigated conditions. As existing Stokes number formulations were found to only capture part of the governing physics, a generalized Stokes number is proposed to incorporate both the viscous and inertial response time scales. A modified restitution coefficient model based on the generalized Stokes number successfully collapses the numerical and experimental data onto a single trend and predicts the wet restitution coefficient with an RMSE of only 4.99%.

authors.name: A. H. Huijgen, F. Bunke, S. Heinrich, Y. Tang, N. G. Deen, M. W. Baltussen

papers.title: Forbidden T-symmetry breaking in time-dependent non-Hermitian systems with gain and loss
papers.summary: Parity-time ($PT$) symmetry has attracted significant interest in photonics and related fields in recent years. With sufficiently weak gain and loss, these systems typically exhibit entirely real energy levels, with all corresponding wave functions remaining $PT$ symmetric. As the strength of gain and loss increases, complex-conjugate energy levels are expected to emerge, signaling the onset of $PT$ symmetry breaking. Similar properties can be found in non-Hermitian systems with other antilinear symmetries as well, where parity is replaced by another operator such as rotation ($R$) or simply the identity operator, resulting in $RT$-symmetric and $T$-symmetric non-Hermitian systems. In this work, we demonstrate that this typical scenario of non-Hermitian symmetry breaking in a finite Hilbert space is forbidden in a class of time-dependent systems with gain and loss and $T$ symmetry: the system remains in its $T$-symmetric phase as we increase the strength of gain and loss, even when the spatial distribution of gain and loss is random. Furthermore, this behavior is also independent of the duration or period of the temporal modulation. In contrast, this forbidden non-Hermitian symmetry breaking does not occur when the same systems are modified to display $PT$ symmetry instead. Our findings highlight contrasting behaviors in time-dependent and time-independent non-Hermitian systems, creating new possibilities and opportunities for future investigations.

authors.name: Li Ge

papers.title: Navigating Quantum Education at the University level: Pedagogical Pathways and a Roadmap for Textbook Selection
papers.summary: Instruction in quantum mechanics (QM) is often categorized by its entry point as 'wave-first' or 'spin-first', yet these labels lack consistent definitions and overlook other established or emerging approaches. Moreover, while capturing broad differences in topic selection and sequencing, this binary framing obscures critical differences in contextualization--how three dimensions (mathematical tools, phenomena and experiments, and theoretical concepts) are framed and connected to support student sensemaking. Research also rarely examines how such pedagogical choices unfold across the undergraduate-to-graduate trajectory. Using textbooks as an analytical lens to map these choices and characterize overarching pathways, encompassing entry points and overall orientations, we comparatively analyze the selection, sequencing, and contextualization of core topics across these 3 dimensions, alongside prefaces and introductions, in 36 university QM textbooks spanning countries and eras. At the topic level, we show that identical topics occupy widely different curricular roles depending on their contextualization. Synthesizing these findings into pathways, we identify three additional entry-point archetypes (labeled path-, qubit-, and axiom-first) and characterize all 5 approaches, showing that most textbooks combine multiple archetypes in their opening chapters. Extending this synthesis beyond entry points, we map textbooks' overall orientations relative to mathematics, experiment and application, and theoretical physics. Interpreting these profiles alongside authors' rationales reveals how educators navigate competing trade-offs among mathematical accessibility, theoretical generality, physical motivation, and modern developments. This study provides a multidimensional framework, substantive examples, and a practical roadmap for textbook selection and curriculum design in QM education.

authors.name: Yajie Liang, Menno Poot, Carsten Schuck, Stefan Heusler

papers.title: Chromatic calorimetry using nanocomposites: status and future challenges
papers.summary: The development of advanced detector technologies will play a key role in future high-energy physics experiments, such as the FCC-ee. In this context, chromatic calorimetry is an emerging concept for electromagnetic calorimeters, with the potential to combine the precise energy measurement of homogeneous calorimeters with longitudinal reconstruction of particle showers. The state of the art in chromatic calorimetry is reviewed, including experimental results from proof-of-concept prototypes and simulation studies investigating quantum-dot-based configurations. Recent progress and current challenges in the development of nanocomposites are also discussed. Finally, future prospects for chromatic calorimetry are outlined.

authors.name: Anne-Mazarine Lyon, Etiennette Auffray, Marco Caporale, Katerina Decka, Michael Doser, Jean-Louis Faure, Greta Gajdan, Yacine Haddad, Jan Kral, Joseph Mariano, Loris Martinazzoli, Emanuele Mazzola, Eva Mihokova, Solangel Rojas Torres, Matteo Salomoni, Vojtech Zabloudil

papers.title: A nonlinear transient finite element analysis of coupled solvent diffusion and large deformation of magneto-elastic hydrogel balloon
papers.summary: This study investigates the transient swelling of an initially spherical magnetoelastic hydrogel balloon. The balloon is inflated at constant internal pressure and exposed to the non-uniform magnetic field of one or two current-carrying coils. The gel is modelled as a compressible Ogden network mixed with solvent through Flory--Huggins theory, with an additive elastic--mixing--magnetic decomposition of the free energy. A fully coupled nonlinear finite element formulation uses a staggered solution scheme and a Taylor--Hood-type discretisation. It follows the balloon from its dry inflated state to either swollen equilibrium or burst. The formulation recovers the analytical free-swelling stretch and the delayed-burst regime, and its converged states agree with equilibrium energy minimisation. Symmetry-breaking (pear-shaped) dry configurations do not survive swelling: they rearrange rapidly and then relax by diffusion onto the symmetric branch. Transient membrane stresses can exceed their equilibrium values by nearly an order of magnitude. For coils which are sufficiently close to undeformed balloon, fields beyond a critical intensity close the slow-inflation curve into a loop. Stable swollen equilibria then exist only within a bounded pressure window that narrows as the field increases, and outside of it the balloon bursts. Under two coaxial coils, asymmetry about the equator appears only when the coils differ in current or radius. The magnetic field therefore acts as a control parameter for shape of balloon and permits or prevents stable swelling at a given pressure.

authors.name: Nadeem Karim Shaikh, Ganesh Tamadapu

papers.title: Closed-loop policy optimisation for cylinder wake control via differentiable simulation
papers.summary: Suppressing vortex shedding behind a circular cylinder is a classical problem in active flow control.Model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL) learns such policies by interacting with the flow without differentiating its dynamics, which typically requires a large interaction budget. This study optimises closed-loop policies by differentiable simulation: control-loss gradients propagate through the simulated flow to the policy parameters, which are updated by reverse-mode automatic differentiation. The policy maps local velocity measurements to a jet amplitude imposed through differentiable synthetic-jet boundary conditions. In a two-dimensional confined cylinder wake at Rey=100, eight policy updates (about 78 shedding periods of forward simulation) give approximately 8% drag reduction and 99.6% suppression of lift fluctuations, the drag level being comparable to reported DRL results. Suppression is sustained by feedback: a mean-matched constant jet does not maintain it, whereas the same policy responds similarly at three activation phases and recovers after upstream disturbances. A velocity-deviation reward alone retains strong suppression, and observations of two instantaneous velocity components at one near-wake or surface location reach about 99.8% suppression, whereas a single surface pressure leaves residual oscillations. Together with related DRL results, this suggests that reward and observation requirements here are set by policy optimisation and flow physics.

authors.name: Siwen Zhang, Xizeng Zhao, Zhouteng Ye, Yulin Xie, Zesheng Yao

papers.title: Ultrasensitive measurement of phase dynamics by time-holographic dark-port readout of a marginally imbalanced interferometer
papers.summary: Resolving displacements and surface irregularities far below a nanometer is now indispensable across fields, from precision manufacturing and biotechnology to nanoscience and fundamental metrology. High-precision optical interferometry reaches this $\lambda/1{,}000$ regime by reading out optical power, which provides a smooth response over the measurement range. Here we instead read out the complex dark-port field of a marginally imbalanced interferometer, whose phase response to small internal phase deviations $\phi_{\textrm{in}}$ near destructive interference becomes extremely steep. For a small arm-amplitude imbalance $\mu$, the tangent $T_{\textrm{out}}$ of the dark-port phase reduces to $\mu^{-1}\phi_{\textrm{in}}$, defining a phase magnification $M=\mu^{-1}$. Crucially, this tangent estimator stays linear over a range $|\phi_{\textrm{in}}|\lesssim\sqrt{|\mu|}$---much larger than the imbalance $|\mu|$ itself for $|\mu|\ll1$---so that fine temporal substructure is resolved within much larger phase excursions. $T_{\textrm{out}}$ is synthesized from the dark-port complex field by optical time-domain holography and Fourier demodulation---a heterodyne readout that is intrinsically immune to laser relative-intensity noise at any magnification, and gives time-resolved access to phase dynamics. In a proof-of-principle Mach--Zehnder experiment, without optimization or environmental isolation, we demonstrate $|M|>10^3$ and optical-path resolution better than $\lambda/100{,}000$ ($\approx5~\textrm{pm}$), with a shot-noise floor orders of magnitude below this environment-limited value. The approach is compact, tunable, and compatible with existing interferometric platforms, offering a practical route to enhanced phase sensitivity in metrology, sensing, and optical instrumentation.

authors.name: F. Silva, A. Molina, A. Esteban-Mart\'{i}n, J. Garc\'{i}a-Monreal, G. J. de Valc\'{a}rcel

papers.title: Stall-Triggered Newton-Krylov-Assisted DIIS and Its Machine-Learning-Accelerated Variant for CCSD Convergence
papers.summary: The iterative solution of the non-linear amplitude equations of coupled-cluster singles doubles (CCSD) theory can encounter convergence instabilities, asymptotic convergence or outright divergence. Direct Inversion in the Iterative Subspace (DIIS) is a widely used extrapolation technique but can also exhibit slow or oscillatory convergence in challenging regimes. In this work, we introduce a robust hybrid solver: Stall-Triggered Newton-Krylov Assisted DIIS (${}{\mathrm{st}}$NK-DIIS) alongside its machine-learning accelerated variant ${}{\mathrm{st}}$NK$^{\mathrm{ML}}$-DIIS which leverages the robust convergence of Newton-Krylov (NK) while avoiding the high computational cost of Krylov iterations. In our methods, DIIS remains the default accelerator and a matrix-free NK procedure is activated when sustained stagnation or divergence is detected with each NK step verified using the non-linear residual before acceptance. To alleviate the cost of Krylov iterations the ${}{\mathrm{st}}$NK$^{\mathrm{ML}}$-DIIS uses a gated recurrent unit (GRU) to predict a scalar logarithmic step-size ratio along the approximately computed Newton direction. When the ML-predicted step fails residual-based verification, the method falls back to a grid-based NK line search. Using CCSD as the underlying electronic-structure theory, we evaluate these methods against conventional DIIS and pure NK for stretched molecules exhibiting convergence difficulties in terms of residual convergence, iteration counts, and wall-time performance. These protocols may be generalizable to other non-linear equation solvers as well, as the ML model learns the convergence pattern of the variables and does not require system-specific knowledge such as atom identities or molecular orbital properties. This allows transferability across atom-type, bonding character and basis-sets.

authors.name: Shamik Chanda, Suhita Basumallick, Sangita Sen

papers.title: Impulsive ejection of Worthington jets by flow focusing. Influence of a soluble surfactant
papers.summary: We experimentally investigate impulsive Worthington jet generation by flow focusing, considering the liquid meniscus location that maximizes the flow-focusing effect. This effect increases the jet velocity by up to two orders of magnitude over the bottom liquid velocity after impact. At sufficiently high liquid velocities, jet formation is governed primarily by inertia, making jet velocity largely independent of liquid viscosity, surface tension, and surfactant effects. Each liquid exhibits an optimum impact velocity that maximizes momentum transfer. Surfynol 465 lowers the impactvelocity threshold for water-jet emission and increases jet velocity by rapidly restoring equilibrium surface tension. In contrast, Triton X-100 has an almost negligible effect because of its slower adsorption kinetics. Importantly, both surfactants reduce jet diameter and, consequently, droplet size. This reduction is particularly significant with Surfynol 465 at high impact velocities, suggesting potential applications, for instance, in high-resolution printing technologies. The jet loaded with Surfynol 465 was even faster than that of the glycerine-water mixture with the same Ohnesorge and Weber numbers. This suggests that adding Surfynol 465 further accelerates jet emission, exceeding the speed attained by a clean interface with the same reduced equilibrium surface tension.

authors.name: T. Gonz\'alez-Rubio, S. Rodr\'iguez-Aparicio, E. J. Vega, J. M. Montanero

papers.title: Beyond the Ground State: Assessing the Machine-Learned Skala Functional in {\Delta}SCF Calculations of Molecular Excitation Energies
papers.summary: We assess the transferability of the machine-learned Skala exchange-correlation (XC) functional beyond ground-state energetics using molecular vertical excitation energies and singlet-triplet gaps calculated with the $\Delta$-self-consistent-field ($\Delta$SCF) approach. We compare Skala with PBE, r$^2$SCAN, and PBE0 on subsets covering small-molecule excitations (QUEST1), inverted singlet-triplet gaps (ST-gap), and intramolecular charge-transfer excitations (QUEST6). Both spin-unrestricted Kohn-Sham (UKS) and restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham (ROKS) formalisms are considered. On QUEST1, Skala achieves the lowest mean absolute errors (MAEs) for singlet and triplet excitation energies with both formalisms, although PBE0 and r$^2$SCAN provide more accurate singlet-triplet gaps through error cancellation. For ST-gap, Skala yields the lowest gap MAEs with both UKS and ROKS. Evaluating the mixed-spin and triplet energy components on the same orbitals optimized for the ROKS open-shell singlet yields negative splittings for seven of eight ST-gap molecules with Skala. Separate triplet optimization increases the gaps, but six remain negative. All three conventional functionals give positive common-orbital splittings and optimized gaps for all eight molecules. For QUEST6, treated with UKS only, Skala yields more accurate singlet excitation energies than PBE and r$^2$SCAN but remains less accurate than PBE0. Across QUEST1 and ST-gap, Skala yields lower MAEs with UKS than ROKS. Overall, these results support Skala's transferability to molecular excited states while highlighting its dependence on the excitation class and open-shell treatment.

authors.name: Egor Trushin, Thomas D. K\"uhne

papers.title: Passivity Correction of the Thermistor Model in Bolometric Power Sensors and Its Dependence on Bead Temperature
papers.summary: This paper closes a series of works on thermistor bolometric power sensors, coaxial and waveguide, by treating what the two have in common. The per-state transformation m introduced in the waveguide work, which corrects the thermistor impedances of the model in each bridge state so that the two-port of the mount is passive, is analyzed on the eleven sensors of the preceding papers: the corrections are a few tenths of a percent in the coaxial mounts and one to two percent in the waveguide mounts, follow one pattern within each family, and the hottest state is the one whose efficiency departs most from the others. The transformation is tested by an independent measurement: the substituted powers of the three states, read with the manufacturer's procedure against a leveled source whose reflection is obtained from the closure of three Apollonius circles, give efficiency ratios of 0.999 +/- 0.016 and 0.997 +/- 0.008 (k = 2), which contain the values at the passivity floor (0.996, 0.998) and exclude those of the first pass (0.941, 1.023). Three sensors were swept in the bridge resistance, 23 and 31 states, and a fourth is treated apart: the correction reduces to one constant per state, the parallel resistance of the bead, represented by a law with one term scaling with the bridge resistance and one exponential in the bead temperature, with one thermal coefficient per family. The same property explains why the cross-ratio of four measured reflection coefficients, invariant under any state-independent two-port, departs from that of the four bridge resistances.

authors.name: Patricio Greco

papers.title: Hot-Layer Ignition in High-Gain Inertial Confinement Fusion
papers.summary: Ignition of the shocked deuterium tritium shell is identified during the thermonuclear combustion of very high-gain targets in inertial confinement fusion (ICF). This mechanism is due to the local energy deposition of the fusion alphas created in this shocked shell, independently of hot-spot ignition, and generates sufficient energy to fully recompress the hot spot. A new analytical criterion for the ignition of the hot layer is presented. A simple three zone model, based on the thick layer hot-spot model, reproduces this mechanism, which breaks down into successive stages: ignition of the hot spot, compression of the shocked shell, ignition of the shocked shell, and subsequent recompression of the hot spot. 1D numerical simulations highlight the onset of this hot layer ignition thereby satisfying the analytical ignition criterion. It is shown that this mechanism amplifies the energy released by the combustion of the target by approximately 50 %.

authors.name: M. Lourmande, B. Canaud

papers.title: Single-Pulse Dosimetry for Ultra-High-Dose-Rate X-Ray Pulses Based on Radiation-Induced Acoustic Signals
papers.summary: Real-time dosimetry of ultra-high-dose-rate (UHDR) pulsed X-rays remains a major challenge. This proof-of-principle study investigates a dosimetry method for UHDR pulsed X-rays based on radiation-induced acoustic (RA) signals from a thin metal foil. The foil combines efficient X-ray absorption and acoustic resonance, converting deposited dose into acoustic signals with discrete resonant frequencies. Single-pulse measurements were performed at six dose levels spanning approximately 1--40 mGy(Si), with one pulse recorded at each level and instantaneous dose rates reaching the order of 10^6 Gy/s at the highest dose settings. The peak-to-peak amplified transducer-output voltage exhibited a linear relationship with the reference dose measured by thermoluminescent dosimeters (TLDs). These results demonstrate the feasibility of single-pulse acoustic dosimetry under the tested conditions. Furthermore, we establish analytical solutions for radiation-induced acoustic signals in a one-dimensional layered medium in both the time and frequency domains, providing a theoretical basis for signal interpretation and detector optimization.

authors.name: Qihang Han, Ke Chen, Chenghao Hua, Haoran Chen, Lili Ding, Changhui Li, Xiaoping Ouyang, Chenhui Wang, Wei Chen, Wenjun Ma

papers.title: Heat cleaning kinetics and thermal degradation of MOCVD-grown GaAs photocathodes
papers.summary: We evaluated metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)-grown GaAs/GaAsP strained-superlattice photocathodes with integrated distributed Bragg reflectors in a low-voltage Mott polarimeter at Jefferson Lab. Without a protective arsenic cap, surface contamination can develop during transport and installation. Heat cleaning removes this contamination by thermally desorbing material bound to the surface, but excessive heating can also damage the photocathode. We modeled quantum efficiency (QE) in terms of surface contaminant coverage to describe its increase with heating time. QE rose more rapidly and reached a plateau nearly twice as high at $550^\circ\text{C}$ as at $450^\circ\text{C}$, while polarization remained near 83%. Further heating reduced QE and polarization. Reflectance measurements showed a shift of the optical resonance to shorter wavelengths, consistent with surface material loss. We also tested the cleaning method in a high-voltage photogun, where QE showed the same initial increase and subsequent decline. The cleaning procedure must therefore balance contaminant removal against loss of photocathode material.

authors.name: Gregory Blume, Adam Masters, Colin Kirk, Sushil Poudel, John Hill, Alimohammed Kachwala, Joseph Grames, Marcy L Stutzman, Sylvain Marsillac, Matt Grau

papers.title: Citizen-informed scenarios to shape energy demand reduction strategies
papers.summary: Growing evidence has demonstrated the important role that energy demand reduction can play in achieving net zero. Despite this, the adoption of such measures in government strategies often remains limited, in part based on perceived public resistance to change. Using a novel combined deliberative-modelling approach, which fills a key gap in the literature, we find this is unfounded. Citizens both recognise the importance of and support demand-side interventions to achieve the UK's net-zero goals. This support, however, is conditional. If policy interventions can make demand-side choices practical and fair, we find citizens are prepared to reduce energy demand by at least 37% between 2025 and 2050, providing 20% of the abatement required to meet net-zero targets. Policymakers could thus unlock a wide range of demand reduction measures by acting on a more comprehensive understanding of public views and needs. Moreover, our approach offers a powerful framework, applicable in other contexts, to underpin policymaking with socially-informed quantitative modelling.

authors.name: Andy Yuille, Oliver Broad, John Barrett, Christian Brand, Alice Garvey, Jonathan Norman, James Price, Steve Pye, Rebecca Willis

papers.title: Feasibility study of two-stage direct laser acceleration of electrons
papers.summary: We present the first numerical demonstration of two-stage direct laser acceleration (DLA) of electrons. The result was obtained using quasi-3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. The first stage ($a_0 = 6$, $\tau = 200~\mathrm{fs}$, $w = 4\lambda$, $\lambda = 0.8~\mu\mathrm{m}$) utilized a nitrogen gas target with an atomic density of $n_a = 0.008n_{cr}$. This stage was designed to accelerate low-energy electrons, achieving a maximum energy of approximately 94 MeV with a two-temperature energy spectrum ($T_1 = 7.0$ MeV and $T_2 = 16.0$ MeV) and a charge of 6.04 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The resulting electron bunch was then injected into the second stage, where hydrogen at a lower density ($n_a = 0.01n_{cr}$) was used, while the laser parameters were the same as in the first stage except that the waist was increased to $w = 8\lambda$. After the second stage, the electrons reached energies up to 225 MeV, with a two-temperature energy spectrum ($T_1 = 18.4$ MeV and $T_2 = 88.3$ MeV) and a charge of 4.55 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The self-injected electrons in the second stage reached a maximum energy of 123 MeV with a charge of 1.14 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The simulation results are compared with a theoretical DLA model, which describes the electron motion in the combined fields of the laser pulse and the quasistatic plasma channel. The model accounts for the transverse size of the channel by incorporating a Gaussian attenuation of the channel fields and off-axis injection. The theoretical model correctly describes the observed acceleration dynamics for both low-energy and pre-accelerated electrons, confirming its validity for designing multi-stage DLA schemes. Thus, the implementation of multi-stage acceleration by the DLA mechanism is successfully demonstrated for the first time in a numerical experiment.

authors.name: E. Starodubtseva, S. Solntsev, I. Tsymbalov, A. Savel'ev

papers.title: Network versus market information in coupled opinion-return dynamics
papers.summary: When making investment decisions, investors can use common signals from the market and local signals from their social networks. We develop an agent-based opinion-return model in which agents follow fixed trading strategies and respond to either local network information or a common market signal. In our model, trend followers and contrarians select either a local network signal or a common market signal and then update their buy, hold, or sell opinions by following or opposing the signal, respectively. The aggregate opinion imbalance determines the return, which sets the market signal. We find that three collective regimes emerge depending on how much network information is used and the fraction of contrarians in the population. Persistent directional states occur when trend followers dominate, market-wide reversals appear when a contrarian-rich population relies on the common market signal, and opposing opinions coexist with small aggregate returns when the same population relies on network signals. With a common market signal, the majority strategy has the higher payoff scores, whereas increasing reliance on network signals reduces this difference. When only network information is used, higher network clustering is associated with greater polarisation and smaller return magnitudes when trend followers dominate. Degree heterogeneity has little effect on aggregate measures but changes the payoff scores of high- and low-degree agents. In contrarian-rich populations, local information thus reduces aggregate return fluctuations even as opposing opinions persist.

authors.name: Yue Yu, Luis Enrique Correa Rocha

papers.title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
papers.summary: Sinusoidal blade pitching can improve vertical-axis turbine performance, but whether a blade could follow the same motion passively depends on the energy exchanged through pitching. This study experimentally examines 480 prescribed-pitch conditions using a single-blade model following a circular trajectory in a water channel at four tip-speed ratios (TSRs) from 1.25 to 3.14. The amplitude associated with the highest measured power decreases from 16{\deg} to 12{\deg} and then 8{\deg} as TSR increases, with the corresponding phase shifting from 0 to pi/4. At TSRs of 1.25 and 3.14, the cycle-averaged power coefficient increases from 0.0047 to 0.1037 and from 0.4698 to 0.5948, respectively. Pitching-energy maps show nearly neutral net hydrodynamic pitching work for the highest-performing motions at the two lower TSRs and net energy transfer from the flow to pitching at the two higher TSRs. Virtual damping narrows the positive-energy region, although the higher-TSR best-tested motions retain an energy surplus at nonzero damping. However, net energy transfer from the flow to pitching also occurs for motions with substantial power losses. At the lowest TSR, phase-resolved force measurements and particle image velocimetry link the gain to delayed dynamic-stall-vortex formation and shedding, prolonged favorable loading, and reduced subsequent negative power. At the highest TSR, the flow and loading change locally, with little alteration of the main power-producing event. The joint maps identify performance-enhancing motions with an energetic margin against assumed dissipation, providing candidates for further passive or assisted pitching studies.

authors.name: Zihan Zhang, Anchi Li, Qimin Feng, Yuanhang Zhu, Qiang Zhong

papers.title: Receptor Abundance Alone Underpredicts Red Blood Cell Adhesion in Gaucher Disease
papers.summary: Red blood cells (RBCs) in Gaucher disease (GD) adhere abnormally to vessel walls and carry more Lutheran/basal cell adhesion molecule (Lu/BCAM), a laminin receptor. Whether receptor abundance sets this adhesion is untested. We simulated RBCs carrying stochastic Lu/BCAM-laminin bonds, calibrated a population on control donors, and predicted GD adhesion from the 1.3-fold receptor rise. On laminin and endothelium the data exceed the prediction 1.6- to 1.7-fold. Matching them requires 2.4- and 4.6-fold more binding-competent receptors, compatible with the estimated 5.7-fold rise in phosphorylated receptors. Neither a stiffer membrane nor higher bond affinity removes the shortfall at high shear stress. In sickle cell disease, given active-receptor counts, the model predicts the fall in adhesion under hydroxyurea within 1.4-fold, while total receptors rise. Adhesion likely follows receptor state more than abundance. Stiffening instead retains cells at a splenic slit.

authors.name: Zhaojie Chai, Pierre A. Buffet, Melanie Franco, George Em Karniadakis

papers.title: Language Diffusion Models are Associative Memories Capable of Retrieving Unseen Data
papers.summary: When do language diffusion models memorize their training data, and how to quantitatively assess their true generative regime? We address these questions by showing that Uniform-based Discrete Diffusion Models (UDDMs) fundamentally behave as Associative Memories (AMs) $\textit{with emergent creative capabilities}$. The core idea of an AM is to reliably recover stored data points as $\textit{memories}$ by establishing distinct basins of attraction around them. Historically, models like Hopfield networks use an explicit energy function to guarantee these stable attractors. We broaden this perspective by leveraging the observation that energy is not strictly necessary, as basins of attraction can also be formed via conditional likelihood maximization. By evaluating token recovery of $\textit{training}$ and $\textit{test}$ examples, we identify in UDDMs a sharp memorization-to-generalization transition governed by the size of the training dataset: as it increases, basins around training examples shrink and basins around unseen test examples expand, until both later converge to the same level. Crucially, we can detect this transition using only the conditional entropy of predicted token sequences: memorization is characterized by vanishing conditional entropy, while in the generalization regime the conditional entropy of most tokens remains finite. Thus, conditional entropy offers a practical probe for the memorization-to-generalization transition in deployed models.

authors.name: Bao Pham, Mohammed J. Zaki, Luca Ambrogioni, Dmitry Krotov, Matteo Negri

papers.title: Tensor cluster expansion as an efficient surrogate for multi-ACE
papers.summary: In this work, we generalize an on-lattice tensor cluster expansion (TCE) framework to an arbitrary correlation order. We show that these generalized tensor cluster expansion features span a subspace of MACE features, suggesting that TCE features can sufficiently pre-screen MACE features for chemical diversity in alloyed transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers. We show that, using maximum-entropy subset sampling, we can empirically recover chemical diversity from MACE features using a cheaper TCE representation. We then fine-tune a multi-ACE (MACE) potential with both subsets, and use this potential to predict temperature-dependent vibrational properties in alloyed TMD monolayers with varying chemical ordering. In our approach, TCE features can be used as cheap surrogate features for pre-screening chemically rich configurations using MACE features, allowing for the more efficient finetuning of atomic cluster expansion (ACE) potentials, thus achieving a tractable prediction of finite-temperature alloy thermodynamics on modest hardware.

authors.name: Jacob Jeffries, Enrique Martinez, Eva Zarkadoula

papers.title: Cup and cap synchronization: higher-order node dynamics from topology
papers.summary: Higher-order node-based synchronization provides distinct mechanisms for discontinuous synchronization transitions. However, a comprehensive theoretical framework capable of encompassing existing models and revealing the role of higher-order interactions beyond triangles is still missing. Here, combining algebraic topology and nonlinear dynamics, we introduce Cup and Cap Synchronization, a unifying theoretical framework for higher-order node-based dynamics that naturally incorporates the topological organization of the underlying higher-order network. We show that Cup and Cap Synchronization can display critical behavior belonging to the universality classes of two existing higher-order Kuramoto-like models, whose distinct critical behaviors were thought to originate from different mechanisms. Remarkably, we demonstrate that Cup and Cap Synchronization displays additional phenomenology not captured by the previously proposed models of higher-order node-based synchronization. Most relevantly, the inclusion of four-body interactions can fundamentally alter the critical properties of the synchronization transition, giving rise to collective phenomena that cannot be observed in models including only interactions mediated by edges and triangles. These findings reveal the importance of going beyond the commonly studied three-body terms and establish Cup and Cap Synchronization as a unifying theoretical framework for understanding collective dynamics in higher-order networks.

authors.name: Runyue Wang, Yuanzhao Zhang, Ginestra Bianconi

papers.title: Stabilized negative viscosity governs ocean jets before, during and after they leave the coast
papers.summary: Eddies in rotating turbulence can feed the jets that spawn them, resulting in the negative viscosity phenomenon. Taken alone, a negative viscosity represents up-gradient eddy fluxes and is often referred to as "antifriction" or "antidiffusion". Mathematically, it leads to an ill-posed problem. In two-dimensional turbulence theory, this problem can be resolved by representing the transfer from small to large scales by a stabilized negative viscosity (SNV), in which a negative Laplacian viscosity is balanced by its positive biharmonic counterpart. In purely two-dimensional turbulence, by the Taylor identity, a negative viscosity is up-gradient transport of vorticity, which mixing cannot produce; on a slope, mixing of potential vorticity can mimic it, and we test for this. Using two years of wide-swath satellite altimetry (SWOT), we measure the eddy momentum flux across the five subtropical western boundary currents in each current's own frame. Along the continental slope the eddies act with a negative viscosity of order $-10^{3}$ m$^{2}$ s$^{-1}$, with the SNV structure resolved in the Gulf Stream and the Agulhas. At separation from the slope the sign reverses in all five currents, and the eddies brake the flow. Downstream, in the free jets, the negative viscosity returns on the cyclonic flank, strengthened to $-10^{4}$ m$^{2}$ s$^{-1}$. Separation is where the current leaves the strong topographic $\beta$ of the slope, the constraint that orders the eddy transfer. In an eddy-resolving reanalysis the SNV form holds across three ocean basins, with its shape parameter set by the deformation radius.

authors.name: Boris Galperin, Alexei Chekhlov, Ilya Staroselsky, Semion Sukoriansky

papers.title: A unified closed-form theory for elastic waves in polycrystals of any crystal symmetry
papers.summary: The coherent elastic wave in random polycrystals is described by the first-order smoothing approximation, whose mass operator remains an integral evaluated only numerically. Here we derive its closed form for equiaxed, untextured polycrystals of any crystal symmetry with an exponential correlation function, giving an explicit dispersion equation at all frequencies. Unlike the integral form, which fails beyond one inverse correlation radius from the real axis, the closed form holds deep in the complex wavenumber plane, where heavily attenuated roots lie. It is compact, reproduces the dispersion equations of Stanke and Kino for cubic grains, extends them to any symmetry and contains the Born and far-field approximations as special cases. It reveals the structure of the roots and their partitions of the coherent field: three roots per polarization, one from the incident wave and one from each of the two scattering channels, without and with mode conversion. It also yields closed-form limits of their velocity, attenuation and partition in the Rayleigh, stochastic and geometric regimes, which show why a single coherent wave has been observed at long wavelengths, whereas more than one can be observed at short wavelengths. These results underpin further theory and quantitative characterization of polycrystalline microstructure.

authors.name: Ming Huang, Stanislav I. Rokhlin, Michael J. S. Lowe

papers.title: Free-Space Excitation of Frozen Waves and Topological Edge States in Graphene at a Time Interface
papers.summary: Time-varying two-dimensional materials, such as graphene under ultrafast photoexcitation, offer a promising platform for engineering temporal interfaces for electromagnetic waves. Rapidly promoting valence electrons to the conduction band generates a high-energy, non-thermal hot-electron population that subsequently thermalizes with the pre-existing thermal electron population. We study the excitation of plasmonic modes in graphene by the time interface created by ultra-fast photoexcitation using a graphene electron-transport model that is self-consistently coupled to electromagnetic simulations. We find that in addition to dynamic, propagating plasmonic modes, the time interfaces result in the excitation of static, spatially varying electromagnetic modes in the interaction region sustained by streaming transverse electrons. We also demonstrate a novel technique for coupling free-space light directly to highly localized topological edge states at the magnetic-inversion boundary on graphene, eliminating the need for near-field excitation techniques.

authors.name: Shivaksh Rawat, Samyobrata Mukherjee, Jeffery W. Allen, Monica S. Allen, Gennady Shvets

papers.title: Frequency-bin-encoded quantum secret sharing with fast basis switching
papers.summary: Frequency-bin encoding offers unique opportunities for fiber-native quantum information processing, yet its full potential has been hampered by challenges in rapid state control and protocol scaling. Leveraging high-speed microwave processing, we overcome several extant hurdles and unlock new fundamental capabilities in frequency-based quantum communications. First, we demonstrate three-party quantum secret sharing, representing, to our knowledge, the first multiparty ($N\geq 3$ users) quantum communication protocol implemented entirely with frequency encoding. Second, we demonstrate active, pseudorandom switching of frequency-bin quantum states and measurement bases at 20 MHz symbol rates, enabling real-time protocol operation without relying on hardware-intensive passive basis-selection schemes. Even under fast switching, we preserve high-contrast three-party correlations ($\geq 0.91$) and low quantum bit error rates ($\leq 4.5\%$). Our work extends frequency-bin quantum communication beyond static, two-party protocols, opening a pathway toward scalable, reconfigurable, and real-time spectrally encoded quantum networking.

authors.name: Chen-You Su, Suparna Seshadri, Hsuan-Hao Lu, Jason D. McKinney, Andrew M. Weiner, Joseph M. Lukens

papers.title: Recovering from Averages: An Inverse Problem Perspective on Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate the potential energy surface of atomistic systems from quantum-mechanical reference data and enable molecular simulation at near-ab-initio accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Since they are fitted to total energies and forces, it is not obvious what is estimated: the total energy or the many-body potentials from which it is assembled. Mathematically, this can be formulated as a question whether a function can be recovered from averages of its values over random clusters. We study it for a linear model of fixed correlation order in simplified statistical setting. We show that, in the population limit, the potential is identifiable in a natural weighted Sobolev space, and derive finite-sample recovery guarantees. Numerical experiments for pair, three-body, and four-body models support the theory.

authors.name: Tina Torabi, Cheuk Hin Ho, Christoph Ortner, Ruo Ning Qiu

papers.title: Benchmarking Quantum Key Distribution Hardware Across Operating Conditions
papers.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is entering national fibre networks, but published secret key rates (SKRs) are measured over different distances, wavelengths, classical traffic loads and clock rates, so systems are hard to compare. We write the SKR as the product of the transmitter clock rate, the channel transmittance and the secret key per received pulse. This third factor, the noise-normalised key rate (NNKR), needs four commonly reported parameters and depends mainly on the equipment wherever the SKR is proportional to transmittance. A companion metric, the implementation efficiency (IE), compares the SKR with the ideal key rate of its channel, including classical-traffic noise. For fixed loss-limited equipment, NNKR is independent of channel loss, whereas the fraction of the repeaterless bound varies 1.6-fold over 2-25 dB. An analytic model relates the flat loss range of NNKR to the detector noise count rate and dead time. We apply both metrics to ten published coexistence experiments, and NNKR to 42,115 measurements from four systems of two vendors and four high-rate laboratory systems. For one production system, NNKR has a 6.9% coefficient of variation over 17 dB of attenuation and agrees within 0.7 dB with three of four published deployments of that platform. Under coexistence, that platform's NNKR and IE stay within 0.5 dB of their standalone values. In decibels, NNKR is a sum of component penalties, as in an optical link budget, and for one laboratory system the budget from its published parameters and measured secure fraction closes within 0.3 dB.

authors.name: Jerry Horgan, Indrakshi Dey, Hajar Bennouri, Daniel C. Kilper

papers.title: Parametric excitation of nano-scale spin waves with controlled phase by an open-resonator-type transducer
papers.summary: Parametric excitation is one of the most effective methods for the excitation of nano-scale spin waves (SW) (or magnons) in magnetic films and nano-waveguides, as this method removes restrictions on the excited wave wavelength imposed by a finite width of the excitation transducer. Especially efficient parametric excitation of SW is achieved if the SW excitation is based on the effect of voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA). However, in a traditional parametric excitation process, the excited propagating waves have an arbitrary phase, which prevents the use of such waves in signal processing applications. Here, we demonstrate that the use of an VCMA transducer in the form of an open resonator with controlled partial reflections of waves at the boundaries allows one to excite SW having only two allowed phase states, controlled by the phase of the parametric pumping and reflections at the transducer boundaries. These reflections, also, lead to a reduced value of the parametric excitation threshold. In addition, micromagnetic simulations reveal the possibility to tune the phase distribution of the excited magnons using static voltage, which could be useful for applications in probabilistic computing.

authors.name: Roman Verba, Vladyslav Borynskyi, Vasil Tiberkevich, Andrei Slavin

papers.title: Power Law Transients in Perovskite Photoluminescence
papers.summary: Carrier dynamics and recombination in perovskite thin films are often explored through transient photoluminescence (PL) measurements and subsequent analysis based on single/multi-exponentials. In contrast, here we show that several experimental PL transients reported in literature vary as power laws with time and are not multi-exponentials. Puzzlingly, the existing theoretical methods are ill-equipped to explain the origin and implications of such power law trends. Our analysis resolves this puzzle and correlates the power law exponents with the trap distributions. Curiously, we show that PL transients could vary as $t^{-2}$ even in the presence of dominant monomolecular recombination while the existing theory associates this unique trend exclusively with dominant bimolecular recombination. These findings identify the limits of applicability of concepts such as differential lifetime and highlight the need for predictive modeling synergistic with insightful data analysis towards performance optimization of perovskite optoelectronic devices.

authors.name: Anas M. M., Pradeep R. Nair

papers.title: Generating grain boundary structures at a specified energy with a symmetry-constrained diffusion model
papers.summary: Grain boundaries (GBs) govern many properties of polycrystalline materials, and inverse design would make the GB structure itself a design variable. Crystal generative models such as MatterGen operate on periodic cells, which contain two GBs. The cell energy defines a single GB only when the two are equivalent, but existing models do not enforce this equivalence. Building on MatterGen, we developed a symmetry-constrained diffusion model in which the two GBs are related by a symmetry operation: atoms near one GB are generated, and those near the other are reconstructed through a symmetry projection applied at every denoising step. We applied it to the $\Sigma 5(210)[001]$ symmetric tilt GB in Al, conditioning generation on the GB energy from a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP). All 350 generated structures kept a geometrically equivalent GB pair after relaxation. Given a target GB energy, the model generated structures at that energy: for the three in-range targets with many nearby training structures, 44% to 70% fell within $\pm 0.1$ J/m$^2$ of the target. Tracking weakened at higher energies and failed outside the training range. Of the 91 near-target structures, 90 matched no training structure under the adopted geometric criterion, indicating that the model can propose configurations near the target energy that are distinct from the training structures, a capability that could help identify unknown metastable GB structures observed in experiments. Building GB-pair equivalence into generation thus makes GB properties well-defined design targets, enabling inverse design of GB structures.

authors.name: Kazuya Miyamoto, Ibuki Okuda, Izumi Takahara, Teruyasu Mizoguchi

papers.title: Unconventional Photon Blockade in Second-Order Nonlinearity Coupled Cavities with Asymmetric Dissipation
papers.summary: We investigate the unconventional photon blockade in a second-order nonlinearity coupled double-cavity system with asymmetric dissipation. By treating the cavity decay rates as independent parameters, we analytically derive two exact families of optimal blockade conditions. While the first family recovers and generalizes the symmetric-dissipation results of previous studies, the second family, arising uniquely from an asymmetric dissipation ratio of $\kappa_B = 2\kappa_A$, completely locks the relative phase of the interference pathways. Importantly, we find that this asymmetric dissipation not only renders the optimal blockade condition strictly immune to frequency detuning, but also enhances the blockade depth by an order of magnitude compared to the resonant case. Furthermore, the mean photon number remains almost unaffected, proving that this enhanced robustness is achieved without sacrificing the brightness of the single-photon source. These findings offer a promising route toward robust single-photon generation in passive cavities with second-order nonlinearity.

authors.name: Zhi-Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Ai Zhang, Yan-Zhe Song, Meng-Li Guo, Yan-Hui Zhou

papers.title: u4lib: An AI-Ready Computational Framework for U(4) Symmetry Algebra, Wigner Coupling, and Racah Recoupling Coefficients
papers.summary: Wigner's supermultiplet symmetry treats nucleon spin and isospin within a common U(4)/SU(4) description. The C++ library u4lib supplies the coupling coefficients and algebraic operations needed for calculations in this scheme. Users can construct irreducible representations (irreps), obtain dimensions and Casimir invariants, conjugate states, enumerate the canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin and physical $\mathrm{SU_S(2)}\otimes\mathrm{SU_T(2)}$ bases with inner multiplicities, and decompose tensor products. Matrix-element routines cover the canonical U(4) generators and the physical spin $\mathbf{S}$, isospin $\mathbf{T}$, and Gamow-Teller-type tensor $\mathbf{U}$. Wigner coupling and Racah recoupling coefficients are evaluated by the 2024 procedure of Dang et al. The implementation builds on u3lib, with a header-only C++ interface and corresponding Python bindings. A catalog of agent skills assists an AI agent in preparing, executing, and checking calculations through natural-language requests.

authors.name: Phong Dang (Department of Physics and Astronomy, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, LA 70803, USA), Daniel Langr (Department of Computer Systems, Faculty of Information Technology, Czech Technical University in Prague, Prague 16000, Czech Republic), Tomas Dytrych (Nuclear Physics Institute, Czech Academy of Sciences, 250 68 \v{R}e\v{z}, Czech Republic, Department of Physics and Astronomy, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, LA 70803, USA), Michela Negro (Department of Physics and Astronomy, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, LA 70803, USA)

papers.title: Electronic Wichmann-Kroll correction to the energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms
papers.summary: Using modern multiloop calculation methods, we obtain correction to energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms due to the leading-order ($\propto\alpha (Z\alpha)^3$) Wichmann-Kroll electronic potential. Our result is expressed in terms of generalized polylogarithms. As a byproduct, we also obtain the Wichmann-Kroll potential in momentum space in terms of the same functions.

authors.name: Roman N. Lee, Alexey V. Popov

papers.title: A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
papers.summary: Cardiovascular fluid dynamics modeling relies heavily on mesh-based numerical methods such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). While accurate, these methods entail significant computational costs and complex meshing workflows that limit their translation to clinical practice. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless alternative that embeds the governing equations directly into neural network training. In this work, we propose a PINN framework for pulsatile blood flow in patient-specific geometries with dynamic lumped-parameter Windkessel (RCR) outlet conditions representing distal vascular impedance. Coupling the Windkessel ODE to a 3D network raises two difficulties: the ODE alone does not fix the pressure level, and the local pressure variations that drive the flow are orders of magnitude smaller than the basal pressure imposed by the outlet. We address them by decomposing pressure into a time-dependent basal part and a spatially varying part, an initial condition and gauge for the Windkessel equation, a global mass-balance constraint, and a periodic Fourier embedding of time. Validated on 2D canonical channels (steady and pulsatile, with and without RCR outlet), the framework is then applied to a patient-specific right pulmonary artery, reproducing outlet flow, mean pressure, and the velocity and dynamic pressure fields with errors on the order of the data resolution. Finally, we solve the inverse problem of identifying the three Windkessel parameters of the outlet from synthetic data, recovering them with errors of about 0.3% from deliberately wrong initial values. Residual biases in the local pressure field and the need to test robustness to noisy clinical data remain open, but the results support PINNs as complementary tools for meshless hemodynamics and patient-specific digital twins.

authors.name: Celia Taboada, Luis Nu\~nez, Ang\'elica Casero, Pedro Navas

papers.title: Optimizing MHz X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy with burst-mode free-electron laser operation
papers.summary: Burst-mode X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) provide a powerful platform for X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) experiments with sub-microsecond temporal resolution, but the achievable performance is constrained in practice by both photon statistics and the sample's dose tolerance. Here, we develop an analytical framework for estimating the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of pulsed XPCS measurements, including pulse-to-pulse fluctuations of the incident intensity. We combine this description with dose constraints and show that, for a fixed maximum dose, acquiring fewer frames at higher per-pulse intensity yields a higher SNR than distributing the dose over a larger number of low-intensity frames. The framework is validated against measurements at the European XFEL, where the intensity fluctuations of the investigated operation mode are found to cause only a negligible reduction in SNR. We further introduce and experimentally demonstrate a rolling bunch pattern with three pulses per train and variable pulse spacings. This scheme enables more than an order-of-magnitude increase in the accessible per-pulse intensity while maintaining equilibrium dynamics. Our results provide practical guidelines for optimizing dose-efficient MHz-XPCS experiments and for evaluating future XFEL operation modes.

authors.name: Johannes M\"oller, Wonhyuk Jo, Trey Guest, Lars Fr\"ohlich, Matthias Scholz, Marc Guetg, Felix Brau{\ss}e, Aliaksandr Leonau, James Wrigley, Ulrike Boesenberg, Lea Brings, J\"org Hallmann, Jan-Etienne Pudell, Angel Rodriguez-Fernandez, Roman Shayduk, Alexey Zozulya, Nimmi Das Anthuparambil, Michelle Dargasz, Sonja Timmermann, Maddalena Bin, Foivos Perakis, Michael Paulus, Felix Lehmk\"uhler, Christian Gutt, Anders Madsen

papers.title: One-Step Self-Assembling Lipopolymer Coatings Enable Direct Longitudinal Biosensing in Native Biological Matrices
papers.summary: Sample-driven cross-reactivity remains a fundamental bottleneck for sensitive and selective biosensing in complex biological environments, particularly in microfluidic systems where high surface-to-volumes ratios amplify non-specific interactions. Here, we address this challenge with a one-step, biomimetic surface functionalization strategy based on engineered lipid-based nanocarriers that self-assemble within minutes into immunoassay-ready, antifouling interfaces that couple pegylated-lipid passivation with biorthogonal, site-specific probe conjugation. This approach enables rapid, tuneable, and reproducible surface functionalization, which suppresses sample-specific cross-reactivity even in undiluted serum, and supports direct, label-free digital biosensing assays directly in native biological environments. When integrated into an optofluidic platform combining digital in-line holography and microfluidics, this approach allows time-resolved quantification of tetraspanin-positive extracellular vesicle secretion dynamics from two-dimensional and three-dimensional lung cancer cell models using 50 {\mu}L of sample within 10 min, without isolation or purification. Because the presented surface functionalization proceeds via self-assembly rather than covalent surface modification, this one-step modular-approach is intrinsically decoupled from device fabrication and applies to both glass and PDMS, coating the entire microfluidic channel, thereby establishing a general route for integrating biomimetic nanostructures into robust, high-performance immunoassays, advancing biosensing beyond end-point measurements, and towards rapid and continuous real-time monitoring.

authors.name: Pascal R\"uedi, Sarina Seiter, Stephan Handschin, Chiara Lombardo, Jaime Ortega Arroyo, Romain Quidant

papers.title: Actively stabilized Fabry-P\'erot notch filters for correlated photons from cold two-level atoms
papers.summary: We report two actively stabilized Fabry-P\'erot cavities operated as reflection-mode notch filters for biphotons generated by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a cold two-level atomic ensemble. In this source, elastic scattering at the excitation frequency increases the single-detector count rates and the accidental-coincidence background, thereby limiting the observed nonclassical correlations. One cavity is placed in each photon-collection mode. An acousto-optic modulator frequency-dithers an auxiliary field, and synchronous demodulation of the transmitted power provides the locking discriminator. Light resonant with the auxiliary field is transmitted, whereas the detuned components are reflected toward the photon detectors. By tuning the auxiliary field to the same frequency as the excitation field, we filter these components and direct a larger portion of the quantum-correlated sidebands to the detection. The cavities have linewidths of approximately 2 MHz and remain locked for longer than a typical correlation acquisition. The measured Cauchy-Schwarz parameter exceeds unity in both configurations, with a higher central value with filtering ($\overline{R} = 4.15 \pm 0.93$) than without ($\overline{R} = 2.33 \pm 0.20$). This architecture provides actively stabilized rejection of a narrow spectral interval, simultaneously, for two fields detected in different directions. Filter performance could be further improved by adjusting the cavity linewidth to better match the spectral width of the central component and by reducing losses in the filters.

authors.name: G. C. Borges, M. Duclerc, G. Palacios, A. A. C. de Almeida, N. R. de Melo, D. Felinto

papers.title: Nutrient limitation drives Turing instabilities in cross-feeding microbial communities
papers.summary: Microbial communities are shaped by metabolic interactions, often in the form of cross-feeding in which microbes exchange metabolites via diffusion through the environment. We show here that the diffusion of cross-fed metabolites generically leads to a Turing instability in resource-poor environments, driven by the feedback between local metabolite availability and cell growth. A coarse-grained model of community biomass identifies the few dimensionless parameters that control the instability, most notably the ratio of environmental energy supply to cellular maintenance costs. We find that the detailed topology of the metabolic interaction network can be coarse-grained into a single effective parameter to quantitatively characterise the instability. Beyond the onset of the instability, the community forms compact aggregates whose merger is prevented by a competition for shared resources. Overall, our results demonstrate how spatial structure can arise as an inevitable consequence of metabolic interactions in a microbial community.

authors.name: Jan Kocka, Steven A. Redford, Jaime Agudo-Canalejo, Kabir Husain

papers.title: Lacrymaria-like dynamics: compression and length change in active slender bodies
papers.summary: Length change is central to the behaviour of many active slender bodies, yet most elastohydrodynamic models of microscopic locomotion treat filaments as effectively inextensible. Here we introduce a compressible $N$-link formulation for planar active filaments, in which both bending angles and segment lengths are dynamical variables coupled through local hydrodynamic drag, modelled using resistive force theory. We first use the model to test whether passive extensibility can improve bending-driven swimming and crawling. Across the parameter ranges studied, passive compressibility usually reduces locomotion speed, indicating that axial compliance alone is not a robust mechanism for propulsion enhancement. We then prescribe active rest-length waves and show that compression can either enhance, suppress, or redirect locomotion depending on its phase, wavelength, and frequency relative to bending. Finally, motivated by the extensible neck dynamics of \textit{Lacrymaria olor}, we apply the method to clamped and free filaments driven by oscillatory follower forces. These examples show that elastic compression-bending coupling can reorganise swimming, exploration, and locomotion in strongly deforming active filaments.

authors.name: Cl\'ement Moreau, Yukinori Nishigami, Johann H\'erault, Kenta Ishimoto

papers.title: Disentangling Lengthscales in Disordered Fracture
papers.summary: The interplay between quenched disorder and collective interactions can generate multiple emergent lengthscales in damage processes, yet their roles in determining the strength of heterogeneous materials remain incompletely understood. Here, we develop a coarse-grained description of load redistribution in the two-dimensional random fuse model (RFM) with Weibull-distributed quenched disorder, interpreting shielding in the crack-tip damage density as a consequence of nonlocal current redistribution. Our numerical results distinguish this emergent screening length, identified as the size of the statistical fracture process zone, from the regularizing length in Bazant's established quasibrittle size-effect law (SEL), revealing their distinct disorder dependences, and challenging previous associations of the two. We further uncover a comparable scaling between the SEL and pre-failure crack extension, suggesting the former may instead be more naturally associated with a percolation process of micro-fractures around the crack-tip. These findings disentangle important emergent lengthscales within the RFM, and highlight a candidate physical mechanism for explaining macroscopic size effects in quasibrittle fracture.

authors.name: Matthaios Chouzouris, Marcelo A. Dias

papers.title: Edge-dislocation interactions with sub 3 nm vacancy and interstitial clusters in FeCr alloys: Mechanisms, Obstacle strength and Fate
papers.summary: Fe-Cr alloys harden at irradiation doses where transmission electron microscopy (TEM) shows no defects, implicating defects too small to be resolved. Their obstacle strength is unknown, so hardening models ignore them and fit measured hardening to visible defects alone. Here, molecular dynamics drives an edge dislocation through relaxed 1-3 nm vacancy and mixed Fe-Cr interstitial clusters in Fe-3Cr, Fe-5Cr and Fe-10Cr at 300 K. Vacancy clusters relax into platelets whose strength rises with size to about 350 MPa at 2.9 nm, following strong-obstacle scaling independently of Cr content, and always survive dislocation passage. Interstitial clusters relax into $\frac{1}{2}\langle 111 \rangle$, mixed or $\langle 100 \rangle$ loops. They are mostly weaker than platelets of the same size, their strength varies up to fivefold with the local Cr arrangement, and most are absorbed. Only $\langle 100 \rangle$ loops in Fe-5Cr and Fe-10Cr often survive. During pinning, Cr collects at the junction between these loops and the dislocation; atom tracking for one loop shows that more than half comes from the loop itself. Surviving loops are not stronger than absorbed ones: strength and survival are thus distinct. Computed dispersed-barrier strengths ($\alpha \approx$ 0.02-0.25) are upper bounds that lie below the $\alpha$ values obtained in earlier studies by fitting hardening to TEM-visible loops. These earlier values are therefore inflated by TEM-invisible defects. Wherever small vacancy clusters form, they are more effective obstacles than interstitial clusters of the same size. These defect-specific strengths and fates provide a physical basis for models of low-dose hardening.

authors.name: Layatmika Sahoo, Suchandrima Das

papers.title: Bayesian Quantum Thermometry of Ultracold Gases with Non-Equilibrium Single-Atom Probes
papers.summary: Precise thermometry is essential for experiments with ultracold quantum gases, but conventional techniques such as time-of-flight thermometry are destructive and lose sensitivity at low atomic densities. Quantum probes provide an alternative route by encoding temperature information in accessible internal degrees of freedom. Here, we implement Bayesian thermometry with non-equilibrium spin-based single-atom probes immersed in an ultracold atomic bath. Temperature-dependent spin-exchange collisions map the bath temperature onto the internal spin populations of the probe atoms. Measurements of these populations are then used to iteratively update a Bayesian temperature estimate. We connect the information gained at different measurement settings to the underlying spin dynamics, identifying intersections of temperature-dependent population trajectories as a source of thermometric ambiguity. Using the expected information gain to optimize measurement settings, we experimentally compare unoptimized, a priori optimized, and adaptively optimized protocols. Both optimized protocols accelerate convergence, with the adaptive protocol reducing the average number of measurements required to reach a prescribed precision by a factor of 2.5 compared with the unoptimized protocol. In the many-measurement regime, we further characterize the protocols through their asymptotic error scaling and the accumulation of Fisher information, while testing consistency with the expected Cram\'er-Rao bound (ECRB) and the Bernstein-von Mises theorem. These results connect the microscopic dynamics of a quantum probe to efficient measurement design and establish Bayesian spin thermometry as a practical approach for ultracold-gas experiments.

authors.name: Julian Fe{\ss}, Luca Granert, Sabrina Burgardt, Silvia Hiebel, Alexander Guthmann, Mohammad Mehboudi, Mart\'i Perarnau-Llobet, Artur Widera

papers.title: Geometrical Estimation of Electromagnetic Degrees of Freedom in Reflecting Environments
papers.summary: The number of spatial degrees of freedom (NDoF) of electromagnetic communication channels in reflecting environments is investigated using a full-vector formulation based on dyadic Green's functions and equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents. The channel correlation eigenproblem characterizes the electromagnetic communication modes and their coupling strengths, while the leading-order NDoF is estimated geometrically from the receiver-accessible phase space volume in the electrically large regime. By combining two geometrical projection Jacobians, the phase space volume is related to the mutual shadow area, establishing the equivalence between the two geometrical NDoF formulations and yielding a two-polarization estimate equal to twice the mutual shadow area divided by the squared wavelength. The free-space mutual shadow formulation is extended to perfect electric conductor (PEC) reflecting environments through image construction and phase space ray tracing, accounting for specular reflections and geometrical visibility constraints. The formulation is validated against the eigenvalue spectra of full-vector electromagnetic channels involving planar PEC reflectors, a parabolic reflector, a parallel-plate waveguide, and a non-line-of-sight L-shaped corridor. The geometrical predictions agree with the observed spectral transitions across configurations involving multiple reflections, focusing, and blockage.

authors.name: Yanwen Chen, Stefano Maci, Mats Gustafsson

papers.title: Cyclic perturbations encode memories in trained neural networks without loss of performance
papers.summary: Many disordered materials exhibit a remarkable form of memory: they retain information about the history of cyclic perturbations. Whether this phenomenon also occurs in artificial neural networks, whose mathematical structure and dynamics share many similarities with disordered physical systems, is unknown. Here we show that cyclically perturbing a trained, overparameterized deep neural network encodes information in the structure of the weights that can subsequently be retrieved, thus retaining memory of the perturbation history. During each write cycle, all weights are displaced, after which the network relaxes through gradient descent. Repeated cycles organise the neural network into a state that is reversible for perturbations up to the write amplitude, allowing the encoded value to be read from the onset of irreversible weight motion. Multiple memories can also be encoded, although under deterministic writing only the largest persists at long times. Inspired by cyclically sheared suspensions, we introduce a novel noisy-write protocol that preserves all encoded memories at long times. Remarkably, neither deterministic nor noisy memory writing measurably affects the network's performance on unseen data from its original learning task. Our results establish cyclic memory as a phenomenon shared by disordered physical systems and deep neural networks, and show that networks can exploit as yet unexplored memory capabilities without compromising their original function.

authors.name: Max Kerr Winter, Liesbeth M. C. Janssen

papers.title: Penalty-Free Constrained Optimization on Dynamic Quantum Circuits via Phase-Protected Tunneling and Closed-Loop Spectral Ratchets
papers.summary: Embedding hard operational constraints into an unconstrained Hamiltonian via large penalty multipliers induces quadratic spectral aliasing during phase estimation and increases two-qubit gate depth. This paper proposes a penalty-free, closed-loop dynamic quantum circuit scheme, designated as Zeno-decoupled gauge-ratchet optimization (Z-GRO), for constrained binary optimization without outer-loop training. Reversible feasibility phase operators within symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes confine evolution to the feasible subspace, while an interaction-correlated commutator gauge operator resolves initial symmetry stall. Directional cooling couples the unpenalized objective Hamiltonian to a reusable ancilla with a zero-two-qubit-gate threshold offset, bypassing echoed tunneling gates on retained branches. A survival-filtered Ramsey controller advances the threshold from a linear-programming bound with automatic overshoot rollback. Exact density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles show a single-check discrimination gain above four orders of magnitude, improving ground-state probability by factors of 3.0 to 4.3 over quantum Zeno dynamics and 11.4 to 22.5 over penalized schemes. Z-GRO reduces the spin-glass time-to-solution scaling base to 1.529 (compared to 1.684 for quantum Zeno dynamics and 1.909 to 2.047 for penalized schemes) and lowers 14-qubit knapsack time-to-solution by factors of 2.4 to 14.5. For two-qubit gate error rates between $5 \times 10^{-4}$ and $5 \times 10^{-3}$, Z-GRO achieves 2.9 to 7.0 times the optimal probability of noisy penalized feedback, while majority shielding limits loss to 6.3% at a 5.0% readout bit-flip rate, recording 0/24, 0/25, 0/96, 3/25, and 2/80 overshoots.

authors.name: Chia-Ho Ou

papers.title: The Fiscal and Economic Implications of Green Mandates: a Boltzmann Approach to Public Governance
papers.summary: Public authorities increasingly need to translate multifaceted policy objectives into concrete fiscal and investment choices while accounting for their socioeconomic consequences. A credible ex-ante impact assessment should report downstream implications attributable to the historical baseline and specified policy targets, without introducing discretionary assumptions about unknown administrative, socioeconomic or other physical processes. Bringing the large-scale perspective of statistical physics to public governance, we construct such an ex-ante impact assessment. Its scope encompasses policy objectives that condition a finite number of generalized moments of observables in the historical baseline, which comprises a sufficiently large collection of projects or public programmes. As a proof-of-principle application, we consider the green transition in the energy-generation sector using the historical baseline of many infrastructure projects from the World Bank. Our earlier results deriving closed-form expressions for coarse-grained combinatorial probabilities enable a tractable statistical and downstream assessment. We assess the statistical compatibility of the historical baseline with different levels of green-power surplus and demonstrate how the same statistical-physics construction can estimate any downstream metric expressible through arbitrary functions of generalized moments of the baseline observables. In the absence of more detailed knowledge about the processes forming the historical baseline, large-scale universality, whenever many unknown influences on collective phenomena become negligible, unambiguously offers a principled route to a self-contained ex-ante impact assessment.

authors.name: Katerina Savvaidou, Georgia Foudoukidou-Louka, Ho-Ryun Chung, Orestis Loukas

papers.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
papers.summary: The performance of Rydberg-atom receivers is seldom stated as a radio-frequency (RF) link budget. The receiver is shown to be an intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical link whose modulator is the laser-driven vapor. The transmission of a warm vapor is derived in closed form by averaging the four-level response over atomic velocities. The conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, intercept points, and spurious-free dynamic range follow from this one function. For a weak probe the instantaneous bandwidth is half the width of the transparency window in two-photon detuning. The local-oscillator beat places the second-order intercept near twice the local-oscillator field, so the local oscillator sets the even-order linearity. For a rubidium transition at 17.04 GHz the closed forms agree with a velocity-resolved density-matrix model to 1% for the slope and the intercepts and to 10% for the bandwidth. They underestimate the group delay by a third. The response is tied to atomic constants, and the sensing volume escapes the Chu limit. However, the noise figure of a warm vapor rules it out as a general replacement for an antenna and low-noise amplifier.

authors.name: David Rosser
