papers.title: Molecular structure breaks universality in screening behavior of electrolyte solutions
papers.summary: Electrostatic screening is one of the most fundamental phenomena in electrolyte solutions. While dilute electrolytes are described by the universal Debye--H\"uckel theory, recent experiments have reported an apparently universal scaling law for screening lengths in concentrated electrolytes, fueling ongoing debate over anomalous underscreening. Yet, liquid state theory has been unable to determine whether molecular details of the solvent, the ions, or both should preserve or break such universality. Using machine-learned classical density functional theory, we compute numerically exact decay lengths across a hierarchy of electrolyte models of increasing molecular complexity. We find that molecular details qualitatively reshape screening: solvent attraction generates a new monotonic decay mode, solvent polarity produces re-entrant behavior, and ionic structure alone can drastically alter screening-length exponents. Consequently, no single scaling law describes screening universally across these molecularly distinct electrolytes. Our results challenge equilibrium interpretations of experimentally observed universality in concentrated electrolytes.

authors.name: Anna T. Bui, Connie J. Fairchild, Dominic P. W. Thomas, Stephen J. Cox

papers.title: Observation of rotonic density enhancement at the boundary of a uniform dipolar superfluid
papers.summary: The collective excitations of a quantum liquid lie at the heart of its emergent behaviour. In many systems, the variation of excitation energy ${\varepsilon}$ with wavevector $k$ exhibits a softening at a characteristic lengthscale, which plays a key role in thermodynamics and transport. These excitations, termed rotons, often reflect an underlying tendency of the liquid to crystallize into a competing symmetry-broken state, such as the solid state of helium or the Wigner crystal of electrons in a magnetic field. More than $50$ years ago, it was predicted that rotons should manifest as emergent density oscillations at the fluid's boundary, but this effect has not been observed. Here, we realize an ultracold dipolar superfluid confined in a homogeneous trapping potential and directly confirm the emergence of rotonic density enhancement at its edge. This is accompanied by rotonic density fluctuations across the bulk, which are linked to the static edge structure via the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. Increasing the dipolar character leads to an azimuthal density modulation of the fluid's boundary, which we show to be analogous to the behaviour of a quasi-one-dimensional fluid confined in an annular optical potential.

authors.name: Jasmine Kalia, Kiryang Kwon, William J. Solorio Hernandez, Rubaiya R. Emran, Aryan Prasad, Richard J. Fletcher

papers.title: Binary Decision Process in Pre-Evacuation Behavior
papers.summary: In crowd evacuation the time interval before decisive movement towards a safe place is defined as the pre-evacuation phase, and it has crucial impact on the total time required for safe egress. This process mainly refers to situation awareness and response to an external stressors, e.g., fire alarms. Due to the complexity of human cognitive process, simulation is used to study this important time interval. In this paper a binary decision process is formulated to simulate pre-evacuation time of many evacuees in a given social context. The model combines the classic opinion dynamics (the French-DeGroot model) with binary phase transition to describe how group pre-evacuation time emerges from individual interaction. The model parameters are quantitatively meaningful to human factors research within socio-psychological background, e.g., whether an individual is stubborn or open-minded, or what kind of the social topology exists among the individuals and how it matters in aggregating individuals into social groups. The modeling framework also describes collective motion of many evacuee agents in a planar space, and the resulting multi-agent system is partly similar to the Vicsek flocking model, and it is meaningful to explore complex social behavior during phase transition of a non-equilibrium process.

authors.name: Peng N. Wang, Peter B. Luh, Peter Sincak, Laura Pitukova, Xuesong Lu, W. M. Wonham, Timo Korhonen

papers.title: Experimental and Monte Carlo Simulation Studies to Characterize a Low-Pressure Gas-Based Positive-Ion Detector with a Nanometer-Equivalent Sensitive Volume
papers.summary: Compact low-pressure gas-based positive-ion detectors offer a promising approach to measuring particle track structure at the nanometer scale. These detectors use electric fields to collect and multiply positive ions produced by the incident radiation in mm-sized holes in dielectric materials, achieving a nm-equivalent spatial resolution of the localization of ionization events when scaled to liquid water at unit density. In this work, a detector prototype featuring a 1.5 mm-diameter hole in a dielectric plate was experimentally characterized. Ion collection and multiplication were achieved by applying a negative high potential to the glass cathode 0.5~mm below the hole, assisted by a low drift field above the plate. A grounded readout electrode with a 0.8 mm hole covers the hole to prevent interactions of collected ions with the hole walls. The experimental setup was further modeled with Geant4-DNA and Garfield++ for deeper insight. By combining the measurements with the Monte Carlo simulations, a per-ion signal formation probability in the low single-digit percentage range was determined. Further, the signal formation mechanism, commonly attributed to ion-impact ionization within the hole, was critically examined. Ion-induced secondary electron emission from surfaces was considered a possible contributor to, or the primary mechanism of, signal formation that has not been addressed in detail in previous studies of this detector concept. Despite the extensive measurements and simulations, the available evidence did not reveal which physical processes governed signal formation or whether either mechanism dominates. We discuss key limitations in the current understanding of this detector class and propose future targeted measurements and simulations to clarify the signal formation mechanism and guide the development of compact positive-ion detectors and nanodosimeters.

authors.name: Victor Merza, Aleksandr Bancer, Vladimir Bashkirov, Ana Belchior, Beata Brzozowska, Jo\~ao F. Canhoto, Piotr Gasik, Jaroslaw Grzyb, Khaled Katmeh, Marcin Pietrzak, Antoni Ruci\'nski, Reinhard Schulte

papers.title: Combined effects of evaporation, sedimentation and solute crystallization on the dynamics of aerosol size distributions on multiple length and time scales
papers.summary: We investigate three aspects of aerosol-mediated air-borne viral infection mechanisms on different length and time scales. First, we address the evolution of the size distribution of a non-interacting ensemble of droplets that are subject to evaporation and sedimentation using a sharp droplet-air interface model. From the exact solution of the evolution equation we derive the viral load in the air and show that it depends sensitively on the relative humidity. Secondly, from Molecular Dynamics simulations we extract the molecular reflection coefficient of single water molecules from the air-water interface. This parameter determines the water condensation and evaporation rate at a liquid droplet surface and therefore the evaporation rate of aqueous droplets. We find the reflection of water to be negligible at room temperature but to rise significantly at elevated temperatures and for grazing incidence angles. Thirdly, we derive a thermodynamically consistent three-dimensional diffuse-interface model for solute-containing droplets that is formulated as a three-phase Cahn-Hilliard/Allen-Cahn system. By numerically solving the coupled system of equations, we explore representative scenarios that show that this model reproduces and generalizes features of the sharp-interface model. These interconnected studies on the dynamics of aerosol droplet evaporation are relevant in order to quantitatively assess the airborne infection risk under varying environmental conditions.

authors.name: Sina Zendehroud, Ole Kleinjung, Philip Loche, Lyd\'eric Bocquet, Roland R. Netz, Erica Ipocoana, Dirk Peschka, Marita Thomas

papers.title: Three-dimensional photon transport in spinodal photocatalytic aerogels: how bicontinuous morphology controls kinetic rate constants
papers.summary: Anatase TiO2 dispersed in a silica aerogel matrix forms porous monolithic photocatalysts promising for indoor air purification and VOC photo-degradation. Their bicontinuous spinodal architecture provides high surface area, structural integrity, and intense UV multiple scattering. Extracting kinetic descriptors from apparent rate constants requires an optical model for the photon fluence, and current practice replaces the 3D pore network by a homogeneous 1D slab with effective optical coefficients -- an approximation never quantified for spinodal geometries. We combine realistic 3D spinodal pore masks from Cahn-Hilliard spectral integration with 3D GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo (MC) photon-migration simulations, introducing the solid-phase-weighted estimator $\Phi_{3D}$ and comparing it with the conventional volume average $\Phi_{1D}$ and the diffusion-approximation (DA) prediction $\Phi_{DA}$. The ratio $\Phi_{3D}/\Phi_{1D}$ equals 1.515 at porosity $\phi=0.70$ and 1.774 at $\phi=0.90$: the solid phase is preferentially illuminated, traced to optical phase contrast. Since pores neither absorb nor scatter, photons cross quasi-ballistically, and the void phase sustains only $r=0.514$ of the solid-phase fluence, diluting the volume average with dark voxels. This ratio is porosity-independent, so the concentration ratio obeys the exact relation $1/[\phi r+(1-\phi)]$, reproducing both simulated values. The kinetic descriptor $k_{surf}\cdot K_{ads}$ is underestimated by 20% via the DA route and overestimated by 51.5% via the volume-averaged route. Homogeneous-slab MC simulations at matched optical thickness show that 84% of the fluence-weighted RMS discrepancy between MC and DA is intrinsic to the bicontinuous architecture and beyond any effective-medium DA. These results give a quantitative correction for kinetic extraction and design rules linking porosity, pore size and photon utilisation.

authors.name: Renaud A. L. Vall\'ee

papers.title: Self-organized photonic time quasicrystal from a single imposed clock
papers.summary: A photonic time crystal usually writes a clock into a medium. Here one clock does more than program the medium: it seeds a quasiperiodic temporal order that the nonlinear medium selects for itself. In a guided-wave lattice of nonlinear dipoles, a single-tone pump modulates the polarization sector, while Maxwell--polarization back-action selects two response frequencies whose only resolved low-order relation is the pump-locked sum condition. Their sum phase locks to the pump and the complementary phase winds, producing a photonic discrete time quasicrystal with torus-like phase dynamics and a discrete combination spectrum. Site-resolved measurements show locked-phase coherence across the measured lattice sites over a finite control-parameter window. These results establish a route from externally programmed time-varying media to self-organized temporal order in nonlinear photonic systems.

authors.name: Minwook Kyung, Kyungmin Lee, Yung Kim, Eun-Gook Moon, Joonhee Choi, Bumki Min

papers.title: Two-way coupling in active suspensions suppresses mobility-selective accumulation and induces non-monotonic flow stabilization
papers.summary: Swimmers live in moving fluids: the flow organizes their spatial distribution, and their collective motion reshapes the flow in turn. We experimentally study the two-way coupling between a swarm of centimeter-scale swimmers (Artemia salina) and an electromagnetically driven quasi-two-dimensional cellular flow. We report two key findings, one in each direction of the coupling. First, at low swimmer density, the swarm recovers the mobility-selective accumulation onto the attracting hyperbolic Lagrangian coherent structures (LCSs) predicted by one-way-coupled simulations: the accumulation is strongest when the swimming speed is comparable to the flow speed. As the density increases, the swarm still accumulates on the LCSs, but the mobility selectivity is progressively lost. Second, we examine the back-action of the swarm on the LCSs. A swarm has previously been found to disrupt the LCSs. We find that the response depends on the swimmer density and the background forcing. Denser swarms tend to disrupt the LCSs more strongly, as previously reported. However, at stronger forcing, adding a moderate number of swimmers instead stabilizes the LCSs.

authors.name: Ziyue Yu, Aineo M. Wu, Lei Fang

papers.title: Biophysics of the Pyrenoid
papers.summary: Phase-separated liquid droplets organize molecules in cells, but the underlying physical principles differ from abiotic mixing and quantitative rules in living systems remain poorly understood. The pyrenoid -- a liquid-like organelle that enhances photosynthetic carbon fixation in algae and hornworts -- provides an unusually tractable model system. Here, we review recent advances in our understanding of pyrenoids from the perspective of biophysics. We highlight how reaction-diffusion models connect compartment architecture to catalytic performance, how soft matter theories link molecular interactions to condensate assembly, and how modern experimental methods enable these predictions to be tested quantitatively. Recent studies suggest that pyrenoid function may be described by a small number of effective transport and reaction processes, while condensate assembly can be understood through molecular design parameters and thermodynamic constraints. Together, these findings establish the pyrenoid as a powerful system for investigating catalytic compartmentalization, biomolecular self-organization and the emergence of effective physical descriptions in living systems.

authors.name: Charley Schaefer, Mark Leake

papers.title: Maximum updraft velocity beyond CAPE: the role of boundary layer dynamics and pressure perturbations
papers.summary: Deep convective updraft velocities influence precipitation extremes, lightning, and the planetary energy budget. Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE) is widely used to explain maximum updraft velocity ($w_{\max}$), but updrafts are also influenced by entrainment, boundary layer dynamics, pressure perturbations, and condensate loading. However, the relative importance of these processes and how they interact to set $w_{\max}$ in individual clouds remains unclear. Here, we use neural networks validated across climate regimes to identify generalizable pre-storm predictors and in-cloud diagnostics of $w_{\max}$ in individual tracked clouds. We then distill these into compact, physically interpretable equations, using idealized radiative-convective equilibrium simulations spanning a range of sea surface temperatures and radiative cooling rates. For pre-storm prediction, CAPE and local mean boundary layer vertical velocity ($\overline{w_{bl}}$) together explain nearly half the variance in $w_{\max}$ across regimes ($R^2=0.47$). CAPE captures regime-mean differences, but it has little predictive value within a single simulation, where $\overline{w_{bl}}$ captures cloud-to-cloud variability, including low $w_{\max}$ at high CAPE. At the time of peak intensity, a simple approximate Bernoulli-like invariant combining maximum pressure perturbation and maximum cloud condensate explains 89% of the variance ($R^2=0.89$). The tight link between $w_{\max}$ and pressure perturbation is consistent with the sticky-thermal view and highlights dynamic pressure effects, often neglected in updraft theories. Both relationships remain skillful in additional simulations at horizontal grid spacings down to 125 m. These results highlight $\overline{w_{bl}}$ as an important regulator of convective intensity alongside CAPE, and indicate that dynamic pressure plays an important role within individual updrafts.

authors.name: Bety Pechacova, Alejandro Casallas, Tom Beucler, Lokahith Agasthya, Caroline Muller

papers.title: Reduced Density Matrix Functional Theory Across Molecules and Periodic Systems: Short-Range Screening and Coupled Optimization
papers.summary: Reduced density matrix functional theory (RDMFT) provides a rigorous framework for describing many-electron systems, yet its application to periodic systems has long been hindered by two major challenges: the lack of accurate, transferable functionals and the computational inefficiency of orbital-occupation optimization. Here, we address both challenges by developing a periodic RDMFT framework that enables the simultaneous optimization of Bloch natural orbitals and their occupation numbers through coupled optimization (CO). Using this framework, we demonstrate that physically motivated short-range screening substantially improves the transferability of the Power functional across molecular and periodic systems. Beyond improving energetic accuracy, short-range screening enhances numerical robustness by smoothing energy profiles during optimization and improves computational efficiency through rapid reciprocal-space convergence of the long-range contribution. The CO algorithm consistently reduces the number of optimization iterations relative to conventional decoupled optimization, with reductions approaching an order of magnitude for representative periodic solids. Furthermore, the screened $\omega$P22 functional outperforms widely used semilocal and hybrid density functionals, including PBE and PBE0, in predicting molecular and surface reaction barriers. These findings establish an efficient computational framework for periodic RDMFT and identify short-range screening as a promising design principle for developing accurate and transferable one-body reduced-density-matrix functionals.

authors.name: Shuxin Pei, Neil Qiang Su

papers.title: Harnessing thermo-optic dynamics for frequency-agile soliton microcombs
papers.summary: Dissipative Kerr soliton microcombs enable compact and scalable frequency comb sources for precision metrology, spectroscopy, communications and coherent LiDAR, where broad and reliable frequency tuning is essential. Thermo-optic response can support thermal locking during soliton operation, enabling resonance tracking and thereby extending the tuning range, albeit modestly. However, it also induces pronounced thermal instability during soliton initiation, hindering reliable access to this extended operating regime and limiting practical deployment in applications requiring frequency agility. Here we show that strong mode coupling reshapes the effective detuning trajectory governing soliton formation, establishing a distinct operating regime in which thermo-optic response is significantly reinforced and constructively harnessed. In this regime, soliton formation proceeds without the thermal instability inherent to conventional operation, enabling robust soliton generation in material platforms previously limited by strong thermal effects. Importantly, the enhanced thermo-optic response strengthens thermal locking during soliton operation, enabling more effective resonance tracking and substantially extending the tuning range. Leveraging this regime in AlGaAs-on-insulator multimode microresonators, we demonstrate soliton generation with a tuning range approaching 100 GHz at a sustaining pump power of 32 mW, following initiation at 50 mW. The same mechanism further enables frequency-agile operation through direct pump-frequency tuning without auxiliary stabilization, allowing massively parallel chirped comb generation with more than 90 channels exhibiting frequency excursions exceeding 10 GHz. These results establish an effective approach for combining direct soliton access with enhanced thermo-optic resonance tuning, enabling robust and frequency-agile integrated soliton microcombs.

authors.name: Yang Liu, Suwan Sun, Yueguang Zhou, Yanjing Zhao, Chaochao Ye, Xinda Lu, Yi Zheng, Leif Kastuo Oxenl{\o}we, Kresten Yvind, Hairun Guo, Minhao Pu

papers.title: Broadly Tunable Compact Non-Coplanar X-Ray Cavity for Cavity-Based Free-Electron Lasers
papers.summary: Cavity-based x-ray free-electron lasers (CBXFELs) require tunable x-ray cavities to serve a broader range of scientific applications. We consider and analyze a compact, tunable, noncoplanar x-ray cavity based on six Bragg-reflecting crystals arranged as two three-crystal backscattering units in either a mirror-symmetric or a twofold rotationally symmetric configuration. Its three-dimensional geometry provides a much larger tuning range than planar bowtie cavities while keeping a compact transverse footprint. We derive analytical expressions for the cavity geometry, crystal kinematics, and polarization-dependent Bragg reflectivity in both the intrinsic and eigenpolarization bases. For a given Bragg reflection, the ideal photon-energy range spans $E_{\mathrm H}$ at backscattering to $2E_{\mathrm H}$ at $\theta=\pi/6$, corresponding to 100\% tunability. Geometrical and polarization constraints reduce the directly usable range to approximately 58\%. Operating in the cavity eigenpolarization basis can extend it further, limited only by the narrowing angular acceptance of the Bragg reflections. By combining fundamental and harmonic diamond reflections, as well as reflections from different crystallographic families, the accessible photon-energy range can be extended from about 3~keV to approximately 18~keV. These results establish noncoplanar multi-crystal cavities as a potentially viable route to compact, broadly tunable x-ray resonators for future CBXFELs.

authors.name: Yuri Shvyd'ko

papers.title: Impact of Environmental Stress on Low Gain Avalanche Diode Sensors Response
papers.summary: Low Gain Avalanche Diodes or LGADs are silicon sensors capable of achieving excellent timing resolution due to their characteristic internal gain. Detectors based on LGAD technology play a crucial role in High Energy and Nuclear Physics experiments, among other applications. However, their performance is affected by environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, and storage conditions. A systematic evaluation of the response of LGAD sensors as a function of these environmental parameters is therefore of essential importance for any application. LGAD sensors fabricated at the Brookhaven National Laboratory are characterized and stress-tested against various operating conditions, such as rapid temperature and humidity changes. Dedicated and detailed simulations are used to interpret the experimental results.

authors.name: Mohamed Hijas Mohamed Farook, Gaetano Barone, Diallo Boye, Gabriele D'Amen, Gabriele Giacomini, Timo Peltola, Jennifer Roloff, Enrico Rossi, Trevor Russell, Sally Seidel, Alessandro Tricoli, Lixing Wang

papers.title: What Photocurrent Versus Effective Voltage Tells Us About Charge Generation in Organic Solar Cells
papers.summary: The photocurrent of an organic solar cell is routinely plotted against an effective voltage and used to extract an exciton dissociation probability, and through it a free-charge generation efficiency. The photocurrent measures neither. Using a drift-diffusion model in which free-charge generation is field independent and losses occur only by bimolecular recombination, we show that the apparent dissociation probability returned by this procedure lies well below unity even for complete dissociation. Across wide variations of carrier mobility and recombination strength it is a single-valued function of the fill factor and coincides with the short-circuit charge collection efficiency, reporting neither the generation yield nor anything about collection beyond what the fill factor already shows. Even for ideal transport the normalised photocurrent saturates below unity at an intensity-independent first-order limit set by recombination of photogenerated carriers with injected equilibrium charge. Applied to four organic solar cells whose generation efficiencies are known independently, the apparent dissociation probabilities track the short-circuit collection efficiency rather than the generation yield. We therefore suggest this construction not be used, particularly in the high-efficiency non-fullerene acceptor systems that are now state of the art.

authors.name: Ardalan Armin, Austin M. Kay, Drew B. Riley, Oskar J. Sandberg, Paul Meredith

papers.title: Dynamic distortion from discretized coupling feedback in soft-spin Ising machines
papers.summary: Although Ising machines (IMs) have grown in popularity as physics-based accelerators for combinatorial optimization, most literature focuses on empirically obtained benchmarks with low universality. We propose dynamic feedback distortion as a universal, platform-agnostic metric for the effect of coupling field discretization in time-multiplexed IMs. Its closed form consists of a static offset and a harmonic series: a mid-tread coupling element (or a half-step bias) removes the former, and injected noise (dither) attenuates the latter. In a simulated optoelectronic IM, 2-bit mid-tread feedback with noise below half a quantization step solves a 50 spin M\"obius ladder in up to 99\% of runs. In a coherent IM, dithered 2-bit mid-tread feedback outperforms 4-bit mid-rise feedback on a M\"obius ladder and matches 4-bit feedback on 2D tiling problems. Triangular dither performs best when the spatial-frequency content of the ground state is unknown. These results show that reducing the static and harmonic components of the network distortion greatly increases the success rate of low-resolution quantized IMs.

authors.name: Victor H. Gonz\'alez, Natalia G. Berloff

papers.title: Continuous-Wave Operation at 30 MV/m of a Superconducting Radio-Frequency Gun Cryomodule with an Exchangeable Cathode Plug
papers.summary: A prototype 185.7 MHz superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) electron gun cryomodule has been developed for the proposed LCLS-II-HE Low Emittance Injector at SLAC. It has an in-situ ultra-high-vacuum exchangeable cathode plug system compatible with semiconductor photocathodes. With a copper plug, the gun achieved continuous-wave RF operation at a cathode field of 30 MV/m. No measurable degradation was observed after plug removal and reinsertion with the cavity at 4.4 K. This result is a significant improvement over past continuous-wave SRF gun systems with exchangeable plugs.

authors.name: T. Konomi, T. Xu, Y. Choi, K. Elliott, B. Gower, B. Tousignant, J. Wenstrom, A. Taylor, C. Compton, W. Chang, X. Du, W. Hartung, S. H. Kim, S. Miller, D. Morris, M. Patil, L. Popielarski, J. Wei, Z. Yin, J. Smedley, J. Maniscalco, C. Adolphsen, M. Murphy, D. A. Gonnella, M. P. Kelly, T. Petersen, A. Arnold, S. Gatzmaga, R. Steinbr\"uck, P. Murcek, R. Xiang, J. Teichert, J. Lewellen

papers.title: Real-Time Event-Based Optical Camera Communication at 80 kbit/s over a 320 m Outdoor Link with 120{\deg} Field-of-View
papers.summary: We demonstrate an event-based optical camera communication system using a 120{\deg} field-of-view sensor. In daylight, three transmitting nodes achieve an aggregate 240 kbit/s, with individual links reaching 106 kbit/s at 1 m and 80 kbit/s at 320 m. Our results, establish a new baseline for event-OCC.

authors.name: Francesco Nardo, Peter Kr\"otz, Ricardo Barrios, Sebastian Randel

papers.title: Multiple harmonics from a hand-struck tube: a simple and precise measurement of the speed of sound
papers.summary: The speed of sound in air can be determined from the resonance frequencies of the harmonic waves inside a thin cylindrical tube. A pressure wave is generated in the tube by striking several times one of its ends with an open hand and keeping the hand in place. In this way pulses of short duration are produced which propagate along the tube and decompose into a superposition of harmonic waves whose frequencies are determined by the harmonics present in a tube open at one end and closed at the other. The tube thus acts as a filter that reinforces those harmonic waves exhibiting an acoustic pressure antinode (particle displacement node) at the closed end and an acoustic pressure node (particle displacement antinode) at the open end. Their frequencies are determined by these boundary conditions, while waves with different frequencies cancel out by destructive interference. Recording the sound with a microphone connected to a computer and analyzing its spectrum with freely available software, the resonance frequencies are obtained and the speed of sound is determined with an accuracy better than $0.5\%$. The whole experiment requires nothing but a tube, a microphone and free software, so it is inexpensive, takes a few minutes to set up and is well suited to introductory physics laboratories.

authors.name: Francisco Echegorri, Martin Monteiro, Cecilia Stari, Arturo C Marti

papers.title: Hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet $2^{3}S(L = 0)-$state in the two-muonic helium ${}^{3}$He $\mu_{2}$ atom
papers.summary: The hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet $2^{3}S(L = 0)-$state in the two-muonic helium ${}^{3}$He $\mu_{2}$ atom is determined to high accuracy. Such a structure arises as a result of hyperfine (or spin-spin) interaction between the triplet two-muonic shell and non-zero spin of the central helicon nucleus. Our result for the hyperfine structure splitting is $\Delta \approx 2.5811701551505 \cdot 10^{8}$ MHz, where the standard uncertainty has been evaluated as $\pm 100$ Hz.

authors.name: Alexei M. Frolov

papers.title: A Momentum-weighted Interface Stabilization Approach for Fluid-Structure Interaction with Strong Added-Mass Effects
papers.summary: Partitioned fluid-structure interaction (FSI) schemes enable the reuse of standalone fluid and structural solvers but may exhibit poor convergence under strong added-mass effects, particularly when structural inertia is small relative to fluid inertia. This work examines the added-mass instability of Dirichlet-Neumann partitioned coupling through a fixed-point analysis of the discrete FSI system. Comparison with the monolithic formulation identifies the interface momentum contributions lagged during partitioned iterations and establishes spectral conditions governing convergence. Motivated by this analysis, a momentum-weighted interface stabilization (MWIS) method is developed by augmenting the fluid pressure operator with an approximation of the coupled interface momentum response. The augmentation is fixed-point consistent, leaving the converged discrete solution unchanged when the coupled equations are solved to convergence. A sparse approximation constructed from fluid and structural interface operators and element metrics limits additional storage and inter-solver data exchange. Numerical experiments involving a linear FSI model and established nonlinear benchmarks demonstrate improved convergence and coupling robustness under strong added-mass effects compared with the baseline Dirichlet-Neumann scheme. The results establish an operator-based framework for stabilizing partitioned FSI iterations while retaining the modularity of standalone solvers.

authors.name: Nihar Bhardwaj Darbhamulla, Aditya Narkhede, Xiaoyu Mao, David Brown, Rajeev K. Jaiman

papers.title: The shear Alfv\'en continuum of optimized stellarators
papers.summary: The shear Alfv\'en continuum has been studied extensively in tokamaks, but its gap structure in modern optimized stellarators has received less attention, despite its importance for energetic-particle confinement in fusion pilot plants. We compute and compare the continua of five reactor-scale stellarator equilibria: two quasi-axisymmetric (QA), two quasi-helically symmetric (QH), and one quasi-isodynamic (QI). We present selective Fourier mode schemes that provide a sufficient resolution of eigenfrequencies within the frequency range of interest. In all five configurations, the widest gap is the HAE(2,$N_{\text{fp}}$) gap, which is driven by rotating ellipticity. This gap lies in the frequency range of strong resonance with prompt fusion-born alphas in the QA configurations but not in the QH and QI configurations, suggesting that QH and QI configurations may be easier to optimize for alpha confinement. Near-axis theory predicts the HAE(2,$N_{\text{fp}}$) and EAE gap widths well but overestimates the MAE gap widths and the gap widths of the QI configuration. These discrepancies likely arise from interactions between gaps, which depend on the rotational transform profile and are not captured by near-axis theory.

authors.name: Abdullah Hyder, Elizabeth Paul, Alexey Knyazev

papers.title: Physics-Based Differentiable Beamforming for Deep Learning-Based Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound Super-Resolution Imaging
papers.summary: Ultrasound is widely used for vascular imaging because it is non-invasive, real-time, and cost-effective. However, its spatial resolution remains limited by diffraction to an order of the acoustic wavelength. This limitation is particularly restrictive for imaging of the microvasculature and high-resolution vector-flow-imaging. In this work, we present a multi-channel physics-based deep learning approach to super-resolve monodisperse microbubbles directly from multi-channel radio-frequency (RF) data. We also present a novel image-based metric for model evaluation. The proposed pipeline combines a learnable deconvolution network with a differentiable beamforming layer, enabling a direct deconvolution of the microbubble (MB) signature prior to image formation. By operating on multi-channel RF data, the method aims to improve localization robustness in the presence of dense microbubble populations and deconvolve the lateral direction in a relatively low-frequency regime (1.7 MHz) where MBs exhibit nonlinear behavior. The model is trained and evaluated on simulated data using monodisperse lipid-coated MBs over a broad range of acoustic pressures and microbubble densities. The proposed method improves the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to the single-channel approach. It achieves sub-wavelength axial and lateral resolution while slightly improving robustness to dense microbubble populations outside the training domain. It also demonstrates generalizability across transmit configurations without requiring explicit training on each transmit configuration.

authors.name: Anass Hameddine, Bram de Wilde, Michel Versluis, Jelmer M. Wolterink, Guillaume Lajoinie

papers.title: Long-Term Stable Three-Axis Single-Beam Alignment-Based Atomic Magnetometer Using an Uncoated Buffer-Gas-Free Rubidium Ampoule for Unshielded Geomagnetic Monitoring
papers.summary: Optically pumped magnetometers achieve exceptional sensitivity, yet sustaining long-term baseline stability in unshielded Earth-field environments (~50,000 nT) remains challenging. We present the design, quantum-interference principles, calibration, and unshielded validation of a three-axis single-beam alignment-based atomic magnetometer built from an unmodified, uncoated, buffer-gas-free commercial rubidium (Rb) ampoule and a single 795 nm VCSEL. Pumped with $45^\circ$-oriented linearly polarized light on the $^{87}$Rb $D_1$ ($F=2 \to F'=1$) transition, the sensor exploits ground-state Zeeman quantum interference (rank-2 spin alignment), intrinsically cancelling first-order vector light shifts. Dual-zone 20 kHz AC heating ($75.0^\circ$C lower liquid Rb reservoir, $85.0^\circ$C upper optical zone) suppresses window condensation and thermal magnetic gradients over 29 days. Without buffer-gas pressure broadening, the VCSEL is stabilized via direct absorption spectroscopy at an optimized 3530 Hz dither frequency, eliminating odd-harmonic intermodulation leakage. A hybrid balanced polarimeter extracts $B_x$, $B_y$, and laser-lock errors from total absorption (sum channel) and $B_z$ from alignment-induced linear dichroism (difference channel) within an active zero-field compensation loop using a 12-bit microcontroller in a dual-stage mid-ranging architecture. Spectral analysis yields sub-LSB noise amplitudes of 0.5-5 pT at 1 Hz (15-150 $\mathrm{pT}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$), rolling off to 0.1-1 pT (3-30 $\mathrm{pT}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$) near 10 Hz. Continuous unshielded geomagnetic monitoring in Okayama benchmarked against synthesized Kakioka and Kanoya observatory records demonstrates high tracking fidelity and bounds instrumental bias instability to $\le 0.1$ nT at 100-200 s integration times.

authors.name: Minaru Kawamura

papers.title: Fermions inside the geometric algebra of spacetime
papers.summary: The (signed) basis versors of the geometric algebra of spacetime form the extraspecial groups of order 32. Ignoring signs and the unit element, we show that the remaining fifteen normalized basis versors can be written as, or factorized into, a unit space bivector (of three-dimensional space) and an isoversor. Isoversors are: the volume trivector of space, the pseudoscalar, and the basis time-axis vector. Our first result is that this central product structure, already known for extraspecial groups, also holds in the geometric algebra of spacetime and is crucial for exhibiting generators of continuous groups in the algebra. In a second main result, inspired by Hestenes' 1982 paper ``Spacetime structure of weak and electromagnetic interactions'', we uncover two pairs of special unitary groups of degree two and three (in various representations). A rich algebraic structure emerges, leading us to our third main result: the description inside the geometric algebra of spacetime of thirty-two particles of matter and antimatter in a single generation. The sixteen matter particles, four leptons (left/right with up/down isospins) and four triplets of quarks (with three colors in addition to chirality and isospin), are gathered four by four into quadrispinors in two different ways: particles in a quadrispinor have either the same color or the same isospin and chirality. Thanks to this twofold distribution of the sixteen matter particles inside four quadrispinors, the same continuous group based on the isoversors produces the electroweak and strong gauge symmetry. However, chirality forbids the gauge mixing of left and right particles, which motivates the restriction to SU(2) $\times$ U(1) for the electroweak interaction. Finally, as a fourth main result, we thoroughly study the dynamics of quadrispinors by generalizing the conventional treatment of bispinors in geometric algebra.

authors.name: Gatien Verley

papers.title: Experimental Evidence for MeV Undulator Radiation Generated by Ultrarelativistic Positrons in a Periodically Bent Crystal
papers.summary: We report evidence for undulator radiation generated by ultrarelativistic positrons in a large-amplitude, long-period crystalline undulator. A pattern of Si$_3$N$_4$ stressors periodically bend the (110) planes of a Silicon crystal with a geometry measured independently by x-ray diffraction. Under planar alignment, the forward energy loss showed a localized excess at $6.8 \pm 0.3$~MeV ($4.05\sigma$), matching the predictions of simulations. Experimental results also indicate that an intense positron beam could make the undulator competitive in brilliance with state-of-the-art inverse-Compton gamma-ray sources.

authors.name: L. Bandiera, N. Canale, S. Carsi, M. Cavallina, F. Cescato, N. Charitonidis, D. De Salvador, M. Diaz Castro, E. Diociaiuti, P. Fedeli, L. G. Foggetta, A. Forlani, A. Gianoli, V. Guidi, L. Malagutti, F. Mancarella, S. Mangiacavalli, A. Mazzolari, R. Negrello, G. Patern\`o, M. Prest, J. Reyes Garrido, M. Romagnoni, A. Saputi, F. Sgarbossa, A. Sytov, V. V. Tikhomirov, E. Vallazza, D. Valzani

papers.title: Polarized positron generation via laser-engineered quasistatic magnetic fields in a spatially extended herringbone target
papers.summary: Polarized positron sources are of interest for precision studies of spin-dependent interactions and future high-energy colliders, yet their laser-driven realization remains challenging because of demanding laser or beam requirements. Here, we propose a target-engineered scheme for generating polarized positrons using a 3.4-PW single-color laser pulse and an initially unpolarized 10-GeV electron beam. Three-dimensional spin-resolved quantum electrodynamics particle-in-cell simulations show that laser-driven return currents in a herringbone target generate spatially extended quasistatic magnetic fields exceeding $\simeq 10^6$ T, with opposite polarities and a duration exceeding 100 fs. These fields correlate positron spin polarization with deflection direction, enabling angular selection of two oppositely polarized positron populations with polarization magnitudes of 63\% and a combined yield of approximately 0.007 positrons per incident electron, compared with a total yield of 0.029. Our results demonstrate a route toward highly polarized positron generation under laser conditions accessible to existing petawatt-class facilities, without requiring frequency-converted ultraintense fields or prepolarized incident beams.

authors.name: Xian-Zhang Wu, Hui-Jing Li, Huai-Hang Song, Wei-Min Wang, Yan-Fei Li

papers.title: GenerativeQC: A Generative, GPU-Accelerated Quantum Chemistry Program
papers.summary: GenerativeQC is an open-source, GPU-accelerated quantum chemistry program that computes energies and analytic nuclear forces from Hartree-Fock (HF) and density functional theory (DFT) to closed-shell density-fitted CCSD(T) and an MP2-assisted CCSD(T)/complete-basis-set (CBS) composite. Its scientific compiler translates symbolic equations into C++ and CUDA code and uses automatic differentiation to generate the derivative and response programs required for analytic forces. A native runtime executes these programs together with hand-written iterative solvers and integral routines. Across Direct and density-fitted HF and DFT benchmarks for eight methods on water clusters of up to 96 atoms, GenerativeQC is faster than GPU4PySCF in every tested case on both RTX 5090 and H100 GPUs. For correlated wave functions, compiler-generated derivative contractions and transpose Jacobian operators enable complete density-fitted CCSD(T) and CCSD(T)/CBS analytic forces on GPUs; a CCSD(T)/CBS energy-and-force calculation for heptane (23 atoms) takes 4.5 min on a single H100 GPU and 17 min on an RTX 5090.

authors.name: Shengrui Xu, Longhan Shen, Wenxi Zhai, Tong Zhu, Jinzhe Zeng

papers.title: Consistent interfacial flow numerics - Part I: The gravity force term
papers.summary: The OpenFOAM solver interFoam for incompressible two-phase flows combines the single-phase PISO/PIMPLE algorithm for the pressure-velocity coupling with an interface advection step. It relies on the standard finite volume discretisation of the momentum equation, which assumes smooth fields, but across a water-air interface the density jumps by a factor of about 1000. The geometric Volume-of-Fluid method isoAdvector, used in interIsoFoam, made the advection step consistent with a sharp interface, but spurious velocities near it remain due to the momentum discretisation. This series revisits it term by term. Here we treat the gravity term, which acts only at the interface and depends on the local interface height. Both solvers crudely assign this height using the face centre positions. We show that this is a key source of the spurious air velocities. Taking the height from the reconstructed interface instead gives an exact discrete balance between pressure and gravity for a horizontal interface on any mesh. We implement this geometric gravity model in a new solver, interIsoGoam. In a tilted box of still water, where the original solvers give air speeds of metres per second, it keeps the velocity of order $10^{-9}$ m/s. This holds for density ratios up to $10^7$ and, with a hydrostatic initial pressure, on skewed and locally refined meshes. In a progressive wave, interIsoGoam has the lowest maximum velocity of the three solvers. At maximum Courant numbers of 0.1 and below it therefore needs up to 43 % fewer steps and up to 38 % less wall-clock time. At 0.5 the wave grows by up to 12 % over 15 periods, so we recommend 0.1 or less. One error remains, namely an overprediction of the horizontal water velocity below the wave crest. All three solvers exhibit this error, which grows steadily with time. In Part II we trace this error to the implicit discretisation of the momentum convection term.

authors.name: Johan Roenby, Konstantinos Missios, Kasper M{\o}ller, Sithik Aliyar, Henning Scheufler

papers.title: Consistent interfacial flow numerics - Part II: The momentum convection term
papers.summary: The two-phase Volume-of-Fluid solvers of OpenFOAM overpredict the horizontal water velocity near the crest of a water wave, and the error grows as the wave propagates. Part I of this series removed the spurious air velocities caused by the gravity term but left this error unchanged. Here we show that it is caused by the momentum convection term. Its mass flux is computed in the interface advection step from the velocity at the start of the time step, whereas the convected velocity is taken at the end of the step, because convection is discretised implicitly. In a progressive wave, where the horizontal and vertical velocities are 90 degrees out of phase, this time lag produces an upward flux of horizontal momentum, proportional to the time step, which accumulates in a spurious current near the surface. The same mismatch makes the response to a force depend on the density at the wrong time level. Explicit convection removes the lag and makes the response consistent with the gravity force, but requires the convected face velocity at the interface to be taken from the upwind cell. Only then is the new velocity of a cell a weighted average of old velocities, whatever the density ratio. We demonstrate both requirements with prescribed flows and with the full solver. For a progressive wave, explicit convection with upwind face velocities at the interface reduces the overprediction of the crest velocity from 26-31 % to within 1 % and removes the near-surface current. The resulting solver, fluxinator, is meant for maximum Courant numbers of 0.1 and below, where it keeps the wave height within 1.5 % over 15 periods on meshes with six or more cells per wave height. Because the spurious velocities that limit the time step are removed, it needs 34-42 % less wall-clock time than interFoam for the tested wave.

authors.name: Johan Roenby

papers.title: Dephasing-free plasma acceleration with millijoule picosecond lasers
papers.summary: Laser-plasma accelerators reach gradients a thousand times above radio-frequency cavities, but need joule-class femtosecond lasers firing about once per second, and electrons outrun the wave. A comb of laser lines spaced by the plasma frequency, each in its own mode of a matched channel, drives a wake moving at the speed of light. In particle-in-cell simulations a 175\,mJ, 0.5\,ps drive holds 21\,GV/m over 10\,mm with a 0.15\,rad phase drift; a test electron gains 208\,MeV, 2.6 times more than in one mode. Because the wave builds up resonantly, the required energy falls steeply with density: a 29\,mJ drive sustains 20\,GV/m, and a 10\,mJ drive, within reach of kilohertz industrial lasers, gives a test electron 170\,MeV over 30\,mm. A simulated stage transfers 5\,\% of the laser energy to the wake; the Manley--Rowe limit is about 18\,\% for five lines.

authors.name: Alexander Pukhov

papers.title: Photonic processors that carry their own unclonable fingerprint
papers.summary: Physically unclonable functions (PUFs) derive cryptographic keys from uncontrollable fabrication disorder, removing the need to store secrets in vulnerable non-volatile memory. Programmable photonic processors are natural candidates for PUFs, because each of their many tunable interferometers carries its own fabrication imperfections. However, we show that the mesh topology itself funnels light along short paths, so that most of this disorder contributes little to the response. Here we introduce an isotropic ring routing scheme that steers light to the core of a hexagonal mesh and redistributes it uniformly towards the perimeter, suppressing a distance-dependent power decay of 14.7 dB and raising the mean Shannon entropy of the response from 1.95 to 3.48 bits by reprogramming alone. Experiments on two independently fabricated 72-unit silicon processors show that a nominally identical device cannot reproduce the target's responses even after its passive phase profile is fully compensated. Combining isotropic routing with spectral readout yields 1107 bits per challenge, exceeding previous results by two orders of magnitude, with 49.8% inter-challenge and 50.0% inter-chip Hamming distances and a 4.9% intra-chip distance. These results establish general-purpose programmable photonic processors as reconfigurable, high-capacity hardware roots of trust.

authors.name: Oxel Arnal Mart\'inez, Pablo Mart\'inez-Carrasco Romero, David \'Alvarez Outerelo, Francisco Javier Fraile-Pel\'aez, Jos\'e Capmany Francoy

papers.title: Trajectory-based cycle-level pedestrian crash prediction at intersections: A novel non-linear link function for block maxima led Bayesian GEV framework addressing heterogeneous traffic conditions
papers.summary: This study develops a cycle-level framework for estimating pedestrian crash risk at signalized intersections under heterogeneous, non-lane-based traffic. Existing approaches often assume linear relationships between covariates and parameters, oversimplifying the complex, non-monotonic interactions among motorized vehicles (MVs), non-motorized vehicles (NMVs), and pedestrians. To address this limitation, the framework introduces a non-linear link function within a Bayesian generalized extreme value (GEV) structure to capture how traffic effects vary. It applies extreme value theory through the block maxima approach using post-encroachment time as a surrogate safety measure, with each signal cycle serving as an analysis block. It also proposes a behaviour-normalized modified crash risk (MRC) metric to account for pedestrians' habitual risk-taking behaviour in Dhaka's mixed traffic. Seven hierarchical Bayesian models were estimated using Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulation and compared using the deviance information criterion. Models with a non-linear link function only in the GEV location parameter fit the data better than their linear counterparts. Results suggest pedestrian speed is negatively associated with crash risk, while flow and speed of MVs, pedestrian flow, and NMV conflicting speed show positive associations, though all remain uncertain. The selected model's MRC estimate was close to the observed crashes at a 93% confidence level tuned to this dataset. These results suggest that the non-linear structure adds flexibility for capturing the non-stationary and non-linear nature of traffic extremes. This framework is a step towards proactive identification of pedestrian crash risk and after wider validation, it could support adaptive signal control and safety interventions in mixed-traffic environments.

authors.name: Parvez Anowar, Nazmul Haque, Md Asif Raihan, Md Hadiuzzaman

papers.title: Efficient Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Long-time Quantum Dynamics
papers.summary: Accurately simulating long-time dynamics of many-body systems is a challenge in both classical and quantum computing due to the accumulation of Trotter errors. While low-order Trotter-Suzuki decompositions are straightforward to implement, their rapidly growing error limits access to long-time observables. We present a framework for constructing efficient high-order Trotter-Suzuki schemes by identifying their structure and directly optimizing their parameters over a high-dimensional space. This method enables the discovery of new schemes with significantly improved efficiency compared to traditional constructions, such as those by Suzuki and Yoshida. Based on the theoretical efficiency and practical performance, we recommend two novel highly efficient schemes at $4^{\textrm{th}}$ and $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of these decompositions on the Heisenberg model and the quantum harmonic oscillator, and find that for a fixed final time they perform better across the computational cost. Even when using large time steps, they surpass established low-order schemes like the Leapfrog. Finally, we investigate the in-practice performance of different Trotter schemes and find the decompositions with more uniform coefficients tend to feature improved error accumulation over long times. We have included this observation into our choice of recommended schemes.

authors.name: Marko Male\v{z}i\v{c}, Johann Ostmeyer

papers.title: Interferometrically Enhanced Asymmetry in Strong-field Ionization with Bright Squeezed Vacuum
papers.summary: We demonstrate that quantum light statistics can be used to control strong-field ionization at the tunneling step leaving the average driving field unchanged. Using a bichromatic linearly polarized field composed of a strong coherent driver and a weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV), we show through simulation that the asymmetry of the resulting photoelectron momentum distributions is significantly enhanced, with the skewness increasing by roughly two orders of magnitude compared with an equally weak coherent perturbation. A semiclassical analysis based on the strong-field approximation (SFA) reveals that the effect originates from asymmetric fluctuations in the instantaneous field amplitude, which strongly modify the tunneling ionization probability while leaving the electron's continuum dynamics essentially unchanged. The resulting amplification provides a proof of concept for enhancing phase-sensitive signatures of sub-cycle ionization dynamics.

authors.name: G. Singh, T. Rook, J. Rivera-Dean, C. Figueira de Morisson Faria

papers.title: Contracting Tensor Networks with Generalized Belief Propagation
papers.summary: Recent years have seen a growing interest in the use of belief propagation (BP), an algorithm originally introduced for performing classical statistical inference on graphical models, for approximate, but highly efficient tensor network contraction. BP is a corner case of generalized belief propagation (GBP), a family of classical inference methods in which messages are passed within a hierarchy of overlapping regions. Here, we detail how to apply GBP to tensor network contraction. We implement GBP with different region choices on finite and infinite tensor networks in two and three dimensions, solving the corresponding fixed point equations numerically and, in tractable cases, analytically. We consider a range of quantum and classical examples, including frustrated Ising models, three-dimensional ice models, independent-set counting on irregular graphs, and the norms of the deformed AKLT state and random tensor network states. Across our examples, including the quantum ones, converged GBP often reduces errors by several orders of magnitude compared with BP.

authors.name: Joseph Tindall, Grace M. Sommers, Hilbert Kappen

papers.title: Quantum Metric and Nonlinear Hall Effect of Photons
papers.summary: Using the path-integral formalism, we show that photons possess a nontrivial quantum metric in momentum space. We derive the semiclassical action and equations of motion by taking into account the quantum metric. In media with a spatially varying refractive index $n(\mathbf{x})$, the quantum metric induces a shift in the trajectory of light at second order in spatial gradients of $n$, whose transverse component may be regarded as a nonlinear Hall effect of light. The quantum metric also gives rise to corrections to photon propagation relevant to gravitational lensing in curved spacetime at second order in wavelength, including a gravitational nonlinear Hall effect arising from the interplay between the geometry of position space and that of momentum space.

authors.name: Keidai Akiba, Naoki Yamamoto

papers.title: Energy spectra and cascade in the spin turbulence of a driven spinor Bose-Einstein condensate
papers.summary: We investigate the spin-interaction energy spectrum of spin turbulence in a driven spinor Bose-Einstein condensate. Continuous spin driving of a spin-1 condensate produces a nonequilibrium steady state with spatially fluctuating magnetization. We observe a power-law scaling consistent with the $-7/3$ exponent predicted for spin-wave turbulence, which persists across our full range of drive strengths despite substantial changes in the spectral anisotropy. After switching off the drive, we track the free-decay evolution and find evidence consistent with a direct cascade of spin-interaction energy toward higher wavenumbers. These results establish an energy-spectral hallmark of spin turbulence and enable quantitative studies of cascade dynamics in spinor superfluids.

authors.name: Junghoon Lee, Jongmin Kim, Donggyu Lee, Yong-il Shin

papers.title: An interpretable closed form for entanglement entropy from bitstrings, guided by a graph neural network
papers.summary: The empirical bitstring distribution is the most accessible observable on Rydberg-atom arrays, but the bipartite von Neumann entropy it constrains is far costlier to obtain. We present a six-term linear closed form for the entropy, built from bitstring features whose choice is guided by a trained graph neural network (GNN). Probing the GNN shows that its entropy prediction is routed through the atom pairs that straddle the bipartition boundary, so we compute the two-point correlators over these pairs only. An exhaustive search scored against exact entropies then selects the form. The form is human-readable but less accurate than the GNN in distribution, where its mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.024 nats is 6.4 times larger. Fit once and applied unchanged, however, it has lower MAE than the base GNN on five of six out-of-distribution pools and ties it on the sixth. Refit per Hamiltonian family, it reaches 29-70 millinats (mnat) on the four sign-definite families we tested. Further out of distribution, we test it on density-matrix renormalisation group ground states of up to one hundred atoms. There the slopes must be refit per size, which gives a cross-validated MAE of 15-37 mnat, and size laws fitted to the slopes without the target size give 24-95 mnat with no labels at that size.

authors.name: Anas Saleh

papers.title: Analysis of polarization drift of optical signals over deployed aerial-inground fiber connections
papers.summary: Polarization measurements of a classical 1550-nm signal are collected and analyzed on 15-km hybrid aerial-inground fiber connections over 11 months. The spectral area and spectral moments of mHz-resolution Fast-Fourier-Transform (FFT) of these measurements are extracted, and related to temperature, humidity, wind speed, and time of day. Spectral area correlations show a strong diurnal structure: daytime maxima align with temperatures/wind speed peaks and humidity dips, with lower levels during the night. These diurnal patterns also show seasonality, with higher mean and variance in summer than winter. A random forest regressor is used to estimate FFT features from environmental measurements, informed by a theoretical model.

authors.name: Aneesh Ramaswamy, Nageswara S. V. Rao, Joseph C. Chapman, Muneer Alshowkan

papers.title: Anomalous reflection of caustic spin-wave beams
papers.summary: Reflection at an interface conserves the wave-vector component parallel to it, which fixes the direction of a reflected plane wave. In anisotropic media, however, beams form at caustic points of the iso-frequency contour, where wave vector and group velocity are strongly non-collinear, and it is unclear which of the two descriptions governs the reflected beam. We image caustic spin-wave beams reflecting at the edges of a yttrium iron garnet waveguide by time-resolved Kerr microscopy, varying field magnitude and angle. For a tilted magnetic field, the reflected beam does not carry the wave vector expected from tangential-wave-vector conservation of the incident carrier. Its direction, wavenumber and wavefront angle instead match the outgoing caustic point. Reflecting every plane-wave component of the measured incident field with its tangential wave vector conserved reproduces the reflected beam for all field angles studied. The components add up in phase at the point where the incident beam hits the edge, which therefore acts as a secondary source of a caustic beam. Both descriptions hold at once, one for each component and the other for the beam as a whole.

authors.name: Franz Vilsmeier, Christian Back

papers.title: Sulfur photochemistry traces mantle redox states of rocky planets
papers.summary: Volatile outgassing from planetary interiors controls the composition of rocky exoplanets' secondary atmospheres. However, observations indicate that disequilibrium processes can strongly alter the chemical structure of hot Jupiters. How outgassing and photochemistry jointly determine the resulting atmospheric composition remains an open question. Sulfur-bearing species are promising tracers of interior-atmosphere coupling because their atmospheric abundances are sensitive to both mantle redox state and stellar irradiation. We investigate how photochemistry modifies outgassed atmospheres of diverse Earth-sized worlds during the magma ocean phase and assess how sulfur traces the interior oxidation state. The PROTEUS planetary interior-atmosphere evolution modelling framework is coupled to two chemical models, FastChem and VULCAN. We ran a grid of planetary evolution simulations spanning diverse mantle redox states, instellation fluxes, and host-star spectra. For each case, we compared atmospheric compositions with three post-processing calculations: thermochemical equilibrium, with disequilibrium vertical transport and with vertical transport plus photochemistry. The bulk atmospheric composition remains controlled by the mantle redox state and the history of outgassing. Reduced mantles produce atmospheres rich in H2 and CH4 and oxidised mantles are dominated by CO2 and H2O. Photochemistry affects the low-pressure upper atmosphere, strongly depleting neutral volatiles and enhancing radicals. Synthetic emission spectra show that photochemical SO2 can generate absorption features at 4 um and at 7.3/8.7 um, reaching ~60 ppm and ~100 ppm, respectively, before sequentially returning to the outgassed signatures of ~30 ppm and ~50 ppm for the oxidised mantle redox state. These signatures are potentially detectable with JWST, motivating targeted observational campaigns.

authors.name: Ioannis Panagiotou, Tim Lichtenberg, Shang-Min Tsai, Harrison Nicholls

papers.title: Passive Entropy Rate Bounds the Information Required for Feedback Control
papers.summary: Living organisms across scales, along with many engineered devices, must control noisy systems with limited information to maintain a desired steady state. Here we ask how the performance of a feedback controller is limited by the rate at which information flows from sensors to control actions. We demonstrate that the minimum information rate required is the rate at which the passive dynamics increase the system's entropy. This general result allows us to quantify the information required to achieve a given target performance for a wide-ranging set of control problems. Next, we ask what explicit control protocol maximizes performance for a given information rate. We demonstrate that in many cases the best control strategy is to probabilistically time-reverse the uncontrolled passive dynamics. Implementing this protocol approaches or saturates our bound across a wide range of applications. We showcase these results through applications to stochastic bit control, nonlinear particle localization, microbial navigation, and experimentally realized information engines. Our findings pave the way for the study of feedback control in any settings where limited information is a key constraint, suggest principled explanations for microbial behavior, and provide new insights into fundamental questions regarding the thermodynamic value of information.

authors.name: Matthew P. Leighton, Jose M. Betancourt, Thierry Emonet, Benjamin B. Machta, Michael C. Abbott

papers.title: Better accuracy with fewer qubits: Single-particle basis set optimization for quantum chemistry on quantum computers
papers.summary: In spite of recent advances, quantum computers are expected to be sufficiently noisy in the coming few years to the extent of limiting quantum chemical calculations to relatively small number of orbitals. However, even with reasonable quality single particle basis sets, small active spaces with limited orbitals can result in a significant fraction of correlation energy being lost, motivating the design of moderate quality qubit-efficient basis sets for quantum algorithms. We begin by reoptimizing the existing minimal basis sets using a genetic algorithm-inspired approach in conjunction with aggressive refinement strategies, and generate modified minimal basis sets (MSTO-kG basis; k = 2-11) for atoms from H through F. The ground state energies of H through F using our MSTO bases at FCI level of theory yield ground state energies that are comparable or sometimes even lower than those obtained using 6-31G basis sets. In the case of Li, the MSTO bases surpass the performance of cc-pVQZ bases. Thus, we obtain better atomic energies with same number of qubits relative to STO bases, and better/comparable energies with fewer qubits relative to higher quality bases. In the case of molecules, H2 performs poorly; a finding that is consistent with an earlier work in literature. For other molecules, Li2, C2, LiH, BeH and BeH2, the FCI results (except C2 for which we employ CISD) from our bases are comparable to/outperform those from 6-31G basis. Finally, we compare the resources required between different bases and find that MSTO bases yield better energies than the competing basis sets while incurring fewer qubits and two-qubit gates with VQE, QPE, and HHL. The logical T-gate counts are also found to be considerably lower for QPE and HHL respectively. Overall, our work paves way for more accurate yet less qubit-hungry quantum chemical calculations using near-term quantum computers.

authors.name: Subimal Deb, V. S. Prasannaa

papers.title: A unified geometric design framework for kirigami structures
papers.summary: Kirigami turns a thin sheet with cuts into a shape-morphing mechanical metamaterial, with applications across science and engineering. While various two- and three-dimensional kirigami design methods have been developed, most of them are only applicable to a limited class of kirigami structures. In this work, we present a unified geometric design framework for kirigami structures. Since the states of a kirigami pattern differ only in which tile corners coincide, one tessellation routine generates them all, and edge-length equalities couple them. A single constrained optimization then designs 2D-to-2D, 2D-to-3D, and 3D-to-3D shape-morphing, compact reconfigurable, and rigidly deployable structures, and one sheet that deploys into two prescribed shapes. The designs further reveal geometric laws hidden in the kirigami mechanism, which explain how reconfiguration transposes the shape of a sheet, how one sheet bends into both a bowl and a saddle, and why the outline of a flat sheet limits the curvature it can reach when it closes again. Altogether, our work paves a new way for the design of shape-morphing mechanical metamaterials.

authors.name: Qinghai Jiang, Gary P. T. Choi

papers.title: Maximum-Temperature Theorem for Nanothermometry
papers.summary: We derive a sharp upper bound on the quasi-steady temperature rise of a sensor of arbitrary shape and known thermometric volume $V_\mathrm{s}$, placed anywhere inside a region enclosed by an isothermal reference surface. The bound also requires the maximum net heat power $\dot Q_{\scriptscriptstyle \mathcal S \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}^{\max}$ crossing any closed surface within the region and a lower bound on its thermal conductivity $\kappa_{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}}$. It is otherwise independent of the heat-source distribution, domain shape, and source-ensor distance. For $\dot Q_{\scriptscriptstyle \mathcal S \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}^{\max}=50~\mathrm{pW}$, $\kappa_{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}} =0.1~\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $V_{\mathrm s}$ equal to the volume of a $60~\mathrm{nm}$-diameter sphere, the theorem permits a maximum temperature rise of approximately $2~\mathrm{mK}$. Neither source localization nor uncertain source--sensor separation can therefore account for reported kelvin-scale intracellular readings under steady-state heat conduction. The result applies to sensors based on nanodiamonds, upconversion nanoparticles, fluorescent polymer beads, and core-shell quantum dots.

authors.name: Taras Plakhotnik

papers.title: The spin-transfer inverse Faraday effect in Au/YIG thin film bilayers
papers.summary: The inverse Faraday effect (IFE) (the generation of an effective magnetic field in a material upon irradiation with circularly polarized light) offers a pathway to ultrafast, non-thermal control of spin dynamics. In metallic/ferromagnetic-insulator (NM/FMI) bilayers, IFE-driven spin polarization in the metallic layer can be an alternative to generate magnon excitations in the magnetic insulator which otherwise would be inaccessible with photon energies below the insulator bandgap, but this avenue has remained mostly unexplored. In this work, we investigate the regime of spin-transfer via IFE in Au/YIG bilayers, by means of ultrafast time-resolved magneto-optical experiments. Understanding the mechanism of this spin-transfer IFE in these NM/FMI heterostructures is crucial for several reasons: it elucidates the fundamental coupling between light's angular momentum and collective spin modes at buried interfaces, it enables all-optical generation and manipulation of pure spin currents, and it paves the way toward THz-frequency spintronic devices leveraging the insulator's long magnon lifetimes.

authors.name: Victor H. Ortiz, Daniel Russell, Fengyuan Yang, Roland K. Kawakami

papers.title: Absence of binding for the helium anion
papers.summary: We study the helium anion in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model with an infinitely massive nucleus and spin-$\frac12$ electrons. We prove the absence of binding, with $E^{\mathrm{F}}(3,2)=E^{\mathrm{F}}(2,2)$ and no three-electron ground state. A decomposition relative to the helium ground state and completion of the square reduce the problem to a one-dimensional variational inequality.

authors.name: Hao Liang

papers.title: Memory kernel and closure for systems driven by intermittent forcing with power-law waiting times
papers.summary: Many systems are driven by an intermittent forcing that takes on a random value for a random time interval. For such renewal step noise, the master equation for the driven variable has a memory kernel whose coefficients are the totally time-ordered cumulants, or $G$-cumulants, of the noise. In the case of Poisson switching, these correspond to the Boolean cumulants of the jump distribution, and the kernel can be summed exactly. We derive an exact decomposition of these coefficients for any waiting-time distribution with independent amplitudes and durations, which separates the jump statistics from the renewal statistics. For power-law waiting-time densities, $\psi(\theta)\propto\theta^{-\mu}$ with $\mu>2$ (finite mean), a long time interval is most likely covered by a single epoch, and we prove that, as a result, the coefficients cross over at long lags, at all orders, from the Boolean cumulants to the ordinary moments of the jump law. The long-lag kernel thus becomes a superposition of the kernels of the frozen deterministic flows, weighted by $\xi^2p(\xi)$, and the corresponding master equation follows in closed form. For $2<\mu<3$, where the noise correlation time is infinite, the second-order closure retains a finite error even for slow dynamics, whereas the frozen-flow master equation yields the exact stationary mean in that limit. The telegraph process is the only renewal step noise for which the second-order closure is exact. An exactly solvable model with correlated additive and multiplicative noise confirms these predictions.

authors.name: Marco Bianucci, Riccardo Mannella

papers.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
papers.summary: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.

authors.name: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr, Axel Kleinschmidt, Franca Lippert, Oliver Schlotterer, Yoann Sohnle

papers.title: A matrix model of an M5--brane on a plane--wave background
papers.summary: We construct the maximally supersymmetric deformation of the recently proposed $\mathcal{A}_6$ matrix model on a plane--wave background. We derive the same theory independently, by reducing the light--cone M5--brane on a five--sphere in this background to its lowest harmonics, including the dynamics of its chiral two--form and of its fermions. We then classify all its classical vacua. We show that one of them is the fivebrane giant graviton, and that its fluctuations form a single $\mathfrak{su}(2|4)$ multiplet, which reproduces the $\ell=1$ level of the spherical transverse fivebrane identified in the large $N$ limit of BMN theory. Moreover, the dynamical tensor supports new families of vacua, where the flux balances the size of the brane, and whose spectrum contains that of a fuzzy membrane. Finally, we show that BLG theory sits inside the model, both on a Coulomb branch of the massless theory and around the giant graviton of the massive one, where the two membranes are polarized into the fivebrane.

authors.name: Carmine Montella

papers.title: Onset of quantum chaos in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories
papers.summary: We exhibit random matrix statistics in the scaling dimensions of non-BPS primary operators in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories. Specifically, we consider the sigma model with K3 target space and $\mathcal N=(4,4)$ supersymmetry in a neighborhood of the Kummer orbifold point $\mathbb T^4/\mathbb Z_2$. At the free-fermion radius, the spin-zero spectrum of the $\mathbb Z_2^4$-invariant sector is exactly degenerate at integer energies. The exactly marginal blow-up deformations that preserve this symmetry form a four-dimensional space, whose directions we parametrize by unit quaternions. Along each deformation direction, we compute the first-order splitting of the degenerate levels, i.e., the leading anomalous dimensions as the coupling goes to zero. In sectors where all exact symmetries are resolved, including a hidden $\mathbb Z_2$ at the even levels, the non-zero first-order shifts along a generic direction follow the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE), as we verify by computing several spectral diagnostics. We compare quantitatively with the well-known singlet deformation, which has enhanced symmetry: even after all its known symmetries are resolved, its first-order spectrum has exact degeneracies, its gap ratio approaches the GOE value only slowly as the energy increases, and its unfolded spectrum lacks the long-range rigidity of the GOE.

authors.name: Felix M. Haehl, Moshe Rozali

papers.title: Energy and Charge Transmission at Conformal Interfaces: Relations and Bounds
papers.summary: Symmetry constrains how independently energy and charge can pass through a conformal interface. For interfaces between Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) models $G_{k_L}$ and $G_{k_R}$ preserving the diagonal affine algebra, we derive an exact relation between the energy and charge transmission coefficients, $c_{LR}=2(\dim G)k_{LR}/(k_L+k_R+2h^\vee)$. Together with positivity of outgoing energy, this relation excludes complete energy transmission at unequal levels. With additional bulk degrees of freedom, the equality is replaced by bounds controlled by the coset central charges. Complete transmission from a lower-level WZW model then imposes a lower bound on the coset central charge on the other side. In linear response, the relation fixes the ratio of thermal to charge conductance to the harmonic mean of the two bulk ratios, independently of the interface, while coset sectors bound the thermal conductance at fixed charge conductance. This interface-independent ratio is a generalized Wiedemann--Franz law for conformal interfaces between WZW models. The charge transmission coefficient $k_{LR}$ also governs equilibrium charge fluctuations and fixes the leading quadratic dependence of the boundary-condition-changing operator's scaling dimension on the rotation angle.

authors.name: Yuma Furuta, Yuya Kusuki, Toshiki Onagi, Yin Tang

papers.title: Perturbative $S$-matrix Unitarity in Higher-Derivative Theory of Fermions
papers.summary: We construct a higher-derivative fermion theory with four-Fermi interactions. In quantum field theory, it is conjectured that good high-energy behavior of tree-level scattering amplitudes implies renormalizability, a notion referred to as the tree-unitarity criterion. To investigate whether this criterion is satisfied in a higher-derivative fermion theory, we examine the structure of the $S$-matrix in detail. Owing to the higher-derivative kinetic term, the mass dimension of the spinor field differs from that of a conventional fermion, rendering four-Fermi interactions renormalizable at the cost of introducing ghost states. We show that, unlike bosonic ghosts, fermionic ghosts inevitably give rise to negative-norm states regardless of the sign of their energy eigenvalues. We further demonstrate that, in contrast to conventional four-Fermi theories, the higher-derivative four-Fermi theory satisfies perturbative $S$-matrix unitarity. In light of the tree-unitarity criterion, these results provide supporting evidence for the renormalizability of higher-derivative fermion theories and generalize our previous findings on higher-derivative scalar theories to the fermionic case.

authors.name: Yugo Abe, Takeo Inami, Keisuke Izumi, Shinsuke Kawai

papers.title: String breaking in a (1+1)-dimensional $e^+e^-$ collider
papers.summary: In this paper, we develop a framework for studying solitons in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories using tensor networks, and we apply it to simulate $e^+e^-$ collisions in the massive Schwinger model.
