These results allow a compact persistent-source contribution and a possible spectral turnover between centimeter and millimeter wavelengths, although the present sensitivity and resolution prevent a firm separation from surrounding star-forming emission.

authors.name: Bunyo Hatsukade, Tetsuya Hashimoto, Yuu Niino, Fumi Egusa, Tzu-Yin Hsu, Kotaro Kohno, Kouji Ohta

papers.title: Detection of GRB 261010A with GRID-11B
papers.summary: We report GRID-11B observations of the main emission episode of GRB 261010A. We measure $T_{90}=5.68^{+1.04}_{-0.32}$ s and a minimum variability timescale of $51.6^{+10.5}_{-9.8}$ ms. Its spectrum is described by a cutoff power law with $E_{\rm p}=1089^{+171}_{-80}$ keV. At both candidate host redshifts ($z=0.070$ and $0.785$), the low $\varepsilon$ values and their positions relative to the Amati relation suggest Type-I-like properties. These properties, despite the long duration, resemble those of GRB 211211A and motivate investigation of a possible compact-object merger origin.

authors.name: Chenyu Wang, Longhao Li, Xiaofan Pan, Hua Feng, Ming Zeng, Zihan Yu

papers.title: Stellar activity demotes GJ 9404 b to a planetary candidate
papers.summary: GJ 9404 is a nearby M dwarf ($d=23.8\,\text{pc}$), around which a $13.4586^{+0.0044}_{-0.0067}\,\text{d}$ planet has been claimed in a recent study using 54 publicly available HARPS-N radial velocities (RVs). We re-analyse the spectroscopy associated with this study, and carry out a joint modelling of: (i) stellar rotation in RV, FWHM, and Mount Wilson S-index through Gaussian processes; (ii) long-term trends in all physical quantities; (iii) planetary signals in RV. Current evidence supports the existence of planets in the period range $2-100\,\text{d}$ by at most $\Delta\ln Z=-0.4$ for any considered stellar-activity model, which is insufficient for a widely accepted planet detection. Additional spectroscopy is necessary to accurately quantify the stellar activity of GJ 9404 and determine whether any RV signals warrant further attention.

authors.name: Atanas K. Stefanov, Alejandro Su\'arez Mascare\~no, Jonay I. Gonz\'alez Hern\'andez, Paul Charpentier, Nicola Nari, Rafael Rebolo, Thomas A. Baycroft

papers.title: PLATON 7: An ultra-fast exoplanet atmospheric retrieval code
papers.summary: PLATON is an open source Python package for atmospheric retrieval, first released in 2018. We introduce PLATON 7, a complete rewrite of PLATON using Claude Fable 5. The biggest changes are that PLATON now uses JAX for all intensive calculations, and these calculations are now performed in single precision instead of double precision. These two changes speed up the code by a factor of ~60 with negligible decrease in accuracy, allowing it to compute a 0.8--5.3 um transmission spectrum at R=20k in 0.35 ms on a RTX 5090. We also introduce several new features, including support for two-limb retrievals, patchy clouds, and more opacities (particularly OCS and CS2). PLATON is available on GitHub at https://github.com/ideasrule/platon.

authors.name: Michael Zhang, Tyler Fairnington, Yayaati Chachan, Kimberly Paragas, Eliza Kempton, Heather Knutson, Jacob Bean

papers.title: Lost in the Signal Model: Confusion Between Deterministic and Stochastic Gravitational Wave Signals in Pulsar Timing Array Data
papers.summary: With growing evidence for the presence of a gravitational wave background (GWB) in pulsar timing array (PTA) data, it is imperative to understand how this signal will act as a foreground for other GW signals, particularly those from individual supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), which are predicted to be detected in the next decade. For PTAs, since these two types of signals are long-timescale persistent signals, a signal from an SMBHB system may already be present in the latest PTA datasets. In this work, we analyze how the presence of this signal could affect our detection statistics for the GWB, and how the presence of the GWB can affect our search for the SMBHB system. We find that individual SMBHB signals can significantly skew the recovery of the GWB amplitude and spectral index. However, when the SMBHB signals are recovered consistently, we are again able to recover the GWB power-law parameters, highlighting the importance of joint searches in future PTA searches for GWs. We also explore the rate of improvement of parameter estimation uncertainty, giving insight to the types of signals most likely to be identified well enough to enable multimessenger analyses.

authors.name: Caitlin A. Witt, Nihan S. Pol

papers.title: Blazars through the eyes of REDSoX and GOSoX
papers.summary: Blazar polarimetric properties provide key constraints on the physical conditions within relativistic jets, offering insights into particle acceleration mechanisms, high-energy radiation processes, and jet composition. The Rocket Experiment Demonstration of a Soft X-ray Polarimeter (REDSoX) will serve as a precursor to the Globe Orbiting Soft X-ray Polarimeter (GOSoX), a state-of-the-art polarimeter designed for observations in the soft X-ray range (0.2-0.4 keV), with a planned launch for 2030. REDSoX and GOSoX will be the first (and currently only) X-ray polarimeters capable of performing observations below 1 keV, opening a new observational window into high-energy polarimetry. In this work, we investigate the soft X-ray polarimetric properties of blazars expected in the REDSoX and GOSoX band and assess the detectability of different samples of sources: one drawn from the RoboPol Monitoring Program, a statistically complete sample of gamma-ray-selected blazars spanning the low-, intermediate-, and high-synchrotron-peaked sources, and one cross-matched between the CAZ (CRTS, ATLAS, and ZTF) and eROSITA catalogs. We estimated the expected source fluxes in the selected energy bands through spectral energy distribution fitting performed with the Bjet-MCMC tool. We investigated the expected polarimetric properties under three competing emission scenarios: leptonic, hadronic, and hybrid, each one predicting distinct observational signatures. We assessed the detectability of every source by comparing our polarization degree predictions with the instrument's minimum detectable polarization function (MDP). Finally, we computed the detection probability for each source. This work offers a set of promising blazar targets for future observations with GOSoX, highlighting the mission's potential for probing relativistic jet physics through soft X-ray polarimetry.

authors.name: Sara Capecchiacci, Ioannis Liodakis, Herman L. Marshall, Swati Ravi, Haocheng Zhang

papers.title: Water-ice formation in Ophiuchus follows the local irradiation
papers.summary: Water ice only appears on interstellar dust grains beyond a certain depth into a molecular cloud. This depth has so far been quoted as one extinction threshold per cloud. We measured the threshold along 43009 sightlines through the Ophiuchus cloud with the ice color-excess method, which converts archival WISE and Spitzer photometry of background stars into the peak optical depth of the 3 $\mu$m water-ice band. We sorted the sightlines by the 12 $\mu$m surface brightness of the cloud at fixed extinction, a proxy for the ultraviolet field that excites the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons at the cloud surface. The onset of ice formation lies at higher extinction toward sightlines with brighter 12 $\mu$m emission, ranging from $A_{K_S}^{\rm th} = 0.67$ to $1.15$ mag. It increases by 0.58 to 0.90 mag in $A_{K_S}$ per factor of ten in 12 $\mu$m brightness, depending on the adopted reddening coefficient. Because the 12 $\mu$m-bright and -faint sightlines lie in different parts of the cloud, we repeated the comparison within each of the five subregions, and four of the subregions show the same trend. The trend also persists among sightlines with a similar amount of diffuse material around them. A later onset in more strongly irradiated gas is expected from photodesorption by external ultraviolet light, although a comparison of its size with models requires a calibration of the 12 $\mu$m brightness against the strength of the field. The extinction at which water ice appears thus varies with the local environment, which complicates comparisons between clouds. Photometric ice maps resolve this variation across entire clouds, and the SPHEREx and JWST ice surveys can test it spectroscopically.

authors.name: Stefan Meingast, Zhetai Cao

papers.title: Charge Exchange Illuminates Turbulent Cold-Hot Interfaces
papers.summary: Cold-hot interfaces are ubiquitous in the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM), galactic winds, and the Galactic Center (GC), yet their microscopic contact regions are difficult to observe. Charge exchange (CX), in which a highly ionized metal ion captures an electron from a neutral donor and emits soft X-ray lines, directly probes these interfaces. We develop a subgrid CX model coupled to a nonequilibrium ionization (NEI) network in hydrodynamic simulations of radiative turbulent mixing layers. CX soft X-rays are confined to a thin, highly corrugated cold-hot interface (corrugation factor $\sim10$), whereas thermal emission fills the hot phase. Turbulent transport sustains high-charge ions at $T\sim 10^4$-$10^5$ K, where they encounter neutral donors. The low-temperature O VIII fraction exceeds that in a uniformly cooling isobaric parcel, demonstrating the importance of mixing to the ionization history. CX depletes this cool ion population, while continued entrainment maintains the supply. Including a metagalactic ionizing background changes the ion distribution and enhances CX surface brightness by a factor of a few in our CGM comparison, but preserves the cool origin of most CX emission. In the limit of sufficient neutral column, CX surface brightness is ion-supply limited: higher donor density increases local emissivity but shortens the reaction layer. The system-wide CX-to-thermal soft X-ray ratio also depends on the volume-to-interface scale $V/A_{\rm int}$, making CX a potential probe of multiphase structure in the CGM, galactic winds, and the GC.

authors.name: Yizhan Zhang, Suoqing Ji, Guiyun Liang, Shuinai Zhang, Zhijie Qu

papers.title: Little Red Dots at Cosmic Noon: Spectroscopy Reveals Declining Abundance but a Non-Evolving Luminosity Function Shape
papers.summary: Little red dots (LRDs) are an extremely abundant population of red, compact, broad-line objects primarily found in the early universe. At $5<z<8$, they are at least 10 times more abundant than UV-selected quasars. Yet, how this population evolves towards lower redshift is unclear. In this work, we present our search for LRDs at cosmic noon ($2\lesssim z\lesssim 4$) in nearly 20 deg$^2$ of the Deep/UltraDeep fields of the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP). Combining multiwavelength wide-field imaging surveys from 0.3 to 4.5 $\mu$m, we identify 266 photometric LRD candidates. With spectroscopic follow-up from Keck/NIRES, VLT/X-shooter, and Magellan/FIRE on 24 candidates, we identify a sample of four LRDs with broad H$\alpha$ emission. With the purity of the photometric sample calibrated by spectroscopy, we estimate the number density of LRDs to be approximately $6.8\times10^{-7}$ cMpc$^{-3}$ at $2.10<z<2.55$---this is nearly a factor of 35 decrease from their flat number density evolution at $4\lesssim z\lesssim8$ estimated from JWST spectroscopic surveys. The knee of the LRD optical luminosity function also remains consistently at $M_{5500}\approx-22$ mag across $2<z<5$, below that of quasars. We further speculate that only the abundance of LRDs, but not the shape of their optical luminosity function, evolves with redshift, and the Roman Space Telescope will be able to test this decisively with a substantially larger sample of low-redshift LRDs.

authors.name: Yilun Ma, Daniel J. Lyon, Jenny E. Greene, Alberto Torralba, Jorryt Matthee, Ivo Labbe, Andy D. Goulding, David J. Setton, Marianna Annunziatella, Aayush Desai, Eiichi Egami, Xiaohui Fan, Karl Glazebrook, Vasily Kokorev, Jiaxuan Li, Xiaojing Lin, Danilo Marchesini, Themiya Nanayakkara, Luke Robbins, Anna Sajina, Marcin Sawicki

papers.title: The MURALES survey. IX. MUSE observations and results for 3C radio sources at 0.3 < z < 0.82
papers.summary: This is the ninth paper in the MUse RAdio Loud Emission lines Snapshot (MURALES) project series, presenting the results of observations of 3C radio sources obtained with the VLT/MUSE integral field spectrograph. Here, we investigate the morphology and kinematics of the extended emission line regions (EELRs) of 26 radio galaxies at intermediate redshift 0.3 < z < 0.82 and their relation with the radio ejecta. EELRs are observed in all but 4 of the 26 sources extending as far as 160 kpc from the host galaxy. They show different morphologies and kinematics usually related with the radio properties. The five sources associated with the smaller radio sources show highly disturbed gas kinematics. Several EELRs have a filamentary morphology, often forming bubbles inflated by the radio lobes. The more extended EELRs usually have elongated morphologies and show well-ordered rotation. We then confirm the general results obtained from the study of the source at lower redshift: radio galaxies are surrounded by super-disks, that is, structures of ionized gas on scales of many tens of kiloparsec, whose properties depend on a combination of the evolutionary state of the radio source and its orientation with respect to the super-disks.

authors.name: B. Balmaverde, A. Capetti, A. Guglielminotti Canun, F. Massaro, A. Marconi

papers.title: From Binary Wind to Radio Burst: Dispersion-Measure Evolution after Accretion-induced Collapse
papers.summary: Secular changes in the dispersion measures (DMs) of repeating fast radio bursts probe the source-local plasma. Such DM time variability has been interpreted with spherical, single-density-profile models. Accretion-induced collapse (AIC) of a white dwarf may instead follow binary interaction and occur inside a finite, anisotropic circumstellar structure. Here, we construct an angle-dependent toy model of aspherical AIC ejecta propagating through a pre-AIC free wind, shocked-wind bubble, swept-up external shell, and polar cavity, exploring a diffuse environment (number density of $1~{\rm cm^{-3}}$, located at $10~$pc) and a compact cloud (number density of $500~{\rm cm^{-3}}$, located at $0.3~$pc), bracketing ionized and initially neutral upstream gas. The unshocked ejecta initially yield ${\rm DM}\propto t^{-2}$, while crossings of the finite wind-bubble interfaces produce breaks and curvature in ${\rm DM}(t)$. In initially neutral models, shock ionization can overcome geometric dilution: the total DM reverses from decline to growth after approximately $10$--$20$ yr and later turns over as the finite reservoir is processed. Ionized-upstream models instead generally decline or flatten. Without fitting individual sources, our models span both signs and the approximate magnitudes of the secular DM-variation rates measured among repeaters. In this dynamical framework, DM evolution is set by shock propagation through the circumsource density and ionization structure, rather than the contemporaneous burst rate, distinguishing it from photoionization-driven scenarios. Consequently, in our model, an instantaneous \(d{\rm DM}/dt\) is not a unique indicator of source age. We suggest that the observed distribution of secular DM variation slope amplitudes and signs will be important for distinguishing among different models of DM variations in repeating FRBs.

authors.name: Smadar Naoz, Victoria M. Kaspi

papers.title: Machine learning reveals new Galactic C-rich and O-rich AGB sources
papers.summary: Identification of carbon-rich (C-rich) and oxygen-rich (O-rich) Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars is crucial to understanding the structure and dust sources of the Milky Way. We present a machine-learning (ML) classification of Galactic AGB candidates using Gaia DR3, identifying 304,090 O-rich and 4,227 C-rich sources. Our two-step approach, which involves similarity-based selection, followed by XGBoost classification that combines colour and spectroscopic features, demonstrates that a small, but high-quality training sample is sufficient for accurate identification even in massive datasets such as ~140 million sources from Gaia DR3. The ML-identified stars occupy distinct regions in colour-magnitude and Gaia-2MASS diagrams, and comparison with stellar isochrones combined with Gaia distances allows estimates of their masses and ages. Spatial distributions show that O-rich AGB stars dominate the inner Galaxy, while C-rich AGB stars are concentrated toward the anti-Galactic centre. Vertical profiles indicate that massive O-rich (5-8 M$_\odot$) stars remain near the Galactic mid-plane, whereas C-rich (2.3-2.5 M$_\odot$) and low-mass O-rich (1-1.5 M$_\odot$) AGB stars are more vertically extended, with scale heights that increase with decreasing stellar mass and increasing stellar ages. C-rich AGB stars trace the Galactic warp at intermediate ages (1 Gyr), with warp amplitudes appearing larger than those traced by Cepheids. Intermediate-mass O-rich AGB stars (~300 Myr) show tentative correspondence with several spiral arm features, while the C-rich distribution is too smooth for reliable identification with the current sample. These results highlight AGB stars as powerful probes of stellar evolution and Galactic dynamical processes.

authors.name: Tanya Kushwahaa, Mikako Matsuura, Jason A. S. Hunt, Daisuke Kawata, Roger Wesson, Timothy A. Davis

papers.title: Effects of Preionisation in Radiative Shocks IV. A Spectral Grid Library of fully Radiative Shock Models with Time--Dependent Precursor
papers.summary: Here we present an extensive set of shock models calculated using an improved version of the MAPPINGS shock and photoionization code. The new version of MAPPINGS, namely MAPPINGS V, has a greatly improved treatment of the precursor emission, a more robust adaptive-mesh shock solver (Sutherland & Dopita 2017), and new atomic data compared to MAPPINGS III, which was used by Allen et al. (2008) to create their widely used shock model grid. The new shock model library covers the shock velocity range 50-1000 km/s, and a wide range of initial conditions and updated abundances. We highlight how the newer models compare to the earlier grid, and discuss where the shock models are most likely to approximate conditions for various types of astrophysical objects. The emission that one expects to observe depends on a variety of factors, including the velocity of the shock, the density and abundance of material the shock is encountering, the magnetic field and the effective age of the shock.

authors.name: Yifei Jin, Knox Long, Ralph Sutherland, Yong Shi

papers.title: Little Red Dots at Cosmic Noon: Spectroscopic Identification and Broad-Line Properties
papers.summary: We present Keck/NIRES, VLT/X-shooter, and Magellan/FIRE spectroscopic follow-up observations of photometrically selected Little Red Dot (LRD) candidates targeting H$\alpha$ at $2<z<3$. The apparent decline of LRDs at cosmic noon raises the question whether they retain the spectra of the high-redshift population. From a parent sample of 266 unresolved sources with V-shaped broadband SEDs, identified in 19.9\,deg$^2$ of the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program Deep/UltraDeep fields, we observe 24 and confirm broad H$\alpha$ in 6. The remaining 18 candidates show no broad H$\alpha$. Four have Ly$\alpha$ redshifts, which place H$\alpha$ outside our coverage for two. The other 14 have only photometric redshifts, so their H$\alpha$ coverage is uncertain; they may have incorrect photometric redshifts, broad H$\alpha$ fainter than $L_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}\approx3\times10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$, or not be LRDs. All six broad H$\alpha$ lines are best fit by exponential profiles, with FWHM $\approx 950$--$2150$ km s$^{-1}$. Three show Balmer absorption, all show Balmer decrements above Case B ($H\alpha/H\beta \approx 8$--$34$, though H$\beta$ is not detected), and four have V-shaped SEDs consistent with JWST-selected LRD samples. Archival \textit{JWST}/NIRCam imaging and NIRSpec spectroscopy independently confirm one source as an LRD. One of the six is X-ray detected at a luminosity typical of ordinary AGN and is better described as a broad-line AGN. Only one of seven dust-reddened F2M quasars and two of 38 heavily reddened quasars at $2<z<3$ meet typical JWST V-shape criteria. Four of the six sources with broad H$\alpha$ ($67$\%) resemble JWST-selected LRDs, showing that ground-based photometric selection and spectroscopy can identify LRDs.

authors.name: Daniel J. Lyon, Yilun Ma, Ivo Labbe, Alberto Torralba, Jenny E. Greene, Jorryt Matthee, Karl Glazebrook, Andy D. Goulding, David J. Setton, Themiya Nanayakkara, Marianna Annunziatella, Aayush Desai, Eiichi Egami, Xiaohui Fan, Vasily Kokorev, Jiaxuan Li, Xiaojing Lin, Danilo Marchesini, Luke Robbins, Anna Sajina, Marcin Sawicki

papers.title: Generative Bayesian modelling of radio antenna beams An application to the MeerKAT radio telescope
papers.summary: Accurate primary beam models are essential for high-fidelity calibration and imaging in radio astronomy. Traditional approaches either lack the ability to represent realistic antenna patterns (analytical models) or become computationally prohibitive to interpolate for wide-bandwidth observations (electromagnetic simulations, direct holographic measurements). We develop a generative beam model that represents both the spatial structure and the frequency variations in the primary beam while remaining tractable for integration into calibration and imaging pipelines, achieving superior accuracy compared to existing parametric models and reducing data storage compared to data-based models. We adopt a non-parametric Bayesian framework grounded in information field theory, implemented using the NIFTy library. The model represents the beam as a base pattern subject to frequency-dependent geometric transformations (scaling and shifting). Performance is validated through posterior predictive checks (chi^2/dof ~ 1) and compared against traditional models (Gaussian, Airy disc, JimBeam, Eidos, electromagnetic simulation). We apply the method to holographic data of the array-averaged MeerKAT Stokes I beam in the L band. The model achieves 400:1 data compression while preserving statistical consistency with holographic measurements, and outperforms existing approaches by more than an order of magnitude in mean squared deviation. Zernike decomposition of the base beam, combined with the geometric transformations, enables efficient beam reconstruction at arbitrary spatial resolution. The 150 kB per-antenna footprint enables memory-slim integration into calibration and imaging software at negligible cost, scales favourably to large arrays and wide bandwidths, and can be readily adapted to other radio telescopes.

authors.name: Morteza Pashapour-Ahmadabadi, Dominik J. Schwarz, Mattieu S. de Villiers, Aritra Basu, Vincent Eberle, Torsten En{\ss}lin, Philipp Frank, Richard Fuchs, Hans-Rainer Kl\"ockner, Anna Nelles

papers.title: Modeling Asymmetries in Be Star Disks Using Spectro-interferometric H-alpha Observations from the CHARA Array's VEGA Instrument
papers.summary: Be stars are rapidly rotating B-type stars with outflowing decretion disks. The observational record shows that in many cases the peaks of their H$\alpha$ flux profile vary on long timescales. These changes are probably caused by the development of disk brightness asymmetries that are related to global disk oscillation modes. Here we present spectro-interferometric observations made with the CHARA Array interferometer and the VEGA beam combiner that document the interferometric data across the H$\alpha$ line for the Be stars $\gamma$ Cas, $\phi$ Per, $\zeta$ Tau, and $\beta$ CMi. The differential interferometric visibility amplitudes and phases across the H$\alpha$ emission line reveal clues about the asymmetries present in their disks. Here we describe a model of the H$\alpha$ formation that calculates the emission intensity at spatial positions around the star and disk. The parameters describing the disk and the oscillation mode are optimized to match the interferometric data and contemporaneous H$\alpha$ spectroscopy. The analysis confirms the presence of strong disk asymmetries at the time of the observations (2020) in the cases of $\gamma$ Cas and $\phi$ Per, and hints that weaker oscillation modes were also present in the disks of $\zeta$ Tau and $\beta$ CMi. The success of this single epoch study demonstrates the promise of future interferometric programs to investigate how the modes precess within the disk and grow and decline over time.

authors.name: Peter Wysocki, Douglas Gies, Denis Mourard, Atsuo Okazaki, Fabien Baron, Gail Schaefer

papers.title: NGC 1300: A rich reservoir of ultraluminous X-ray sources
papers.summary: We present the first systematic multi-epoch study of the X-ray source population of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 1300, using 12 archival Chandra observations spanning more than 15 years and archival Swift/XRT monitoring. Within the optical extent of the galaxy, we identify 42 X-ray sources, including six ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) and 13 ULX candidates. The candidates have measured luminosities below $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$, but their upper uncertainty bounds reach or exceed this threshold in at least one epoch. We examine source luminosities, long-term variability, broad-band spectral properties, and epoch-resolved X-ray luminosity functions (XLFs). Ten sources meet our transient criterion, seven have a variability significance of $S_{\rm var}\geq3$, and four meet both criteria. X32 is a highly variable ULX with a peak X-ray luminosity of $1.5\times10^{40}$ erg s$^{-1}$, more than 715 times the non-detection upper limit. The hardness-intensity diagrams show diverse spectral behavior among the luminous sources, with no common hardness-luminosity evolution. X32 remains predominantly hard despite its large luminosity variations, and its X-ray colors are consistent with the empirical high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB) region of the color-color diagram. The cumulative XLFs above $10^{38}$ erg s$^{-1}$ have slopes of $\beta\simeq0.6$ to $1.0$, with evidence for a broken power law in only a few epochs. The number of off-nuclear sources reaching $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$ ranges from zero to four per epoch. Long-term source variability thus strongly shapes the bright end of the XLF and makes the observed ULX census of NGC 1300 strongly epoch dependent. Multi-epoch monitoring is essential for establishing representative ULX populations in nearby galaxies.

authors.name: Sinan Allak, Faruk Soydugan, Andrea Santangelo, Wei Yu, Santina Piraino, Daniel Kulinsky

papers.title: Searching for substellar companion candidates with Gaia IV. New planetary-mass companions found in debris disks
papers.summary: When spatially resolved, debris disks often exhibit structures (gaps, rings, and spirals) that may indicate the presence of unseen planetary-mass companions. However, such planets have not been detected in most cases. Gaia opens a new mass-separation parameter space for detecting unseen planets. A tool named GaiaPMEX has been developed to detect and characterize companions to stars. It is based on two binarity indicators derived from DR3: the Gaia astrometric signature and, when the sources were also observed by Hipparcos, the Gaia-Hipparcos proper motion anomaly. We used GaiaPMEX on 94 stars hosting resolved debris disks to search for companions. When companions were identified, we combined GaiaPMEX results with high-contrast imaging and radial velocity data to further constrain their mass and orbital properties. We found stellar or substellar companions around five targets (HD 54341, HD 146897, HD 206893, HD 107146, and HD 106906) and indications (2 sigma) for companions around three additional targets (BD+45 598, TWA 7, and HD 120326). The companion to the 150 Myr star HD 107146, which harbors a ring-like dust disk, is found to be a 2-6 Jupiter-mass planet orbiting between 2-10 au. A massive 3-20 Jupiter-mass companion is found 3-10 au from the close binary HD 106906, which already hosts a remote planet orbiting at more than 700 au, and an edge-on disk. The tentative companions to TWA 7 and HD 120326 are planetary-mass companions at 1-3 au. Both stars host a multiple-ring system. We finally provide meaningful upper limits on the possible presence of companions in the range of 0-100 au around a few emblematic stars (49 Cet, AU Mic, beta Pic, and epsilon Eri) and stars hosting well-defined ring-like structures.

authors.name: A. -M. Lagrange, S. Toucheboeuf, F. Kiefer, P. Rubini, J. Milli, L. Matr., H. Beust, C. Perrot, M. M. lin, A. Boccaletti, C. Wilkinson, P. Delorme

papers.title: SciPIC-lite: A flexible Halo Occupation Distribution pipeline aimed at clustering observables
papers.summary: The Halo Occupation Distribution (HOD) framework provides a flexible approach to modelling the galaxy--halo connection in cosmological simulations, encoding the statistical relationship between galaxies and their host dark matter haloes. We present SciPIC-lite, a new public Python library for fast, flexible, and user-friendly HOD modelling, designed to populate dark matter haloes extracted from cosmological simulations with galaxies and to provide a comprehensive suite of tools for their subsequent analysis. The library is built around a modular and extensible codebase that incorporates the full breadth of the HOD framework, from the core occupation functions to a wide range of physically motivated extensions, making it suitable for a broad spectrum of galaxy clustering applications. We validate and characterise the performance of SciPIC-lite by developing a pipeline to fit the two-point correlation functions of H$\alpha$-selected galaxies from the Flagship~2 simulation across multiple redshift bins. To this end, we populate AbacusSummit dark matter haloes with galaxies according to a variety of HOD parametrisations. We assess the robustness of the fits with respect to the choice of HOD parametrisation and the inclusion of physically motivated extensions, including assembly bias, velocity bias, conformity, and halo profile rescaling. The best-fit models are found to be remarkably robust across different HOD parametrisations and fitting configurations, with reduced $\chi^2$ values clustering tightly around a common value regardless of the model adopted. We exploit these results to generate new AbacusSummit-based galaxy mocks that accurately reproduce the clustering properties of the Flagship~2 H$\alpha$ galaxy population.

authors.name: Gabriele Parimbelli, Martin Crocce, Giosu\`e Gambardella, Alexander Eggemeier, Pablo Fosalba, Elizabeth J. Gonzalez, Sujatha Ramakrishnan, Isaac Tutusaus, Zahra Baghkhani, Jorge Carretero, Francisco Castander, Andrea Pezzotta, Pau Tallada-Cresp\'i

papers.title: The Effect of Dust Grain Growth and Stellar Metallicity on Gas Giant Planet Formation by Disk Instability
papers.summary: The formation of gas giant planets by the gas disk gravitational instability (GDGI) mechanism depends sensitively on the thermodynamics of the protoplanetary disk gas: disk gas must be able to cool on orbital timescales for dense clumps to become gravitationally unstable and contract to form protoplanets. Since disk cooling is regulated by the opacity of the dust grains embedded in the gas, the properties of these dust grains are critical for the GDGI mechanism. Grain growth to larger sizes than assumed in traditional opacity models for solar metallicity, as well as protostars with sub-solar metallicity, should have lower opacity disks that are more conducive to planet formation by GDGI. Here we use a three dimensional radiative hydrodynamics and gravitation code to compute the evolution of the GDGI in $0.091 M_\odot$ disks with varied initial minimum values (1.3 to 2.7) of the Toomre criterion orbiting solar-mass protostars. Three sets of eight models are computed: one with the standard opacity, and two more with the opacity reduced by arbitrary factors of 10 or 100. As expected, the reduced opacity models result in enhanced disk fragmentation by the GDGI and the production of more self-gravitating clumps than the standard opacity models. Nevertheless, all three opacities form similar self-gravitating clumps at this early phase of clump evolution, with masses of 0.2 to 0.7 $M_{Jup}$ and semimajor axes between 6 and 13 au. Significant dust grain growth should enhance the ability of the GDGI to form protoplanets around super-solar metallicity protostars.

authors.name: Alan P. Boss

papers.title: Dynamical friction on an extended satellite revisited
papers.summary: The original formulation of Chandrasekhar dynamical friction (DF) was developed for a point-like particle moving in a infinite and homogeneous medium. However, despite very useful order of magnitude estimates of the slowing-down time scales of a test mass in more realistic finite-sized models, high resolution $N-$body simulations often hint at a breakdown of Chandrasekhar's formalism (typically overestimating the effect of DF) for massive satellites sinking in the host galaxy. More advanced semi-analytical treatment of the DF expression managed to partially reduce said discrepancy, even though an accurate comparison with numerical simulations still remains difficult, specifically due to the interplay between the DF force and the tidal stress effects on an extended stellar systems sinking in the gravitational potential of the parent galaxy or halo. In this study we perform ad hoc $N-$body simulations of a satellite orbiting in a simple spherical galaxy model, for different values of the initial orbital eccentricity, satellite mass, scale radius and velocity anisotropy profile of the host model. We adopt an $N-$body code where the self-consistent interaction among the particles representing the galaxy can be substituted by the effect of the static smooth potential of the system's continuum limit. Moreover, the satellite itself is either modeled with $N_{\rm sat}$ particles or represented by a single particle with an effective size parametrized in the form of the force exchanged with the other simulation particles representing the galaxy. We find that, at fixed galaxy model and satellite mass, the more extended the satellite, the weaker is the effect of DF. This trend, which is found for both isotropic and radially anisotropic host systems, is particularly evident for orbits with initial orbital eccentricity exceeding $\approx0.3$.

authors.name: Pierfrancesco Di Cintio, Carlo Nipoti

papers.title: Kinetic Sunyaev Zel'dovich Velocity Reconstruction Using Vision Transformers
papers.summary: Kinetic Sunyaev Zel'dovich (kSZ) velocity reconstruction uses correlations between maps of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and a tracer of large scale structure (LSS) to infer the large-scale peculiar velocity field. Standard approaches to kSZ velocity reconstruction use quadratic estimators that are Fisher optimal for purely Gaussian fields. Here, we develop a pipeline for kSZ velocity reconstruction based on Vision Transformers (ViT) and show that this approach can improve the fidelity of velocity reconstruction. This is consistent with the network utilizing non-Gaussian information in the inputs that the quadratic estimators do not, though with the single simulation realization we have access to, we cannot exclude overfitting. Our approach can be applied to full-resolution maps from existing and near-term CMB and LSS datasets.

authors.name: Sophie Coulombe, Matthew C. Johnson

papers.title: Information-Criterion-Driven, Non-linear Deprojection of Angular Imaging Systematics for the SPHEREx Galaxy Clustering Sample
papers.summary: Imaging systematics that inject false, or suppress true, galaxy clustering signals are of primary concern for current- and next-generation galaxy surveys, such as the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx) in its search for local primordial non-Gaussianity $f_{\rm NL}$. As statistical errors shrink with growing galaxy samples, systematic rather than statistical uncertainties come to dominate the cosmological error budget. For effects whose spatial patterns are known or well-modelled \emph{a priori}, a common mitigation approach regresses (deprojects) the density variation associated with a known angular template. In this work we present and demonstrate novel aspects of this procedure as will be applied to the SPHEREx galaxy clustering sample. These include flexible -- but, crucially, constrained and interpretable -- non-linear basis regression with polynomial/spline bases, and aggressive information criterion-driven automated template selection with an associated unbiased two-stage regression, using agreement between two independent selectors as a consistency diagnostic. The method automatically selects a template set of minimal-but-sufficient complexity while limiting the number of templates actually regressed, minimising cosmological information loss and making modern additive-plus-multiplicative approaches tractable. We demonstrate these features on SPHEREx-like lognormal mock catalogues with injected contamination of various spatial profiles, amplitudes, and levels of complexity. Principled, signal-preserving deprojection of the kind demonstrated here is a crucial step towards achieving SPHEREx's goal of $\sigma(f_{\rm NL}) < 0.5$.

authors.name: James R. Cheshire, Sean T. Bruton, Charuhas W. Shiveshwarkar

papers.title: Determining the Spin and Orbital Period of the Asynchronous Cataclysmic Variable X10 in 47 Tucanae
papers.summary: The X-ray source X10 in the globular cluster 47 Tuc has been identified as a cataclysmic variable (CV). With a suggested 4.7 hour periodicity, and a soft X-ray spectrum, it appears to be an unusually X-ray luminous ($L_X=2.2\times10^{32}$ erg s$^{-1}$) polar CV. We use 286 ks of Chandra X-ray Observatory observations of 47 Tuc to study the X-ray timing behavior of 47 Tuc X10. X10 shows clear pulsations in the data, with occasional phase shifts. These suggest that X10 is an asynchronous polar CV, where the spin and orbital periods are slightly misaligned, and the dominant accretion flow shifts from one pole to the other. We use a Lomb-Scargle periodogram to suggest potential spin and orbital periods, then model the X-ray lightcurve using simple sinusoids to represent emission from each accretion pole, switching which pole is visible on the beat period. We find a white dwarf spin period of $P_{\mathrm{spin}} = 4.2683$ h and derive an orbital period of $P_{\mathrm{orb}} = 4.6779$ h from the beat modulation. This large degree of asynchronism (8.8%) suggests that X10 is in an unstable equilibrium, and may be a transitional system between an intermediate polar and a fully synchronized polar.

authors.name: Daniel Mendoza-Fredes, Craig O. Heinke, Matthew Lang, Asma Hattawi

papers.title: The role of gas on the collisional runaway path to supermassive black hole seeds
papers.summary: The origin of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remains unclear, despite observational evidence for their rapid formation in the early Universe, as evidenced by active galactic nuclei (AGN) at high redshift. In this paper, we investigate stellar dynamics in dense, gas-embedded clusters. We explore how gas influences the runaway collision process and the subsequent formation of SMBH seeds in a global instability scenario. We perform a series of coupled N-body and SPH simulations using the AMUSE framework, with the stellar and gaseous components interacting gravitationally via the BRIDGE method. We use 12 initial condition models with equal-mass stars following Plummer distributions, with total masses ranging from $10^3$ to $5 \times 10^5~M_{\odot}$, virial radii from $0.005$ to $0.1$ pc, and stellar masses of $1$, $10$ and $50$ $M_{\odot}$. For each model, we perform four simulations with gas fractions ranging from 0\% to 20\%, resulting in a total of 48 simulations. The gas is sampled with the same spatial distribution as the stars, with a mass ratio per particle of $m_{\rm SPH}/m = 0.01$, where $m$ is the stellar mass. We find that in most of our simulations, higher gas fractions lead to the formation of more massive black hole, as the core collapses earlier, triggering collisions through gas--star interactions. Our results show increases in BH mass of $\sim 8\%$ for low gas fractions, to $\sim 44\%$ at 20\% gas fraction. The core collapse time is also shortened, with the strongest reduction at $20\%$ gas fraction ($\sim 27\%$). The transonic regime of our initial conditions is where dynamical friction is most efficient in principle. Although our simulations do not fully resolve this effect, gas--star interactions are the principal mechanism driving the enhancement in BH formation efficiency, in the absence of other dissipation mechanisms.

authors.name: Boris Cuevas, Basti\'an Reinoso, Andr\'es Escala, Marcelo C. Vergara, Sebasti\'an Valdebenito, Dominik R. G. Schleicher

papers.title: Magnetic vector potentials and helicity in periodic domains
papers.summary: For a magnetic field in three-dimensional Euclidean space, we argue about the existence of a magnetic vector potential in a finite cuboid with periodic boundary conditions. We first argue in physical terms by representing periodic domains as tori and show that in some cases, the generating electric current is unphysical. We then represent magnetic fields and vector potentials as differential 2 and 1-forms. For a given magnetic field we ask the question whether a corresponding vector potential exists. Singly periodic domains are shown to always allow for a vector potential. For doubly periodic domains it only exists if the net magnetic flux through the non-periodic dimension vanishes, while for triply periodic domains the net flux must vanish in all directions. This has implications for the definition of magnetic helicity in periodic domains. We show that periodic domains together with a mean magnetic flux lead to contradicting results about the value of the magnetic helicity and we show in a few thought experiments fundamental contradictions to the interpretation as the linking of magnetic field lines. For the helicity we can even construct magnetic fields in periodic domains for which the magnetic helicity exists, but the calculations of the magnetic helicity do not lead to meaningful results due to the gauge freedom. With that we conclude that in presence of a mean magnetic field the calculated magnetic helicity cannot be interpreted geometrically in a straightforward way. However, using the winding gauge we can recover the geometric interpretation of the helicity as the flux averaged magnetic field line winding. Finally, for the solar relevant non-periodic domain with finite point-wise flux and zero integrated flux, using an appropriate gauge transformation the magnetic helicity can be shown to vanish. The winding helicity, however, would lead to a non-vanishing value here.

authors.name: Simon Candelaresi

papers.title: Broad-line ambiguity in IC 1495
papers.summary: Published analyses disagree on whether the 2004 6dFGS spectrum of IC 1495, a barred Seyfert galaxy in the 2MIG isolated-galaxy catalogue, contains broad H-alpha. We compare it with a 2024 SDSS-V/BOSS spectrum to assess changes in broad-line visibility. In 2024, the [O III] profile favours a blueshifted wing with intrinsic FWHM ~640 km/s, while [S II] and [O I] favour single-component fits. Among six H-alpha+[N II] models with free narrow-line kinematics, the BIC-preferred fit includes broad H-alpha with intrinsic FWHM ~2000 km/s. However, adding broad H-alpha worsens the BIC when H-alpha and [N II] share two narrow kinematic components. Broad H-alpha is not detected in the 2004 spectrum under the adopted criterion. Injection-recovery simulations of a reference broad component (FWHM ~1930 km/s; broad-to-narrow H-alpha flux ratio 0.82) yield recovery fractions of 27-35% in baseline simulations and 11-55% across the grid. At 1.5 times this flux ratio, baseline recovery rises to 42-55%. Aperture and flux-calibration uncertainties limit absolute line-flux comparisons. Narrow-line excitation, Chandra spectroscopy (intrinsic N_H ~2.3 x 10^23 cm^-2 in the fiducial model), and long-term optical and mid-infrared variability support an absorbed, variable Seyfert nucleus. The model-dependent 2024 broad-H-alpha candidate and limited 2004 sensitivity do not establish a change in broad-line visibility between the epochs.

authors.name: I. O. Izviekova, O. V. Kompaniiets, I. B. Vavilova, D. V. Dobrycheva

papers.title: A High-Resolution Stellar Extinction Map of M31 from PHAT and PHAST Photometry
papers.summary: High-resolution extinction maps of resolved external galaxies, such as M31, are crucial not only for accurately correcting dust extinction and reddening toward individual sources within the galaxy, but also for characterizing the distribution and evolution of interstellar dust in external galactic environments. We aim to construct a high-resolution and large-coverage stellar-traced extinction map of M31, based on multi-band photometric data from the HST PHAT and PHAST surveys. Using a stellar template library built from the PARSEC stellar evolution models and adopting the average extinction law of M31, we apply a matching method analogous to the SPar algorithm to derive A_V values for approximately 65 million stars. The extinction map is then generated using a HEALPix adaptive-resolution scheme. The resulting map covers approximately two-thirds of the star-forming disk of M31, with a maximum spatial resolution of 1.61 arcsec. The median extinction across the map is A_V = 1.24 mag. Comparison with previously published stellar- and dust-emission-based extinction maps shows broadly similar large-scale morphology, while differences remain in the extinction values. The extinction map further reveals fine-scale features such as inter-arm filaments, supernova-driven cavities, and spur-like structures. The map has been publicly released through the NADC platform and is expected to serve as an important observational basis for extinction correction in subsequent astronomical observations and for related M31 scientific studies.

authors.name: Mingxu Sun, Bingqiu Chen, Yuxi Wang, Jian Gao, Yuhui Chen, Wenyuan Cui

papers.title: High-precision proper motions toward the Galactic bulge Baade's window from a decade of DECam observations
papers.summary: A complete characterization of the Galactic bulge stellar populations could offer important clues on the formation and evolution of our Galaxy. However, most bulge fields are hampered by high stellar crowding, strong interstellar extinction, and by heavy contamination from foreground disk stars. We aim to derive proper motions (PMs) towards the Baade's window by using DECam observations, extending kinematic studies of the Galactic bulge below the turn-off to a much larger field of view. We combined three datasets observed with DECam in the $r$-band spanning a ${\sim}$ 10-year baseline. As a pilot study, we only analyzed the field covered by a single detector. We developed an astrometric calibration pipeline that corrects for the DECam tree-ring pattern and residual distortions, tying all positions to the Gaia DR3 reference frame, and used them to derive PMs. We isolated the bulge population through a strict cut in $\mu_{\ell^\ast}$, refined with a Gaia DR3 parallax selection. We measured PMs for $48\,239$ stars in the pilot field, with a median uncertainty of $0.65$ mas yr$^{-1}$ at $r_0<18$ mag. Our PMs agree closely with Gaia DR3, and reaches ${\sim}1.5$ magnitudes deeper than Gaia and a comparable depth to VIRAC2 in terms of relative completeness. We found velocity dispersions along Galactic longitude and latitude of $\sigma_{\mu_{\ell^\ast}}=2.76\pm0.03$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and $\sigma_{\mu_b}=2.49\pm0.02$ mas yr$^{-1}$ for the Galactic bulge, consistent with HST studies. We estimated a foreground contamination of ${\sim}14\%$ before any kinematic selection. The cleaned color-magnitude diagram reaches below the main-sequence turnoff, and shows no evidence for a large population younger than ${\sim}4$-$5$ Gyr in this field. Moreover, since the LSST camera shares the same CCD technology as DECam, this work offers a valuable precursor for crowded-field astrometry in the Rubin era.

authors.name: C. Salvo-Guajardo, A. Calamida, C. I. Johnson, M. Dall'Ora, M. Zoccali, A. Luna, M. Gholami, J. Olivares Carvajal, T. M. Brown, A. Saha, M. Catelan, N. Rodr\'iguez-Segovia, \'A. Valenzuela Navarro, M. Gennaro, R. Contreras Ramos

papers.title: Accretor Luminosity as Probe of Orbital Evolution and Magnetic Braking in AM CVn Binaries
papers.summary: AM CVn binaries are ultracompact systems with orbital periods $P_{\rm orb} \lesssim 70$ min, where a white dwarf accretes from a He-rich semidegenerate donor. At short orbital periods ($P_{\rm orb} \lesssim 20$ min), rapid accretion reheats the accretor. As the system widens and the mass transfer rate decreases, the accretor follows standard white dwarf cooling at longer orbital periods ($P_{\rm orb} \gtrsim 30$ min). The accretor cooling luminosity then acts as a powerful probe into the orbital evolution of the binary. Recent observations show that the accretor appears brighter (younger) at long orbital periods, compared to models where orbital angular momentum loss is solely set by gravitational wave emission. We show that additional angular momentum loss, which we ascribe to magnetic braking of the donor, can better reproduce observations of accretor luminosity. We test and constrain various proposed magnetic braking formalisms, for the white dwarf, helium star, and evolved cataclysmic variable (CV) channels for AM CVn formation. None of the magnetic braking formalisms in their original form can reproduce the observations, but the widely popular magnetic braking proposed by Rappaport et al. 1983 boosted by a factor $\approx 5$, or the saturated magnetic braking proposed by Matt et al. 2015 boosted by a factor of $\approx 150$, yields satisfactory results. We also find that the CARB formalism, recently applied to the evolved CV channel, is strongly in tension with observations of accretor luminosity. Our models motivate UV spectroscopy observations, and dedicated WD atmosphere models for AM CVn accretors.

authors.name: Tin Long Sunny Wong, Peter Scherbak, Jim Fuller

papers.title: Precise Radii of Visual Binaries with Dynamical Masses: $\xi$ Bootis $\&$ 70 Ophiuchi
papers.summary: A new orbital solution for $\xi$ Bootis (GJ 566 AB, P=152 yrs) and the recently revised orbital solution for 70 Ophiuchi (GJ 702 AB, P=88 yrs) yield component masses precise to 0.4\%. Their relatively wide separations ($>0.4^{\prime\prime}$) allow the components to be studied independently, making them ideal for testing the predictions of stellar evolutionary models. We use the six-telescope near-infrared MIRC-X and MYSTIC beam combiners at the CHARA Array to measure the angular diameters of all 4 stars. Combined with precise Gaia DR3 parallax values and bolometric fluxes, these interferometric measurements translate to stellar radii that are precise to $<2.4\%$ and effective temperatures precise to $<1.7\%$. We compare the measured radii and temperatures to four stellar evolutionary models (Lyon, Dartmouth, PARSEC, MIST). Over the mass range $0.67 - 0.91$ M$_\odot$, all models reproduce the observed properties within a few standard deviations, with no systematic offsets. The pairs are coeval and consistent with independent age estimates, further validating model predictions. With physical separations greater than 20 au, these pairs show no evidence of radius inflation, despite being spectroscopically classified as chromospherically active, and in the case of $\xi$ Bootis, probable members of the adolescent age ($\sim 0.4$ Gyr) Ursa Majoris Moving Group. In contrast, a set of 21 short-period ($P\lesssim$ 10 days) eclipsing binary stars with similar dynamical masses and metallicities are larger and often cooler than these same model predictions. Within this mass range, radius inflation appears to be associated with short-period binary star systems.

authors.name: Becky E. Flores (Georgia State University), Russel J. White (Georgia State University), Gail Schaefer (The CHARA Array of Georgia State University), Mark R. Giovinazzi (Amherst College), Simone Lilavois (Amherst College), Ryan Purviance (Amherst College), Henry Dennen (Amherst College), Daniella Bardalez Gagliuffi (Amherst College), Caleb K. Harada (University of Hawai'i, University of California Berkeley), Brian D. Mason (US Naval Observatory), Rachel A. Matson (US Naval Observatory), Isabelle Baraffe (University of Exeter, Ecole Normale Sup\'erieure de Lyon), Chi Thanh Nguyen (University of Trieste), Greg Feiden (University of North Georgia), John D. Monnier (University of Michigan), Stefan Kraus (University of Exeter), Narsireddy Anugu (The CHARA Array of Georgia State University), Claire L. Davies (The CHARA Array of Georgia State University), Tyler Gardner (The CHARA Array of Georgia State University), Mayra Gutierrez (The CHARA Array of Georgia State University), Noura Ibrahim (The CHARA Array of Georgia State University), Cyprien Lanthermann (The CHARA Array of Georgia State University), Norman Vargas (The CHARA Array of Georgia State University), Olli Majoinen (The CHARA Array of Georgia State University)

papers.title: Disentangling Disk and Broad-Line Region Continuum Emission in a Sample of Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.summary: Recent continuum reverberation-mapping measurements of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) indicate that the inter-band time lags are significantly larger than those predicted by the light travel times across the standard thin model. In addition, the observed $u$-band excess suggests the presence of diffuse continuum (DC) radiation originating in the broad-line region (BLR). Spectroscopically, the Balmer and Paschen jumps in DC emission are unique indicators to quantify the contributions of the BLR to the observed continuum. Here, we study the DC contributions of 31 AGNs, whose spectra are obtained with the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS) on the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and with X-shooter on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). In each spectrum, at least one of the Balmer and Paschen jumps is covered. For each object, we performed radiative transfer calculations using Cloudy within the Locally Optimally-emitting Clouds (LOC) model to construct source-specific DC spectral templates. We quantified the DC contribution by incorporating these templates as continuum components in spectral decomposition. The average ratio of the DC to total (i.e., disk+DC) continua is ~33% just below the Balmer jump (~3625 \AA). The Balmer jump provides a stronger constraint on the DC component than the Paschen jump. Simulations based on mock spectra further demonstrate that an unsuitable template can introduce systematic, wavelength-dependent biases to the inferred DC fraction. Our results underscore the importance of employing appropriate DC templates in the spectral decomposition to infer the substantial DC contribution. Upcoming time-resolved spectra will enable more detailed modelling and tighter constraints on the disk and BLR.

authors.name: Manqi Fu, Shuying Zhou, Hengxiao Guo, Zhi-Xiang Zhang, Marcin Marculewicz, Mouyuan Sun

papers.title: Ultraviolet Observations of Solar Active Phenomena
papers.summary: Ultraviolet observations of the Sun have revolutionized our understanding of the structure and dynamics of the solar atmosphere. From the chromosphere all the way to the corona, there are ubiquitous jets due to magnetic reconnection and associated with type III radio bursts. Sporadic flares occur in the corona, representing an inevitable breakup of magnetic energy accumulation as new magnetic flux continues to pump into the solar atmosphere, which is further shuffled by solar surface motions. Once large-scale eruptions occur, magnetized plasmas are expelled out into the interplanetary space, leaving globally propagating waves and the following dimmings. The waves can be utilized to diagnose the coronal magnetic field which cannot be measured directly, and the dimmings can be used to estimate the ejected mass of eruptions and magnetic connectivity. Extreme ultraviolet spectroscopic observations provide information on the fractionation of different chemical elements, in particular those elements with low first ionization potential. Thanks to the high spatial resolution of solar observations, all these results are believed to shed light on our understanding of the activity on other stars which cannot be imaged.

authors.name: P. F. Chen, G. Del Zanna, L. Feng, J. H. Guo, Y. J. Hou, H. Tian, D. Tripathi

papers.title: IGRINS-2 Reveals an Oxygen-rich Dayside Atmosphere of WASP-12 b: Resolving the C/O Controversy
papers.summary: Recent studies have shown that measurements of hot-Jupiter atmospheric composition, including carbon-to-oxygen (C/O) and refractory-to-volatile (R/V) abundance ratios, provide powerful diagnostics of the chemistry and formation of gas giant planets. Important questions remain about the atmospheric composition of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b: its dayside C/O ratio remains under debate, and its R/V ratio is not yet well constrained. We present high-resolution (R $\sim$ 45,000) near-infrared dayside emission spectroscopy of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b with IGRINS-2 on Gemini North during post-eclipse phases. Cross-correlation analysis reveals volatile molecular signals of H$_2$O and CO together with tentative signals of OH and gas-phase refractories in the planetary atmosphere. The planetary signals appear in emission, indicating a thermal inversion in the dayside atmosphere. A chemically consistent Bayesian retrieval yields C/O $=0.72^{+0.08}_{-0.10}$, disfavoring carbon-rich dayside solutions with C/O $>1$ at greater than $5\sigma$. This independent, line-resolved measurement supports an oxygen-rich atmosphere, providing a new constraint on the long-standing C/O controversy surrounding WASP-12 b. Our retrieval also yields a host-star-normalized R/V ratio, $[\mathrm{R/V}]_{*}=0.17^{+0.22}_{-0.23}$, which is consistent with those of other ultra-hot Jupiters similarly characterized with IGRINS/IGRINS-2. Although the sample remains small, this consistency suggests a shared atmospheric chemistry among these planets, potentially reflecting similar proportions of accreted volatile and refractory material.

authors.name: Changwoo Kye, Yeon-Ho Choi, Krishna Kanumalla, Michael Line, Jae-Joon Lee, Stefan Pelletier, Peter Smith, Vatsal Panwar, Yuya Hayashi, Jae-Rim Koo, Swaetha Ramkumar, Sung-Chul Yoon

papers.title: The relation between DCN/DNC ratios and gas temperature in late-stage massive star-forming regions using Yebes observations
papers.summary: Deuterated molecules probe the physical and chemical evolution of molecular clouds and star-forming regions. Their abundances depend on temperature, density, and evolutionary stage. DCN and DNC are relatively abundant deuterated isomers that probe temperature-dependent deuterium chemistry. Although [HCN]/[HNC] is often thought to increase in warmer gas, the temperature dependence of [DCN]/[DNC] remains less well constrained. To investigate how [DCN]/[DNC] depends on the gas kinetic temperature, we observed the $J$=1-0 transitions of DCN, DNC, H$^{13}$CN, HN$^{13}$C, HC$^{15}$N, and H$^{15}$NC toward 101 late-stage massive star-forming regions using the Yebes 40m telescope. Gas kinetic temperatures were estimated from CH$_3$CCH 5-4, whose rotation temperature is closely related to the kinetic temperature of dense gas. These temperatures were adopted in the column density calculations and in the analysis of temperature-dependent abundance ratios. We find a moderate positive correlation between the abundance ratio [DCN]/[DNC] and kinetic temperature, which is statistically significant and indicates that DCN becomes progressively more abundant relative to DNC in warmer gas. A weak negative correlation with temperature is observed for $D_{\rm frac}({\rm HNC})$, whereas no statistically significant correlation is found for $D_{\rm frac}({\rm HCN})$. The [HCN]/[HNC] ratios show substantial scatter and no statistically significant correlation with temperature, possibly due in part to optical-depth effects in the $^{13}$C isotopologues and the limited sensitivity of the $^{15}$N isotopologue observations. These results suggest that [DCN]/[DNC] may be governed not only by HCN/HNC isomeric chemistry but also by temperature-dependent deuterium fractionation pathways and the chemical evolution of dense gas.

authors.name: Yuqiang Li, Junzhi Wang, Aran Lyo, Juan Li, Siqi Zheng, Woojin Kwon, Seokho Lee, Jongsoo Kim, Huangxue Feng, Miguel Santander-Garc\'ia, Jos\'e Jairo D\'iaz-Luis, Shaoyuan Lu, Fu Mo

papers.title: Fast and accurate large-volume Lyman-$\alpha$ forest mocks with three-dimensional U-Net trained on IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO
papers.summary: The Lyman-$\alpha$ forest probes matter structure at $z\gtrsim2$, constraining baryon acoustic oscillations, neutrino masses, and dark matter properties. Interpreting current and upcoming spectroscopic surveys requires mock catalogues spanning Gpc-scale volumes while capturing small-scale intergalactic medium physics. This combination of high resolution and large volume is prohibitively expensive for hydrodynamical simulations. We present a field-level emulator, based on a three-dimensional U-Net, that maps approximate density and velocity fields directly to Ly$\alpha$ optical depth and transmitted flux. At $z\sim3$, we train in small volumes and test on much larger, independent ones in two settings: IllustrisTNG (training on a $110\,\mathrm{cMpc}$ box and testing on a $300\,\mathrm{cMpc}$ box with 2LPT and $N$-body inputs) and FLAMINGO (training on $1\,\mathrm{cGpc}$ and testing on $2.8\,\mathrm{cGpc}$ with $N$-body inputs). The hydrodynamical statistics of TNG and FLAMINGO differ appreciably over their common $k$-range, by $\sim15\%$ in $P_{\rm 1D}$, $\sim17\%$ in the bispectrum, and $\sim40\%$ in the connected trispectrum, although their normalized power-spectrum correlation structures remain broadly similar. Within each suite, the emulator reproduces $P_{\rm 1D}$ to $2.8\%$ in TNG and $5.6\%$ in FLAMINGO, the bispectrum to $4$--$5\%$, and the trispectrum to $10$--$16\%$, while also recovering the flux PDF and broad correlation structure. Field-level emulation thus provides a practical route to large-volume Ly$\alpha$-forest mocks for current and future surveys.

authors.name: Bhaskar Arya, Soumak Maitra, Shadab Alam

papers.title: Accurately Measuring Variability Properties from Noisy Light Curves
papers.summary: Modern time-domain surveys probe optical variability near photometric error, challenging weak-signal recovery. The structure function (SF) is widely used for characterizing variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs), but its statistical recovery limits are unclear. Using simulated light curves with realistic errors, we compare three SF estimators from the literature: two non-parametric (pairwise noise subtraction and Bayesian) and one parametric. All recover intrinsic SF when variability dominates, but diverge in the weak regime. The pairwise noise-subtraction estimator approaches an artificial floor when negative variance estimates are discarded, with the floor set by photometric precision and sampling rather than intrinsic variability. The parametric method suffers degeneracy, while the Bayesian estimator yields nearly unbiased SF estimates given well-calibrated photometric errors and adequate sampling. We also derive an idealized detection threshold linking intrinsic variability, photometric precision, and pair counts, providing a reference for assessing the detectability of weak signals. Our results establish statistical limits for SF measurements in the weak-variability regime and offer a framework for accurately measuring low-amplitude variability in AGNs (e.g., extremely stable quasars) and in new populations such as little red dots discovered by JWST.

authors.name: Zhen-Bo Su, Zhen-Yi Cai, Ruisong Xia, Shi-Jiang Chen, Lulu Fan, Hengxiao Guo, Mouyuan Sun, Jun-Xian Wang

papers.title: Baryon-Enhanced Strong Lensing Signatures of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Subhalos
papers.summary: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) is generally expected to suppress subhalo strong lensing through core formation, with subsequent gravothermal collapse potentially enhancing it. We show that compact stars can make a viable population of galaxy-hosting SIDM subhalos more efficient lenses than their cold dark matter (CDM) counterparts. When the baryonic potential weakens or reverses the inner velocity-dispersion gradient, SIDM halos suppress or bypass core formation, allowing inner densities to grow from early times. The evolved SIDM subhalos produce larger deflection angles and tangential caustics than in CDM. Such galaxy-hosting subhalos also dominate the galaxy-galaxy strong-lensing (GGSL) budget in clusters, yet lie far below the resolution of cosmological simulations. We calibrate a baryonic parametric SIDM model to predict their effects in the three most massive TNG300-1 clusters, finding GGSL cross sections 1.4--2.7 times those in CDM, comparable to the excess inferred in recent analyses. Baryon-enhanced SIDM lensing can thus account for the observed GGSL excess and predicts stronger perturbations from luminous satellites, testable through resolved distortions of background arcs and rings.

authors.name: Meiwen Yang, Daneng Yang, Siyuan Hou, Yi-Ying Wang, Yiping Shu, Yue-Lin Sming Tsai

papers.title: Revisiting the Double Cluster in Perseus: Are NGC 869 and NGC 884 a true binary system?
papers.summary: We perform a comprehensive study of the Double Cluster in Perseus, NGC 869 and NGC 884, to investigate their nature and evolutionary state. By combining new CCD $UBV(RI)_{KC}$ photometry with high-precision astrometry and photometry from \textit{Gaia} DR3, we determine robust astrophysical parameters, including colour excess, distance, and age. Our analysis confirms that both clusters are young, with an age of $12\pm1$ Myr, and share similar photometric distances of $2.29$ kpc. By integrating these observational constraints with completeness-corrected mass estimates and a suite of N-body simulations, we examine the kinematic and phase-space properties of the system. We find that the internal kinematics of NGC 884 exhibit a stronger and more coherent expansion signature than NGC 869. Our dynamical simulations demonstrate a rapid increase in the separation of the pair during the first 100 Myr, exceeding $1$ kpc. These results indicate that the system is not currently gravitationally bound and does not constitute a binary cluster. Instead, the Double Cluster is presently unbound, and the forward integrations predict that its components will continue to diverge under the influence of their relative motion and the Galactic potential.

authors.name: Zahra Al, Juan Casado, Sergio S\'anchez-Sanju\'an, Y\"uksel Karata\c{s}, Yasser Hendy, Raul Michel, Dana Kovaleva, Doaa Eid

papers.title: Interstellar extinction estimates for nearly 90 million stars based on synthetic photometry from Gaia XP spectra
papers.summary: Accurate stellar extinction measurements are essential for recovering intrinsic stellar properties and investigating the three-dimensional distribution of interstellar dust. We present reddening estimates for 87,270,425 stars using synthetic SMSS gri photometry derived from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra, combined with Gaia BP and RP, 2MASS JHKs, and WISE W1 photometry. Stellar extinction is determined through empirical SED fitting based on reference stellar loci constructed separately for dwarfs and giants. Comparisons with three external extinction catalogs show good overall agreement, with dispersions of 0.049-0.075 mag in E(B-V). The catalog covers approximately 99.99% of the sky. Using stars with sigma_d/d < 0.2, we further construct reddening maps in four distance ranges from 0 to 5 kpc, revealing prominent molecular clouds and large-scale Galactic dust structures. Extinction-corrected color-absolute-magnitude diagrams show significantly tighter stellar sequences and consistent red-clump features in different Galactic fields. The resulting catalog provides a homogeneous data set for stellar extinction correction and studies of Galactic dust structure.

authors.name: Bao-Kun Sun, Yan-Hui Chen, Zheng Yu, Bai-Song Zhang

papers.title: Characterising stellar photometry with invertible neural networks: Joint inference of stellar parameters and extinction
papers.summary: We introduce an extension to a simulation-based deep-learning approach for the characterisation of stellar photometry and investigate the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar properties and extinction. We used the PARSEC stellar evolutionary models to train a conditional invertible neural network (cINN) to jointly estimate full posterior distributions of stellar parameters and extinction. We tested our cINN on synthetic data and real Gaia+2MASS photometry of the two star-forming regions Taurus and Upper Scorpius. We compared our predicted extinction maps to two independent catalogues based on Gaia XP-spectra. On synthetic test data, our trained cINN exhibited a good predictive performance, achieving root mean squared errors (RMSEs) for the maximum a posteriori point estimates of about 0.16 mag for $A_V$, 0.07 dex for $\log(T_{eff}/K)$, 0.16 dex for $\log(g/cms^{-2})$, 0.2 dex for $\log(L/L\odot)$ and 0.1 dex for $\log(M_{ini}/M_\odot)$. Only $\log(age/yr)$ has proven harder to constrain with an RMSE of 0.56 dex. On the Gaia+2MASS observations of Taurus and Upper Scorpius, we retrieved reasonable extinction maps, exhibiting structures that are visually consistent with local clouds. Compared to the independent XP-spectra-based extinction studies, we found a good qualitative agreement and recovered the same prominent spatial structures. Quantitatively, however, we identified an average systematic overestimation of extinction in our approach of 0.5-0.7 mag compared to the spectroscopic studies. We investigated these offsets and identified photometric and distance uncertainties, which are currently unaccounted for in our approach, as likely causes. In conclusion, we demonstrated the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar parameters and extinction with our cINN approach, making it a promising avenue to further pursue for robust and efficient analysis of large photometric surveys.

authors.name: Victor F. Ksoll, Isabelle Joncour, Prasanta Gorai, Ralf S. Klessen

papers.title: Obliquity of Mercury with a fluid core and a deformable mantle
papers.summary: In anticipation of BepiColombo's orbital insertion in 2026, this study revisits the rotation of Mercury, modelling it with a fluid core and a deformable mantle. For this well-established physical model, we provide an analytical solution based on a novel Lagrangian formalism. Our approach enables a comprehensive 3D solution for the mantle's orientation, including the phase in longitude at the perihelion. The model incorporates dissipative torques from core-mantle boundary friction and tidal deformations, conservative pressure torques, and the effect of the planet's apsidal precession. We validate the equilibrium positions obtained numerically in previous studies, but identify discrepancies in earlier analytical works. These inconsistencies overestimated the out-of-Cassini-plane offset induced by tidal deformation by a factor of 100. Additionally, we explore the parameter space to determine where the spin axis deviates most from the Cassini plane and identify a region exhibiting bifurcation in the spin axis equilibrium position. This region cannot be adequately analysed using a model linearised with respect to the obliquity angle.

authors.name: Valentin Etienne, Gwena\"el Bou\'e, Clodoaldo Ragazzo

papers.title: Predicting HCN, HCO$^{+}$, multi-transition CO, and dust emission of star-forming galaxies
papers.summary: We present an analytical model of a turbulent clumpy star-forming disk that reproduces the spatially resolved observations for 6 molecular lines and 3 continuum bands at 250-700~GHz in the central 30~pc of the Circinus Galaxy. Using the properties of the stellar disk as input, and when matched to the line and continuum emission, the model yields the Toomre $Q$ parameter, mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$, metallicity $Z$, and cosmic ray ionization rate $\zeta_{CR}$. These in turn are used to infer the gas properties (surface density, velocity dispersion, and radial velocity) as well as the star formation rate. Our main findings from the model include a low CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor that varies with radius in the range $\alpha_{\rm CO}=0.5$--1.5 $M_{\odot}$pc$^{-2}/({\rm K\,km\,s}^{-1})$, close to the canonical value for such environments. It shows that CO(3-2) is a poor tracer of the gas mass surface density $\Sigma_{{\rm H}_2}$ on these small scales, which is better represented by molecules such as HCO$^+$(3-2) with higher critical density. The steep relation between $\Sigma_{{\rm H}_2}$ and star formation rate surface density $\dot{\Sigma}_*$ is typical of compact starburst systems, and the star formation rate (10~$M_{\odot}$kpc$^{-2}$yr$^{-1}$ averaged over the disk) is high enough to drive a wind. Despite this, and in contrast to typical large scale galactic disks, the energy injection rate into the ISM is dominated by gas inflow through the disk rather than the supernova rate. As such, the decreasing inflow rate at smaller radii could be caused by a wind, or indicate a recent increase of the mass inflow from larger scales. We suggest that such variations in the inflow rate could be associated with the nested spiral structures which have been observed in Circinus.

authors.name: B. Vollmer (Observatoire astronomique de Strasbourg, France), D. Iung (Observatoire astronomique de Strasbourg, France), K. R. W. Tristram (ESO, Santiago, Chile), R. I. Davies (MPE, Garching, Germany), W. M. Goesaert (Leiden Observatory, The Netherlands)

papers.title: Ultra-diffuse Galaxies in the Kilo-Degree Survey: Globular Cluster Systems in Cluster and Field Environments
papers.summary: Ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) are extreme low-surface-brightness systems whose formation pathways remain debated. Globular clusters (GCs) can trace their early assembly, but wide-area studies of UDG GC populations remain scarce. We study GC systems of 545 high-quality UDG candidates identified in the Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS) with UDGnet, using a dedicated GC-detection pipeline. We identify 24 UDGs with $N_{\rm GC} \geq 3$ (14 associated with groups or clusters and 10 in the field), and use the globular cluster luminosity function to estimate their distances and physical sizes. At fixed luminosity or stellar mass, group- and cluster-associated UDGs tend to have higher GC counts and specific frequencies than field UDGs, although the distributions overlap substantially. Most systems with $S_N \gtrsim 40$ reside in groups or clusters, while field UDGs generally occupy the lower part of the distribution. Group- and cluster-associated UDGs also more often lie near the upper envelope of the $N_{\rm GC}$--$M_\star$ relation. Empirical GC--halo mass relations consequently imply higher halo masses at fixed stellar mass and lower stellar-to-halo mass ratios, although this environmental trend is mild. These findings are consistent with efficient early GC formation followed by suppressed or prematurely quenched field-star formation, suggesting that GC-rich UDGs may represent an extension of the dwarf-galaxy population. The environmental trends may reflect differences in early assembly, quenching, infall, and survival histories rather than a sharp field--cluster dichotomy.

authors.name: Hao Su, Nicola R. Napolitano, Rui Li, Crescenzo Tortora, Fucheng Zhong, Zhenping Yi, Yang Liu

papers.title: Hard X-ray spectroscopy of a short-period asynchronous polar: IGR J19552+0044
papers.summary: IGR J19552+0044 is an asynchronous polar with a beat modulation of $\approx2$ days due to $\approx3$% spin-orbit asynchronism. We present the first hard X-ray properties of this system using a NuSTAR observation. Spectral modeling yields a shock temperature of $kT_{\rm s}=44.50^{+3.60}_{-3.29}$ keV, implying a white dwarf mass of $M_{\rm WD}\geq 0.85\,M_\odot$. We infer an average accretion rate of $\dot{M}\sim 3.0\times 10^{-11}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, consistent with expectations for short-period systems (orbital period $<2$ h). Even at this low accretion rate, we detect a significant Compton reflection component that gives a shock height of $H\sim 0.3\,R_{\rm WD}$. Time-resolved spectroscopy of the observation, covering $\approx61$% of a beat cycle, reveals a variation in $\dot{M}$ by a factor of $\sim 4.5$, providing X-ray evidence for the magnetic valve mechanism. Despite the large variations in $\dot{M}$, no significant change in shock temperature is observed. This weak thermal response constrains the shock structure on the white dwarf surface, favoring a shock height that remains approximately constant as $\dot{M}$ changes, potentially due to variations in the fractional accretion area $f$.

authors.name: Akash Agarwal, Vikram Rana

papers.title: The First Adolescent Super-Earth-Sized Multi-Planet System Around an M Dwarf: TOI-2079
papers.summary: We identify two planets in close-in orbits around the M-type star TOI-2079 as the first super-Earth-sized planets orbiting a multi-planet M dwarf with a well-determined age of $1$-$2$\,Gyr. The interior planet, TOI-2079 b, has an orbital period of $1.49232359^{+0.00000099}_{-0.00000086}$ d, and the outer planet, TOI-2079 c, has an orbital period of $9.3174523\pm0.0000098$ d. The host star characterization is based on spectroscopic observations, which classify it from an M1.5 to an M3.5 dwarf with an effective temperature of $3695\pm77$ K. Further analysis determined TOI-2079's rotation period to be $17.33^{+0.29}_{-0.28}$ d. Multiple ground-based follow-up observations, combined with a state-of-the-art validation procedure, allow us to rule out possible astrophysical false-positive scenarios and validate the planetary nature of both objects. We find that the inner planet has a radius of $1.320\pm0.050 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 867\pm27$ K, while the outer planet has $R_{\rm p} = 1.671\pm0.051 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 473\pm15$ K.
