Hopkins (Caltech)

papers.title: CARMApy: An Open-Source Python Framework for Simulating Microphysical Clouds in Planetary Atmospheres
papers.summary: CARMApy is a new open-source python code that performs bin-scheme microphysical modeling of clouds in exoplanet atmospheres. It models key cloud properties such as particle size distributions and microphysical rates from first principles. The code is a wrapper of ExoCARMA, a well tested Fortran code with an almost half century long heritage. CARMApy includes the microphysical processes of homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation, condensational growth, evaporation, coagulation, and vertical transport. CARMApy has 10 built-in default condensates and allows the user to specify additional condensates. In this work we describe CARMApy and the data products that it can generate, along with the history of its code heritage. We additionally compile a complete description of the theory and methods used in CARMA. Lastly we benchmark CARMApy and show that its results are consistent with previous versions of CARMA, while executing the code ~1.9 times faster single threaded ~3.8 times faster multithreaded.

authors.name: Wolf Cukier, Diana Powell, Xi Zhang, Peter Gao, Dominic Samra, Vighnesh Nagpal

papers.title: Probabilistic redshift estimation of undetected galaxies from multi-band background light maps
papers.summary: Accurate knowledge of the redshift distributions of undetected galaxy populations is essential for extracting the cosmological information encoded in the cosmic optical background. We present the first framework for estimating these distributions directly from multi-band maps of unresolved background light, using conditional normalising flows trained on realistic image simulations. For imaging quality comparable to that expected from the Euclid survey and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), our model achieves sub-per cent accuracy in both the mean and standard deviation of the flux-weighted redshift distributions when the training and target samples are statistically well matched. Furthermore, the network proves highly resilient to incomplete photometric coverage when combined with tailored data imputation strategies. To address the challenge of statistical mismatches between simulations and real observations, we propose incorporating observational quantities into the target variables, providing a built-in diagnostic to assess model reliability and uncertainty from the predictions themselves. We also demonstrate the feasibility of map-based tomographic analyses, showing that the model retains sufficient pixel-level detail to recover redshift distributions for tomographically defined subsamples with near sub-per cent accuracy across all bins.

authors.name: Shun-Sheng Li, Hendrik Hildebrandt, Ludovic Van Waerbeke

papers.title: Cataclysmic variables from Gaia XP spectra: The Gaia emission-line magnitude (GEM) diagram
papers.summary: Gaia DR3 opens a new window for the census of Galactic stellar populations in all-sky surveys, specifically for identifying cataclysmic variables (CVs). While the majority of CVs are distributed below the main sequence on the Gaia HR diagram, identifying them among dominant background stellar populations remains a significant challenge. Here, we present the Gaia Emission-line Magnitude (GEM) diagram - a tool designed to isolate CV candidates from background stars located below the main sequence. Using Gaia photometric data and low-resolution BP/RP (XP) spectra, we construct the GEM diagram by plotting the extinction-corrected absolute magnitude ($M_{G0}$) against the pseudo-equivalent width of the H$\alpha$ line ($pgEW_{H\alpha}$), which is computed via a Gaussian line-profile approximation. We find that known CVs and major stellar background populations, including white dwarfs, hot subdwarfs, and white dwarf-main sequence binaries, occupy distinct regions on the GEM diagram, reflecting both their physical properties and the low-resolution nature of the Gaia XP spectra. We define an empirical selection line on the GEM diagram to separate true H$\alpha$-emitting CVs from background contaminants. As a proof of concept, we apply the GEM diagram to a Gaia volume-limited sample within 250 pc ($G<17.5$ mag) distributed below the main sequence, recovering known CVs. Additionally, we identify three new CV candidates whose accreting nature is supported by archival X-ray data and optical variability. Compared to traditional optical color-based selection techniques, the GEM diagram uses Gaia's low-resolution spectra for initial target identification in all-sky surveys. This provides a more reliable framework for the statistical selection of CV candidates prior to ground-based spectroscopic follow-up and can be scaled to future Gaia data releases to map Galactic emission-line star populations.

authors.name: Ilkham Galiullin, Vladislav Dodon, Antonio C. Rodriguez, Askar Sibgatullin

papers.title: Locating the missing baryons in the warm-hot intergalactic medium with fast radio bursts and the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect
papers.summary: Traditional astronomical censuses in the late-time Universe can only account for a fraction of the baryonic matter budget. Hydrodynamical simulations predict that the missing baryons reside in the vast filamentary structures of the cosmic web as a highly diffuse, warm-hot intergalactic medium (WHIM). Observing the WHIM directly has remained a long-standing challenge due to its typical temperature. In this study, we measure the angular cross-power spectrum between the dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) from the second CHIME/FRB catalog and the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) Compton-$y$ map from the Planck satellite. After masking cataloged galaxy clusters, we find a positive correlation between FRB DMs and the tSZ map at $>98\%$ confidence ($p_{\rm null}=0.0169$). With a temperature normalization of $2.4\times10^6\ {\rm K}$, we infer that a fraction $f_{\rm WHIM}=0.375^{+0.165}_{-0.161}$ of cosmic baryons resides in the hotter WHIM. These measurements constrain a substantial reservoir of hotter diffuse gas in the cosmic web and statistically close the cosmic baryon budget in the local Universe under the adopted density and pressure model.

authors.name: Dao-Hong Zhai, F. Y. Wang, Zi-Gao Dai, Renyue Cen

papers.title: Automatic detection of fast oscillations of dark matter scalar field and updated cosmological constraints on QCDM
papers.summary: It is well known that a scalar field dark matter with a quadratic potential undergoes fast oscillations when the time period represented by the mass scale in the Klein-Gordon equation becomes much smaller than that set by the Hubble parameter. This makes a solution to the equation numerically intractable. Many works in the literature have addressed the problem by either switching between solving the Klein-Gordon equation in the well-behaved regime to solving the fluid equations at the onset of oscillations, or by introducing a new set of variables that can absorb these oscillations. Despite being successful, these techniques rely on an estimate of when the oscillations start. For large scale scans of a model's parameter space, this can become cumbersome. Furthermore, the techniques have been used mainly for non-interacting dark matter models. In this work, we introduce an averaging technique with an automatic detection of the onset of oscillations, capable of capturing the non-interacting as well as the interacting dark matter scenarios. The technique, implemented in \texttt{CLASS}, is tested on the QCDM model and shows excellent detection and averaging abilities. We also update the cosmological constraints on the model using the most recent public data.

authors.name: Amin Aboubrahim, Pran Nath

papers.title: Hydrogen Engulfment into Sub-Neptune Cores through Magma Ocean Convective Surface Renewal
papers.summary: A convective surface renewal explanation for ingassing of hydrogen from H2-rich envelopes into molten cores of growing planets is presented, with particular application to sub-Neptunes. The ingassing of hydrogen occurs at a moving front comprising the upper boundary of the magma ocean that engulfs hydrogen from the envelope above as it moves. The mechanism of engulfment is surface renewal as the upper diffusive boundary layer is diluted by convection. Surface renewal results in ingassing even where the stabilizing buoyancy of the low-density hydrogen neutralizes the destabilizing thermally-driven buoyancy. It is ultimately driven by cooling. Beginning during the gaseous disk phase, when hydrogen is effectively available in infinite supply, sub-Neptunes can acquire enough hydrogen to permit global core-envelope equilibrium. The structures are therefore consistent with hydrogen-rich, supercritical magma oceans overlain by hydrogen-rich envelopes. The process of surface renewal has implications for other magma ocean - atmosphere interactions in general.

authors.name: Edward D. Young

papers.title: Early Supermassive Black Holes and Little Red Dots Require Free-Fall Growth
papers.summary: Supermassive black holes/active galactic nuclei (SMBHs/AGN), forming only a few hundred million years after the Big Bang as observed with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), challenge theoretical understanding. How could they grow so massive $(M_{\rm BH} > 10^6 {\rm \,M}_\odot)$ so quickly after initial seeding? Is this rapid growth related to the numerous and enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs), compact sources with AGN-like characteristics, discovered by JWST? To address these mysteries, we consider the first-order constraint on SMBH growth: enough baryonic material has to reach the vicinity of the SMBH seed, located near the bottom of the gravitational potential well of the host dark matter halo. We specifically examine cold-mode accretion, where gas from the cosmic environment flows into the virialized halo in cold streams without being shock-heated, efficiently reaching the center on a free-fall timescale. We find that cold mode accretion is necessary to supply material for the SMBHs to reach the observed masses, whereas for shock-heated gas inflow the required amount could only be supplied by implausibly rare halos. Moreover, cold-mode inflow in rare $(\sim1$ Gpc$^{-3}$) halos matches the mass and number of the massive quasars, and halos able to support super-Eddington accretion for massive SMBHs ($\sim10^7$ M$_\odot$) match LRD number densities. The decreasing LRD abundance at lower redshifts may then reflect the termination of cold-mode accretion in the growing host halos. The populations of massive SMBHs and LRDs at early times may thus arise naturally from cosmological structure formation, based on the abundance of halos capable of supplying sufficient material through cold accretion.

authors.name: Junehyoung Jeon, Volker Bromm, Michael Boylan-Kolchin, Julian B. Mu\~noz

papers.title: A systematic search for long GRBs without supernovae: global properties and rate of events
papers.summary: Some long duration gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) are not associated with bright supernovae (SNe), indicating that their explosion mechanism differs from the traditional collapsar channel. SN-less LGRBs are rare, thus it remains unclear whether they are sporadic outliers or a substantial component of the GRB population. In this work, we use two decades of Swift observations to conduct a systematic search for nearby ($z\lesssim$0.35) LGRBs without a confirmed SN association. Our analysis reveals a heterogeneous population linked, in part, to star-forming or dusty environments and, in part, to quiescent galaxies. Through the analysis of their high-energy properties, afterglows, and environments, we identify a sample of LGRBs with robust SN limits and distance scales, more than doubling the number of candidate SN-less events. From our fiducial sample, we derive a volumetric rate, not corrected for beaming, of $R = (0.5 \pm 0.2) {\rm~Gpc^{-3}\ yr^{-1}}$, comparable to the apparent rate of short duration GRBs (SGRBs) and standard LGRBs with SNe with luminosities $L \gtrsim\,10^{50}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$. For plausible beaming factors, the inferred rate of SN-less LGRBs is consistent with several compact binary merger channels, although the allowed parameter space is already narrow if the entire population is attributed to a single progenitor channel. Owing to the small number of candidate events and the uncertainties in their distance scale, our sample leaves the low-luminosity tail unconstrained. A larger sample will be needed to determine whether they are the faint tail of known progenitor channels or evidence of a distinct route to relativistic explosions.

authors.name: Yu-Han Yang, Eleonora Troja, Nicolas Monsalves, Massine El Kabir, Narjes Shahamat Dehsorkh, Hira Waseem

papers.title: Kink instability as a particle acceleration mechanism in X-ray binaries and the connection to the outburst cycle
papers.summary: We consider whether the kink instability can explain particle acceleration in hard state 'compact' X-ray binary jets. We apply a 1D model to assess the expected growth rate of the instability for a variety of jet models, then scale results from simulations to estimate a dissipation rate for the magnetic energy in the jet. We then consider the effects of radiative cooling on the system. We find that hard state 'compact' X-ray binary jets are likely to be unstable to the kink instability within their acceleration zones across a plausible parameter space. We further find that depending on the parameters of the model, the jets may radiate over a variety of length scales ranging from length scales attributable to a 'failed' jet scenario, to those in keeping with resolved radio observations of 'compact' jets. We discuss the expected evolution of this model through the outburst cycle.

authors.name: Emma L. Elley, James H. Matthews, Alex J. Cooper, Fraser J. Cowie, Rob Fender

papers.title: The 1.6 $\mu\mathrm{m}$ $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump as a diagnostic of TP-AGB contributions and recent quenching. I. Insights from stellar population models
papers.summary: The 1.6 $\mu\mathrm{m}$ $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump arises from a minimum in the opacity of the negative hydrogen ion in cool stellar atmospheres. Although it is recognized as a common feature in galaxy spectra, its potential for studying stellar populations and recent quenching remains underexplored. Its enhancement at intermediate ages is strong in some stellar population models with substantial thermally pulsing asymptotic giant branch (TP-AGB) contributions but weak or absent in others. This variation makes the feature both a potential age diagnostic and a source of model uncertainty. We use models based on the X-shooter Spectral Library (XSL) and Flexible Stellar Population Synthesis (FSPS) to examine what drives this behavior and what it can reveal about quenching. Controlled FSPS experiments show that the $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump depends on both the amount of TP-AGB light and the stellar template used to represent it. The adopted XSL and TP-AGB-on FSPS models predict a transient enhancement of the $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump following rapid quenching, while optical spectral features D4000 and H$\delta$ produce monotonic responses. Combining these diagnostics can therefore provide additional information about recent quenching, although the interpretation depends on the population model and star-formation history. The $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump -- $\mathrm{D}4000$ plane shows that models including TP-AGB contributions can describe the observed JWST NIRSpec data reasonably well. These results motivate further use of the $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump to test TP-AGB prescriptions and investigate quenching with current and forthcoming observations.

authors.name: Pengjun Lu, Song Huang, Sijia Cai, Francesco D'Eugenio, Meng Gu, Li Shen, Cheng Li

papers.title: Widespread steep X-ray spectra of luminous $z=5.85-7.64$ quasars and their implications for future X-ray surveys
papers.summary: Luminous quasars (QSOs) at the Epoch of Reionization (EoR, $z\gtrsim6$) host billion-solar-mass black holes assembled within the first Gyr of cosmic time. Their X-ray emission probes the innermost accreting regions and constrains the physical state of the corona during early supermassive black hole (SMBH) growth. Previous results from the HYPerluminous quasars at the Epoch of ReionizatION (HYPERION) sample of $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs, powered by the most rapidly accreted SMBHs, suggested a link between X-ray spectral slope and long-term growth efficiency. We test whether the steep X-ray spectra of luminous z>6 QSOs are a general property of early SMBH growth or a peculiarity of the most efficiently grown SMBHs, using a sample extended mainly to the lowest growth efficiencies. We analysed the largest and most X-ray sensitive sample of 28 luminous QSOs at $z = 5.85-7.64$ (26 used in the correlation analysis), combining HYPERION targets, luminous non-HYPERION sources, and QSOs powered by moderately accreting SMBHs newly observed in our XMM-Newton Large Programme. We re-derived black hole masses and growth indicators for the entire sample homogeneously, incorporating the latest JWST-based spectroscopic measurements to ensure the most consistent and high-quality characterization across all targets. We found no statistically significant correlation between coronal spectral parameters and BH growth indicators: luminous $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs systematically show steep X-ray continua, with high photon indices and/or low high-energy cutoffs, consistent with cold coronae, possibly linked to rapid accretion. Finally, if steep X-ray slopes are common among early AGN, they may significantly reduce count rates, at fixed intrinsic luminosity, in future surveys of the EoR, affecting the detectability of steep-spectrum X-ray sources and thus the census of the early AGN population.

papers.title: Extinction by non-spherical particles with the Nanoparticle Transition Matrix Code: perspectives for interstellar medium and exoplanetary atmospheres
papers.summary: The Transition Matrix formalism (T-matrix) offers an optimal solution to the problem of radiation scattering and absorption by particles characterized by a high degree of chemical and structural complexity. However, its application to particle models composed by large numbers of constituents has been classically limited by the substantial computational burden of the method. As a consequence, the investigation of light scattering and absorption processes, in cases where particle asymmetry and non-homogeneity play an important role, typically need to rely on simplifying assumptions which affect the correct interpretation of transmission spectra and extinction curves. This problem has a huge impact on many fields of scientific application. In particular, it has a critical role in astrophysics, because the ability to model highly non homogeneous particles is a fundamental requirement to understand the role of extinction in different phases of the interstellar medium (ISM), as well as to probe the physics of light transmission in planetary atmospheres within the Solar System and beyond. In this work we describe the application of a new implementation of the T-matrix formalism, based on the framework originally developed by Borghese, Denti & Saija and named Nano-particle Transition Matrix code, which leverages the power of modern hardware architectures to reduce the computational costs related to the solution of relevant particle models for the investigation of dust in the ISM and of hot-Jupyter class planets atmospheric aerosols. This new implementation of the T-matrix formalism can handle calculations of increasing complexity with a direct impact in the interpretation of the transmission spectra of transiting exoplanets produced by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and of those expected from the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey (ARIEL).

authors.name: G. La Mura, G. Mulas, M. A. Iat\`i, C. Cecchi-Pestellini, G. Aresu, S. Rezaei, R. Saija

papers.title: Multi-Method Machine Learning Classification of Astronomical Sources with Rubin Data Previews: a Spectroscopy-Free Approach with DP1 and DP2
papers.summary: We present a multi-method machine-learning study for the binary photometric classification of point-like and extended sources in the Rubin Observatory Data Preview 1 (DP1) and Data Preview 2 (DP2). The workflow runs on the Rubin Science Platform using DP1 and DP2 ugrizy photometry, the DP1 ancillary photometric-redshift catalog, and the Monster astrometric and photometric reference catalog, without relying on external spectroscopy. Six methods (SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, k-Nearest Neighbors, an Artificial Neural Network, and a soft Voting ensemble) are benchmarked in the deepest DP1 field, the Extended Chandra Deep Field South. These methods reach 10-fold cross-validation macro-F1 scores of 0.95-0.97 on the balanced training subset and test macro-F1 scores of 0.87-0.92 on the imbalanced held-out set, with RF and the SV ensemble tied at the top (0.918); the differences among the leading methods are within the statistical uncertainty. Permutation importance identifies FWHM as the dominant feature, and the six methods agree on 79.5% of the full catalog. The same pipeline is then applied without retuning the settings to the two other DP1 fields with full ugrizy coverage and photometric-redshift support, Euclid Deep Field South and the Low Galactic Latitude Field. Together, the three fields span a factor of approximately 7 in E(B-V) and approximately 10 in stellar density, yet headline macro-F1 remains above 0.87 in every field. We then apply the same pipeline to four DP2 fields (ECDFS, COSMOS, EDFS, and ELAIS-S1). Using colors and morphology, the best method reaches a test macro-F1 of 0.83 to 0.88 across these fields, and the six methods agree on 77 to 86% of each catalog. Adding the per-band photometric uncertainties as features raises the best macro-F1 to about 0.95 in ECDFS DP1 and 0.97 in ECDFS DP2 (and to approximately 0.97-0.98 in the other fields).

authors.name: Andr\'es Alejandro Plazas Malag\'on, Yasna Ordenes-Brice\~no, Dan S. Taranu, Alex Broughton, Yumi Choi, Jeffrey L. Carlin, Sophie Reed, Karla Pe\~na Ram\'irez, Sean Patrick MacBride, Hurum Maksora Tohfa, Arianna Ranabhat

papers.title: No Significant Rotation of the Spiral Structure in the IM Lup Protoplanetary Disk
papers.summary: Spiral structures are often observed in protoplanetary disks, but their origins remain uncertain. Yoshida et al. (2025) reported a pattern speed consistent with local Keplerian rotation for the $m=2$ spiral in the dusty disk around IM Lup using multi-epoch ALMA observations, supporting a gravitational instability (GI)-driven origin. However, recent studies revise the disk geometry of IM Lup, motivating a reassessment of its spiral pattern speed. In this study, we reanalyze the disk geometry of the same multi-epoch data using visibility-based continuum emission modeling. The inferred disk geometries differ from those adopted in previous studies by a few degrees but are consistent across epochs and with recent independent estimates based on gas emission analyses. The revised geometries yield weaker residuals and more physically plausible radial spiral phase profiles. Unlike previous studies, our remeasured spiral pattern speeds are consistent with zero rotation within the uncertainties. We conclude that the previously reported Keplerian-like motion can be explained by a mismatch in the adopted disk geometry, which affects the spiral phases measured in Band 6 (2017, 2019) and Band 7 (2024) differently. In addition, we identify a tentative large-scale one-armed spiral-like structure extending beyond the known $m=2$ spiral, which may provide clues to additional perturbations, such as an embedded planet or late-stage infall. Future high-resolution Band 6 observations with a longer time baseline will be essential for more accurately determining the spiral pattern speed.

authors.name: Yuto Hiraide, Masataka Aizawa, Munetake Momose

papers.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of the H$\alpha$ Luminosity Functions at $z\sim 1.3$ and $z\sim 2.0$ in the CANUCS Lensing Fields with JWST NIRISS
papers.summary: We present H$\alpha$ luminosity function (LF) measurements at redshifts $z\sim1.3$ and $z\sim2.0$. We adopt JWST grism data in five lensing cluster fields and their parallel fields from the CANUCS program: ABELL-370, MACS-J0416, MACS-J0417, MACS-J1149, MACS-J1423. Based on emission lines spectroscopically identified in the F115W, F150W and F200W filters, our final sample consists of 762 H$\alpha$ emitters, including 433 at $1.1<z<1.5$ and 329 at $1.8<z<2.2$. Through detailed effective volume and completeness analysis for each source, we construct the H$\alpha$ LF in two redshift bins. Thanks to the sensitivity of NIRISS WFSS and gravitational lensing magnification, our sample reaches intrinsic H$\alpha$ luminosities down to $L_{\rm H\alpha}\sim10^{40.6}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $L_{\rm H\alpha}\sim10^{41}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim2.0$ with completeness larger than 80\%. The larger survey volume and coverage of multiple independent sightlines help mitigate cosmic variance. After accounting for cosmic variance, we constrain the faint-end slopes to be $\alpha_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}=-1.51^{+0.06}_{-0.04}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $-1.42^{+0.09}_{-0.06}$ at $z\sim2.0$, indicating a mild evolution between the two redshift bins. We find a negligible contribution from bright active galactic nuclei in our sample. We estimate integrated cosmic star formation rate densities of $0.103^{+0.008}_{-0.007}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $0.149^{+0.016}_{-0.013}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim2.0$. The emission-line samples presented here will enable further detailed studies of galaxy properties including metallicities. The methodology presented here can be readily applicable to other JWST slitless spectroscopic datasets and future wide-field slitless surveys, including those from Euclid, Roman, and the Chinese Space Station Telescope.

authors.name: Qianqiao Zhou, Yuxuan Pang, Xin Wang, Karl Glazebrook, Shengzhe Wang, Hang Zhou, Pengfei Ren, Shamuhawu Hailanhazi, Peter J. Watson, Nicha Leethochawalit, Matthew A. Malkan, Themiya Nanayakkara, Xue-Bing Wu, Hu Zhan

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). An overview of the Science Ground Segment architecture and operations
papers.summary: The Euclid mission is designed to address fundamental questions on the nature of dark energy and dark matter by mapping the extragalactic sky with a wide-area survey complemented by targeted deep observations. The required scientific performance places stringent demands on the Euclid Science Ground Segment (SGS), which transforms raw telemetry into calibrated, validated, and scientifically exploitable products. The SGS is a distributed system comprising the Euclid Science Operations Centre, the Science Data Centres, Instrument Operation Teams, and supporting Organisation Units, within a common architectural and procedural framework. This paper presents the SGS as implemented for Data Release 1 (DR1), describing its organisation, architecture, processing functions, and operational model. We outline the main components of the SGS common infrastructure. A key element is the Euclid Archive System (EAS), the central metadata repository based on a common data model. It comprises a Distributed Storage System, providing scalable storage of data files across the Science Data Centres; a Data Processing System used by the pipelines to register and access files and their lineage; and a Science Archive, distributing validated data products. Processing is coordinated by a common orchestration framework based on the Infrastructure Abstraction Layer, providing workflow management and resource abstraction of distributed compute clusters. Software development, integration, and deployment are supported by the Common Development Environment. We describe daily operations, calibration, and quality control, followed by the DR1 production campaign, including processing flows, validation strategy, and computational and data volumes. This infrastructure enabled Euclid DR1, involving 35 million jobs across nine Science Data Centres and 6.7 million core-hours, demonstrating robustness and scalability of the SGS.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): NISP-P point-spread function modelling pipelines
papers.summary: The images collected in photometric mode by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) instrument of the Euclid satellite are used to model the point-spread function (PSF) of a selection of sources detected in single and combined frames. We used Q1 and DR1 data to improve the development of the PSF module of the near-infrared processing function (NIR PF) and to refine the models currently provided. We explored a few methods normally used to evaluate the quality of the derived models and discuss possible variations related to the position of the sources in the focal plane and to the wavelength and time of the observations. The procedure of fitting the PSF profile, compared to other methods used for flux estimation, such as aperture photometry, indicates that updated models are better than those provided by Q1 images. The current results are in agreement with several key requirements defined for the mission, but there is still room for further improvements, which we plan to investigate and implement in future releases.

papers.title: Orion I: Discovery of an Isolated dE,N Galaxy at 60 Megaparsecs
papers.summary: Inspection of deep JWST images centered on the lensing cluster of galaxies MACS J0454.1-0300 reveals a small, well resolved stellar system that is clearly in the foreground. Photometric measurements including a color-magnitude diagram and radial profile show that it is a nucleated dwarf early-type galaxy (dE,N) at a distance of ~60 Mpc and with structurally normal properties. This object (J04:54:07.39-02:59:22.5, referred to as Orion I for shorthand) may be an outlying member of a previously known small galaxy group, or may be simply an isolated field galaxy depending on the accuracy of its distance estimate. The discovery of Orion I suggests that other small stellar systems in the nearby universe might be found through a search of the many deep \jwst imaging fields that are now being accumulated.

authors.name: W. E. Harris, T. Carleton, R. Ortiz, L. Furtak, J. Berkheimer, R. Honor, B. Frye, B. Holwerda, C. Willmer, R. Windhorst

papers.title: Multi-epoch imaging observations of the Galactic Center with NIRCam and MIRI
papers.summary: The center of the Milky Way is the densest and most extreme environment in our Galaxy, its most active star forming region, and the only galaxy nucleus where we can resolve stars down to about a solar mass on the main sequence. The Galactic Center (GC) contains a nuclear stellar disk, a nuclear star cluster, and a supermassive black hole, all embedded within the so-called Central Molecular Zone, which showcases conditions of the interstellar medium that are typically found in high-redshift star-forming regions. The GC hosts the highest concentration of massive stars in the Milky Way and hosts a large concentration of rare objects, such as Wolf Rayet stars and X-ray binaries. The GC is therefore an astrophysical target of outstanding importance. A multi-epoch JWST program enables novel science including the lifetime of planet-forming disks, the search for intermediate mass black holes, direct measurements of the multi-scale gravitational potential, and a deep measurement of the star formation history. Multi-epoch imaging observations with JWST's NIRCam and MIRI instruments will go far beyond Roman WFI surveys in terms of depth and astrometric and photometric precision because of its $3\times$ better resolution, and it expands spectral coverage in narrow bands and mid-infrared wavelength coverage. The proposed observations would correspond to a Treasury Program of about 420\,h, distributed over three epochs spaced three to five years apart.

papers.title: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk$-$new insights from GALAH DR4
papers.summary: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk has drawn extensive attention since ESA's \textit{Gaia} launch. Complex structure appears across a multi-parameter space of stellar abundances, ages, and kinematics. Using GALAH DR4, we investigate ridge and phase-spiral structures in chemical-abundance, phase ($v_i,x_i$), action--angle ($J_i,\theta_i$), and frequency--action ($\Omega_i,J_i$) spaces ($i=R,\phi,z$). Our sample includes 333,412 disk stars with reliable chemodynamical data. In the $R$--$v_\phi$ plane, ridges trace near-constant $J_\phi$ tracks and show coherent variations in $\theta_R$ and $\theta_\phi$. In $J_\phi$--$J_R$, ridges are most prominent when encoded by $z_{\rm max}$ and preferentially associate with metal-rich, low-$\alpha$ populations. In the solar neighbourhood ($R=7.2$--$9.2$\,kpc), we recover a clear phase spiral in $z$--$v_z$. Encoded in $v_\phi$, $\Omega_R$, or $\Omega_\phi$, one-armed spirals appear, whereas the $v_R$-encoded map shows a two-armed spiral. Projecting actions onto $z$--$v_z$ reveals residual spiral signatures in $J_R$ and $J_\phi$, indicating that the phase spiral encodes in-plane orbital information. Both structures depend on age: ridges remain at similar locations with varying contrast, while the phase spiral is more tightly wound in younger and more loosely wound in older populations. Several ridges correspond in $J_\phi$ to known moving groups, and excluding stars in all six moving-group regions makes the phase spiral less distinct in mean radial velocity maps. These links support interpreting ridges, phase spirals, and moving groups within a common phase-space dynamical framework. Combined with trends in orbital properties, age, and abundance, these findings suggest a common dynamical origin and distinct chemodynamical responses of a perturbed Galactic disk.

authors.name: Peng Yang, Hai-Feng Wang, Joss Bland-Hawthorn, Guo-Jun Cheng, Yu-Zheng Wang, Yang-Ping Luo, Kun Wang

papers.title: Nuclear pasta in hot neutron-star matter and proto-neutron stars
papers.summary: We investigate nuclear pasta phases appearing in hot neutron-star matter based on the compressible liquid-drop model, where the matter consists of a dense liquid phase and a dilute gas phase separated by a sharp interface.The surface tension is calculated self-consistently from the Thomas-Fermi approximation, and it depends on temperature and isospin asymmetry. We employ relativistic mean-field (RMF) models with different symmetry energy slopes to describe nuclear interactions. It is found that the RMF models with smaller symmetry energy slopes result in various pasta phases at low temperatures, whereas those with larger symmetry energy slopes yield only the droplet configuration up to the crust-core transition density. We examine the occurrence and influence of pasta phases in proto-neutron stars with a constant entropy per baryon. These pasta phases may occur in the inner crust and play an important role in the thermal evolution of the star.

authors.name: Jian Zhou, Junbo Pang, Hong Shen, Jinniu Hu

papers.title: Parameter Estimation on LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4a Binary Merger Triggers with Sub-solar Mass Components
papers.summary: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration has reported the results for searches for sub-solar mass components in compact binary coalescence during observing run O4a. No detection candidates were identified, but the most significant seven triggers were reported. We present the results of Bayesian parameter inference on these triggers. Five of the triggers show agreement between the Bayesian parameter estimation and the search pipeline trigger. Our results show that three of the triggers may contain a possible sub-solar mass component. Parameter estimation indicates that the other two events, if real, would be neutron star - black hole binaries. The remaining two triggers do not provide informative parameter estimation. We also study three O4a compact binary coalescence triggers, and one O3 trigger, that have been noted by three other groups, and our parameter estimation indicates that three of these may contain a sub-solar mass component. We study the data quality associated with these triggers. Finally, we discuss the challenges for parameter estimation on compact binary coalescence events containing a sub-solar mass component: long signal duration, possible small chirp masses, possible small mass ratios, and data quality issues over potentially hundreds of seconds of data.

authors.name: Nelson Christensen, Neil Cornish, Florian K\"{u}hnel, Mairi Sakellariadou, Andres Santiago Villares Guanga

papers.title: Reference-Filter-Driven Transition Probabilities for IMM-Based Satellite Maneuver Detection
papers.summary: Detecting maneuvers of non-cooperative satellites is essential for space situational awareness. The interacting multiple model (IMM) filter has been applied to detect unannounced maneuvers, but the standard IMM assumes a fixed Markov transition probability matrix (TPM) that must be tuned without knowledge of the maneuver rate of the target. To avoid the tuning, adaptive-TPM approaches update the TPM online from statistics computed inside the IMM. However, the statistics already depend on the TPM through the interaction step, and the dependence forms a feedback loop. The loop itself can raise the maneuver probability in the absence of a maneuver or suppress its rise when a maneuver occurs. In this paper, the TPM is driven by the normalized innovation squared (NIS) of a reference coast filter that is decoupled from the IMM, and the NIS is mapped continuously to the coast-to-maneuver transition probability. The reference-driven IMM (RD-IMM) is evaluated with four space-based optical sensors tracking a geostationary target. In the simulation, the reference filter keeps its sensitivity after small maneuvers, whereas the NIS of the coast sub-filter of the IMM is reduced by the interaction step. RD-IMM detects 1-3 m/s maneuvers, which the fixed-TPM IMM rarely detects, with a false-declaration rate below the false-alarm probability of 0.05 set for the reference filter. In the first hour after the 1-3 m/s maneuvers, RD-IMM also has a lower position error than the compared filters.

authors.name: Euiseok Han, Sangheon Choi, Seung-Hyun Kong

papers.title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
papers.summary: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.

authors.name: Tomoyuki Maruyama, A. Baha Balantekin, Myung-Ki Cheoun, Toshitaka Kajino, Eunseok Whang

papers.title: Causal Event Networks: Entangled Tensor Graphs, Connectome Quotient Topology, and Subjective Experience as Geometric Dual
papers.summary: We introduce a chromatically constrained tensor-product construction that generates sparse recurrent computational graphs whose coloring bounds the number of sequential execution phases: vertices are computational units, edges are causal message-passing channels, and the graph can grow arbitrarily large while its chromatic causal depth stays fixed. Coarsened to the scale of the Budapest Reference Connectome, the community quotient of a simple local construction reproduces the connectome's broad degree profile, passes a nine-criterion topological test and comes close to the connectome on most of a further battery of complexity, spectral, controllability and clique measures, while the fine parent graph shows a scale separation: multiscale organization is intrinsic to the fine graph, and short-path integration appears only under coarsening. Placing short-path integration directly in the fine substrate, with chromatically admissible bridges and targeted sparsification, yields quotients far less modular than the connectome across a wide range of coarsening schemes. Relocating edges into the interiors of quotient nodes instead produces a quotient that matches the connectome's degree profile, edge count and fiber-bundle distribution, passes the full nine-criterion test and comes close on most complexity and spectral measures; its fine substrate fails only the two near-random path criteria. Used as the deep-feature pathway of a U-Net encoder-decoder, the graph-derived recurrent module improves image inpainting over the convolutional baseline. We close with a conjectural, structural account of subjective experience in holographic terms: the graph acts as an evolution operator that fixes the admissible causal order and the geometries the substrate can support, and experience occupies the position of the bulk dual of a particular activity state.

authors.name: Vahid R. Ramezani

papers.title: Integrated Stress Responses and ABCB11 Repression in Drug-Exposed Human Hepatocytes
papers.summary: Drug-safety information systems must distinguish direct bile salt export pump (BSEP) inhibition from transcriptional changes in hepatic transport programs. We investigated whether repression of ABCB11, which encodes BSEP, tracks an integrated stress response (ISR) after accounting for dose and liver-identity proxies. We analyzed 197 human hepatocyte RNA-seq dose conditions for 50 compounds using compound-centered models and 2,000 compound-bootstrap resamples. The association remained negative after dose and 436-gene identity adjustment ($\beta=-0.288$; 95\% interval, $-0.416$ to $-0.127$), and after jointly adding global-expression, oxidative-stress and apoptosis scores ($\beta=-0.198$; $-0.342$ to $-0.039$). The adjusted partial correlation ($r=-0.422$) exceeded in absolute magnitude those obtained for all but 1 of 5,000 expression-matched and 16 of 5,000 expression- and variance-matched random six-gene sets. Several comparator transporters also declined, indicating that the association was not restricted to ABCB11. Adding an interpolated source-screen viability proxy to all controls retained a negative estimate but an interval including zero ($\beta=-0.190$; $-0.335$ to $0.009$; 152 conditions, 39 compounds). Exposure-restricted uncertainty likewise depended on identity adjustment. Published modules from 240 external microarray conditions for 80 perturbagens showed consistent stress--metabolic covariation, without gene-level replication. A separate assay/FDA audit exposed sparse joint coverage and source-dependent associations. Together, these analyses link hepatocyte stress to ABCB11 repression and provide a biologically grounded approach to integrating biochemical, transcriptional and regulatory evidence for drug-safety assessment.

authors.name: Pratyush Kumar Shukla

papers.title: Infection Spreading and Stochastic Extinction in Finite Spatially Inhomogeneous Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible and Susceptible-Infected-Recovered Systems
papers.summary: Demographic fluctuations can drive finite epidemic populations into an absorbing disease-free state even when the corresponding infinite system supports sustained activity. By means of Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate how spatial coupling of two distinct subsystems modifies stochastic extinction and epidemic spreading in susceptible-infectious-susceptible (SIS) and susceptible-infectious-recovered (SIR) models on inhomogeneous two-dimensional square lattices. For isolated SIS systems, extinction times exhibit approximate power-law scaling near the epidemic threshold even for small systems. Traversal times characterize the distinct propagation dynamics of SIS and SIR infection clusters. We consider diffusively coupled regions with different transmission characteristics in coupled SIS-SIS, SIR-SIS, and SIR-SIR configurations. Invading fronts can reactivate a vulnerable SIS region after its initial infection has disappeared and establish a long-lived active epidemic state. This stabilization can be induced by either a sustained SIS source or a single transient SIR epidemic wave. Spatial correlation measurements support a mechanism in which the invading activity generates an extended correlated infectious population, effectively providing favorable initial conditions for renewed epidemic spreading. Correlations develop particularly strongly parallel to the subsystem interfaces. Decoupling the regions after some elapsed period demonstrates that autonomous persistence requires sufficient coupling time beyond the first interface arrival for this correlated population to become established. Increasing system size delays invasion but enhances the probability of ultimate successful stabilization. In two coupled SIR regions, transmission can initiate a macroscopic secondary outbreak, while permanent immunity restricts both epidemics to transient activity.

authors.name: Sara Shabani (Virginia Tech), Uwe C. T\"auber (Virginia Tech)

papers.title: Topology-only Local Network Alignment, Part 2. DijSLA: Stochastic Greedy Extension for Cross-Species GO Annotation Prediction
papers.summary: Sequence similarity has long been a strong signal for protein function prediction, whereas the predictive value of network topology has been difficult to verify. Since a protein's function is largely defined by its interaction partners, and since similar interactions are expected across species, aligning protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks by topology alone should uncover functionally related proteins. Topology-only global network alignment has recently produced high-quality functional predictions, but it has yet to be shown that local regions of topological similarity can do the same. We introduce DijSLA (Dijkstra-inspired Stochastic Local Alignment), the first local network alignment algorithm designed from the ground up to use only topology. We adopt a seed-and-extend strategy: starting from seed pairs of proteins with similar network topology, we expand the alignment in a Dijkstra-inspired manner, following edges out of the aligned set to node pairs with near-maximal similarity. Rather than expanding deterministically, we inject randomness so that we can sample many high-quality alignments, in which node pairs with robust topological similarity "rise above" the noise and reveal functional similarity. Using networks and GO annotations from April 2010, we predict annotations validated against those from April 2020. With Network Alignment Frequency (NAF), a robustness measure that correlates with prediction precision, we make predictions with precision on par with or better than the best sequence-based methods and broadly similar to that of global topological alignment. Compared with existing local aligners, DijSLA produces larger, topologically high-quality alignments, which yield dramatically more predictions with higher validation rates, while using less CPU time and far less memory. Code is available at https://github.com/waynebhayes/BLANT/tree/master/CDijkstra.

authors.name: Yiran Jin, Tingyin Ding, Utsav Jain, Grady Jaron Yu, Burwin Liu, Wayne B. Hayes

papers.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
papers.summary: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications. In the semi-regular regime, where all tallies and sums are uniform, we use complex martingale techniques to derive asymptotic formulas for the number of doubly constrained arrays as $N$ and $P$ grow with bounded ratio, over the whole feasible region. The leading term is governed by the Shannon entropy of the frequencies of the four possible pairs of entries at a position of the two matrices; on the boundary one or two of them vanish, changing the Gaussian correction. We then ask whether the two families carry information additively, that is, whether an independence heuristic predicts the doubly constrained count up to a bounded factor. Measured against the smallest set of arrays defined by a constraint that each family implies on its own, additivity holds only on a set of measure zero. It includes an edge of the feasible region with correction factor $e^{-1/4}$, extending our earlier result at the symmetric point. Thus, how far the two summaries jointly narrow down individual-level ancestry and genotype configurations cannot generally be predicted from how far each does on its own.

authors.name: Alan J. Aw

papers.title: Classical visual illusions in vision-language models under an instruction ladder
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) often name the "illusory" answer when shown a classical visual illusion, but it is unclear whether that answer comes from the picture or from knowledge about famous figures. We drew 300 new stimuli of 25 classical illusions in three conditions--the illusion, the illusion with its inducing elements reversed, and a control with the inducing elements removed--and asked about each image at eight rungs of an instruction ladder that runs from a false fact, through a neutral question and an instruction to report the physical truth, to telling the model the name of the illusion and finally the true answer. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5, with thinking off and on, gave 460,800 answers. When asked for the physical fact, all four settings almost never gave the illusion answer, and they resolved real 10% differences in the same displays. When asked how the picture looks, the illusion answers returned, and they did not vanish after the true answer was stated. Two measures that cancel position preferences and recognition of the figure suggest that much of this depends on the stimulus: among side answers, Sonnet with thinking chose the illusion side in 85% of cases after being told the truth (95% CI 74--96%), with 16 of the 25 illusions showing a stimulus-driven effect. Yet for five figures--the Fraser spiral, Kanizsa triangle, Pinna--Brelstaff rings, Ouchi pattern and, for Haiku, the rotating snakes--the models gave the illusion answer to the control images as well, which suggests that they answered from the figure rather than from the effect. A false fact was mostly followed on control images but not on illusion images. The stimuli, prompts, all responses and the code are released for testing further models; the Python code that draws the stimuli is parametric and can generate new illusion images for other studies with models or human observers.

authors.name: Eiji Watanabe

papers.title: Critical slowing down in hive temperature does not provide actionable early warnings of honey bee colony collapse
papers.summary: Early warning signals (EWS) based on critical slowing down (CSD) have been proposed as model-independent indicators of approaching ecological regime shifts and may help anticipate honeybee colony collapse. However, whether theoretically expected signals can be reliably observed and provide useful prediction in real-world systems remains uncertain. Here, we combine structural analysis, mechanistic modeling and longitudinal observations to assess the dynamical plausibility, detectability and predictive accuracy of CSD-based EWS for honeybee colony collapse. Our results show that the presence of EWS is not equivalent to successful prediction of the transition. The analyzed models exhibit regime shifts accompanied by CSD, but detecting these signals in finite and noisy observations requires longer and more densely sampled time series than typically available for practical monitoring. Moreover, in empirical temperature records, CSD-like trends were detectable but provided limited discrimination between colonies that subsequently collapsed and those that survived. Declining mean temperature provided slightly greater discrimination than conventional CSD indicators, although its predictive value remained modest. Non-Gaussian correlated noise and the imperfect correspondence between hive temperature and colony strength further constrained EWS performance. These findings show that EWS can exist at the dynamical level without becoming useful predictors at the observational level, at least for our case study, thus cautioning against treating CSD-based indicators as generic predictors of ecological collapse.

authors.name: Daniele Proverbio, Els Weinans, Davide Frizzera, Desiderato Annoscia, Francesco Nazzi, Giulia Giordano

papers.title: The Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback: A teachable perception-action framework for everyday self-regulation
papers.summary: Everyday stress is largely a learned pattern: a familiar cue, a fast reading of threat, an automatic reaction and a body that stays activated. Body-based practices such as mindfulness, interoceptive training, Somatic Experiencing and yoga target these patterns, but they are usually taught as techniques without a map of the mechanism they act on. Pain neuroscience education suggests that understanding such a mechanism can itself change experience. No comparable model exists for everyday self-regulation. This paper proposes the Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback, developed over six cohorts of a workshop for non-clinical adults. The loop describes any action as four steps: Sense (exteroception, proprioception and interoception), Process (perception as inference, weighted by context and safety), Choose (habitual reaction or goal-directed response after a pause) and Execute (autonomic and somatic output). Feedback from each outcome acts beneath all four steps, through synaptic plasticity, habit formation and allostatic load. The paper integrates the perception-action cycle, information-processing stages of choice, interoceptive inference, the autonomic space model and the defence cascade. It places a set of practices on the loop: full sensory awareness, grounding, orientation, resourcing, the pause, reduced stimulus and choice, slow movement and relaxation, each with a proposed mechanism and an assessment of the evidence. It also describes the model's translation into four practitioner skills. Seven testable propositions are derived for future evaluation. The model is offered as a teachable framework for wellbeing, not a treatment.

authors.name: Sundeep Kapila

papers.title: Self-organized fractional silencing of pyramidal neurons under global depolarization in a spatial neuron-glial microcircuit model
papers.summary: Pathological transitions in nervous tissue, including epileptiform discharges and cortical spreading depolarization, depend on the interplay between cellular and interstitial mechanisms. We develop a biophysically detailed two-dimensional model of the neurogliovascular unit (NGVU) integrating neuronal populations in the Hodgkin-Huxley formalism, astrocyte-regulated extracellular potassium dynamics, extracellular neurotransmitter spillover, and noradrenergic neuromodulation. Numerical simulations show that inhibitory interneurons enter depolarization block (DB) at significantly lower extracellular potassium concentrations and stimulation intensities than pyramidal neurons. Early loss of inhibition shifts the local excitation-inhibition balance and triggers network hyperexcitability. In the spatially extended network, exceeding a critical stimulation threshold induces a transition from heterogeneous but spatially uniform firing to network fragmentation into stable active microclusters with self-sustained high-frequency firing. Pyramidal neurons with lower excitatory synaptic input receive less recurrent excitation, which protects them from DB. By continuously releasing potassium ions and glutamate into the extracellular space, pyramidal neurons drive strong depolarization in more densely connected neighbors and push them into deep DB. Simulations of localized astrocytic dysfunction predict a spatial limit for potassium clearance defects. Small damaged cores are fully compensated by diffusion and uptake by surrounding healthy astrocyte units. However, above a critical damage size, activity-dependent potassium buildup and firing positive feedback disrupt homeostasis in surrounding units, promoting persistent depolarized centers with self-sustained, spatially segregated pathological activity.

authors.name: Stanislav V. Lagosha, Andrey Yu. Verisokin, Darya V. Verveyko, Alyona V. Berezhnaya, Nadezda A. Brazhe, Alexey R. Brazhe

papers.title: Spatial model of neurogliovascular unit: arachidonic acid can control the stability
papers.summary: Arachidonic acid metabolites can have both vasoconstrictor and vasodilator effects, thereby influencing neuronal activity. In this work, to analyze possible patterns of activity of nervous tissue in response to changes in the metabolic profile, a mathematical model of a spatially distributed system of connected neurogliovascular units was developed. We simulate the influence of arachidonic acid metabolites on the dynamics of the neurogliovascular unit during cortical spreading depression in order to determine the ways in which astrocytic activity influences the spatiotemporal characteristics of the propagating cortical depression wave. It is assumed that in the future the results of the theoretical study can be used to find ways to remove nervous tissue from pathological conditions that occur in epilepsy, migraines and a number of neurodegenerative diseases, including those associated with the occurrence of cortical depression waves.

authors.name: Darya V. Verveyko, Andrey Yu. Verisokin, Pavel O. Lukin

papers.title: Mammalian gonadal development: origins, specification and differentiation of ovary and testis cell lineages
papers.summary: Testicular and ovarian development requires the coordinated formation and assembly of multiple cell types that enable these organs to fulfill their roles in sexual differentiation, reproduction, and endocrine function. A defining feature of gonadal development is that both testes and ovaries arise from a common bipotential primordium, the genital ridge, composed of multipotent progenitors. In this Review, we synthesize current knowledge on the origin, specification, differentiation, and function of the major fetal gonadal somatic lineages, drawing primarily on mouse and human studies. We describe how the adrenogonadal primordium (AGP) gives rise to the gonadal primordium (GP), how coelomic epithelium-derived progenitors generate the supporting, steroidogenic/stromal, and supporting-like cell lineages, and how these progenitors become progressively fate-restricted. We highlight recent evidence for early lineage priming within spatially organized domains of the coelomic epithelium. We further examine the molecular pathways and cellular processes governing sex-specific differentiation of these lineages and discuss remaining gaps in our understanding of how bipotential gonads differentiate into testes or ovaries, and their implication for human health.

authors.name: Serge Nef, Maeva Guy, Marie-Christine Chaboissier

papers.title: Saddle Buckling of a Multicellular Alga Driven by Differential Growth
papers.summary: During development of many simple multicellular organisms there is a complex interplay between cell growth and generation of an extracellular matrix that confers structure. We study this problem quantitatively using $Gonium~pectorale$, a 16-cell alga that transforms from a flat to a buckled shape during growth without cell division or rearrangement. Cell-level measurements and 3D reconstructions show that the $12$ peripheral cells grow faster than the central $4$, producing hoop stress that selects the saddle mode, whose amplitude displays a continuous bifurcation with classical square root singularity. These results are consistent with a continuum model of differential growth within F\"oppl--von K\'arm\'an theory, which yields information on the mechanical properties of the ECM. Implications of this transformation in evolutionary transitions to multicellularity are discussed.

authors.name: Zhao Wang, Sumit Kumar Birwa, Jane Y. Y. Chui, Kyriacos Leptos, Raymond E. Goldstein

papers.title: A Categorical Compositional Distributional Modelling for the Language of Life
papers.summary: The Categorical Compositional Distributional (DisCoCat) model is a mathematical framework for computing the meaning of a sentence from the meanings of its words and the grammatical structure that combines them. Because biological sequences can be viewed as a "language of life", it is tempting to ask whether the DisCoCat model can also give insight into biological macromolecules. Here we take a first step in this direction for proteins, whose linguistic features are the most prominent among the macromolecules. We treat a protein as a sentence and its domains as words, take the biological function of a domain or protein as its meaning, and regard the arrangement of domains as the syntax. We give pregroup grammar types to protein domains and to the linker regions between them, show how type reductions are lifted to multilinear maps between vector spaces, and use these maps to compute a vector representation of a protein's function from vector representations of its domains. In particular, linkers act as relational "words" whose order-three tensors combine the two flanking domains into a vector in a single protein meaning space, so that the functions of proteins with different domain architectures can be compared by an inner product. We extend the construction to proteins with any number of domains, illustrate it with a numerical toy example and five Drosophila melanogaster proteins, discuss how the linker tensors could be learned and how the model could be tested, and relate it to protein language models and other developments since 2019.

authors.name: Yanying Wu

papers.title: An Open Petri Net Implementation of Gene Regulatory Networks
papers.summary: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are a central object of systems biology, and many formalisms have been used to model them, among them Petri nets. Ordinary Petri nets, however, provide no built-in way to assemble a large network from smaller, separately specified pieces. Open Petri nets, in the sense of Baez and Master, supply exactly this: an open Petri net is a Petri net with designated boundary places, and open Petri nets are composed by gluing boundaries together (a pushout), giving a symmetric monoidal double category Open(Petri). In this paper we (i) state precisely the standard encoding of activation, inhibition and degradation as Petri net transitions; (ii) distinguish the classical "Petri nets are monoids" view of Meseguer and Montanari, which describes how processes inside one net compose, from the open Petri net view, which describes how nets compose; (iii) show, with a worked example, how a GRN can be cut into open Petri net modules along shared genes and recovered exactly by composition, together with simple rules that make such a decomposition correct; and (iv) use the compositional rate-equation semantics of Baez and Pollard to show that the mass-action dynamics of the composite network are obtained by gluing the dynamics of its modules, linking Petri net models of GRNs to their ordinary differential equation counterparts. We close by discussing what the reachability semantics does and does not give for GRN modules, and the limitations of the approach.

authors.name: Yanying Wu

papers.title: Direction and speed selectivity properties for spatio-temporal receptive fields according to the generalized Gaussian derivative model for visual receptive fields
papers.summary: This paper gives an in-depth theoretical analysis of the direction and speed selectivity properties of idealized models of the spatio-temporal receptive fields of simple cells and complex cells, based on the generalized Gaussian derivative model for visual receptive fields. According to this theory, the receptive fields are modelled as velocity-adapted affine Gaussian derivatives for different image velocities and different degrees of elongation. By probing such idealized receptive field models of visual neurons to moving sine waves with different angular frequencies and image velocities, we characterize the computational models to a structurally similar probing method as is used for characterizing the direction and speed selective properties of biological neurons. By comparison to results of neurophysiological measurements of direction and speed selectivity for biological neurons in the primary visual cortex, we find that our theoretical results are consistent with (i) velocity-tuned visual neurons that are sensitive to particular motion directions and speeds, and (ii) different visual neurons having broader vs. sharper direction and speed selective properties. Our theoretical results in combination with results from neurophysiological characterizations of motion-sensitive visual neurons are also consistent with a previously formulated hypothesis that the simple cells in the primary visual cortex ought to be covariant under local Galilean transformations, so as to enable processing of visual stimuli with different motion directions and speeds.

authors.name: Tony Lindeberg

papers.title: Invasion with size-dependent dispersion range
papers.summary: The coalescing colony model provides a minimal framework for biological invasions with long-range dispersion. In its standard formulation, the dispersion range is assumed independent of the size of the invading population. Here, we relax this assumption and consider size-dependent dispersal: a main colony of linear size $r$ emits secondary colonies at distance $r^\mu$, with $0 \leq \mu \leq 1$. We derive the generalized dynamical equations for this extended model and map out the growth phase diagram for the leading order contribution. Depending on $\mu$, the main colony exhibits distinct regimes: linear expansion, power-law growth, exponential regime and finite-time blow-up. We confront these theoretical predictions with a spatially explicit physical model. While the coalescing colony approach correctly captures the scaling of the perimeter, it fails to predict the scaling of the volume. We trace this discrepancy to an effective breakdown of circular symmetry in the morphology of the main colony. Finally, we quantify temporal evolution of the population fraction residing outside of the main colony. The coalescing colony model predicts its decay to~$0$ like a power-law when~$\mu\mu^*\approx 0.7$. Broadly, our findings highlight how coupling dispersal range to population size fundamentally alters invasion dynamics, with implications for biological invasions, metastatic growth, and urban expansion.

authors.name: Ulysse Marquis

papers.title: Mathematical modeling to study combination strategies for neural stem cell therapy in glioblastoma
papers.summary: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are a promising treatment platform due to their ability to cross the restrictive blood-brain barrier and migrate toward damaged regions of the brain. These properties can be leveraged to target brain tumors, as NSCs can infiltrate tumor lesions and deliver therapeutic agents such as drugs, oncolytic viruses, and genetic materials. Despite the advantages of NSCs, translational challenges remain, including patient-specific chemotactic signaling and immune responses, variability in migration and localization at tumor sites, and optimization of delivery strategies. In this work, we focus on intranasal delivery of NSCs and combination strategies for the treatment of brain cancer. To investigate strategies for improving NSC arrival at the tumor site, we developed a hybrid mathematical model of NSC migration that couples an agent-based model with a partial differential equation, where cell motion is guided by the spatial dynamics of chemoattractants. Using data collected from a murine model and our mathematical model, we {investigate treatment-motivated downstream effects associated with three combination strategies:} (1) IL-10 pretreatment, (2) CXCL12 pretreatment, and (3) radiotherapy. We find that IL-10 pretreatment improves NSC arrival numbers at tumor only under the Gaussian chemoattractant profile, whereas CXCL12 pretreatment moderately improves arrival numbers when the tumor is located in the anterior brain. Radiotherapy significantly enhances the tumor arrival under uniform profiles. These simulation studies suggest that both treatment strategies and chemoattractant distribution influence intranasal NSC delivery, and the proposed model can be used to predict how targeted modulation of chemotactic signaling and tissue-guided migration may improve delivery outcomes.

authors.name: Ashley Harrison, Austin Hansen, Anthony E. Bishay, Greg Grigoryan, Vikram Adhikarla, Russell C. Rockne, Margarita Gutova, Heyrim Cho

papers.title: Biases and Limits of AlphaFold Predictions for Non-Globular Proteins
papers.summary: AlphaFold has transformed protein structure prediction, making structural models accessible across the life sciences. We explore experimentally validated cases of non-globular proteins to uncover where predictions diverge from biologically relevant structural states and how molecular context shapes these discrepancies, guiding a more informed interpretation of AlphaFold models.

authors.name: Maria Cristina Aspromonte (University of Padova, Italy), Alexander M. Monzon (University of Padova, Italy), Miguel A. Andrade-Navarro (Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Germany), Oriol B\'arcenas (Universitat Aut\`onoma de Barcelona and IQAC-CSIC, Spain), Viktor Bartosik (Masaryk University, Czech Republic), Pau Bernad\'o (Centre de Biologie Structurale, Montpellier, France), Juan Cort\'es (LAAS-CNRS, Universit\'e de Toulouse, France), Zsuzsanna Dosztanyi (Universit\'e de Montpellier, France), Gabor Erdos (E\"otv\"os Lor\'and University, Hungary), Isabella C. Felli (University of Florence, Italy), Helena Gradi\v{s}ar (National Institute of Chemistry, Ljubljana, Slovenia), San Had\v{z}i (University of Ljubljana, Slovenia), Tam\'as Heged\H{u}s (Semmelweis University, Hungary), Khalil Joron (Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel), Pavel Kaderavek (Masaryk University, Czech Republic), Eitan Lerner (Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel), Dirk Linke (University of Oslo, Norway), Pablo Mier (Universidad Pablo de Olavide, Spain), Ana Panteli\'c (University of Belgrade and IMGGE, Serbia), Roberta Pierattelli (University of Florence, Italy), Salvador Ventura (Universitat Aut\`onoma de Barcelona and IQAC-CSIC, Spain), Marija Vidovi\'c (University of Belgrade and IMGGE, Serbia), Metaxia Vlassi (National Center for Scientific Research DEMOKRITOS, Greece), Lukas Zidek (Masaryk University, Czech Republic), Silvio C. E. Tosatto (University of Padova, Italy)

papers.title: Persistence of Multifractal Dynamics at the Mammalian Neuromuscular Junction Across Extracellular Calcium Conditions
papers.summary: The neuromuscular junction represents a relevant experimental model for revealing important biophysical mechanisms underlying synaptic transmission. In this work, we revisited the time-series analysis of electrophysiological recordings obtained from mammalian diaphragm neuromuscular junctions. We applied multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MFDFA) to assess whether intervals between spontaneous potentials exhibit multifractal behavior at physiological extracellular calcium concentrations and at hypocalcemic and hypercalcemic levels. Surprisingly, we observed a robust, stable multifractal profile across all electrophysiological recordings, regardless of calcium concentration. Therefore, our results provide support for a rich and complex scenario governing neurotransmitter release. Based on these findings, we discuss their biophysical significance and physiological implications.

authors.name: Adriano J. da Silva, Sergio Floquet, Ricardo F. Lima

papers.title: HP-GSBS: Accelerating greedy state boundary search with reusable interval statistics
papers.summary: Greedy State Boundary Search (GSBS) identifies transitions between relatively stable neural activity patterns in continuous recordings. Repeated template reconstruction and time-pair correlation scans make analyses across brain regions, large cohorts, and parameter sweeps computationally prohibitive. We present HP-GSBS, an open-source implementation built on an exact mathematical reformulation that decomposes the matching objective into additive interval contributions from temporal prefix sums and computes Welch t-distance through constant-time rectangle queries over two-dimensional correlation prefix tables. Combined with streaming candidate search, local-window refinement, and active-block caching, this formulation drives unified CPU, PyTorch CUDA, and Triton backends. Across controlled benchmarks spanning recording lengths, feature dimensions, and search depths, HP-GSBS achieves 154- to 1,730-fold speedups while identically reproducing reference boundary histories and selected state counts (maximum $|\Delta\mathrm{TD}|=1.88\times10^{-11}$). Cross-backend numerical equivalence is further confirmed on four human electroencephalography recordings from the Brain, Body, and Behavior Dataset (120--173 states). Applied to naturalistic movie-viewing functional magnetic resonance imaging from 16 participants (4,230 angular-gyrus voxels), HP-GSBS completes group and individual fits in 213.10 s on a single CPU and reveals intersubject boundary alignment above a circular-shift null (mean pairwise $F_1=0.414$ vs. 0.325, $p=0.001$). HP-GSBS reduces hour-scale benchmark fits to seconds or fractions of a second. Recording-level parallelism and an optional low-memory execution path make cohort-level and multi-timescale analyses tractable on standard laboratory hardware.

authors.name: Yanzhe Zhao, Yongzhang Ji

papers.title: Certification of non-stabilizerness in multi-qubit systems via worst-case random access codes
papers.summary: Recent works have proposed semi-device-independent frameworks to certify non-stabilizerness, but the complexity of the stabilizer polytope makes these methods infeasible beyond a few qubits. In this work, we address this limitation by moving to partially characterized measurements in the context of worst-case random access codes. We first establish a simple condition, which we term the stabilizer pigeonhole criterion, that certifies non-stabilizerness in $m$-qubit pure states, and show how it can be applied to reduced states. As an application, we certify magic in $W$ states of arbitrary size using only eight preparations and three single-qubit measurement settings. Motivated by recent work on the stabilizer marginal problem, we then construct prepare-and-measure correlations generated by global $m$-qubit quantum states for which every $k$-qubit marginal lies inside the stabilizer polytope, yet the combined correlations cannot be reproduced by any global stabilizer mixture. Finally, we derive analytical upper and lower bounds on the worst-case bias attainable with mixed stabilizer preparations in an $m$-qubit random access code with $n$ Pauli measurements. For the complete set of $4^m-1$ non-identity Pauli measurements, we show that the optimal quantum and mixed-stabilizer biases both scale as $2^{-3m/2}$, and that their ratio is asymptotically bounded by a constant ($\lesssim 1.85$), showing that in this setting, magic in the preparations alone yields at most a constant-factor advantage over stabilizer mixtures.

authors.name: Santiago Zamora

papers.title: Improved Digitization Bounds for U(1) Lattice Gauge Theory via Semiclassical Analysis
papers.summary: Simulating lattice gauge theories on a digital quantum computer or using tensor network methods requires a finite-dimensional approximation of the gauge field, a process often called digitization. Controlling the resulting error is essential for assessing the accuracy and resource requirements of these simulations. In this work, we derive a digitization error bound for low-lying eigenstates of the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian for pure U(1) gauge theory and translate it into a bound on time-evolution error. Compared with existing bounds, our result achieves exponentially improved dependence on the inverse lattice spacing $1/a$ and evolution time $T$, together with improved dependence on the inverse coupling $1/g$. The key idea is to identify a small parameter in the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian and apply tools from semiclassical analysis. Specifically, we adapt Agmon's method to establish exponential decay of the error with the truncation threshold. These results sharpen estimates of the local Hilbert space dimension and qubit resources needed to simulate gauge theories near the continuum limit, at weak coupling, and over long times.

authors.name: Di Fang, Yu Tong

papers.title: Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
papers.summary: If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. Numerical examples confirm that the results for quasi-continuous spectra remain clearly recognizable in finite systems, with only small finite-size effects.

authors.name: Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin

papers.title: Efficient Tensor Decomposition of the Coulomb and Coulomb-like Potentials and Its Application to Probing Molecular Geometries Using a Quantum Computer
