We show that it is always optimal to increase the number of modes under fixed power constraint. We derive an analytical formula for the ensemble-averaged Holevo capacity in the case of random passive transformations. The analogous results are also obtained for capacities achievable under homodyne and heterodyne detection. We further discuss the generalization of the model to include weak active transformations.

authors.name: Maria Pop{\l}awska, Marcin Jarzyna

papers.title: Spin-Momentum Impedance and Filtering at a Spin-Coupled Absorbing Boundary
papers.summary: In a separable harmonic waveguide, transverse confinement leaves the longitudinal bulk Hamiltonian unchanged. Earlier simulations nevertheless found that stronger confinement suppresses prompt detection of a spin-1/2 particle at a spin-coupled absorbing boundary. Here we identify the local boundary response underlying this effect. We treat the boundary as an effective detector, identifying the squared-norm loss rate with the detection-time probability density. The incident transverse ground state has a distribution of momenta parallel to the detecting plane, with characteristic scale proportional to $\sqrt{\omega}$, where $\omega$ is the confinement frequency. For each parallel momentum, we resolve the boundary relation into two spin channels. At fixed normal wave number and detector parameter, local matching gives these channels equal absorption probabilities but generally different reflection phases. Their common absorption probability decreases with the magnitude of the parallel momentum. Simulations over several observation windows distinguish reduced detection probability from changes in recorded-click timing. The mean detection time capped at horizon $T$ is summarized by the empirical fit $A_T+B_T\sqrt{\omega}$ over the sampled range, with setup- and horizon-dependent coefficients. The local response makes detection sensitive to transverse confinement; propagation, interference, and repeated encounters of the undetected wave shape the detection-time distribution.

authors.name: Alireza Jozani

papers.title: Quantum Convolutional Autoencoders for Reconstruction-Based Anomaly Detection
papers.summary: Quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) are increasingly used in quantum machine learning (QML) due to their efficient parameterization and hierarchical representation of quantum information. Anomaly detection has important applications across many domains, including scientific data analysis. In this work, we adapt a QCNN architecture into a quantum autoencoder (QAE) framework for semi-supervised, reconstruction-based anomaly detection. The models are trained on normal samples to reconstruct feature-extracted and dimensionally reduced time-series data, with reconstruction error used as an anomaly score. We investigate two quantum convolutional autoencoder architectures that differ in their treatment of latent information: a hierarchical architecture in which information remains distributed across the circuit and a bottleneck-based architecture in which information is explicitly compressed and reconstructed using additional decoder qubits. The latent-space size is varied to study its influence on reconstruction and anomaly-detection performance. The approaches are benchmarked against a variational quantum circuit and classical baselines using the Kepler exoplanet dataset and pulsar candidates from the High Time Resolution Universe Survey (HTRU-2). The models are evaluated over ten deterministic optimization seeds at matched four- and eight-component input dimensions and matched latent-space sizes where feasible. Across all available compressed matched configurations, the bottleneck QAE achieves higher ROC AUC than the hierarchical QAE, with all differences remaining significant after Holm correction. The preferred compressed latent-space size depends on the dataset and architecture. The strongest classical autoencoder performs better than both quantum autoencoder families on HTRU-2, while the supervised neural network achieves the strongest overall discrimination on both datasets.

authors.name: Donovan Slabbert, Francesco Petruccione

papers.title: Nonlinear Optics Mediated by Chiral Waveguide QED: Generation of Momentum-anticorrelated Photon Pairs
papers.summary: In recent years, chiral quantum optics has emerged as an active research area due to the promising applications in quantum information processing as well as nonlinear optics. In this work, we present results on the properties of the incoherent component of the transmitted light after transmons chirally coupled to a waveguide. The well-known resonance fluorescence of one chiral transmon resembles nonlinear quantum optics as it can convert the coherent light, with photons having spatially extensive coherence and Poisson distribution, into a field with spatially localized coherence and bunching photon statistics. However, another chiral transmon can undo the effect of the first transmon regardless of the Rabi frequency under the idealization involved in this work. A full wavefunction calculation shows that, in the weak driving limit, this incoherent light mainly comes from two-photon processes - one chiral transmon converts two independent photons into a momentum-correlated photon pair. In addition to the driving through the waveguide, we study the role of a local drive with independently tunable amplitude and phase that can address each transmon individually. The interplay between the waveguide and local driving modulates the contribution of the incoherent transmission and hence enables the engineering of the quantum statistics of the transmitted field, with tunable $g^{(2)}(0)$ spanning anti-bunched, coherent, and strongly-bunched regimes.

authors.name: Wenqi Tong, Spencer J Walsh, H. Alaeian, F. Robicheaux

papers.title: Thermal Quantum Correlations in Coupled Andreev Spin Qubits with Tunable Superconducting Phase and Spin Orbit Interaction
papers.summary: We investigate thermal quantum correlations in two coupled superconducting spin qubits described by an effective Andreev spin-qubit Hamiltonian with spin-orbit interaction. Using Local Quantum Fisher Information (LQFI) and Local Quantum Uncertainty (LQU), we examine the effects of superconducting phase difference, tunneling amplitude, spin-orbit coupling, and temperature. Our results show that quantum correlations decrease with increasing temperature but are enhanced by stronger tunneling and spin-orbit interaction. The superconducting phase induces periodic variations in the correlations through its modulation of the effective exchange couplings. We further demonstrate that larger energy gaps between the ground and first excited states suppress thermal excitations and enhance the stability of quantum correlations. A comparison with negativity reveals the distinct behaviors of these correlation measures, while LQFI is consistently greater than or equal to LQU in the investigated parameter regime. These findings clarify the mechanisms governing thermal quantum correlations and highlight the roles of phase engineering, spin-orbit interaction, and tunneling in protecting quantum resources in superconducting hybrid systems.

authors.name: Mohammad Reza Pourkarimi, Mina Shiri, Mehdi Monemi, Vadim Ohanyan

papers.title: Entanglement and non-local magic in a non-unitarily deformed non-Hermitian bipartite system
papers.summary: Non-Hermitian degeneracies are usually discussed through spectral coalescence, whereas entanglement is a property of eigenvectors and need not be fixed by the eigenvalues alone. We formulate a compact bipartite model that separates these two notions. A Hermitian operator with a degenerate eigenspace is transformed by an invertible non-unitary similarity map. The resulting Hamiltonian is non-Hermitian and retains a non-defective degeneracy at every finite value of the non-Hermiticity parameter. For an exactly solvable two-qubit realization, the right eigenstates evolve continuously from product states to maximally entangled states although the spectrum is unchanged. We distinguish the positive right-state reduced density matrix from the generally non-positive biorthogonal reduction, for which entropy may become complex. The same two-qubit solution gives a closed partial-transpose negativity and a Schmidt-gauged non-local magic. Entanglement grows monotonically with the non-Hermiticity parameter, whereas the non-local magic vanishes for both the product and maximally entangled limits and is largest at an intermediate coupling. In larger bipartite spaces, the Page entropy and Haar-averaged purity provide reference values for eigenstate typicality. These diagnostics separate non-defective degeneracy, exceptional-point sensitivity, Haar-typical entanglement, and non-stabilizer correlations without relying on a proliferation of basis-dependent spectral quantities.

authors.name: Chen-Huan Wu

papers.title: Geometric signatures of the onset of many-body ergodicity
papers.summary: Identifying universal, robust, and interpretable signatures of the onset of many-body quantum ergodicity remains a major challenge. The adiabatic gauge potential has been noted to act as a sensitive probe of quantum chaos. Here, we generalize the features of the adiabatic gauge potential to multi-parameter perturbations, yielding an emergent quantum geometry. This new geometry --- whose metric we dub the Hilbert-Killing metric --- provides a tool for probing the onset of ergodicity. The Hilbert-Killing metric exhibits a quantifiable fastest growth in the boundary regime, which we corroborate by exact diagonalization of the mixed-field Ising chain and the disordered PXP chain.

authors.name: Chris Ventura-Meinersen, Edmondo Valvo, Stefano Bosco, Francisco Machado, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ

papers.title: A State-of-the-art Squeezed-Light Source for Hybrid Quantum Photonics: Current Performance and Remaining Challenges
papers.summary: Hybrid quantum photonics seeks to combine the complementary advantages of continuous- and discrete-variable quantum optics. This typically entails photon-counting measurements on entangled states generated by interfering many single-mode squeezed-vacuum (SMSV) states. However, because conventional photon-counting schemes are mode-insensitive, it is critical that the SMSV states occupy a single, well-defined mode. Achieving this requires careful engineering of the process, which determines both the spatial and spectro-temporal properties of the generated state. In addition, the ideal source must be massively scalable, capable of efficiently generating strong squeezing, and remain compatible with existing detection schemes and fiber networks. Although many platforms address one or more of these requirements, satisfying all of them simultaneously remains challenging. Here, we present a source that simultaneously addresses all of these requirements: a single-pass, periodically poled, Type-II potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP) waveguide optimized for scalable hybrid quantum-photonic architectures. The SMSV state produced by the source has a measured effective mode number of 1.24. Furthermore, the source is extremely bright (producing up to 40 000 photons per pulse) and operates at a central wavelength of 1546nm, optimized for fiber-network compatibility and which, in combination with picosecond duration, also enables intrinsic photon-number resolution in superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Although this source constitutes an ideal source in a simplified picture, the ultimate limitations of any source will be governed by complex dynamics that arise when the system is driven at high-gain or due to unavoidable loss during state generation. We have therefore developed a complete theoretical framework that enables a comprehensive photon-counting-based characterization...

authors.name: Kai-Hong Luo, Denis Kopylov, Florian L\"utkewitte, Jan-Lucas Eickmann, Simone Atzeni, Fabian Schlue, Benjamin Brecht, Torsten Meier, Polina Sharapova, Michael Stefszky, Christine Silberhorn

papers.title: Auditing Encoder Reseeding for Quantum Error Correction under a Bounded Cloud Fault Model
papers.summary: Quantum error correction (QEC) is essential for large-scale quantum computation due to the inherent noise in physical qubits, which renders them unsuitable for algorithm execution. This issue poses a security risk for shared cloud processors, where faults may be introduced by adversaries rather than random noise. Given that the same code is used for every execution, an adversary who identifies an undetected fault can exploit it in all subsequent executions. This study evaluates whether per-run reseeding, which involves encoding each execution with a new random circuit derived from the seed, can prevent such replay attacks. We examine two types of cloud adversaries: the provider, who compiles the circuit and thus knows the seed, and a co-tenant, who shares the processor but selects faults without seed knowledge. To address this, we define accepted corruption as the logical alteration caused by a fault in executions that the verifier accepts. We also derive the expected accepted corruption over Haar-random encoders in closed form; this expectation is exact for uniform Clifford encoders, thereby quantifying the threat posed by any fault chosen without seed knowledge. Our findings indicate that seed-blind reseeding reduces the proportion of executions corrupted by a replayed fault under both adversaries to a rate that decreases exponentially.

authors.name: Ziqing Guo, Anthony Lawrence, Renyu Wang, Randy Kuang, Ziwen Pan

papers.title: Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios with Agent-like Observers on Quantum Computers
papers.summary: The Wigner's friend thought experiment raises the question of whether quantum theory can be applied consistently to systems that include observers. Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios include spatially separate observers sharing entanglement. In the Local Friendliness (LF) framework, these scenarios lead to experimentally testable inequalities derived from Absoluteness of Observed Events and Local Agency, assumptions weaker than those needed for Bell inequalities. Their violation therefore has stronger implications, but LF tests are more experimentally challenging because they require an observer implemented as a quantum system. Drawing from the literature on artificial intelligence, we implement the "friend" with explicit agent-like functionality in a reversible quantum circuit. The agents store measurement outcomes, condition subsequent operations on stored information, and, in the most structured case, use Born-rule probabilities to bet on outcomes of their own future observations based on past observations. We study the circuits through ideal simulations, simulations using an IBM-device noise model, and experiments on the IBM processor ibm_marrakesh. Ideal simulations reproduce the maximal quantum violation of an LF inequality up to finite-shot fluctuations, while hardware runs show positive LF violations for all agents. These results are a step towards more sophisticated agent-like observer models in LF experiments on quantum computers. By focusing on functionality rather than size alone, this approach complements tests of quantum theory in the macroscopic regime and opens a direction for studying agents whose use of quantum theory is implemented within coherently controlled quantum dynamics.

authors.name: Joshua Laux, Eric G. Cavalcanti

papers.title: The effects of shot noise on the quantum computation of NMR spectra
papers.summary: Recent advances in the field of quantum computing hardware motivate the search for applications which demonstrate so-called quantum advantage. One promising use case that has been identified is the simulation of quantum many-body systems. The computational resources required for performing such a simulation on a classical computer generally grow exponentially with the size of the system being modeled, which is ultimately due to the exponential growth of the Hilbert space in which the dynamics of such a system take place. While digital quantum computers natively evolve quantum states directly in such a Hilbert space, thus naively avoiding this problem, the result of such a computation is typically not obtained as a deterministic output. Rather, it requires projective measurements which are fundamentally affected by shot noise. Any desired expectation values must therefore be reconstructed from repeated measurements, making the number of those measurements a relevant computational resource, and thus an important consideration for any potential claims of quantum advantage. In this work, we study how this resource scales with system size (a scaling which itself depends on the desired accuracy of the final result), using the simulation of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra as a test case. We study this scaling for both real-world molecules, as well as a class of model NMR Hamiltonians which allow for efficient large-scale simulations with one-dimensional, two-dimensional, and all-to-all interactions. We find that the required resources increase only weakly with molecular size, far below the exponential growth of the underlying Hilbert space. This result suggests that shot noise should not pose a fundamental barrier to achieving quantum advantage in the simulation of NMR systems, and perhaps for many-body systems more broadly.

authors.name: Sebastian Walch, Keith R. Fratus, Jan-Michael Reiner, Igor Lesanovsky

papers.title: Quantum Encoding Agents: A Natural Language Interface for Data Embedding Strategy Selection in Quantum Machine Learning
papers.summary: Selecting a data encoding is a central and poorly tooled decision in quantum machine learning. The feature map fixes the geometry of the Hilbert space, the expressibility of quantum kernels, and whether the circuit can run on near-term hardware. This paper presents Quantum Encoding Agents, an open-source system that turns encoding selection into a natural-language interaction. Given a dataset and an optional task description, it profiles the data, applies a hardware-aware policy using the gate-error threshold p* approximately 10^{-3}, returns a copyable Qiskit circuit with a justification in Portuguese or English, and scores the quantum kernel by Kernel-Target Alignment (KTA). When a numerical matrix is available, it estimates the correlation fractal dimension D_2 and selects original columns with FD-ASE, using q* = max(2, ceil(D_2)) as a qubit budget so that angle and IQP maps are not proposed at a width where the fidelity kernel has collapsed. The service implements seven encoding families: amplitude, angle, dense angle, IQP, basis, data re-uploading, and custom feature map. On benchmark datasets, KTA separates these encodings under realistic NISQ constraints.

authors.name: Ana Paula Appel

papers.title: Materialised symmetries of 2D translationally invariant codes
papers.summary: There has been significant recent interest in near-term qLDPC codes as high-performance alternatives to surface and color codes. One such class of codes is 2-dimensional translationally invariant (TI) codes, such as bivariate bicycle codes, which share similar properties to topological codes. Fundamental objects in the study of such codes are the materialised symmetries, which can be used for the construction of matching-based decoders. These decoders generalise the minimum-weight perfect matching decoder for toric codes and provide similar asymptotic performance guarantees that heuristic decoders such as BP and its variants lack. Despite this, the mathematical structure of symmetries along with their properties under translation and restriction to finite-sized lattices has not been well-studied. We describe a decomposition of symmetry spaces of 2D CSS TI codes on infinite lattices into translation-invariant subspaces which allow us to write an explicit basis of symmetries in a plane-wave-like form. We then describe how to adapt this infinite lattice basis so that any corresponding rectangular periodic lattice basis can be obtained by restriction to basis elements compatible with the periodic boundaries. This allows us to describe how the symmetry space varies with different rectangular dimensions. We illustrate via examples that it is often straightforward in practice to determine a basis of symmetries on twisted boundaries as well, without needing to recompute the decomposition. We comment on the applications of this framework to matching-based decoders and provide examples of symmetries of such codes as the gross code.

authors.name: Andrew Li, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, Campbell K. McLauchlan

papers.title: Semiclassical dynamics of higher-order squeezing: self-adjoint extensions and coherent returns
papers.summary: Higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians have several self-adjoint realizations, while their classical trajectories reach infinity in finite time. We relate these extension problems through boundary amplitudes and the semiclassical propagation of coherent states. A discrete Fourier transformation gives the sink-to-source ray matrix of each quantum realization. After the first passage through infinity, the full Husimi probability measure converges to point masses on outgoing classical branches, with weights equal to the squared moduli of the matrix entries. The proof combines finite-order approximate tail solutions satisfying the exact extension boundary condition with full-norm Gaussian matching and a square-summable residual estimate. For positive energy, we determine the limit after any fixed number of passages: amplitudes evolve by powers of the unitary ray matrix, not by iterations of its squared-modulus matrix. We also realize these limits by concentrated complex amplitudes for an energy-preserving Liouville extension, distinguishing deterministic classical gluings from coherent boundary mixing.

authors.name: A. E. Teretenkov

papers.title: A Unified Protocol for Arbitrary Z Rotations of a Class of Bosonic cQED Qubits
papers.summary: Bosonic-qubit encodings provide diverse approaches to storing and processing quantum information, with logical operations often implemented through encoding-specific physical strategies. Here, we identify a class of bosonic Fock-based qubits in circuit QED for which distinct implementations of arbitrary $Z(\theta)$ rotations share a common structure. The applicability of the proposed framework is determined by specific conditions involving the greatest common divisor of the photon numbers and a parity criterion for the logical codewords. These conditions provide a systematic means of identifying bosonic Fock-based cQED qubits that admit the common implementation.

authors.name: Vahid Shaghaghi

papers.title: Time-Switching Energy-Harvesting Quantum Relay-Assisted FSO Communication with Displaced Squeezed Signaling
papers.summary: This paper investigates a quantum relay-assisted free-space optical (FSO) communication system in which a decode-and-forward relay is powered by time-switching optical energy harvesting and forwards the decoded information using displaced squeezed signaling (DSS). To obtain a physically con sistent description of turbulence-induced loss for non-classical signaling, each hop is modeled as a pure-loss bosonic chan nel whose random transmissivity follows a truncated Gamma Gamma law, i.e., the Gamma-Gamma irradiance conditioned on the physically admissible range of a transmittance. Under this channel, coherent states remain pure, whereas squeezed states are mapped to mixed Gaussian states. Under Helstrom-optimal detection, the average error of the coherent hop is derived in exact Laplace-series form. For the DSS hop, we derive the output states, a closed-form Gaussian fidelity with rigorous two sided bounds on the Helstrom error, and prove the existence of a loss-aware optimal photon partition. Furthermore, we prove that optimized squeezing preserves both the turbulence-induced diversity order and the leading asymptotic constant of coherent relaying, so that its benefit is a finite-photon-budget effect, and that an interior throughput-optimal harvesting fraction exists. A covariance-preserving benchmark with an exact series representation yields an analytical upper bound on the achievable throughput whose absolute gap vanishes as the relay photon budget grows. Numerical results based on the exact mixed-state Helstrom error quantify the benefit of squeezing and the regime in which it is useful.

authors.name: Nizar Khalfet, Francisco A. Monteiro, Ioannis Krikidis

papers.title: Entangled Measurement Outcomes for Optimal Postselection in Quantum Batteries
papers.summary: We determine when an entangled measurement outcome is necessary to maximize the ergotropy of a postselected quantum battery. For a pure battery-auxiliary state mixed with global white noise of strength $0<p<1$, the maximum conditional ergotropy is $1-p$ times the largest generalized eigenvalue of a matrix pair determined by the state and the battery Hamiltonian. A product outcome attains this maximum if and only if the corresponding generalized eigenspace contains a product vector. For two auxiliary qubits, the product optimum is strictly smaller precisely when this eigenspace is one-dimensional and spanned by an entangled vector. For the noisy four-qubit W state, the optimal outcome changes from a Bell vector to a product vector at $J=\epsilon_A+\epsilon_B$. At this coupling, the maximizing generalized eigenspace is two-dimensional and contains both types of outcomes. The probability-weighted averages of capacity and ergotropy are independent of the complete rank-one projective measurement basis for this noise model, although the optimal selected outcome can change.

authors.name: Yali Du, Zhipei Zhou, Xiaoli Hu

papers.title: Engineered Learning Problems on Noisy Quantum Processors
papers.summary: Despite quantum machine learning being an active topic of research, demonstrations of algorithms run on quantum hardware beating classical methods remain rare. In this work, we demonstrate a significant performance gap using a projected quantum kernel for $n=15,30$ and $45$ qubits over classical methods on an engineered classification problem, and show reproducibility of the results over different quantum processor units. We also demonstrate how error mitigation can widen this gap, both by improving hardware performance but also by increasing the classical difficulty, with different techniques contributing unequally to these phenomena. This work provides strong evidence that superior empirical performance of quantum hardware over all classical techniques is an achievable goal in quantum machine learning, albeit for an artificial problem. However, as with any application relying on observables, beating state-of-the-art simulation methods remains the primary challenge, as our matrix product state results here show.

authors.name: Esteban Payares, Nadia Milazzo, Ghada Ben Slama, Thomas Cope

papers.title: How Many Shots Does a Quantum Reservoir Need? Measurement Cost and Its Scaling in Buffered Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.summary: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) inherits from classical reservoir computing the property that only a linear readout is trained, but unlike a classical reservoir its state is never directly observable: every feature is an expectation value estimated from a finite number of measurement shots. The shot budget is therefore a first-class hyperparameter with no classical analogue. Its effect on QRC has recently begun to be studied; what remains unsettled is how a required budget should be defined, and whether competing definitions agree. This paper argues that they do not, and that the disagreement is systematic rather than incidental. This paper distinguishes a \emph{precision budget} $N_\varepsilon$, the shots needed to estimate the reservoir features to a fixed relative accuracy, from a \emph{convergence budget} $N_\star$, the shots needed for the trained readout to approach its own noise-free ceiling. Proposition~\ref{prop:confound} shows that $N_\star$ depends on the noise-free error floor by construction, so that a configuration with a worse floor appears cheaper, and that configurations should therefore be compared at a fixed measurement budget rather than by the budget each needs to reach its own ceiling.

authors.name: Raman Khurana

papers.title: Non-Hermitian edge accretion
papers.summary: Under the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE), it is generally taken for granted that the open boundary condition (OBC) spectrum is encircled by the periodic boundary condition (PBC) spectrum. Intuitively, this is because boundaries tend to block the directed NHSE amplification, thereby suppressing $\operatorname{Im}(E)$. In this work, we analytically and numerically demonstrate how this conventional scenario can be dramatically violated: In a phenomenon which we term non-Hermitian edge accretion (NHEA), strongly coupled competing NHSE channels conspire to amplify a state whenever it bounces off an edge, instead of attenuating it. This unexpected behavior arises from underappreciated consequences of non-Bloch eigenspinor orthogonality, which control the reflection coefficients as well as the balance between propagating and evanescent waves. Operating in the strongly coupled regime, NHEA is fundamentally distinct from conventional critical NHSE scaling, which is characterized by amplification feedback generated in the bulk, not the edges. Requiring only strongly coupled antagonistic NHSE chains with suitable mode orthogonality, the NHEA is platform-agnostic, and can be identified through periodically growing edge bounces in generic non-Hermitian metamaterials and quantum simulators.

authors.name: Wei Li, Ching Hua Lee, Fuxiang Li

papers.title: The Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture fails over the reals
papers.summary: In 1986 Bapat and Sunder asked whether $\operatorname{per}(A)$ is the largest eigenvalue of $F_A=[a_{i,j}\operatorname{per}(A(i,j))]$ for every positive semidefinite Hermitian $A$, where $A(i,j)$ deletes row $i$ and column $j$. Drury disproved this over the complex field in 2018 and conjectured that the property holds for real positive semidefinite matrices. We disprove Drury's conjecture with a rank-$4$, $32\times32$ integer Gram matrix and an integer vector whose Rayleigh quotient exceeds $\operatorname{per}(A)$; verification uses integer arithmetic. Together, the two counterexamples resolve the Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture negatively over both fields. Counterexamples exist of every order $n\ge32$. As an application to quantum optics, the violation yields a $36$-mode orthogonal interferometer and a direction of relative arrival-time delays among $32$ photons with identical-variance Gaussian wave packets along which every sufficiently small nonzero delay increases the probability that all photons are detected within four designated output modes.

authors.name: Logan R. Chalmers

papers.title: Lowering the temperature of two-dimensional fermionic tensor networks with cluster expansions
papers.summary: Representing the time-evolution operator as a tensor network constitutes a key ingredient in several algorithms for studying quantum lattice systems at finite temperature or in a non-equilibrium setting. For a Hamiltonian composed of strictly short-ranged interactions, the Suzuki-Trotter decomposition is the main technique for obtaining such a representation. In [B.~Vanhecke, L.~Vanderstraeten and F.~Verstraete, Physical Review A, L020402 (2021)], an alternative strategy, the cluster expansion, was introduced. This approach naturally preserves internal and lattice symmetries and can more easily be extended to higher-order representations or longer-ranged interactions. We extend the cluster expansion to two-dimensional fermionic systems, and employ it to construct projected entangled-pair operator (PEPO) approximations of Gibbs states. We also discuss and benchmark different truncation schemes for multiplying layers of PEPOs together. Applying the resulting framework to a two-dimensional spinless fermion model with attractive interactions, we resolve a clear phase boundary at finite temperature.

authors.name: Sander De Meyer, Atsushi Ueda, Yuchi He, Nick Bultinck, Jutho Haegeman

papers.title: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
papers.summary: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\to\tau$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(\tau/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.

authors.name: Joon Hyung Lee

papers.title: Anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior driven by dichotomous Markov noise in a quantum Ising chain: Generalized stochastic resonance in the defect density
papers.summary: The anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior may arise under noise, adding a noise-induced contribution to the defect density beyond the conventional Kibble-Zurek term. Most investigations of such behavior have so far been restricted to Gaussian noise. For Gaussian colored noise (GCN), the power spectrum dictates a monotonic variation of this term with the correlation time. Here, we focus on dichotomous Markov noise (DMN), a prototypical non-Gaussian colored noise, in the quantum Ising chain. We show that the noise-induced defect density, taken as the response function, exhibits generalized stochastic resonance: it is nonmonotonic in the correlation time, growing in the fast-noise regime and decreasing in the slow-noise regime. This resonance stems from the anomalous AKZ behavior in the slow-noise regime, where the DMN-induced trend is nonmonotonic, in contrast to the monotonic GCN case. The underlying mechanism lies in the sparse realizations of DMN in the slow-noise regime, a feature not captured by the power spectrum. Our work thereby reveals a fundamental distinction between Gaussian and non-Gaussian noises in the nonequilibrium critical quench dynamics of the quantum Ising chain.

authors.name: Mingwei Yang, Peng Li

papers.title: Topologically Obstructed Kondo Hybridization: A Route to Kondo Semimetals
papers.summary: The interplay of strong correlations, topology, and symmetry can reshape the low-energy electronic structure of quantum materials and drive the emergence of novel quantum phases. In heavy-fermion systems, the Kondo effect entangles localized $f$ moments with conduction electrons, giving rise to coherent heavy-electron bands at low temperatures, typically characterized by a Kondo hybridization gap. Here we show, however, that the topology and symmetry of the conduction-electron Fermi surface can obstruct the opening of the Kondo hybridization gap at certain momenta. Treating the Fermi surface of a three-dimensional system as an effective two-dimensional manifold, we demonstrate that nontrivial topological invariants defined on this manifold impose a topological obstruction to opening a full hybridization gap, forcing the $fc$ hybridization to vanish at certain momenta on the Fermi surface. These hybridization zeros lead to crossings between $c$ and $f$ bands, giving rise to nodal points or lines near the Fermi energy within the Kondo phase. Our results establish topological obstructions to Kondo hybridization as a route to Kondo semimetals, revealing a fundamental connection between Fermi-surface topology and the emergence of correlated electronic phases.

authors.name: Yue Liu, Junze Deng, Haoyu Hu

papers.title: Off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing in one dimension from critical density fluctuations
papers.summary: A central theme in the theory of unconventional superconductivity is that Cooper pairing can be mediated by bosonic collective modes other than lattice vibrations. However, collective fluctuations in reduced dimensions can also have a destabilizing effect on superconductivity, by suppressing long-range order or by destroying Fermi-liquid quasiparticles in the normal state. In this work, we study a one-dimensional (1D) model of spinless fermions with local interactions that exhibits a continuous quantum phase transition from a Luttinger liquid to a phase-separated state. Combining field-theoretic arguments with numerical exact diagonalization and matrix-product-state methods, we find that the quantum critical point exhibits two-particle off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing. Our work shows that critical density fluctuations at a phase-separation instability can act as pairing glue for unconventional superconductivity in 1D, overcoming the disordering effect of phase fluctuations and the absence of long-lived fermionic quasiparticles in the normal state.

authors.name: Matthew D. Thomson, Simon M. Martin, Frank Marsiglio, Joseph Maciejko

papers.title: When the magnetic force theorem fails: dressed exchange in the induced-moment magnets FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd
papers.summary: Effective spin Hamiltonians for itinerant magnets are commonly parameterized by magnetic-force-theorem (MFT) exchange constants, which are subsequently used to compute the behavior of complex and delicate spin textures, for example skyrmions. We show that for systems containing atoms with large spin susceptibility, such as Pd or Pt, this approach misses important parts of the energetics. For FePt, it even predicts the wrong ground state. Benchmarking against fully self-consistent spin-spiral density-functional calculations - in which the electronic structure, including the induced Pd/Pt moments, relaxes for every spin configuration - we quantify the missing energetics for the ordered L1$_0$ alloys FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd. By comparing a family of models that differ only in their treatment of the induced Pt moment, including the configuration-dependent models of Mryasov and Polesya, we identify the origin: the energetics of the induced moments are governed by the exchange-enhanced (dressed) susceptibility, of which the frozen-potential MFT captures only the bare part - about one third of the Pt-mediated interaction in FePt. We derive a general bound showing that no on-site (intra-atomic) refinement can supply the missing strength. The dressing decides the magnetic ground state in FePt, where the interlayer ordering rests entirely on the Pt-mediated interactions, and shifts the Curie temperatures of the other alloys by several hundred kelvin. Computed ordering temperatures, magnon spectra and spin wave stiffness for all four compounds are provided.

authors.name: Vladislav Borisov, Maryna Pankratova, Rohit Pathak, Pamela Costa Carvalho, Erna K. Delczeg-Czirjak, Sagar Sarkar, Anders Bergman, Qichen Xu, Nezhat Pournaghavi, Manuel Pereiro, Hermann D\"urr, Mikhail I. Katsnelson, Olle Eriksson, Anna Delin

papers.title: Large deviations, effective dynamics, and dynamical phase transitions in random maps
papers.summary: Large deviation theory provides a natural framework to characterize rare fluctuations of time-averaged observables in deterministic and stochastic systems. Building on previous results for deterministic chaotic maps, here we extend the Doob transform to random maps, constructing an effective dynamics in which rare events become typical. This makes it possible to directly reproduce the dynamics of rare trajectories that are exponentially difficult to sample under the original dynamics. We further apply spectral large-deviation methods to characterize dynamical phase transitions in random maps. The spectral structure of the tilted operator provides insight into the mechanisms underlying these transitions and, in particular, allows us to identify the appropriate initial states that select one dynamical phase or another. Our results extend the connection between large deviation theory, spectral methods, and effective dynamics to random chaotic maps, providing a general framework to study rare events and dynamical phase transitions in these systems.

authors.name: \'Angela Tajuelo-Valbuena, Jorge Hidalgo, Ricardo Guti\'errez, Carlos P\'erez-Espigares

papers.title: Impact of spin fluctuations on spectral functions and transport in a model altermagnet
papers.summary: Understanding spin dependent transport in altermagnets is important for incorporating them in next generation spintronic technologies. Motivated by the discovery of altermagnetism in strongly correlated quantum materials, we explore this physics in the checkerboard lattice Hubbard model using a fermion Monte Carlo approach which tracks the full spatial dependence of spin fluctuations as a function of temperature. We present results for the evolution of the spin-dependent single particle spectral functions and transport as we go from the ordered ground state into the high temperature disordered paramagnetic phase. Our results could be tested in future spin-selective angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin transport experiments in candidate altermagnets realized in solid state quantum materials or in proposed ultracold atomic systems.

authors.name: Sourav Chakraborty, Manoranjan Kumar, Arun Paramekanti

papers.title: Atomic layer etching of niobium via alternating O$_2$ and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures
papers.summary: Niobium thin films are a key component of superconducting detectors and electronics, and film surface quality, surface roughness, and geometrical dimensional accuracy affect many performance metrics. Atomic layer etching (ALE) is of interest for modifying film surfaces owing to its Angstrom-scale etching precision and surface smoothing characteristics. Here, we report a plasma-enhanced ALE process for Nb based on sequential O$_2$ plasma and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures. The process achieves an etch per cycle of 5-7 Angstrom/cycle and exhibits surface smoothing. The superconducting transition temperature of the ALE-treated films is maintained up to the expected decrease associated with reduced film thickness. Our ALE process could find applications in superconducting electronics for which surface quality and precise thickness control are of high importance.

authors.name: Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, Azmain A. Hossain, Yifei Yan, Austin J. Minnich

papers.title: Emergent Long-Range Entanglement in the XXZ Quantum Spin Chain with Competing Orders
papers.summary: Competition between short-range and long-range interactions is a largely unexplored route to one-dimensional quantum matter. We introduce a spin-1/2 XXZ chain with ferromagnetic nearest-neighbour and antiferromagnetic power-law couplings. Using DMRG and spin-wave theory, we show this competition stabilises a gapless phase with central charge $c=0.997(17)$, a twofold-degenerate ground state and entanglement spectrum, absent in nearest-neighbour models, and is long-range entangled as diagnosed by finite quantum conditional mutual information. The model also generates a unique gapped quantum phase and gapless antiphase with non-decaying correlations.

authors.name: Anthony Balchin, Eytan Grosfeld, Eran Ginossar

papers.title: Fully Automated Discovery of Phase Diagrams Using Agentic Large Language Models
papers.summary: Classifying phases of matter and mapping out phase diagrams are central problems in physics. Recently, machine learning techniques have emerged as promising tools for phase classification, ranging from supervised learning to various unsupervised methods. However, these techniques provide limited qualitative insight into the discovered phases, typically work only for specific system classes, and do not by themselves efficiently map out the phase diagram. Autonomously constructing the phase diagram of a general system purely from measurements, without prior knowledge of the system, while also yielding qualitative understanding of the phases, remains an open task. In this work, we introduce Phasonaut, a two-agent framework that leverages the tool-use capabilities and broad knowledge of large language models (LLMs) to drive an active learning loop that constructs phase diagrams of physical systems and provides interpretations of the discovered phases. Starting from scratch, it iteratively selects and performs measurements, analyzes the resulting data, and segments the parameter domain into the phases it discovers. Phasonaut recovers the phase diagrams of classical and quantum spin systems to substantial precision. In the future, this framework could enable rapid exploration of systems with unknown phase diagrams, including in autonomously driven experiments.

authors.name: Robert Amelung, Maximilian N\"agele, Florian Marquardt

papers.title: Geometric properties of Wilsonian flows of periodic potentials in two dimensions
papers.summary: Periodic interactions can possess multiple competing minima and barriers, whose evolution under coarse-graining offers a geometric perspective complementary to the scaling of Fourier harmonics. We study this evolution in two dimensions by deriving a functional Wilsonian renormalization-group flow for a general smooth periodic potential and its running sine-Gordon frequency within a constant-kinetic projection. Reaction--diffusion and Burgers representations reveal two key properties of the flow: discrete translation symmetries are preserved, and the number of extrema can only remain constant or decrease. Consequently, the nonlinear generation of Fourier harmonics may accompany a progressive simplification of the potential landscape. We illustrate the role of symmetry with two complementary examples. A weak breaking of the $\pi$-translation symmetry allows a reduction from four extrema to two, whereas a non-sinusoidal interaction retaining this symmetry evolves from eight extrema to the four protected by its periodicity. These results highlight how symmetry and coarse-graining jointly reorganize competing minima and barriers in periodic interactions.

authors.name: Daniel G. Barci, Nathan O. Silvano

papers.title: Prediction of lattice thermal conductivity of half-Heusler compounds by machine learning and transfer-function calibration
papers.summary: High-throughput searches for half-Heusler thermoelectrics increasingly rely on lattice thermal conductivity ($\kappa_L$) from first-principles calculations, or from machine-learning models trained on them. These calculations describe an ideal single crystal, whereas measurements are made on polycrystalline samples, in which grain boundaries and defects scatter heat as well. The resulting gap between calculated and measured $\kappa_L$ has been noted for individual compounds but not, to our knowledge, quantified across a materials class, so the values used for screening carry an unknown, systematic bias. Here we quantify and correct this bias for cubic half-Heusler compounds with 18 valence electrons. Using a curated literature corpus that keeps calculated and measured values apart, we show that calculations overestimate measured $\kappa_L$ in most bonding families, and that the excess shrinks with temperature. Scattering by defects, added to the intrinsic scattering between lattice vibrations, would give such a trend, but the data do not single out one cause. A simple transfer function with this temperature dependence removes the median offset, and refitting its magnitude within a bonding family lowers the median error further, though not consistently compound by compound. Combined with a machine-learning model that predicts the calculated value from crystal structure, and tested on chemistries withheld from all fitting, the method predicts measured $\kappa_L$ in this class about as closely as independent laboratories agree with one another, and provides testable predictions for compounds not yet measured.

authors.name: Shivam Randive, Ojaswini Randive, Heet Lungaria, Himanshu Pandey

papers.title: Tuning the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in CoFeB thin film heterostructures
papers.summary: The Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (DMI) is essential for stabilizing chiral spin textures in spintronics, yet achieving consistent quantitative measurements across different techniques remains a significant challenge. Heterostructures consisting of magnetic thin films sandwiched between non-magnetic heavy metals have been shown to possess substantial DMI; however, these vary in both magnitude and handedness for supposedly identical samples, indicating the sensitivity of DMI to both interfacial properties and measurement techniques. Here, systematic tuning of the DMI in ultra-thin magnetic heterostructures of Pt/CoFeB/Ta/Pt is achieved by varying the thickness of a tantalum sub-monolayer with thicknesses ranging from $0.1\,\mathrm{nm}$ to $0.4\,\mathrm{nm}$. The magnitude and sign of the DMI are measured using three independent methods: the parallel stripe domain model, edge nucleation field analysis, and Brillouin light scattering. The three independent approaches reveal excellent agreement within the experimental error. This ability to controllably tune and reliably quantify DMI provides a viable route toward engineering chiral magnetic textures, including domain walls and skyrmions, for next-generation spintronic devices. The necessity for precise measurements of magnetic parameters and careful attention to detail are discussed because calculations of the DMI for each technique depend on different parameters.

authors.name: Rabindra R Oliya, Christopher Keck, Lia Compton, Jing Guo, Kristen S Buchanan, Robert Streubel, Shireen Adenwalla

papers.title: Simple Routes to Turing-Like Patterns
papers.summary: Spots, stripes, and networks recur in systems with very different microscopic dynamics, suggesting that the competing processes behind Turing-like patterns may be easy to realise. We ask whether local amplification coupled to suppression over a wider region can generate these geometries in simple systems beyond chemical reaction--diffusion models. We test this idea in two settings, a binary cellular automaton obtained by adding a distant neighbour count to Conway's Game of Life and a self-gravitating toy universe described by particle motion and two continuous fields. The automaton produces spots, stripes, and coexistence across its control plane, while a rule retaining only the two opposing counts produces islands, stripes, and holes. Directional correlations and intrinsic dimension identify the same region of orientational order. In the gravitational system, convergence increases local density while mass transport depletes the surroundings. The two-field and particle densities have a smoothed spatial correlation of $0.962$ at scale factor $a=1$ under the original force law, and strengthening its long-wavelength component drives both descriptions toward fewer dense condensations. Together, these results show how simple counting rules and redistribution of a conserved quantity can realise competing growth and suppression, providing two concrete routes by which Turing-like geometries can recur across different dynamics.

authors.name: Zhan Zhao, Xiang-Ning Li, Wen-Wen Li, Ji-Chong Yang

papers.title: Geometric Contribution to the Electron-Phonon Coupling Constant: Checkerboard and Hyper-diamond Models
papers.summary: Recent theoretical studies on electron-phonon coupling (EPC) - a key ingredient in the emergence of diverse quantum phases such as superconductivity and charge-density waves - have revealed a distinct contribution to its strength arising from the quantum geometry of electronic bands. Here we investigate the quantum geometric contribution, characterized by the quantum metric, to the dimensionless EPC constant in the checkerboard and hyper-diamond models, under the Gaussian approximation. We show that in the checkerboard model, the geometric contribution can be tuned independently while keeping the energetic part fixed, demonstrating the possibility of enhancing EPC strength through quantum geometry. In the hyper-diamond model, the geometric contribution accounts for roughly $50\%$ of the total EPC constant across all spatial dimensions, generalizing the $d=2$ result for graphene to higher dimensions.

authors.name: Thomas Caligiure, Daniel P. Arovas, Jiabin Yu

papers.title: Artificial Spin-Glass of Antiferromagnetic Co3O4 Nanocubes Using Spin-Polarized Oxygen
papers.summary: Preferentially exposing (100) surface terminations of Co$_{3}$O$_{4}$ using cube-shaped nanoparticles yields an unconventional rearrangement of ions that generates spin-glass-like magnetism from the antiferromagnetic nanocubes. The necessary magnetic frustration arises out of competition between polarized Co-O bonds from charge transfer between O 2p and Co 3d orbitals, and highly anisotropic Co$^{2+}$ ions combined with anomalous high spin Co$^{3+}$ ions in octahedral sites. Size control permits tuning this novel combination of ions via preferentially polarizing Co-O bonds. The presence of control over frustrated magnetism among antiferromagnetic nanocubes yields an artificial spin glass platform for exploring unconventional nanomagnetism and engendering new opportunities for emerging technologies like spintronics and physical reservoir computing.

authors.name: Gurleen K. Uppal, Alberto Acosta, Rachel Nickel, Christoph Klewe, Yanna Chen, Chengjun Sun, Charles A. Roberts, Johan van Lierop

papers.title: First-principles-based Prediction of Phase Fields: Part II. Solid Solution Tunability in Refractory Complex Concentrated Alloys
papers.summary: Refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCAs) offer a high-dimensional composition space for designing either robust single-phase solid solutions or controlled multiphase microstructures. However, most RCCA studies have examined isolated compositions, often near the equimolar point, rather than determining how solid-solution stability varies across the surrounding composition space. Here, we use rapid thermodynamic phase-field calculations to map the topology of solid-solution stability in RCCAs composed of Cr, Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, V, W, and Zr. Benchmarking the model against 109 experimentally reported quaternary-to-senary compositions produced through diverse processing routes yields an overall classification accuracy of 80%. We then introduce percentage miscible region, a metric that separates robust solid-solution-forming systems from those exhibiting compositionally tunable microstructures. Analysis of ternary, quaternary, and quinary RCCAs reveals that higher-order miscibility is strongly inherited from constituent binary subsystems, indicating the importance of choosing suitable binary interactions when designing RCCAs. Element-specific trends further show that Ti, Ta, Nb, and Mo generally stabilize solid solutions, whereas Cr and Zr promote ordered precipitation and phase segregation. Hf, W, and V, meanwhile, enable tuning between these regimes. These results establish a composition-space framework for the targeted design of RCCAs with robust solid-solution stability or tunable multiphase microstructures.

authors.name: Pravan Omprakash, Nicholas Crnkovich, Nathan Curtis, John Cavin, Adrien Couet, Rohan Mishra

papers.title: Interfacial Transition Waves and Domain Wall Self-Pinning in Bi-stable Mechanical Metamaterial
papers.summary: The understanding of transition waves in mechanical metamaterials currently derives from architectures fitting one of three archetypes as distinguished by the stability and order parameter: multi-stable with scalar or vector order parameter, and bi-stable with scalar order parameter. However, a fourth archetype is conspicuously absent: bi-stable with vector order parameter. Completing the tetrad, in this article, we numerically examine the transformation dynamics unique to bi-stable mechanical metamaterials with vector order parameter. We report two types of interfacial transition waves, whose propagation is restricted to the narrow region of configurational boundaries (e.g., domain walls). We show that the wave speed may depend on its polarization. In addition, we reveal an approach to regulate the severity of discreteness effects, which elevates discreteness as an intrinsic, tunable mechanism for controlling the wave speed -- including pinning/de-pinning of the domain wall -- without altering the metamaterial architecture. The results support applications in, e.g., reconfigurable mechanical circuits and complex domain patterning, and motivate further investigation of metamaterials with unconventional transition processes.

authors.name: Michael J. Frazier

papers.title: High-Sensitivity Magnetometry with Scalable Mixed SQUID Arrays
papers.summary: The utilisation of Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUIDs), a loop of superconducting material hosting two Josephson junctions, has long been at the forefront of quantum sensing. To enhance performance and signal power, modern architectures connect multiple SQUIDs into two-dimensional series-parallel arrays called Superconducting Quantum Interference Filters (SQIFs). A major recent advancement, called a mixed-SQUID array, integrates junction-free ``bare" loops alongside active SQUID loops, offering a promising strategy to engineer high-performance alternatives to traditional SQIF technology. However, a rigorous theoretical optimization and performance scaling analysis for this novel geometry remains lacking. In this work, an analytical framework, validated against full numerical simulations, is developed to establish fundamental design rules for this technology. This work systematically examines how key quantum sensing parameters evolve as a function of loop inductance, parasitic coupling, and overall array dimensions. Crucially, it is demonstrated that these mixed SQUID arrays circumvent the severe inductive screening losses inherent to conventional SQIF designs, achieving a performance boost in flux sensitivity in the range of $2-4\:\times$ under realistic device parameters.

authors.name: Anjishnu Bose, Jonathan Marenkovic, Giuseppe C. Tettamanzi

papers.title: Unveiling plastic rearrangements in silica glass through persistent homology
papers.summary: Plastic deformation of amorphous solids proceeds through localised atomic rearrangements. While much effort has been devoted to identifying where such rearrangements occur, how the local structure changes during a rearrangement is less well understood. In silica glass, a rearrangement can involve both distortion within SiO4 tetrahedra and deformation of the network connecting them, but the contributions of these two modes have rarely been quantified. Here, we characterise plastic rearrangements in silica glass under athermal quasistatic shear using persistent homology, which extracts rings from atomic configurations, and link the changes in the persistence diagrams to individual rings in real space. We classify rearrangement events into two types according to bond-coordination changes. By performing inverse analysis, we reveal that Si-centred triangles within tetrahedra, hinge triangles spanning two corner-sharing tetrahedra, and the other (non-hinge) O3 triangles are the dominant sources of topological changes upon rearrangements. The birth-time changes of Si-centred and hinge triangles closely follow the change in the angle opposite the longest edge, whereas that of non-hinge triangles also reflects changes in inter-tetrahedral O--O distances. Further, we clarify that triangles with large birth-time changes are localised in the rearrangement region. Comparing the two types of triangles, we find that the ratio of their birth-time changes is larger for coordination-changing events than for coordination-preserving events, indicating that such events involve relatively more intra-tetrahedral deformation compared with network deformation. These results demonstrate that persistent homology separates intra-tetrahedral and network deformation and quantifies each as a continuous quantity within a single framework.

authors.name: Fuya Katsuyama, Kumpei Shiraishi, Emi Minamitani

papers.title: Transition-Metal Substitutions in MOF-5: A Hybrid-DFT Study of Oxygen Electrocatalysis
papers.summary: Hybrid density functional theory calculations were used to investigate the stability, electronic properties, and catalytic activity of transition-metal impurities substituting Zn sites (M\(_{\rm Zn}\)) in the MOF-5 metal-organic framework [Zn\(_4\)O(BDC)\(_3\), BDC = 1,4-benzenedicarboxylate], with M = Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu. Most substitutions introduce \(3d\) states within the MOF-5 band gap and induce localized magnetic moments. Partially occupied \(3d\) states promote orbital hybridization and charge transfer with oxygenated intermediates, activating the dopant sites toward oxygen electrocatalysis. The oxygen reduction and evolution reaction (ORR and OER) activities were evaluated using the computational hydrogen electrode model. Mn\(_{\rm Zn}\) and Fe\(_{\rm Zn}\) exhibit calculated ORR overpotentials of 0.57~V, while Mn\(_{\rm Zn}\) and Co\(_{\rm Zn}\) yield OER overpotentials of 0.42 and 0.51~V, respectively, approaching those of benchmark precious-metal electrocatalysts. These findings identify Mn substitution as a promising strategy for achieving bifunctional ORR/OER activity in MOF-5 and establish a link between dopant electronic structure and catalytic performance to guide the design of MOF-based electrocatalysts.

authors.name: Pedro H. Souza, Walter Orellana

papers.title: Growth and anisotropic directional dependent transport properties of Altermagnetic CrSb
papers.summary: CrSb is a metallic altermagnet exhibiting large momentum-dependent spin splitting and antifer- romagnetic ordering well above room temperature. Although its electronic and magnetotransport properties have attracted considerable attention, a systematic comparison of crystals prepared us- ing different growth methods remains limited. Here we investigate the structural, magnetic, and anisotropic transport properties of CrSb single crystals grown by Sb(self)-flux, Bi flux, and chem- ical vapor transport (CVT). Each of these growth reveals distinct crystal morphologies. Magne- tization measurements exhibit broadly consistent antiferromagnetic responses, with an additional low-temperature contribution observed in Bi-flux-grown crystals. All samples display metallic resis- tivity and positive, nonsaturating magnetoresistance up to 9 T. Sb-flux- and CVT-grown crystals exhibit comparable residual resistivity ratios and magnetoresistance, whereas Bi-flux-grown crys- tals show enhanced residual resistivity and a substantially reduced magnetoresistance, consistent with stronger carrier scattering. Hall measurements reveal a pronounced dependence on the field- current configuration, including nonlinear field dependence and opposite Hall polarities for different crystallographic orientations. These results establish the reproducibility of anisotropic magneto- transport across distinct growth routes while highlighting the sensitivity of carrier scattering to crystal-growth conditions. Our findings provide a comparative framework for selecting CrSb single crystals for orientation-dependent transport and spintronic investigations.

authors.name: Resham Babu Regmi, Hari Bhandari, Sk Jamaluddin, Abhijeet Nayak, Ashok Chaudhary, Mohamed El Gazzah, Alex T. Sheardy, Maksym Zhukovskyi, Allen G. Oliver, Nirmal J. Ghimire

papers.title: Quantum order by disorder among lozenge tilings: a staircase of hub-free crystals between the Lieb ferrimagnet and the antiferromagnet
papers.summary: Lozenge tilings of the triangular lattice define an exponentially large family of bipartite networks, from the dice lattice, a Lieb ferrimagnet with the largest sublattice imbalance, to square-type tilings, which are compensated antiferromagnets. For the classical Heisenberg antiferromagnet all of them are degenerate. We show that quantum fluctuations lift this degeneracy through a local mechanism: the zero-point energy is, to leading order, a sum of site terms that are convex in the coordination $z$, so that Jensen's inequality at fixed $\langle z\rangle=4$ selects the square-type tiling. An expansion about the Ising limit explains the convexity: a site with more bonds has more channels for quantum fluctuations, but each fluctuation frustrates more bonds. A magnetic field couples to the Lieb moment and competes with this selection. Because the moment is carried most cheaply by threefold and fivefold sites, sixfold hubs are avoided, and bond counting together with the Lieb--Mattis theorem limits hub-free tilings to $3/5$ of the dice moment. Quantum Monte Carlo and a complete enumeration of periodic tilings with small unit cells show that the classical jump is replaced by a staircase of periodic crystals. Its widest step is a hub-free crystal that saturates the bound; below it, threefold and fivefold defects pack ever more densely in a shallow sequence of crystals, controlled by a short-ranged attraction between defects of equal curvature and a repulsion between defects of opposite curvature. Selection energies scale as $JS$. In the height representation the coordination is the discrete Gaussian curvature and the Lieb moment its sublattice-staggered part. We give spectroscopic signatures and discuss realizations in nanographenes, atomic spin arrays and quantum simulators.

authors.name: Suhwan Yoo, Jeehoon Choi, Chaeyeon Kim, Hee Young Kwon, Changyeon Won

papers.title: Axial Thermal Transport in Transition Metal Chalcogenide Nanowires from Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.summary: Transition metal chalcogenide M6X6 nanowires (M = Mo or W; X = S, Se, or Te) are promising one-dimensional (1D) building blocks for nanowire bundles and arrays, but how elemental composition controls their intrinsic axial heat transport remains unclear. Here we develop a multicomponent neuroevolution potential (NEP) from first-principles reference data and use homogeneous nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations to quantify the thermal conductivity of six MX6 nanowires. The Mo6X6 series show a nonmonotonic composition dependence, whereas the thermal conductivity of the W6X6 series decreases monotonically with increasing chalcogen mass. Frequency-resolved thermal conductivity and phonon mean-free path analyses show that axial heat conduction is dominated by low-frequency phonons. Vibrational density of states and spectral energy density analyses further reveal that the contrasting trends arise from a competition between metal-chalcogen vibrational matching and phonon softening induced by heavier chalcogen atoms. A phenomenological model incorporating the combined atomic mass and the relative mass difference between the metal and chalcogen atoms reproduces these trends. These results link elemental composition, phonon characteristics and axial thermal conductivity in M6X6 nanowires, providing an atomistic basis for selecting heat-conducting units in nanowire bundles and arrays.

authors.name: Wenwu Jiang, Hekai Bu

papers.title: Kinetic Arrest of a Disordered First-Order Phase Transition in Strained V2O3 Thin Films
papers.summary: We develop a continuum phenomenological theory for the kinetic arrest (KA) of a first-order phase transition (FOPT), taking the thermal and electric field-driven metal-insulator transition (MIT) in epitaxial V2O3 thin films as a prototype. By defining a coarse-grained mesoscopic order parameter representing the metallic volume fraction coupled to the primary structural monoclinic distortion, we formulate a Time-Dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) framework integrated with a non-local elastic interaction kernel and an Imry-Wortis quenched disorder landscape. We derive an explicit dynamic criterion for the kinetic arrest boundary TK(E) by analyzing the divergence of the intrinsic order-parameter relaxation time relative to experimental observation timescales. Our framework rigorously decouples the thermodynamic driving force from the kinetic activation barrier. We demonstrate that epitaxial substrate-induced clamping elevates local elastic barriers, pinning domain boundaries and stabilizing an arrested, inhomogeneous mosaic of metallic and insulating phases down to cryogenic temperatures. The simulated transformation kinetics exhibit an Avrami exponent suppression to values n < 1, reflecting slow, hindered domain-wall propagation. Furthermore, we examine the effect of an external electric field as an isothermal mechanism that lowers this kinetic barrier, providing a phenomenological description of threshold de-arrest and multi-level resistance states. We critically discuss this electronic barrier-lowering mechanism in comparison with electrothermal Joule heating, establish diagnostic criteria to distinguish them, and contextualize these non-equilibrium dynamics with related phenomena in disordered superconducting films.

authors.name: Sindhunil Barman Roy

papers.title: Ultraslow vorticity modes in colloidal fluids
papers.summary: In the conventional unsteady-Stokes picture, vorticity generated by a transient disturbance relaxes rapidly through viscous diffusion once the forcing ceases. This view presumes a quiescent solvent. In colloidal and biological fluids, thermal motion continually perturbs the surrounding fluid, raising a natural question: can equilibrium fluctuations, mediated by hydrodynamic coupling, sustain vorticity over mesoscopic scales and times? Here, using high-speed confocal microscopy of moderately dense colloidal suspensions, we reconstruct the conditional mean hydrodynamic response to Brownian displacements of prescribed magnitude and direction. We find a long-lived, spatially structured vorticity field that decays far more slowly than predicted by unforced unsteady-Stokes dynamics. A coarse-grained phenomenological model based on fractional Brownian motion, constrained by independently measured single-particle subdiffusion, quantitatively captures its temporal and spatial decay. These findings reveal a field-level manifestation of hydrodynamic memory in fluctuating low-Reynolds-number flows, with implications for transport and collective dynamics in complex fluids.

authors.name: Satyam Raheja, Noman Hanif Barbhuiya, Tsvi Tlusty, Chandan K. Mishra

papers.title: Quantum effects on the Peierls stress for screw dislocations in {\alpha}-Fe
papers.summary: The large discrepancy between the Peierls stress calculated using atomistic methods and that measured in experimental studies is well known. Despite significant research efforts over the past decades, our understanding of this mismatch remains limited. This work presents a multiscale study on the kinetics of screw dislocations in {\alpha}-Fe at 0.7K, employing the phonon description of temperature and using the Concurrent Atomistic-continuum (CAC) method as the simulation tool. Our simulations are shown to preserve the Bose-Einstein distribution of phonon modes and reproduce the nucleation and propagation of kink pairs. Large-scale CAC simulations with dislocation line lengths ranging from 0.1 to 2.1 microns, a typical range of lengths for screw dislocation lines, are performed, providing a quantitative and mechanistic understanding of the phonon-dislocation in {\alpha}-Fe. The experimentally measured Peierls stress in {\alpha}-Fe has been successfully reproduced, and the quantum effects on Peierls stress are quantified. Dependencies of phonon-dislocation interactions on dislocation line length and specimen size are explored and discussed.

authors.name: Jiaqu Sun, Yang Li, Boyang Gu, David McDowell, Youping Chen

papers.title: Recoverable Necking Enabled by Reverse Phase-Boundary Motion in Liquid Crystal Elastomers
papers.summary: Strain localization is often associated with plastic flow and permanent deformation. Here we show that a tensile neck in a crosslinked nematic network can undergo nearly complete recovery through reverse phase-boundary motion, leaving little residual deformation. In a monodomain liquid crystal elastomer stretched perpendicular to its initial director, this recovery occurs during an isothermal loading-unloading cycle. Digital image correlation resolves the process as the retreat of interfaces separating low- and high-stretch regions, where the high-stretch domain shrinks while previously necked material thickens, despite substantial mechanical hysteresis. Within the recoverable-necking regime, increasing temperature lowers the loading plateau stress but raises the unloading plateau stress. A nonconvex constitutive description provides an energetic basis for the coexistence of the two stretch states, while gradient regularization accounts for the finite width of their interfaces through an equilibrium reference profile. These results identify the spatial mechanism of neck recovery and distinguish recoverable strain localization from mechanical reversibility in an orientationally ordered polymer network.

authors.name: Weida Kang, Yufeng Zhang, Changyue Liu, Zhijian Wang, Xudong Liang

papers.title: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe2-xTex Polytypic Heterostructures
papers.summary: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure-superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2-xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range-from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T' structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8)shows suppressed Tc (~ 2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin-orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.

authors.name: Xiangqi Liu, Haonan Wang, Ziguang Liu, Peihan Sun, Xiang Xu, Jing Jiang, Zhengyang Li, Ziyi Zhu, Wei Xia, Xia Wang, Leiming Chen, Ke Qu, Yulin Chen, Cheng Chen, Kai Liu, Zhenzhong Yang, Yanfeng Guo

papers.title: Revealing the growth of structural length in glass-forming liquids without using dynamical information
papers.summary: Dynamical heterogeneity underlies the dramatic slowdown of supercooled liquids and has long been a central topic in glass physics. Despite considerable progress in identifying structural motifs and order parameters correlated with dynamical heterogeneity, a general characterization of structural descriptors remains elusive because they can vary among glass formers and are not generally known \emph{a priori}. To address this challenge, we establish a unified framework that can be applied to varieties of glass formers to extract structural signatures of dynamical heterogeneity directly from their static configurations. The framework combines a graph neural network (GNN) with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Across three canonical three-dimensional glass-forming models, the resulting structural field exhibits a characteristic correlation length that tracks the corresponding dynamical correlation length. Notably, a network trained on small systems can be applied to larger systems without retraining, indicating that the extracted features are encoded in local and mesoscopic structural correlations. These results demonstrate that static configurations encode structural signatures of dynamical heterogeneity and establish a scalable, interpretable route for extracting them.

authors.name: Min Liu, Daisuke Nishigaito, Yusuke Hara, Norihiro Oyama, Takeshi Kawasaki

papers.title: Tailoring Phonon Transport in Bi-based Quaternary Half-Heusler alloys for Thermoelectric Applications
papers.summary: Quaternary half-Heuslers (QHHs) are substitutionally disordered derivatives of conventional halfHeusler (HH) compounds, which offer a potential route to modify phonon transport and enhance thermoelectric performance. Here, we investigate the thermoelectric properties of the quaternary half-Heuslers ZrHfRh2Bi2, ZrHfIr2Bi2, Zr2RhIrBi2, and Hf2RhIrBi2 using first-principles calculations and anharmonic lattice dynamics. Among four compounds, ZrHfRh2Bi2 and Zr2RhIrBi2 exhibit semiconducting electronic structure and others are semimetallic in nature. Both the semiconducting compounds show favorable electronic transport properties. However, quaternary substitution substantially modifies the phonon dispersion, lowering the average phonon group velocity by about 17-22% relative to the parent compounds while leaving the anharmonic scattering rates comparable. The combination of high power factor and low kl results in high thermoelectric performance, with maximum ZT values of 2.28 and 2.18 at 1000 K for p-type ZrHfRh2Bi2 and Zr2RhIrBi2, respectively, with maximum thermoelectric power conversion efficiency 16.3% for p-type ZrHfRh2Bi2. Further reducing the grain size enhances the thermoelectric performance, with maximum ZT values of 2.51 and 2.58 at 1000 K for p-type ZrHfRh2Bi2 and Zr2RhIrBi2, respectively, at a grain size of 30 nm. Our results demonstrate that combining substitutional disorder with grain boundary engineering, provides an effective strategy to enhance the thermoelectric performance of HH compounds.

authors.name: Supriya Ghosal, Sayan Paul, Swapan K. Pati

papers.title: Normal-state exponential muon-spin relaxation and its implications for time-reversal symmetry breaking in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$
papers.summary: The low-temperature increase of the zero-field muon-spin relaxation rate in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ has long been regarded as evidence for spontaneous internal fields associated with time-reversal-symmetry-breaking (TRSB) superconductivity. Here we directly test this interpretation using muon-spin rotation/relaxation ($\mu$SR) measurements on high-quality Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ single crystals. For all four samples, the onset temperature of the additional exponential relaxation in the zero-field$\mu$SR data, $T_{\Lambda}$, lies below the bulk superconducting transition temperature $T_{\rm c}$, even in the absence of applied strain. More importantly, in transverse-field $\mu$SR measurements we find a quantitatively similar exponential relaxation in a field of 80 mT applied along the crystallographic $c$ axis. This field exceeds the upper critical field of the crystals studied in transverse-field geometry and suppresses bulk superconductivity, demonstrating that the characteristic relaxation persists in the normal state.
