Measurements below the upper critical field reveal an additional superconducting mixed-state contribution superposed on this normal-state channel. Our results show that the zero-field $\mu$SR relaxation in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ cannot, by itself, be regarded as a unique signature of superconducting TRSB. They call for a reassessment of a key experimental signature of TRSB in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ and highlight the need to distinguish superconducting and normal-state relaxation channels in other unconventional superconductors.

authors.name: Rustem Khasanov, Thomas J. Hicken, Jonas A. Krieger, Maxime Lamotte, Toni Shiroka, Jake S. Bobowski, Vadim Grinenko, Thomas Johnson, Naoki Kikugawa, Hans-Henning Klauss, Shubhankar Paul, Benjamin M. Huddart, Stephen J. Blundell, Hubertus Luetkens, Yoshiteru Maeno

papers.title: Nonmonotonic Magnetic Correlations in Decorated Lieb-Lattice Anderson Models
papers.summary: The interplay between electronic correlations and lattice geometry can strongly modify the competition between magnetic correlations and local singlet formation in multiorbital Hamiltonians. Here we use determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations to investigate two periodic Anderson-like models constructed by selectively hybridizing localized orbitals to the inequivalent sites of a Lieb lattice. The resulting geometries possess partially filled flat bands and different sublattice imbalances. We examine the evolution of local spin correlations and orbital-resolved magnetic structure factors as the hybridization is increased. Although correlations between hybridized orbitals evolve relatively smoothly toward local singlet formation, the longer-range magnetic correlations exhibit a striking nonmonotonic dependence on hybridization. In particular, we observe a pronounced suppression at intermediate hybridization followed by a substantial recovery on undecorated lattice sites. We discuss these results in relation to earlier studies of depleted periodic Anderson models and the constraints imposed by Lieb's theorem. Our findings illustrate how selective hybridization and flat-band structure can produce unusual redistributions of magnetic correlations in strongly interacting multiorbital systems.

authors.name: Raymond Hmuifoo, Edwin W. Huang, Annabelle Ancheta, Richard T. Scalettar

papers.title: Decoupling Entropic and Enthalpic Elasticity in Crosslinked Polymer Nanocomposites
papers.summary: Nanoparticle-induced local interface regions significantly enhance the bulk mechanical behavior of polymer nanocomposites, yet their energetic contribution in crosslinked elastomer networks remains poorly understood. Here, we decouple the entropic and enthalpic contributions to the elasticity of crosslinked poly(dimethylsiloxane) nanocomposites using temperature-dependent thermomechanical measurements. While the measured bulk elastic modulus exhibits a monotonic increase with nanoparticle volume fraction $\phi_{\rm n}$, we observe that the effective crosslink density initially increases before saturating at larger $\phi_{\rm n}$. These results are independently validated across two nanoparticle systems (silica and titania) and directly confirmed by X-ray scattering experiments on silica-based composites, highlighting the generality of the observation. The trends in effective crosslink density indicate that the elastic response is predominantly entropy-driven at low nanoparticle concentrations, whereas enthalpic contributions become increasingly significant at higher loadings. Assuming a linear superposition of interface and bulk contributions, these results reveal that the effective crosslink density at the particle interface decreases by an order of magnitude below a critical mean interparticle separation, indicating that localized particle proximity and clustering constrain the entropic elasticity at higher loadings.

authors.name: Chiranjit Majhi, Sivasurender Chandran, Krishnacharya Khare

papers.title: Gap-label bounds and optical reconstruction of Landau-subband quantum geometry
papers.summary: We derive a magnetic gap-label lower bound on the internal quantum weight of Landau subbands that remains nonzero even when the occupied Chern number vanishes. Using the second fundamental forms of nested subbundles to decompose the quantum geometric tensor, we isolate the constraint imposed by the uniform parent curvature and show that the excess quantum weight above the bound equals twice the weaker circular transition weight. For a noninteracting parabolic band with a periodic scalar potential, Landau-level mixing preserves the integrated relative curvature while the occupied direct gap remains open. Nevertheless, uncorrected sub-cyclotron absorption need not satisfy the projected bound. Using exact circular-dipole relations, we reconstruct the low-frequency guiding-centre weight and signed dichroism from circularly polarized absorption. This reconstruction removes the first-order orbit-polarization contribution. For an insulating filling of an isolated lowest-Landau-level-derived cluster, a potential-gradient estimate bounds the omitted remote-transition weight quadratically at weak coupling. This yields a finite-window lower bound on reconstructed quantum weight and bounds the deviation of reconstructed dichroism from the integrated relative curvature.

authors.name: \"Ozg\"ur Kelek\c{c}i

papers.title: Role of antisite disorder in dictating the Ising anisotropy and ferromagnetic ground state of NdGaSi
papers.summary: Single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions together set the magnetic ground state of rare-earth intermetallics, yet the role of chemical disorder on the ligand sublattice remains little explored. Here, we show that Ga/Si antisite disorder in NdGaSi stabilises the centrosymmetric $I4_1/amd$ structure and raises the Nd$^{3+}$ site symmetry to $D_{2d}$, which forbids all $m=\pm2$ Stevens operators in the crystalline electric field (CEF) Hamiltonian. Magnetization, specific heat, single-crystal neutron diffraction, and x-ray absorption spectroscopy establish the disordered structure and a collinear ferromagnetic order below $T_\mathrm{C}\approx11$~K with Ising anisotropy along $c$. A CEF analysis that fits the susceptibilities along both axes and the magnetic specific heat simultaneously yields a ground-state doublet that is $\sim97\%$ pure, in contrast to the strongly mixed ground state of the Al/Si-ordered NdAlSi ($C_{2v}$ site symmetry of Nd$^{3+}$). We argue that this ground-state purity makes the ordered moment rigid against the modulation due to frustrated exchange, selecting a $\mathbf{k}=0$ ferromagnet in NdGaSi instead of the incommensurate ferrimagnet of NdAlSi. Antisite disorder, thus, acts as a handle on CEF ground-state purity and can, thereby, select between fundamentally different magnetic ground states.

authors.name: Anyesh Saraswati, Sourav Kanthal, Subhajit Nandy, Jhuma Sannigrahi, Matthias Gutmann, Nitesh Kumar

papers.title: Frustration-Stabilized Hexamerons and Their Topological Magnons in Janus MXene
papers.summary: Frustrated magnets on triangular lattices favour noncollinear order, and when inversion symmetry is broken they can host localized topological textures on top of that order. Here we show that the Janus MXene MnHf2C2FI is such a system. Combining first-principles calculations with atomistic spin simulations, we find that magnetism is confined to the Mn layer, where a strong antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor exchange together with a sizable Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction stabilizes a frustrated 120 Neel ground state. On top of this ground state we identify a metastable hexameron: a composite of six merons and antimerons, one vortex-antivortex pair on each of the three sublattices, whose sublattice-resolved topological charges compensate. Linear spin-wave theory confirms that the hexameron is a local energy minimum, and its noncoplanar cores act as potential wells that bind discrete in-gap magnon modes below the bulk continuum. In a periodic hexameron array the magnon bands carry nonzero Chern numbers, and the resulting Berry curvature produces a magnon thermal Hall response whose sign depends on which of the two time-reversal partners of the hexameron is realized. Our results establish Janus MXenes as a two-dimensional platform in which frustration, broken inversion symmetry, and spin-orbit coupling combine to produce metastable antiferromagnetic solitons with distinct spectroscopic and transport fingerprints.

authors.name: C. B. Subba, Z. Pachuau, Samy Brahimi, Samir Lounis, D. P. Rai

papers.title: Pushy Random Walk on the Bethe lattice: a Galton-Watson perspective
papers.summary: Pushy random walks are minimal models of transport in deformable media, in which the walker displaces the obstacles it bumps into rather than being blocked by them. On the Bethe lattice, we show that the walkable structure dynamically created by a pushy walker can be generated a priori as an explicit multi-type Galton-Watson tree, so that the walker reduces to a simple random walk on a static random tree, and its escape to infinity coincides with the survival of the underlying branching process. Standard generating-function tools then give direct access to the escape properties of these walks. For the Sokoban walk, which pushes a single obstacle, we recover the known critical density $\rho_c = 1-(z-1)^{-2}$ and the behavior of the escape probability close to $\rho_c$, and derive its small-density asymptotics. For the second-order pushy walk, which can push trains of two obstacles, we establish the conjectured $\rho_c = 1-(z-1)^{-3}$, and compute the escape probability at all densities. Beyond escape, the same framework yields the statistics of the trace of trapped walkers: the distribution of the maximal depth follows from the extinction probabilities, while the distributions of the visited volume and of the number of dead ends are encoded in explicit functional equations for their generating functions, which we invert numerically. All predictions agree with Monte Carlo simulations.

authors.name: J\'er\'emie Klinger

papers.title: Pure Orbitronics: Hall Responses and Torques by Orbital Exchange in Spinless Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides
papers.summary: Recent studies have identified orbital exchange fields as a novel mechanism for controlling electronic and magnetic phenomena through the orbital degree of freedom. In contrast to conventional spin exchange fields, orbital exchange fields couple directly to orbital angular momentum and can emerge from purely orbital interactions or dynamically through couplings to chiral excitations such as phonons and magnons. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the transport and torque responses generated by orbital exchange fields in two-dimensional materials. Using monolayer H-phase MoS$_2$ as a prototypical transition-metal dichalcogenide, we introduce a Zeeman-like orbital exchange field that breaks time-reversal symmetry in orbital space while leaving the spin degree of freedom inactive. We demonstrate that this perturbation induces a sizable intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity even in the absence of spin magnetism and spin--orbit coupling driven mechanisms. Simultaneously, the orbital Hall response remains robust in the weak-field regime and undergoes substantial reconstruction at larger exchange strengths due to pronounced band modifications. In addition, we show that currents can generate sizable current-induced orbital torques on the orbital magnetization. Our results establish orbital exchange fields as an effective route toward Hall transport and nonequilibrium torque phenomena driven purely by orbital physics, opening new perspectives for orbitronics and orbitally engineered quantum functionalities.

authors.name: Mahmoud Zeer, Dongwook Go, Yuriy Mokrousov

papers.title: Hall effect in electrolyte solutions: Self-consistent Debye-Huckel-Onsager theory
papers.summary: A self-consistent statistical-mechanical theory of the Hall effect in electrolyte solutions is developed by extending the self-consistent Debye-Huckel-Onsager (SCDHO) framework to crossed electric and magnetic fields. The theory incorporates non-local ionic charge distributions through Slater-type form factors and ion-specific coefficients describing the effective Lorentz response, with experimental input for protons and hydroxide ions. Within the random-phase approximation, the Hall conductivity is expressed as mean-field, correlation, and electrophoretic contributions. Both interaction channels include the Lorentz rotation of the complete electric-field-induced ionic velocity. In the point-charge limit with hydrodynamics suppressed, the relaxation correction agrees with independent odd stochastic density functional theory and the relaxation part of Friedman's classical result. For 22 dilute aqueous electrolytes, the mean absolute relative deviations from measured Hall constants and Hall numbers are about 17 percent. At finite concentrations, the theory predicts a nonmonotonic Hall number for NaBPh4 and sign changes of the electrophoretic correction for NaI and HCl. Correlation effects dominate for HCl and LiOH, whereas the two interaction channels become comparable for KOH and aqueous imidazolium salts. The results clarify how ionic mobilities, effective Hall coefficients, charge distributions, and solvent hydrodynamics determine electrolyte magnetotransport.

authors.name: Yury Budkov, Nikolai Kalikin

papers.title: How many states does an exact relaxation model need? Sharp state complexity and geometric obstructions for reversible chains
papers.summary: How many states does a reversible Markov model need to reproduce two prescribed relaxation modes exactly? We maximize the smaller of the two stationary coordinate variances over all finite reversible chains whose states lie in a given convex region and whose coordinates relax at rates $1$ and $\rho$. Detailed balance turns this into the equilibrium of a tension-only cable network whose loads depend on the stationary masses. For the moment curve of the Wright-Fisher diffusion no finite chain is optimal: maximizing sequences converge to a unique beta law, and the best deficit with $N$ states is of order $N^{-2}$. We find the exact leading constant for states on the curve and for states in its convex hull, together with the optimal cube-root density of states. The hull constant is the curve constant times $c/(1+c)$, $c=(\rho-2)/\rho$; at $\rho=5/2$ the hull needs $\sqrt{6}$ times fewer states, although the limiting law is the same. For $\rho>8/3$ any upward enlargement of the hull lowers the constant again. All lower bounds hold for arbitrary transition graphs. At every fixed number of states an optimizer exists. On a seven-gon the smallest optimal chain jumps from three to four states while the optimal value stays constant, and a family of polygons forces the state count to grow linearly with the number of sides. Monotone vector fields give exact upper certificates, which solve an asymmetric quadrilateral at all rates and 381 polygon-rate instances in exact arithmetic. We formulate a finite-realizability problem and a finite-dictionary conjecture for polygons, and derive state budgets and exclusion tests for finite kinetic models.

authors.name: Murad Aznagulov

papers.title: A Negative-U Double Quantum Dot in a LaAlO3/SrTiO3 Membrane on Silicon
papers.summary: The development of freestanding oxide membranes creates new opportunities to integrate oxide functionalities with silicon technology. A central question is whether local gates can control the correlated electronic states of transferred membranes at the scale required for hybrid mesoscopic quantum devices. Here, we demonstrate local electrostatic control of freestanding LaAlO3/SrTiO3 (LAO/STO) membranes transferred onto silicon. In a dual-gated constriction in the interfacial electron system, we observe an oxide-based double quantum dot (DQD) in the regime of attractive on-site interactions (U < 0). Low-temperature transport reveals the characteristic honeycomb charge stability diagram, and spectroscopy identifies a paired-electron ground state at low magnetic fields, with odd-occupancy states becoming accessible above the pairing field. The observed transport spectra are reproduced by simulations within an attractive two site Hubbard model, and we extract the relevant DQD parameters, including intradot and interdot interactions, interdot tunnel coupling, and spin-orbit-assisted tunnel coupling. These findings establish oxide membranes as hosts for DQDs and extend coupled quantum dot systems into the regime of attractive on-site interactions.

authors.name: Giulia Meucci, Thies Jansen, Pinelopi O. Konstantinopoulou, Dags Ol\v{s}teins, Damon J. Carrad, Carina Babu Maliakkal, Jordi Arbiol, Nicolas Bergeal, Manuel Bibes, Roberta Citro, Emiliano Di Gennaro, Alexei Kalaboukhov, Nicola Manca, Carmine A. Perroni, Marco Salluzzo, Pawe{\l} W\'ojcik, Felix Trier, Nini Pryds, Fabio Miletto Granozio, Alessia Sambri, Thomas S. Jespersen

papers.title: Conductivity of electrolyte solutions: Self-consistent Debye-H\"{u}ckel-Onsager theory
papers.summary: This study presents a novel approach to addressing the limitations in understanding the behavior of charged particles in solutions. The approach is based on the development of the Self-Consistent Debye-H\"uckel-Onsager (SCDHO) theory, which integrates the effects of non-local charge distributions using a Slater-type charge form factor model. This results in a modified Coulomb potential at short distances, unlike traditional approaches such as the classical Debye-H\"uckel-Onsager theory. The proposed method relies on explicit expressions derived from gradients of local chemical potentials rooted in classical Density Functional Theory (DFT) and the Ornstein-Zernike formalism for correlation functions. Our theoretical framework enables the derivation of analytic equations that describe both correlation (aka relaxation) and electrophoretic contributions to total electric conductivity. Within the established theoretical framework, the model of smeared charges with Slater-type charge form factors provides an accurate predictive tool that can be applied to a wide range of ion valences, concentrations, and temperatures, including both aqueous and non-aqueous electrolyte solutions.

authors.name: Yury Budkov, Nikolai Kalikin

papers.title: Decoupling Exciton Energetics from Wavefunction Geometry in Imide-Based Defect Double Antiperovskites
papers.summary: The excited-state properties of imide-based defect double antiperovskites AE$_5$AsPn(NH)$_2$ (AE = Ca, Sr; Pn = Sb, Bi) are investigated using spin--orbit-coupled quasiparticle calculations, the model Bethe--Salpeter equation (mBSE), and analytical descriptions of lattice-polarization effects. Across five tetragonal ($P4/mmm$) and monoclinic ($Cm$) structural models, the calculated exciton binding energies range from 140 to 210 meV. Chemical substitution modifies both the binding energies and the hydrogenic estimates of exciton spatial extent. By contrast, the structural distortion from tetragonal $P4/mmm$ ($D_{4h}$) to monoclinic $Cm$ ($C_s$), which removes inversion and fourfold rotational symmetry, produces comparatively modest changes in binding energy but appreciably reshapes the real- and momentum-space exciton distributions. This contrast reveals a partial decoupling between exciton energetics and wavefunction geometry, and identifies a symmetry-associated sensitivity of exciton geometry to structural distortion. The changes are understood to occur together with modifications of local coordination and electronic dispersion, rather than as an isolated effect of symmetry alone. Lattice polarization provides an additional screening channel, reducing the estimated exciton binding energies by approximately 9--16\%. Complementary Fr\"ohlich-polaron calculations yield moderate mass enhancement and model-estimated electron-polaron mobilities of 39--99 cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$, with comparatively modest differences between the two polymorphs. These results highlight the distinct responses of exciton energetics, exciton wavefunction geometry, and carrier transport to chemical and structural modifications.

authors.name: Dhriti Mandal, Saswata Bhattacharya

papers.title: Spectral and dynamical properties of quasiperiodically kicked staggered chains
papers.summary: We study a one-dimensional lattice driven by Fibonacci-ordered kicks of a staggered potential. We ask what the quasienergy spectra of periodically repeated finite segments reveal about the nonrepeating drive. For weak kicks, one temporal Fourier amplitude predicts both the quasienergy gap and the frequency of interband oscillations under periodic repetition. As the segment grows, the gap tends to zero, but a finite limiting coupling sets the oscillation frequency under the nonrepeating drive. At special momenta, the difference between kick counts on even and odd steps determines the exact interband population at any kick strength. Under the nonrepeating drive, the maximum magnitude of this imbalance grows logarithmically with time. For weak kicks, the time to first reach a fixed upper-band population therefore grows exponentially in the inverse kick strength. Under repetition of a fixed even-length segment, it grows linearly in the inverse kick strength. Temporal ordering thus controls interband oscillations and the time needed to populate the upper band.

authors.name: Sanghoon Lee, Kyoung-Min Kim

papers.title: Adaptive obstacle deposition drives dynamical localization in chase-and-escape dynamics
papers.summary: Most pursuit--evasion models assume a fixed environment, although defensive actions can leave persistent structures that affect subsequent encounters. We study a two-dimensional lattice model in which threatened escapers deposit permanent obstacles, coupling capture kinetics to the geometry explored by their pursuers. Increasing the deposition probability enhances escaper survival and strongly suppresses chaser transport. For dilute chasers, the mean-squared-displacement exponent decreases from values near unity towards zero, trajectories contract to a few lattice spacings and the localized fraction rises sharply. The localization response becomes weaker as chaser abundance increases. Time-resolved obstacle densities support a kinetic explanation: rapid capture depletes obstacle-producing escapers before a comparably confining environment can develop. At intermediate parameters, broad or bimodal distributions of trajectory radii and MSD exponents reveal simultaneous mobile and localized subpopulations. Thus deposition redistributes trajectories between distinct dynamical behaviors, producing heterogeneity beyond a uniform slowdown. We summarize the coupled survival and transport response in an empirical map of mobile, heterogeneous and trapping-dominated regimes, interpreted as finite-time crossovers. These results identify the lifetime of the obstacle-producing population as a key control of adaptive localization: a stronger instantaneous pursuit pressure can weaken confinement by shortening the period over which the environment is modified.

authors.name: R. G. Rossatto, Amin Bakhshandeh, H. Arial Alvarez, C. Manuel Carlevaro, Jos\'e Rafael Bordin

papers.title: Annular Terahertz Near-Field of a Breathing Charged Vortex
papers.summary: We study the radial electric field around a singly quantized vortex in a charged BCS superconductor, when the Higgs amplitude mode is driven by a uniform terahertz (THz) electromagnetic pulse. In a local-density approximation the pairing gap vanishes on the vortex axis at all times, so the particle density on the axis cannot oscillate, whereas the curvature of the density profile around the axis does. Starting from the electrostatic-lens formalism of our previous work, we show that this converts the electrically neutral Higgs oscillation into an alternating radial electric field that vanishes on the axis. When the electrostatic screening length is much shorter than the vortex core, we obtain the field in closed form: it has a ring-shaped profile, with a maximum at a distance of the order of the coherence length from the axis, and the Higgs drive modulates it by a fraction $2\eta$, where $\eta$ is the relative oscillation of the gap. For niobium nitride and $\eta=0.1$ the static field of the vortex is about $140$~V/m and its modulation about $30$~V/m, independently of the carrier density and of the dielectric constant. We also discuss how the thermodynamic factor entering the field changes toward the BCS-BEC crossover.

authors.name: I. Tolbatov, L. Salasnich

papers.title: Rotation-induced supersolidity in a spin-imbalanced unitary Fermi gas
papers.summary: We show that a supersolid can be spontaneously generated by a persistent current in a spin-imbalanced unitary Fermi gas in a ring. As polarization increases, stable superflow turns dissipative via vortex emission before superfluid and crystalline order coexist. Pairing and spin densities are modulated with an even number of nodes, where the pairing phase jumps by $\pi$ and excess majority spins accumulate. Even at fixed polarization, the modulation period changes with the winding number, unlike in FFLO states. The modulation slides freely, supporting a gapless translational Goldstone mode.

authors.name: Bu\u{g}ra T\"uzemen, Gabriel Wlaz{\l}owski, Piotr Magierski, Klejdja Xhani

papers.title: Minimal chiral $p$-wave superconductor
papers.summary: Chiral $p$-wave superconductors are among the most intriguing topological phases: their vortices bind Majorana zero modes and their edges carry chiral Majorana modes, yet no material has been unambiguously identified as one. Here, we carry the bottom-up approach of Kitaev chains to two dimensions, proposing a minimal chiral $p$-wave superconductor from a square array of quantum dots coupled via Andreev dots. Rashba spin-orbit coupling in the tunnel barriers provides the $p$-wave winding, and a Zeeman field renders the dots spinless. At a sweet spot, the edge states are confined to the outermost row, so that a chiral thermal conductance and a vortex-bound Majorana zero mode with sub-percent splitting emerge already in $3\times3$ and $5\times5$ arrays. Our setup is realizable with existing InAs and Ge quantum-dot arrays.

authors.name: Fabian Hassler, Michael Wimmer

papers.title: From non-universal spectra at the RS-RSB transition to the universal $\omega^4$ regime inside the glassy phase
papers.summary: The universal low-frequency nonphononic density of states $\mathcal{D}_\mathrm{G}(\omega)\sim\omega^4$ is a robust feature of structural glasses, yet its origin remains poorly understood. Here we investigate this question using the mean-field KHGPS model of interacting anharmonic oscillators. We show that the universal quartic spectrum is deeply rooted in the glassy, replica-symmetry-broken (RSB) phase, whereas the gapless density of states found at the boundary of the replica-symmetric (RS) phase is non-universal and depends sensitively on the details of the quenched disorder. We formulate a simplified variant of the KHGPS model that allows us to characterize the crossover between these two regimes and provides a physical interpretation of the associated crossover frequency scale. We further show that the conventional, spin-glass-like, continuous RS-RSB transition, accompanied by diverging susceptibilities, can be suppressed by an appropriate choice of the quenched disorder, allowing for a discontinuous RS-RSB transition even in the absence of an external field. Our results establish a direct connection between the emergence of the universal $\omega^4$ spectrum and the glassy phase, and provide a simple framework for exploring the low-temperature properties of glasses and the soft localized excitations that emerge from bistable local potentials.

authors.name: Tommaso Pettinari, Edan Lerner, Gustavo D\"uring

papers.title: Designing Perovskites for Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production
papers.summary: Perovskites are promising materials for chemical looping hydrogen production (CLHP) due to their compositional flexibility and tunable redox properties. However, cation substitution opens a vast compositional space, making screening for new high-performing materials computationally demanding. Here, an autonomous active-learning framework combining a Wasserstein autoencoder (WAE) with a deep ensemble surrogate model was used to search for perovskites with a high hydrogen production capacity (HPC). In seven independent runs of 50 cycles, the mean HPC of the acquired compositions rose from 0.41 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$ in the starting set to 2.05 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$, and the best compositions reached 2.65-2.99 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$. All runs enriched Sn on the B-site, mostly combined with Ti and with Mg, Ce, K and Y on the A-site. Twenty diverse candidates (2.22-2.84 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$) were then selected by a multi-objective ranking that also accounts for raw-material price, supply resilience and potential environmental and health impacts. The approach links materials discovery with practical deployment constraints, and the methodology is transferable to other chemical looping processes.

authors.name: Ivana Stani\v{c}i\'c, Alfred Juhlin Onbeck, Anders Hellman, Tobias Mattisson, Magnus Ryd\'en

papers.title: Modeling the contact area and intersurface forces between Pb nanoparticles and suspended graphene
papers.summary: We perform large-scale atomistic simulations to explore the contact mechanics of Pb nanoparticles (NPs) physisorbed on a suspended graphene sheet at zero external load. The study considers the kinetics of the NPs' relative contact area and the distributions of intersurface atomic force magnitudes acting on the NP during self-assembly from the liquid phase, and the size scaling of these quantities for the solidified NPs. The functional forms of both the repulsive and attractive parts of the normal intersurface force distributions for solidified NPs are size-independent for nanoislands with a linear lateral size larger than about 10 nm (or a surface area-to-volume ratio less than about 1 nm$^{-1}$). To first order, the repulsive tail decays exponentially, while the cutoff power law fits more precisely, especially for the high-probability repulsive forces. In both cases, the decay exponent is around -5 nN$^{-1}$. The exponentially modified Gaussian is the best fit for the attractive part for most NP sizes. The time-averaged relative contact area calculated directly in the simulations shows considerable fluctuations for NPs a few nm in diameter, while converging to approximately 0.44 for larger NPs. Based on fitting the normal-force distributions, we obtain analytical expressions for the relative contact area. Ensemble-averaged relative contact areas for NPs larger than around 10 nm, calculated using the analytical expressions, match the time-averaged MD values within statistical error. Our model is the first step towards developing analytical approximations for quantitative estimates of the relative contact area of Pb NPs adsorbed on suspended graphene.

authors.name: Mykola Prodanov, Anton Samilyk, Oleksii Khomenko, Antonina Biesiedina

papers.title: Capillary partitioning of solutes on conformally coated colloidal monolayers: a universal geometric threshold
papers.summary: Depositing a conformal solid film on a hexagonal monolayer of spheres progressively closes the interstitial pores, and this closure controls where a dilute solute spin-coated from a volatile solvent ends up after drying: buried in the interstitial valleys or spread over the exposed caps. We derive the fraction of solute that ends in the valleys from first principles, for any sphere radius, film thickness and wetting liquid. The control parameter is the film thickness divided by the sphere radius, and a purely geometric threshold, about 0.155, separates two regimes for all sphere sizes. Below it, the three-sphere interstice is an open cup that the liquid fills through a narrow throat at the sphere equator, and about nine tenths of the solute end in the valleys. Above it, the throat pinches shut, sealing the cup and leaving only a shallow surface dimple, so this fraction drops more than twofold, never to recover. Treating the throat as a nearly triangular duct gives a closed-form filling rate, confirmed by exact flow calculations. During spin-coating, filling outpaces drying by up to five orders of magnitude, except within a fraction of a nanometre of the threshold. Partitioning is therefore set by capacity alone, through a one-parameter ratio of exact void volumes, identical for all sphere sizes. Thin-film simulations confirm the direction of liquid transport. For dye in ethanol on tantalum-pentoxide-coated polystyrene lattices, the predicted on-cap fraction rises from 0.06 to 0.76 across the threshold, agreeing at both ends with values inferred from measured Purcell factors.

authors.name: Renaud A. L. Vall\'ee, Carlos Drummond

papers.title: Silver/alumina-capped Janus particles: a dispersible hyperbolic metamaterial
papers.summary: Hyperbolic metamaterials (HMMs) made of alternating layers of metal and dielectric have been heralded as promising materials for super-resolution imaging and spontaneous emission enhancement sought after in biological applications. However, the practical utilization of HMMs has been limited, primarily by the solid and stiff nature of the underlying substrate, usually a silicon wafer or glass substrate. An ability to transfer HMMs to colloidal substrates would introduce dispersibility to HMMs and potentially enable their use in medical applications while extending the curved HMM geometry to discrete particles. Here, spherical particles with alternating metal and dielectric layers are used to fabricate hyperbolic metamaterial-capped Janus particles (HMMJPs). Alternating layers of silver (metal) and alumina (dielectric) films are evaporated onto polystyrene particle monolayers with and without fluorescent properties to study the impact of particle curvature on the layer structure in the cap. The thickness and number of layers are chosen such that the final cap film resembles the structure of a 4P-HMM film, four periods of alternating silver/alumina, previously characterized as an HMM at wavelengths above 403 nm. The fluorescent character of the polystyrene particles is used to illuminate the pathway of light in the HMMJP clusters as a function of cluster size and geometry. Subsequently, resonance imaging microscopy (RIM) with the HaloElement is used to independently verify the HMM nature of a single HMMJP.

authors.name: Samhita Kattekola, Raymond R. Dagastine, Alexander Couzis, Ilona Kretzschmar

papers.title: Atomistic theory of the $d$-wave phonon angular momentum splitter effect
papers.summary: Phonons offer a bosonic route to angular-momentum transport in solids, but how their momentum-space textures manifest in transport remains unclear. Here we develop an atomistic theory of the phonon angular momentum splitter effect in an antiferromagnetic square lattice with checkerboard-modulated elastic couplings, analogous to the spin-splitter effect in $d$-wave altermagnets. We calculate the transport and accumulation of phonon angular momentum driven by a temperature gradient and find that the transverse response separates into Hall and $d_{xy}$-wave splitter contributions. The splitter contribution requires both the antiferromagnetic order and the checkerboard elastic modulation and exhibits a characteristic $d_{xy}$ angular dependence, whereas the Hall contribution is nearly isotropic. Their combination enables directional control of the edge phonon angular momentum accumulation.

authors.name: Daniel A. Bustamante Lopez, Dominik M. Juraschek

papers.title: Lattice-geometry dependence of Type-I and Type-II magnetic flux responses in strongly correlated bosons
papers.summary: Superfluids and superconductors are classified into Type-I and Type-II according to their response to a magnetic flux, but this classification has hardly been addressed for lattice bosons under magnetic flux, where the Meissner and vortex phases have been studied mostly in ladder geometries. Here, we study the flux response of the extended Bose-Hubbard model with nearest-neighbor interaction $V$ at half filling on square and triangular ladders with two to four legs by using the density-matrix renormalization group. On the square ladders, the vortex phase is confined to a region near $V=0$. At finite $V$, a magnetic flux-induced charge-density-wave (CDW) order replaces it, and the response becomes Type-I-like. In contrast, on the triangular ladders, the vortex phase persists over the whole range of $V$ studied, and the response remains Type-II-like. By extrapolating the ladder results to two dimensions, we argue that the Type-I or Type-II character of the flux response depends on the lattice geometry, which suggests a role of geometric frustration.

authors.name: Takayuki Yokoyama, Yasuhiro Tada

papers.title: General Transport Signatures of Odd-Parity Magnets: Charge--Spin Selection Rules and Temporal--Spectral Separation
papers.summary: While even-parity altermagnets are known for spatially separating charge and spin currents via the crystal spin Hall effect, the defining transport counterpart for odd-parity magnets remains to be established. Here, we establish temporal and spectral charge--spin separation as a general transport signature across all spin-splitting classes of collinear and noncollinear odd-parity magnets with unitary spin-flip inversion $\mathcal U=[C_2^\perp\Vert P]$. This symmetry restricts charge responses to odd orders and $z$-polarized spin responses to even orders, independent of microscopic mechanism and without requiring spin conservation. For ac drives that reverse sign after half a period, charge and spin currents exhibit opposite half-period parities, and their spectra contain only odd charge and even spin harmonics. This allows dc spin rectification without a dc charge counterpart, even in longitudinal transport and beyond weak fields. We show that although antiunitary $\mathcal T\tau$ enforces odd-parity bands, it reverses the charge--spin selection of Berry-curvature and Berry-curvature-dipole responses, providing a direct transport fingerprint distinguishing the two protecting symmetries. We verify the selection rules for all linear and second-order transport mechanisms and demonstrate harmonic separation in a minimal odd-parity model, representative Floquet-engineered collinear MnPS$_3$, and the equilibrium noncollinear VCl$_2$ family.

authors.name: Junxi Yu, Pu Zhang, Yichen Liu, Yongpan Li, Cheng-Cheng Liu

papers.title: Shift current as a stacking spectroscopy of hexagonal boron nitride multilayers
papers.summary: Out-of-plane polarization can be tuned by sliding polar monolayers in van der Waals materials; the bulk photovoltaic effect is emerging as a natural optical probe, provided the photocurrent tracks the polarization. We test that assumption by computing the polarization and the shift-current tensor from first principles across the stacking landscape of bi-, tri-, and tetralayer hexagonal boron nitride. The two quantities share one robust property: the vertical response reverses with the polarization while the in-plane one does not. Beyond this rule, the correspondence must be read with caution: stackings with identical polarization carry vertical monochromatic photocurrents of opposite sign; the spectra reorganize and even reverse sign at some photon energies along a constant-polarization plateau; and the strongest vertical peak of the entire pathway sits where the polarization crosses zero. The reason is structural: the polarization counts polar interfaces, while the shift current reads their positions. Broadband illumination reads the domain sign; monochromatic photocurrent maps can read the stacking registry. In a sliding ferroelectric, the bulk photovoltaic effect can operate as a stacking spectroscopy.

authors.name: Sanber Vizcaya, Juan M. Florez, Eric Su\'arez Morell

papers.title: Corrections to the Fick-Jacobs Description of Diffusion across Pickering Droplet Interfaces
papers.summary: Particle-laden interfaces give rise to important classes of multiphase materials, including Pickering-Ramsden systems and bicontinuous interfacially jammed emulsion gels (bijels). In these systems, colloidal particles adsorb at fluid-fluid interfaces and form semipermeable layers that provide structural stability and controlled diffusive transport. These properties make them attractive for encapsulation applications and motivate understanding transport across particle-laden interfaces. Diffusion through geometries with varying cross-section, including those found at particle-laden interfaces, is commonly described using the Fick-Jacobs formalism. However, this approach relies on the assumptions of slowly varying geometries and rapid equilibration in the transverse direction. Subsequent studies have developed corrections based on higher-order geometric derivatives, but an elegant closed-form description remains elusive. Here, we compare predictions of the Fick-Jacobs model with fully resolved simulations of 2D Pickering droplets. We find that discrepancies in model predictions increase with interfacial particle crowding, revealing the limits of the Fick-Jacobs approximation. We show that the required correction can be understood through simple geometrical arguments. Our results provide an effective framework for describing transport across particle-laden interfaces and lay the foundation for a more general description of diffusion in complex geometries.

authors.name: Rohit Khandoori, Wim Thielemans, Joost de Graaf

papers.title: Magnetic-Field Response of a Hyperbolic Kitaev Spin Liquid
papers.summary: Hyperbolic geometry can give rise to Kitaev spin liquids with distinct flux structures and Majorana spectra, raising the question of how these fractionalized states respond beyond exactly solvable limits. We address this question on the Kekul\'e-colored hyperbolic {8,3} lattice by developing an infinite projected entangled-pair-state approach with flux-resolved loop-gas initialization and geometry-adapted tensor-network contraction. Under uniform and staggered [111] magnetic fields, we find markedly different many-body responses. The uniform field induces a sharp change between competing variational branches at weak field, whereas the polarization and mean plaquette flux evolve over a much broader field range under the staggered field. Exchange-energy competition helps explain the different response scales, while third-order effective Majorana models in a fixed-flux background exhibit contrasting low-energy spectra. Our results connect the geometry-dependent fractionalized structure of a solvable hyperbolic spin liquid to its many-body response under physical perturbations that break flux conservation.

authors.name: Tao Yang, Baigeng Wang, Rui Wang, Z. Y. Xie

papers.title: Voltage-Controlled Dielectric Cavity Magnonics in Epitaxial Fe Films on SrTiO3 Single Crystal Substrates
papers.summary: Cavity magnonics relies on the hybridization between collective spin excitations and well-defined photonic or mechanical cavity modes, enabling fast and efficient coupling of spintronic devices to microwave circuits and optical information carriers. In this work, we present a hybrid material heterostructure that combines an intrinsic dielectric microwave cavity with a ferromagnetic medium, establishing magnon-photon interaction with coupling rates in the order of 0.1-1 GHz. Demonstrating effective voltage-control of the hybrid mode spectrum at cryogenic temperatures, we achieve a highly tunable photo-magnonic material, that could provide significant advancements for high-performance and power-efficient cryogenic RF-applications, including hybrid quantum technology, superconducting electronics and nonlinear microwave devices for unconventional computation and signal processing.

authors.name: Stijn Reniers, Ekaterina Gorokh, Lukas Nulens, Andries Boelen, Christian Haffner, Clement Merckling, Alejandro V. Silhanek, Kristiaan Temst, Joris Van de Vondel

papers.title: Prediction and characterisation of cation topology of pentanary high-entropy alloy (MoWNbTaV)S$_2$
papers.summary: High-entropy transition-metal dichalcogenides offer properties tuned by composition, yet two basic questions remain open: which arrangement of the metals forms under synthesis conditions, and how it can be recognised in experiment. Density functional theory (DFT) cannot sample the vast space of possible arrangements, and the ground-state energies usually employed to screen them do not take into account the temperatures at which these materials are made. This work solves both issues for the pentanary (MoWNbTaV)S\textsubscript{2} monolayer with a Gaussian approximation potential trained on DFT data by iterative learning. Gibbs free energy calculations reveal that vibrational entropy reshapes the stability ranking, while five selected configurations retain their trigonal-prismatic framework during nanosecond molecular dynamics up to \qty{1300}{\kelvin}. Raman and infrared spectra combine parent-monolayer signatures with disorder-activated modes, providing fingerprints for experimental identification. % The predicted lattice parameter follows Vegard's law and agrees within \qty{0.8}{\percent} with X{-}ray diffraction on a sputtered alloy film, which identifies the solid solution but not the arrangement of its metals: distinguishing between arrangements requires the vibrational fingerprints. The potential and its development workflow enable further atomistic simulations and offer a transferable approach to screening related two-dimensional high-entropy materials.

authors.name: Shubham Agarwal, Tahir Wahab, Jesper Byggm\"astar, Antonio Cammarata, Tomas Polcar

papers.title: Interaction and confinement effects for a ${}^6\mathrm{Li}_2$ condensate in a shaken lattice
papers.summary: A shaken optical lattice can form Floquet-engineered band structures. For a one-dimensional lattice, this method can hybridize the ground and first excited bands into a double-well dispersion. A molecular Bose-Einstein condensate (mBEC) loaded into this band bifurcates into two clusters at opposite quasimomenta, but short cluster lifetimes (2 ms to 3 ms) have limited earlier work. We improve our $^6$Li mBEC experiment by aligning the lattice axis with the trap and using a multifrequency shaking sequence to counterdiabatically load into the double-well minima. Together, these improvements allow us to extend the experiment timescale beyond 10 ms. At these longer times the momentum distribution depends qualitatively on the confinement. With stronger confinement in the lattice direction, there is a peak in the momentum distribution at the Brillouin zone edge. Shaking-frequency spectroscopy confirms this zone edge population and shows it splits roughly equally between the ground and first excited bands. The longer lifetime also lets us ramp the magnetic field from 650 G, where molecules interact weakly, to 800 G, near the Feshbach resonance. As the interaction strengthens, the bifurcation weakens and disappears. We suggest that the increased molecular size causes this change.

authors.name: Yang-Hao Lee, Duc Trong Le, John Karnosh, Colin V. Parker

papers.title: Linear Response Theory of Nitrogen K-Edge X-ray Absorption of TCNQ
papers.summary: The linear response of the density is computed in the frequency domain within the generalized Kohn--Sham framework of adiabatic time-dependent density functional theory, employing hybrid exchange-correlation functionals. It is shown that the generalized Casida equations imply a Dyson-like equation for the linear-response of the full frequency-dependent one-electron reduced density matrix of the reference GKS system. We implement this formalism in the \textsc{Crystal} code and apply it to the nitrogen K-edge near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) of 7,7,8,8-tetracyano-$p$-quinodimethane (TCNQ), the acceptor in the charge-transfer salt TTF-TCNQ. We interpret the spectrum through a step-by-step construction by building blocks of increasing complexity. This procedure separates the effects of $\pi$ conjugation, of multiple equivalent absorbing centers and of the ring on the in-plane ($\pi_\parallel$) and out-of-plane ($\pi_\perp$) resonances. The theoretical result is confirmed by a comparison with angle-resolved experiments. In contrast with earlier assignments based only on the ground-state density of states, we find that the lowest-energy resonance is dominated by the ground-state KS LUMO contribution. Indeed, comparison with the independent-particle approximation shows that the exact-exchange contribution to the kernel is essential for a correct assignment of the peaks.

authors.name: Alberto Boccuni, Vita Ilakovac, St\'ephane Carniato, Jacques Kontak-Desmarais

papers.title: Group-III doping of the p-type oxide SnO
papers.summary: Al-, Ga-, and In-doped tin monoxide (SnO) films were grown by molecular beam epitaxy. Hall measurements reveal acceptor character of all investigated group-III dopants in SnO, which correspond to theoretical calculations and previous experiments for Ga and In, but contradicts theoretical calculations predicting donor character for Al in SnO. Doping concentrations of 10e18-1e22 cm-3 were tested and maximum hole concentrations of 2e19, 3e19, and 1e19 cm-3 with doping efficiencies of 3 percent, 9 percent, and 1 percent were found for Al, Ga, and In, respectively. The observed doping limit in the mid e19 cm-3 aligns with the limits observed in literature for different dopants, hinting to fundamental aspects of the SnO defect chemistry. Due to the unexpected Al acceptor behavior, we hypothesized Al1+ being present instead of Al3+. To stabilize the higher Al3+ oxidation state, another sample series of Al-doped SnO was grown in an oxidizing atmosphere. Despite the oxidizing atmosphere, these samples showed p-type character. A more complex defect chemistry is thus expected to explain the Al acceptor character.

authors.name: Nicola Gutmann, Georg Hoffmann, Aidan Flynn Campbell, Jonas Laehnemann, Oliver Bierwagen

papers.title: Minkowski Correlation Functions (MCF): Long-range, robust shape descriptors for point patterns
papers.summary: A morphometric analysis of point patterns using Minkowski functionals is short-sighted, whereas correlation functions do not provide robust, i.e., additive shape descriptors. To combine the advantages of both standard techniques and to overcome their weaknesses, we introduce ring-based Minkowski correlation functions (MCFs) as robust and sensitive descriptors of disordered point patterns. By assigning to each point a spherical shell and quantifying the resulting two-phase morphology via Minkowski functionals, MCFs capture structural information across multiple length scales, remain sensitive at radii where conventional disk-based Minkowski functionals have saturated, and implicitly encode higher-order correlations beyond the pair correlation and structure factor. We present an exact and efficient algorithm for planar patterns extending the established disk-based morphological approach to long ranges. Applications across scales -- active colloids (Quincke rollers), longleaf pine trees, and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field -- demonstrate clear and systematic deviations from homogeneous Poisson references, with distinct responses of covered area, boundary length, and Euler characteristic. The approach combines short computation times, robustness to noise, and straightforward edge handling with clear interpretability as low-dimensional functions of the outer ring radius.

authors.name: Dominik Pabst, Michael A. Klatt, Klaus Mecke

papers.title: Structure and relaxation of long-lived odd-parity modes in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
papers.summary: In two-dimensional Fermi liquids, odd-parity deformations of the Fermi surface relax anomalously slowly at a rate $\sim T^4$, where $T$ is the temperature. However, the leading-logarithmic prediction for the magnitude of this rate $\sim m^4 \ln m$, where $m$ is an angular harmonic index, exceeds exact-diagonalization results and the $\ln m$ scaling is not observed. We resolve this discrepancy by evaluating the 2D Fermi-liquid collision integral for general regular isotropic potentials to leading order in $T/T_F$, including the nonlogarithmic term beyond the $\ln(T_F/T)$ term. We find that the local temperature modulation of the odd mode, which we call the thermal dressing, suppresses relaxation by collinear scattering, with residual relaxation set by large-angle scattering. Such large-angle processes give corrections of order $\ln m/\ln(T_F/T)$ that are not small and must be resummed. We benchmark our results against exact-diagonalization calculations for constant interactions and find agreement over a range $m^2 T/T_F \lesssim 0.4$, and we provide closed-form results for the slowest odd-mode relaxation rate of a spin-polarized dipolar gas.

authors.name: Stan Boeve, Johannes Hofmann

papers.title: Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
papers.summary: Electron transport is typically described in terms of relaxation times, which measure how quickly Fermi-surface deformations decay. We show here that the thermopower of a two-dimensional Fermi liquid instead probes the structure of these deformations in the form of their local temperature change, which we call the thermal dressing. This structure leads to an overshoot of the thermopower over its hydrodynamic value $- s/(ne)$ with increasing wave vector, before it falls to half that value in the ballistic limit. At low temperatures, the excess thermopower does not have the linear-in-temperature scaling expected of a Fermi liquid, but decreases only logarithmically as $1/\ln(T_F/T)$ at optimal wave vector. The overshoot is caused by collinear scattering, which redistributes energy over the Fermi surface and induces the thermal dressing, the strength of which grows with the angular harmonic index $m$ of the deformation. In contrast to tomographic effects in the charge conductivity, this overshoot does not rely on an odd-even effect in quasiparticle lifetimes and defines a distinct thermographic transport regime. The thermopower overshoot survives realistic disorder and should be detectable in a thermocouple with high-mobility samples.

authors.name: Johannes Hofmann

papers.title: Quantum-classical dynamical density functional theory for solvation dynamics
papers.summary: We provide a unified modeling framework for thermalization and non-equilibrium spectroscopy in overdamped polar environments. This framework extends dynamical density functional theory to describe the coupled quantum-classical evolution of a molecular electronic subsystem and an overdamped polar solvent represented by a reaction-field coordinate. The nonadiabatic dynamics is formulated in terms of an operator-valued distribution obeying a quantum-classical Ehrenfest--Smoluchowski equation which exhibits nonlinear classical diffusion and non-increasing free energy, thereby retaining detailed balance. In contrast, a quantum-classical Liouville--Smoluchowski model with quantum-classical linear diffusion develops unstable long-time behavior and fails to reach a stationary thermal state. The method is applied to a two-level model of a polar dye in three different solvents: chloroform, dichloromethane, and dimethyl sulfoxide, each differing in polarity and dielectric relaxation time. Absorption and time-resolved emission spectra are obtained from dipole-dipole correlation functions, capturing the solvent-induced spectral broadening, the dynamic Stokes shift, and the time evolution of the emission bandwidth. The calculated solvent spectral response agrees well with the experimental relaxation trends of the three solvents.

authors.name: Paul Bergold, Irene Burghardt, Francesco Di Maiolo, Cesare Tronci

papers.title: Non-Abelian Quantum Turbulence in Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensates
papers.summary: We numerically investigate statistically steady quantum turbulence in the cyclic phase of a spin-2 spinor Bose--Einstein condensate (BEC) driven by large-scale energy injection via a divergence-free external velocity field. In the full non-Abelian cyclic system, the mass-current spectrum exhibits an anomalous $k^{-7/3}$ scaling, whereas the spin-current spectrum approximately follows a $k^{-5/3}$ power law. To isolate the role of non-Abelian vortex dynamics, we compare this system with an Abelian-restricted cyclic system sharing the same Hamiltonian parameters and driving conditions. Strikingly, the Abelian restriction collapses both the mass- and spin-current spectra into a single $k^{-5/3}$ scaling, identical to that of a scalar BEC, despite the three distinct turbulent states maintaining nearly identical vortex-line densities. A Helmholtz decomposition reveals that the mass- and spin-current spectra are predominantly incompressible and transverse, respectively, thereby confirming that the anomalous scaling cannot be attributed simply to compressible fluctuations or to the transverse nature of the energy injection. Local spectral exponents further quantify these distinct scaling regimes. The disappearance of the mass-spin spectral separation under the Abelian restriction, alongside the formation of a large-scale web of rung-connected non-Abelian vortices, provides compelling evidence that non-Abelian vortex dynamics fundamentally govern the organization of turbulent mass flow.

authors.name: Michikazu Kobayashi, Masahito Ueda

papers.title: Dynamics and stability of U(1) spin liquids beyond mean-field theory: Triangular-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model
papers.summary: Quantum spin liquids (QSLs) are long-range entangled phases of frustrated magnets exhibiting fractionalised spin excitations. In two dimensions, there is limited analytical understanding of their excitation spectra beyond parton mean-field theories, which fail to capture many features of the finite frequency dynamical response. We use a self-consistent mean-field theory combined with the random phase approximation (RPA) for the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model on the triangular lattice to describe the strong spinon-spinon interactions of the U(1) Dirac QSL. We obtain quantitative results for the dynamical spin structure factor and phase diagram compatible with comprehensive numerical efforts. We show the continuum response at the Brillouin zone corners is described by a spinon-exciton hybridised with monopole gauge excitations. We further show that the transition from the QSL to 120-degree coplanar order is in the QED$_3$ O(3)-GN universality class. We extend the method to chiral QSLs and XXZ anisotropy, and discuss its broad range of applicability to other models and for describing inelastic neutron scattering experiments in KYbSe$_2$.

authors.name: Josef Willsher, Johannes Knolle

papers.title: Large Dense Thermodynamic Networks Nearly Minimize Entropy Production
papers.summary: Many have speculated whether nonequilibrium systems obey principles of maximum or minimum entropy production. In this work, we use stochastic thermodynamics to derive the condition for the minimum entropy production state (MEPS) for continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs), even far from equilibrium. We show that real nonequilibrium steady states (NESS) generally violate both the Minimum and Maximum Entropy Production (MINEP and MAXEP) principles. However, through numerical sampling of large densely-connected CTMCs, we find that as system size increases, the steady-state entropy production tends to converge to a value close to the minimum. By contrast, sparsely-connected thermodynamic networks become less efficient. This suggests that large dense nonequilibrium networks may self-organize to use thermodynamic resources efficiently, offering a nuanced perspective on the longstanding debate between MAXEP and MINEP.

authors.name: Kyle J. Ray, Alexander B. Boyd

papers.title: Strain and Correlation Modulated Magnetic Anisotropy and Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya Interaction in 2D H-FeTe$_2$
papers.summary: In the ongoing research on two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnetic materials with strong intrinsic Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction (DMI), most efforts have focused on doping, Janus engineering, or heterostructure formation to break inversion symmetry and enhance spin--orbit coupling (SOC). Here, we demonstrate that a pristine 2D material, monolayer H-FeTe$_2$, can naturally host robust DMI and magnetic anisotropy due to its intrinsic broken inversion symmetry and the strong SOC of Te atoms. We explore the effect of biaxial strain and electron correlation on H-FeTe$_2$ using first-principles DFT+$U$ calculations. We systematically investigate the Heisenberg exchange interaction, magnetic anisotropy, and DMI in the space spanned by strain and correlation. Our results reveal a distinct, non-monotonic strain dependence of both magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) and DMI, including a strain-tunable crossover between in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic easy axes. A remarkable enhancement of the in-plane DMI is observed under the combined influence of strain and strong correlations, which is unusual for pristine 2D materials and suggests a favorable regime for spintronic applications.Notably, even in the absence of strain, H-FeTe$_2$ exhibits finite DMI and considerable anisotropy, which is rare for a pure 2D material. Through these findings, we present H-FeTe$_2$ as a unique pristine 2D system with robust and tunable spin interactions for exploring fundamental spin--orbit-driven magnetic phenomena.

authors.name: Dimple Rani, B. R. K. Nanda, Prasanjit Samal

papers.title: Optimizing optimal transport: Role of final distributions in finite-time thermodynamics
papers.summary: Performing thermodynamic tasks within finite time while minimizing thermodynamic costs is a central challenge in stochastic thermodynamics. Here, we develop a unified framework for optimizing the thermodynamic cost of performing various tasks in finite time for overdamped Langevin systems. Conventional optimization of thermodynamic cost based on optimal transport theory leaves room for varying the final distributions according to the intended task, enabling further optimization. Taking advantage of this freedom, we use Lagrange multipliers to derive the optimal final distribution that minimizes the thermodynamic cost. Our framework applies to a wide range of thermodynamic tasks, including particle transport, thermal squeezing, and information processing such as information erasure, measurement, and feedback. Our results are expected to provide design principles for information-processing devices and thermodynamic machines that operate at high speed with low energetic costs.

authors.name: Kaito Tojo, Rihito Nagase, Ken Funo, Takahiro Sagawa

papers.title: Facile On-Chip Growth and Spatially Selective Color Tuning of CsPbBr$_{3}$@TFA Nanoplatelets via Ion Engineering
papers.summary: Metal halide perovskite (MHP) nanoplatelets are attractive for integrated optoelectronics because of their strong light-matter interactions and composition-tunable optical response. However, their high surface-to-volume ratio promotes surface defects and trap-assisted nonradiative recombination. In addition, their ionic nature facilitates rapid halide migration and limits selective composition tuning. Here, we combine in-synthesis (in situ) and post-synthesis ion engineering to suppress nonradiative recombination and enable selective on-chip color conversion. CsPbBr$_{3}$ nanoplatelets were grown directly on-chip via a solution process incorporating trifluoroacetate (TFA$^{-}$) pseudohalides. CsPbBr$_{3}$@TFA emits at 520 nm with a linewidth of 14.56 $\% \pm$ 0.5 nm and an average lifetime of 26.38 ns. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows that TFA$^{-}$ passivates uncoordinated Pb$^{2+}$ and suppresses metallic lead (Pb$^{0}$) formation. Spatially selective halide exchange was then achieved using a photolithographically patterned PMMA/Al$_{2}$O$_{3}$ mask to confine HCl vapor exposure. In the unmasked regions, the photoluminescence peak shifts from 520 nm to 413 nm, producing laterally defined green- and violet-emitting regions. The nanoplatelets were further integrated with graphene field-effect transistors, yielding responsivities of 2.5 x 10$^{5}$ A W$^{-1}$ at 450 nm and 1.9 x 10$^{5}$ A W$^{-1}$ at 370 nm, respectively. Our method enables scalable growth and selective color tuning of MHP nanoplatelets for on-chip optoelectronic integration.

authors.name: Sana Khan, Saeed Goudarzi, Lars Sonneveld, Felix Thiel, Stephan Sch\"affer, Bart Macco, Ke Ran, Sercan Ozen, Naho Kurahashi, Peter Haring Bol\'ivar, Felix Lang, Bruno Ehrler, Burkay Uzlu, Thomas Riedl, Gerhard M\"uller-Newen, Surendra. B. Anantharaman, Maryam Mohammadi, Max. C. Lemme

papers.title: Evidence for itinerant electron-local moment interaction in Li-doped $\alpha$-MnTe
papers.summary: We use inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to study the impact of Li doping on the semiconducting altermagnet $\alpha$-MnTe. Introducing Li reorients the ordered moment direction from in-plane to out-of-plane and increases the density of itinerant carriers. While our ARPES measurements do not indicate any notable doping-induced changes in the electronic band structure or the magnitude of the altermagnetic band splitting, our INS measurements reveal an abrupt doping-induced decrease in the spin-wave lifetime near the zone boundary at high energies. This finding is consistent with a new magnon decay channel driven by subtle, doping-induced changes in the band structure and enhanced interactions between Mn$^{2+}$ local moments and itinerant electrons. By extracting the local dynamic susceptibility from INS spectra and applying the total moment sum rule, we find that both undoped and Li-doped $\alpha$-MnTe exhibit a nearly full expected Mn$^{2+}$ local moment of $\approx5.9~\mu_\mathrm{B}$ with $S=5/2$. These findings suggest that $\alpha$-MnTe hosts robust local-moment altermagnetism which shows a breakdown at high energies upon addition of itinerant carriers, highlighting the importance of carrier-spin coupling in magneto-transport and spin dynamics of altermagnets, even in the dilute-carrier limit.

authors.name: Tingjun Zhang, Steven J. Gomez Alvarado, Sijie Xu, Thomas A. Hulse, Yucheng Guo, Shuting Peng, Travis J. Williams, Xiaoping Wang, Junhong He, Matthew B. Stone, Colin Sarkis, Feng Ye, Aaron Bostwick, Christopher Jozwiak, Eli Rotenberg, Zhaoyu Liu, Jinyulin Li, Aparna Jayakumar, Zehao Wang, Yaofeng Xie, Yiheng Wang, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Robert J. Birgeneau, Ming Yi, Pengcheng Dai

papers.title: Digital-Alloy Bragg Mirrors in High-Q Microcavities for Polariton Lasing
papers.summary: We present an approach to the molecular beam epitaxy of high-$Q$ planar GaAs-based microcavities in which the AlGaAs high-index layers of the distributed Bragg reflectors are replaced by short-period GaAs/AlAs superlattices (digital alloys) engineered to provide the same effective Al content. This design enables a significant reduction of interface roughness, precise control of both the $\lambda/4$ optical thickness and the effective Al content, suppression of the propagation of certain structural defects, and efficient tuning of the intrinsic absorption at the polariton emission wavelength through optimization of the superlattice parameters. Using this approach, we have grown a microcavity with a low polariton lasing threshold of $P_{\mathrm{th}} \approx (570 \pm 90)$ W/cm$^2$ and a high experimental quality factor of $Q_{\mathrm{expt}} \approx (5.4 \pm 0.1) \times 10^4$. This value exceeds by a factor of 2 the theoretical estimate obtained within a model in which the digital alloy is replaced by a ternary AlGaAs alloy with the same effective Al content. We demonstrate that accurate modeling of the stop-band characteristics and the $Q$ factor requires incorporation of the modified electronic density of states in the superlattice, including quantum-confinement and excitonic effects.

authors.name: V. A. Stolyarov, A. S. Kurdyubov, A. V. Trifonov, M. Yu. Petrov, I. V. Ignatiev, V. A. Lovtcius, S. A. Eliseev, Yu. P. Efimov, M. S. Lozhkin, A. V. Kavokin

papers.title: Probing Plasmonic Oscillations in 2D Moir'e Nanocrystal Superlattices by Low-Loss EELS
papers.summary: Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) has been established as a powerful analytical technique for investigating the oxidation state, band structure, and dielectric properties of materials with exceptional spatial resolution. Inspired by twisted 2D materials, we utilize low-loss EELS to examine the plasmonic excitations in 2D moir\'e Au nanocrystal superlattices (NCSLs) formed by liquid-air interface self-assembly using a double-dipping method. This approach produces stacked hexagonal layers that can be twisted, forming moir\'e patterns in NCSLs whose twist angles are precisely measured via scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Low-loss EELS effectively mitigates challenges arising from fabrication-induced non-uniformity and reveals a blue shift in plasmonic excitation when comparing single-layer, double-layer, and twisted configurations. This sharply contrasts with the optical spectroscopy measurements, which show an overall red shift relative to the EELS data. The high spatial resolution of STEM-EELS further demonstrates that twist-induced symmetry breaking strongly influences plasmonic behavior. Coupled dipole modeling explains the observed discrepancies: the electron beam excites out-of-plane polarization modes unavailable to optical probes, while optical measurements average over ensembles. Our findings highlight that EELS provides complementary information to optical spectroscopy for understanding how structural arrangements at the nanoscale influence collective electronic properties, advancing the design of plasmonic metamaterials.

authors.name: Swarnendu Das, Shengsong Yang, Kevin N. Moser, Marc R. Bourgeois, Quentin M. Ramasse, David J. Masiello, Christopher B. Murray, Eric A. Stach

papers.title: X-ray spectroscopic responses to magnetoelastic symmetry breaking in altermagnets
papers.summary: The multipole description of x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), established through the sum rules of x-ray dichroism, provides a framework to describe magnetic and orbital responses in terms of ferroic multipole order parameters. X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) is known to probe spin, orbital, and anisotropic magnetic dipole moments. Its applications to altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets have revealed that the XMCD response is often governed by the ferroic component of the photoexcited electronic states. In this work, we apply the multipole-based analysis of x-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD) to altermagnets and demonstrate that XMLD response in altermagnets can be understood as a manifestation of magnetoelastic couplings between magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments. Using symmetry analysis combined with exact diagonalization calculations of $L_{2,3}$-edge XAS, we systematically investigate representative altermagnets, including $\alpha$-MnTe, MnF$_2$, and CrSb. We show that the ferroic ordering of higher-rank magnetic multipoles, particularly spinful magnetic octupoles, gives rise to characteristic field-odd XMLD responses that directly reflect the underlying piezomagnetic response tensors allowed by magnetic point-group symmetry. Furthermore, we discuss XMCD responses induced by piezomagnetic effects, in which strain generates magnetic dipole moments. Our results establish XMLD and XMCD responses as element-specific probes of magnetoelastic multipole order in altermagnets and provide a general symmetry-based pathway to identify hidden ferroic multipoles and strain-controllable spin phenomena beyond conventional ferromagnetism.

authors.name: N. Sasabe, H. Koizumi, Y. Ishii, Y. Yamasaki

papers.title: Non-equilibrium generalized Langevin equation for multi-dimensional observables
papers.summary: The Mori-Zwanzig formalism is a powerful theoretical framework for deriving equations of motion for coarse-grained observables in the form of generalized Langevin equations (GLEs) involving evolution and projection operators. Using a time-dependent many-body Hamiltonian and a multi-dimensional Mori projection operator, we derive a non-equilibrium Mori GLE for a multi-dimensional observable of interest $\vec{A}$ that consists of a Markovian force, a non-Markovian friction force, and an orthogonal force that is often interpreted as a random force. We study the structure of the derived GLE in three limiting cases: when the components of $\vec{A}$ are uncorrelated, when the Hamiltonian is time-independent and thus the system is at equilibrium, and when both conditions are simultaneously satisfied. Our non-Markovian framework is a first step towards the systematic modeling of the coupled kinetics of coarse-grained reaction coordinates in biological complex systems, for example for the coupled intra- and inter-protein fibril dynamics of the human islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP), for which we present some illustrative molecular dynamics (MD) simulation data.

authors.name: Benjamin J. A. H\'ery (Department of Physics of Freie Universit\"at Berlin), Lucas Tepper (Department of Physics of Freie Universit\"at Berlin), Andrea Guljas (Department of Physics of Freie Universit\"at Berlin), Artem Pavlov (Institut f\"ur Chemie und Biochemie of Freie Universit\"at Berlin), Beate Koksch (Institut f\"ur Chemie und Biochemie of Freie Universit\"at Berlin), Cecilia Clementi (Department of Physics of Freie Universit\"at Berlin), Roland R. Netz (Department of Physics of Freie Universit\"at Berlin)

papers.title: Symmetry-Resolved Spectral Weight Reveals Charge Localization in Correlated Insulator
papers.summary: Can crystalline symmetry reveal where charge localizes in a strongly correlated insulator? We show that occupied symmetry-resolved spectral weights of the exact electronic Green's function define effective atomic limits. In an interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, their displacement tracks the spin-resolved many-body polarization across distinct insulating phases. A quantum metric of the one-body reduced density matrix provides a complementary geometric characterization. Our results extend real-space symmetry analysis beyond occupied-band projectors.

authors.name: Theo N. Dionne, Maia G. Vergniory

papers.title: Rippled graphene pores as fluidic memristive devices with synaptic and neuromorphic functionalities
papers.summary: Nanofluidic memristive devices work with nanoscale pores and ions dissolved in water, which harness the ionic memory effect aiming to store and process information. These devices share the same charge carriers as biological systems and bring hope for better emulating the neural functions and developing ionic circuits for neuromorphic applications. Specially, theory and experiments suggest that nanoconfinement is essential for inducing a memory effect, which places limit on the pore size to nm-scale or smaller. Such devices are difficult to scale up with precision and operate with long-term stability. Here, we show that a micrometer size pore, generally expected to exhibit a linear ion transport, can display a pronounced memory effect, if its rim is wrapped by strongly curved and tightly stacked graphene. We attribute the observation to slow ion dynamics confined in the rippled graphene edges. The devices are easy to scale up and integrate into fluidic circuits. The memory effect is ion-selective and exhibits long endurance comparable to the lifetime of synaptic proteins, which enables reversible modification of the conductance states using programmable voltage spikes and various electrolytes over a long time, akin to biological synaptic plasticity. Thanks to this plasticity, our devices and their integrated circuits enable storing, transmitting and processing information with high reliability, fidelity and accuracy, as evidenced in the identification of both greyscale and color images, and in the real-time analysis of emulated neural signals. Our results highlight nanoscale morphology of the pore wall as an important parameter regulating ion transport and indicate that the stringent nanoconfinement for ionic memory can be lifted from restricting the pore size to designing its rim structure. The devices and their integrated circuits may find use in ionic neuromorphic applications.

authors.name: Wenzhe Zhou, Dongjiao Ge, Ao Zhang, Jincheng Xu, Yu Ji, Yiran Gong, Wenchang Zhang, Jidong Li, Li Lin, Zhiping Xu, Pengzhan Sun

papers.title: Spectral Diagnostics of Higher-Order Structural Reorganization in Finite Statistical Systems
papers.summary: Phase transitions are conventionally characterized by thermodynamic observables, but they also entail a reorganization of statistical structure. In finite systems, third-order pseudo-transitions reveal additional structural reorganization preceding or accompanying conventional criticality. Here we use the eigen-microstate approach to diagnose this reorganization from the full distribution of normalized spectral weights. Central moments about the uniform weight level characterize spectral concentration and asymmetric large-weight deviations, while spectral projection exposes residual organization after dominant modes are removed. Applications to Ising and Potts models on regular lattices and random regular networks reveal ordered-side modal redistribution and critical-window residual-weight reorganization that are not captured by leading-mode condensation alone. The resolvability of these features depends on the number of states, topology, and spectral truncation. High-temperature extrema in finite Wolff ensembles are sampling-protocol sensitive and are therefore not assigned equilibrium pseudo-transition temperatures. These results show that full and projected eigen-microstate spectra provide complementary diagnostics of higher-order structural organization.

authors.name: Wei Liu, Songzhi Lv, Xin Zhang, Fangfang Wang, Kai Qi, Zengru Di

papers.title: Electronic structure, quasiparticle renormalizations, and magnetic correlations in the alternating single-layer bilayer nickelate La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$
papers.summary: Using DFT+DMFT we study the electronic structure and magnetic correlations in the recently discovered alternating single-layer bilayer Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$ (1212-LNO). Our results exhibit qualitative differences for the structurally distinct single-layer and bilayer Ni ions, implying the importance of confinement and orbital-dependent correlations. The Ni $e_g$ states originating from the bilayer Ni ions form strongly renormalized quasiparticle bands with a large enhancement factor $m^*/m \sim 3.5$ and 4.2 for the Ni $x^2-y^2$ and $3z^2-r^2$ orbitals. Moreover, the $e_g$ states of the single-layer Ni ions exhibit an orbital-selective Mott insulating state, with a narrow energy gap for the Ni $3z^2-r^2$ states and metallic, strongly non-Fermi-liquid Ni $x^2-y^2$ ones. Our analysis of magnetic correlations suggests the formation of intertwined spin and charge density wave stripes in the bilayer NiO$_6$ slab, in close similarity to the double-layer material.
