We identify two major instabilities: a leading one associated with a propagating wave vector ${\bf Q}=(\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3})$ ("up-down-0" spin pattern or "$d^8$-$d^8$-$d^8\underline{L}$'' charge-density wave with Ni $d^8\underline{L}$ ions bonded in an interlayer spin polaron), competing with $(\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{4})$ ("up-up-down-down") stripe state. The single-layer Ni $3d$ electrons exhibit an instability toward the N\'eel magnetic state. Under pressure, 1212-LNO undergoes an orbital-selective Mott insulator-to-metal transition, associated with metallization of the single-layer Ni $e_g$ states. The single-layer Ni $e_g$ bands exhibit non-Fermi-liquid behavior with strongly incoherent spectral weights near $E_F$. We note that correlation effects result in a crossover from single-layer (as obtained within DFT) to double-layer dominated magnetic correlations.

authors.name: I. V. Leonov

papers.title: Monte Carlo study of the superfluid phase of $^4$He
papers.summary: Detailed numerical results obtained with state-of-the-art Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations are presented for the superfluid phase of He-4 at saturated vapor pressure. The aim of this contribution is that of providing reliable, up-to-date estimates for this archetypal superfluid, reflecting the methodological progress that has taken place over the past two decades. We simulate a system comprising 2,048 helium atoms, i.e., an order of magnitude greater in size than those for which results currently regarded as standard references were originally obtained. We offer revised estimates for energetic and structural properties, as well as for the ground state condensate fraction.

authors.name: Massimo Boninsegni

papers.title: Nonlinear frequency shift and bistability of magnon-polarons
papers.summary: We investigate the nonlinear dynamics of strongly coupled surface acoustic waves (SAWs) and spin waves (SWs) in a magnetoacoustic resonator based on a YIG/ZnO heterostructure by combining microwave reflection measurements with microfocused Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy. In the linear regime, the electrical response reveals clear hybridization between standing SAW cavity modes and finite-wave-vector SWs, resulting in pronounced avoided crossings. At elevated drive powers, the hybrid system exhibits a strongly field-dependent nonlinear response characterized by a positive frequency shift of the driven SW mode. Using the vector Hamiltonian formalism for nonlinear spin-wave dynamics, we show that this shift is dominated by a cross-shift term. In our resonator geometry, this contribution becomes significant because the standing SAW cavity mode simultaneously excites counterpropagating SWs with wave vectors $+k$ and $-k$. For suitable field detuning, the nonlinear shift drives the SW mode into resonance with the SAW excitation, leading to a strong enhancement of the magnon population, broadband nonlinear scattering, and bistable foldover behavior. Beyond the foldover threshold, both the magnon and phonon responses stabilize. These results establish SAW-driven $k \neq 0$ magnon-phonon hybrids as a promising platform for nonlinear magnetoacoustics and wave-based information processing.

authors.name: Kevin K\"unstle, Matthias Wagner, Philipp Knaus, Yannik Kunz, Ephraim Spindler, Katharina Lasinger, Matthias R. Schweizer, Philipp Pirro, John F. Gregg, Mathias Weiler

papers.title: Bounds on the Entropy Production in Stochastic Resetting with Harmonic Traps
papers.summary: We study the entropy production associated with stochastic resetting of a Brownian particle in an optical trap, where resetting is implemented by increasing the trap stiffness to restore a localized distribution. We interpret the dynamics as a thermodynamic cycle consisting of thermal expansion during diffusion and compression performed by an external resetting agent. Within this framework, we distinguish between the irreversibility of the resetting cycle and the additional entropy production associated with its physical implementation. We establish a lower bound based on the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between forward and reversed trajectory ensembles. For a harmonic trap, this divergence can be expressed entirely in terms of the probability distributions before and after resetting, independently of the resetting protocol. An upper bound is obtained by adding the operational entropy production associated with instantaneous compression, quantified by its excess work relative to quasistatic resetting, to the KL contribution. For free diffusion between resetting events, we derive explicit analytical expressions for both contributions to the entropy-production rate as functions of the resetting rate. Remarkably, they approach the same finite value in the limit of vanishing resetting rate, as the increasing entropy production per cycle compensates for the decreasing frequency of resetting events. At high resetting rates, both contributions vanish as the particle remains effectively confined to its initial distribution, with little time to spread between resets.

authors.name: Oded Farago

papers.title: Impact of capacity volatility and input substitutability on supply chain resilience
papers.summary: Supply chains are inherently vulnerable to stochastic shocks due to their sequential dependence on production. Employing the Feld-Barthelemy (FB) framework [Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf 134} 217401 (2025)], we investigate how capacity volatility and input substitutability determine critical demand that a supply network can withstand. By controlling the variance in production capacity, we show that reducing capacity volatility is more effective than increasing average capacity in long supply chains, highlighting the necessity of firm-level stabilization. In the extended FB model that incorporates substitute suppliers, we find that diversifying suppliers independently increases critical demand, even when average production capacity remains constant. Surprisingly, improving network connectivity can also increase critical demand without changing the number of suppliers. This implies that the effect of input substitutability on critical demand is heavily influenced by network topology, even in the absence of stock. Our findings reveal that mitigating capacity volatility and securing structural diversity in supply routes are just as crucial to supply chain resilience as expanding stock capacity.

authors.name: Jaeseok Hur, Juha Jang, Meesoon Ha, Hawoong Jeong

papers.title: Double quantum spin Hall phase in bilayer ZrTe$_5$
papers.summary: Quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulators host helical edge states that enable dissipationless transport, but realizing multiple conducting channels in experimentally accessible materials with large band gaps remains challenging. Here, we show that AB-stacked untwisted bilayer ZrTe$_5$ naturally realizes a double QSH phase in its energetically most stable structure, revealing an unexpected multichannel transport regime. The phase hosts two pairs of helical edge states and a doubled quantized spin Hall conductivity, with spin Chern number $C_s=2$ despite the conventional $\mathbb{Z}_2=0$ classification. Lattice deformation tunes the system through a metallic state to a conventional QSH phase with $\mathbb{Z}_2=1$, enabling control of the number of helical channels. Remarkably, the quantized spin Hall response persists over an energy window substantially larger than the bulk band gap, exceeding 100~meV. Our results establish bilayer ZrTe$_5$ as an experimentally accessible multichannel QSH system in which interlayer coupling and lattice deformation control topological edge transport.

authors.name: Chao Chen Ye, G\'abor Kalla, Marcio Costa, Jianting Ye, Jagoda S{\l}awi\'nska

papers.title: Competing redox and material redistribution during electrode ageing
papers.summary: Electrochemical processes can involve coupled redox reactions, active-material redistribution and morphological evolution at buried electrode-electrolyte interfaces1-3. Operando imaging has revealed nanoscale heterogeneity in these processes3-9, but how reversible redox and cumulative material redistribution interact during cycles to govern electrode ageing remains unclear. Here we develop fast operando soft X-ray spectro-ptychography to track oxidation state, morphology and iron redistribution in the same nanoscale region of an alkaline iron anode over 20 h of cycling. We distinguish two coexisting processes operating on different timescales. Within each cycle, iron undergoes rapid, reversible conversion between metallic iron and iron oxyhydroxide (FeOOH) with little net iron redistribution. Across cycles, slower iron redistribution, consistent with dissolution and redeposition, promotes FeOOH-rich particle growth. Particle-resolved trajectories reveal that reversible conversion and iron accumulation coexist within individual particles, while particles with similar apparent growth exhibit markedly different changes in iron content. Local capacity initially increases as particles grow, then declines as more iron remains oxidized after charging and the reversible redox swing narrows. These findings suggest that cumulative Fe redistribution competes with reversible redox by progressively limiting the Fe available for charge storage. More generally, electrode ageing can begin during nearly reversible cycling, before capacity loss becomes apparent.

authors.name: Xiao Zhao, Yuchen Cao, Evan Z Carlson, Angel Burgos, Daniel Jacobs, Hanfeng Zhong, Lily Taylor, Haozhi Sha, Feng-yang Chen, Yu Shan, Hendrik Ohldag, Alexander Ditter, Jos\'e A. Rodriguez, David Shapiro, William Chueh, Jianwei Miao

papers.title: Quasiclassical theory of nonlinear response in d-wave superconductors
papers.summary: Motivated by recent THz pump-probe experiments in unconventional superconductors, in this paper we use Keldysh--Nambu quasiclassical theory of $d$-wave superconductors to analyze the third-harmonic generation. A systematic perturbative solution of the out-of-equilibrium Eilenberger equation for the Keldysh propagator is developed with respect to the amplitude of an external electromagnetic field. We show that in a clean superconductor and for a spatially uniform electromagnetic field third harmonic response is absent. In the presence of elastic impurity scattering which we treat using the self-consistent scattering matrix approximation in the Born limit we find that the third-harmonic current density is a sum of the Higgs (amplitude) mode and quasiparticle contributions. We compute their dependence on disorder, temperature, frequency and polarization of external radiation.

authors.name: Aidan Steineman, Samuel Awelewa, Maxim Dzero

papers.title: Mapping the Growth of Two-Dimensional $\pi$-Conjugated Polymers on Au(111): Organometallic Intermediates and Edge Terminations
papers.summary: Kagome lattices provide an exciting space for the exploration of graphene-like $\pi$-conjugated molecular systems with flat bands. Using heterotriangulene-derived precursors, along with an on-surface Ullmann coupling process, makes growing polymers with Kagome lattices accessible and straightforward. Here, we use scanning tunneling microscopy alongside high-resolution atomic force microscopy to examine the evolution of tribromotrioxaazatriangulene on Au(111) into ordered, covalent films. Using density functional theory and scanning probe methods, we find previously unreported organometallic intermediate states involving Au adatoms incorporated within the growing polymer lattice. We also find that a majority of polymer edges remain brominated up to 250 $^{\circ}$C and a large number of edges bonded to Au adatoms coordinated to an adjacent bromine atom. These observations suggest that residual bromine could play a role in stabilizing the polymer edges to Au adatoms and thereby influence the growth pathways that lead to ordered Kagome polymer lattices.

authors.name: Simon W. Briesenick, Wyatt A. Behn, Manuel Gonz\'alez Lastre, Chang Wan Kang, Pablo Pou, Ekaterina D. Ulyanov, Rub\'en P\'erez, Dmytro F. Perepichka, Peter Grutter

papers.title: Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d-wave superconductor: a quantum Monte Carlo study
papers.summary: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating N\'eel state and the nodal $d$-wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background $\pi$-flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the N\'eel and $d$-wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the $d$-wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.

authors.name: Chuang Chen, Subir Sachdev, Zi Yang Meng

papers.title: Local moment magnon spectrum in conduction electron tunnelling
papers.summary: The surface tunnelling spectrum of a dual system consisting of localised moments with antiferromagnetic order coupled to conduction electrons by on-site exchange interaction is investigated. In the static approximation of the local moment order it is known that magnetic band reconstruction leads to an anomalous tunnelling spectrum at the magnetic ordering vector of local moments although the latter cannot contribute directly. In this work we consider dynamic effects by including the scattering of conduction electrons from the local moment magnon excitations. They lead to self energies and renormalisation of conduction states which in turn appreciably modify the tunnelling spectrum beyond the influence of static order, interpreted as the appearance of magnon sidebands.

authors.name: Peter Thalmeier, Alireza Akbari

papers.title: 2D Transport in an in-plane magnetic field
papers.summary: A parallel in-plane magnetic field could, in principle, distinguish between two competing physical scenarios for the experimentally observed density-tuned 2D metal-insulator transition (where decreasing the carrier density leads to a crossover from an effective metal to an effective insulator): Wigner crystallization or Anderson localization. Since the main scattering mechanism in 2D doped semiconductors arises from screened random charged impurities and screening in turn depends on the electronic density of states, the in-plane magnetic field could distinguish between the two by decreasing screening through spin polarization and this enhances the effective critical density for Anderson localization compared with Wigner crystallization. We give the general theory and provide results for the quantitative magnitudes of the spin polarization effect on the transition density by focusing on two recent experiments [Z. Ge, et al, Nature (London) 654, 902 (2026), T. Han, et al, arXiv:2604.00113], noting that the critical density may actually decrease if the dominant scattering is by short-ranged defects instead of long-ranged charged impurities. The difference between the two cases arises from whether spin polarization dominates screening (enhanced critical density) or the Fermi surface (suppressed critical density).

authors.name: Aryaman Babbar, Sankar Das Sarma

papers.title: Perspectives on inverse design for AI magnonics
papers.summary: Inverse design - specifying a desired functionality and letting a computational algorithm search for a structure that meets it - has emerged as a powerful paradigm for magnonic device engineering. In this article, we survey the rapidly growing field of inverse-design magnonics, organising it along two axes: the design variables (topology, material parameters, and magnetic field landscape) and the algorithmic toolbox (gradient-free, gradient-based, and neural-network-based methods) together with the differentiable micromagnetic solvers that enable them. We then identify open frontiers that we consider most promising for the next phase of the field: sensitivity analysis and robust design to bridge the gap between simulation and experiment; input shaping and transducer optimisation; the incorporation of nonlinear spin-wave effects as an explicit design resource; spatially structured amplification; self-adapting media and machine-learning-based design; and the long-term vision of a universal, reconfigurable magnonic platform. We argue that magnonics and artificial intelligence (AI) are converging from two directions - machine-learning tools for designing magnonic devices, and magnonic devices as hardware for neuromorphic computation - and propose the term AI magnonics to describe this emerging paradigm.

authors.name: Franz Vilsmeier, Florian Bruckner, Claas Abert, Dieter Suess, Andrii V. Chumak

papers.title: Predictive Renormalization-Group Theory of Universality Classes in Nonlinear Systems
papers.summary: Universal scaling behavior appears across a wide range of nonlinear systems despite substantial differences in their governing equations and physical mechanisms. We develop a renormalization-group (RG) framework that identifies two complementary RG mechanisms underlying such universality. First, scale invariance generates RG fixed points corresponding to asymptotic self-similar solutions. Second, repeated RG transformations eliminate non-scale-invariant irrelevant structures, causing broad classes of equations to flow toward the same fixed points and thereby form universality classes. The framework applies to finite-time singularities, long-time intermediate asymptotics, stochastic Edwards--Wilkinson growth, nonlinear diffusion, density-dependent biological diffusion, and fluid-interface dynamics. In each case, it reproduces known scaling behavior and identifies the associated universality class through explicit irrelevance criteria. A central feature of the framework is its predictive character. Once a scale-invariant fixed point is identified, the theory predicts whole classes of nonlinear equations sharing the same asymptotic self-similar solution. While the diffusion class is partially supported by existing mathematically rigorous results, most universality classes identified here have not previously been established and therefore constitute testable predictions. These results provide a unified RG perspective on universality in nonlinear systems and show that universality emerges from the same fundamental RG principles that underlie critical phenomena.

authors.name: Ko Okumura

papers.title: Flux Jamming and Bimodal Dynamics in Bounded Spin Networks
papers.summary: Finite-sized frustrated magnetic networks relax through pathways that are strongly shaped by their boundaries; yet, whether their kinetic barriers can be predicted from geometry alone has remained unclear. Here, we present a transfer matrix framework for finite artificial square ice that links local coordination to the effective energy landscape and the temperature-dependent barriers governing magnetic flux transport. By combining nonhomogeneous transfer matrices with the local coordination hierarchy, we identify the geometric bottlenecks that govern the relaxation dynamics, and show that the leading steady-state weight falls on charge-neutral, ice-rule configurations, which are thermodynamically preferred due to their reduced electrostatic energy and greater configurational multiplicity. The resulting two time-scale structure suggests bimodal behavior: (1) long intervals of trapping in charge-compensated manifolds are interrupted by (2) sudden avalanche-like relaxation events. Applied to Husimi-tree representations, the framework yields a low-temperature initial arrest probability that collapses across forty generations onto a common scaling function of $g-\xi(T)$, with a crossover length $\xi \sim T^{-\nu}$ and $\nu=1$. These results show that boundary geometry alone can produce kinetic arrest and suggest intermittent transport, even in the absence of quenched disorder, reminiscent of athermal granular jamming. More broadly, our framework connects the coordination landscape, equilibrium energetics, and nonequilibrium relaxation in finite frustrated magnets and provides a route to understanding boundary-controlled dynamics in artificial spin ice.

authors.name: Paula Mellado, Hanu Arava

papers.title: Superfluid helium
papers.summary: We present a mathematically solvable toy model of the phase transition between the normal liquid and superfluid phases of helium--4, and use it to show how a symmetry-based order parameter can be obtained for the superfluid. We also present a range of models in which one can obtain sharp bounds on the transition between the normal liquid and gas phases, arbitrarily close to the superfluid.

authors.name: Charles Radin

papers.title: Non-Equilibrium Instantaneous Approximation and Dipole Forbidden d-d Transitions
papers.summary: Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy provides direct access to pump-induced changes in the electronic structure of correlated materials, but its theoretical description generally requires computationally demanding two-time non-equilibrium calculations. We introduce an instantaneous approximation for pump-driven correlated systems, based on a separation between the rapid decay of the Green's functions in the relative time variable and their slower evolution in the average time. Combined with a one-shot dynamical mean-field construction at the Hubbard I level, the method incorporates the driven dynamics of the local correlated shell into the lattice Green's function while retaining momentum resolution. We also derive an effective coupling for nominally dipole-forbidden d-d excitations. It arises from a dipole-allowed d-p transition followed by p-d hybridization; beyond the instantaneous limit, the same process produces an energy-dependent vertex correction to the optical response. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to paramagnetic and antiferromagnetic FePS3, using a density-functional theory derived tight-binding model together with a supercell unfolding procedure. The calculated momentum-resolved spectra reproduce the main qualitative features observed after excitation of the first and second d-d transitions in recent time-resolved photoemission experiments.

authors.name: Marco Marino, Lasse Sternemann, Mirko Cinchetti, Frithjof B. Anders

papers.title: Chiral Spinterfaces as an Overlooked Component of the Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity Effect
papers.summary: The chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect is commonly associated with spin-selective transport through chiral molecules, while the role of molecule-electrode interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that adsorption of chiral amino acid derived molecules on ferromagnetic Ni films with native NiO layer induces a remanent chirality-dependent magneto-optical response. Systematic control experiments establish that this response originates from the molecule-NiO/Ni interface, rather than the molecular layer or bulk ferromagnet. First-principles calculations reveal preferential carboxylate binding and interfacial charge redistribution extending into the NiO surface layers, demonstrating how molecular adsorption modifies the electronic structure of the oxide. Together, these results provide evidence for the formation of chiral spinterfaces, where molecular chirality and interfacial electronic structure give rise to a distinct magnetic response. Our findings highlight the previously overlooked role of molecule-electrode interfaces in CISS-related systems and identify interfacial electronic and magnetic properties as important considerations for understanding and controlling spin selectivity.

authors.name: Franziska Sch\"olzel, Ayb\"uke G\"ulkaya, Rico Ehrler, Dominik Hornig, Lokesh Rasabathina, Aleksandra Lindner, J\"urgen Lindner, Aleksandr Kazimir, Christina Lamers, Dietrich R. T. Zahn, Michael Mehring, Olav Hellwig, Shuxia Tao, Georgeta Salvan

papers.title: Thermodynamic Realizability of Hidden Markov Processes: Attainment, Observable Certificates, an Architecture-Independent Floor, and the Price of Architecture
papers.summary: What is the least dissipative finite Markov machine that reproduces a given stochastic process exactly? We show that a minimizing sequence cannot escape through diverging rates at any fixed hidden dimension: vanishing states can be traced out and fast clusters contracted without raising entropy production or changing the observed path law, so the exact-law cost $V_n(P)$ is attained and lower semicontinuous with no cap on rates or activity. A positive price per hidden state yields an optimum over all dimensions, represented exactly as a supremum of globally calibrated observable certificates, and an architecture phase diagram whose slope is the selected state count. We then bound the diagram from below uniformly in architecture. Every Markov jump process has a reversible companion on the same states whose path law is within relative entropy $T\sigma/4$ of the original on windows of length $T$. Combined with a Loewner-order estimate for reversible sojourn cycle operators, this gives $\sigma \ge 4 r_C D_{\rm CM}(f_C)$ for every finite realization of any size, where $f_C$ is an observed sojourn density and $D_{\rm CM}$ its relative entropy from the completely monotone cone, a convex program with a dual certificate. For a time-symmetric two-block renewal family $P_q$ this gives $V_\infty(P_q)>0$ for all $0<q<1$, with $V_\infty(P_{1/20}) \ge 0.1025$. The v1 conjecture $V_\infty(P_{1/20})=0$ is false, and complexity-assisted approach to reversibility is excluded. Exact rational realizations with four to six phases show that the three-state machine is not optimal: $V_7(P_{1/20}) \le 2.73611 < (1-q)\log(1/q)$.

authors.name: Murad Aznagulov

papers.title: Probing proximity-induced superconductivity in bilayer graphene using gate-defined quantum dots
papers.summary: Van der Waals heterostructures enable the combination of two-dimensional (2D) materials with different electronic properties in a single device. Bilayer graphene (BLG) is particularly attractive as its electrically tunable band gap enables local control of tunnel barriers and quantum dots (QDs). Here, we realize an all-2D hybrid platform based on BLG proximitized by superconducting NbSe$_2$. Using electrostatic gates, we define tunnel barriers and QDs at different distances from the superconductor-semiconductor interface. The QDs serve as local spectroscopic probes of the proximitized BLG channel, forming tunable superconductor-quantum dot-normal conductor junctions. Coulomb blockade and finite-bias spectroscopy reveal a proximity-induced superconducting gap of up to $80\,\mathrm{\mu eV}$ and allow to track its evolution with distance from the NbSe$_2$ contact. The local density of states remains suppressed over distances exceeding $1\,\mu$m. Our results demonstrate the potential of BLG-superconductor hybrids as a tunable platform combining QDs and quantum point contacts with superconductivity.

authors.name: Philipp Schmidt, Mathies Funke, Till Tenger, Katarina Stanojevi\'c, Hubert Dulisch, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Fabian Hassler, Christian Volk, Szabolcs Csonka, Christoph Stampfer

papers.title: Logarithmic Quasi-Long-Range Order and Novel Continuous Phase Transition in the Two-Dimensional XY Model with $1/r^4$ Interaction
papers.summary: We investigate the phase diagram and critical properties of the two-dimensional classical XY model with interactions decaying as $1/r^{2+\sigma}$. At the marginal case $\sigma=2$, we show that the low-$T$ phase is characterized by logarithmic quasi-long-range order (log-QLRO), where spin correlations decay algebraically with the logarithm of distance as $C(r)\sim(\ln r)^{-\eta_\ell}$ with $\eta_\ell\propto T$, and that the transition into this phase is a continuous transition beyond both the Ginzburg-Landau-Wilson paradigm and the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless mechanism. Our analysis combines a near-exact Gaussian spin-wave theory, an adiabatic renormalization-group analysis, and large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. We find that the $1/r^4$ interaction logarithmically modifies the spin-wave stiffness kernel as $\gamma(k)\simeq\kappa k^2\ln(1/k)$, which suppresses vortex proliferation and gives rise to a nonuniversal correlation-length exponent $\nu \simeq 1/\sqrt{2\pi\kappa}$. Crucially, our simulations reveal that the short-range algebraic QLRO phase is unstable against an arbitrarily weak long-range perturbation for $\sigma\le2$. These results establish $\sigma=2$ as the crossover boundary between the long-range and short-range universality classes and resolve the long-standing controversy over the phase diagram.

authors.name: Xianzhi Pan, Zhijie Fan, Youjin Deng

papers.title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
papers.summary: A liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) exhibits a two-way coupling between its mesogen order and network elasticity: the mesogen order sets the undeformed network conformation, and the network deformation reorients the mesogens. This coupling gives rise to large, reversible stimuli-responsive actuation, as well as to soft elasticity, a finite deformation at nearly zero stress. This article reviews the elastic theory of ideal LCEs, bridging single-chain statistics and continuum constitutive models. The "ideal" elastic behavior rests on the assumption of anisotropic Gaussian chains that retain no memory of the crosslinking state, such that the director can rotate at no cost of free energy when accompanied by a corresponding stress-free, ground-state deformation. The resulting neo-classical free energy of a monodomain LCE, when minimized over the director, is non-quasi-convex, with a continuous family of stress-free ground states, leading to thermally induced spontaneous deformation and soft elasticity accommodated by coexisting stripe domains. The quasi-convex relaxation of the free energy classifies the behavior of polydomain LCEs into three phases, each with a distinct macroscopic mechanical response depending on the stretch state. The ideal elastic theory can be further extended to incorporate additional behaviors and physical processes, including thermo- and photomechanical coupling, Frank elasticity from director distortion, semi-soft or non-soft behavior arising from network nonideality, and temperature- and rate-dependent viscoelasticity.

authors.name: Zumrat Usmanova, Ruobing Bai

papers.title: Spin Space Symmetry Without Spin Space Groups
papers.summary: Spin space groups provide a complete symmetry classification of magnetic structures in the non-relativistic limit. Each spin space group with a given parent space group is specified, up to spin-only symmetries, by a real representation of that space group acting in spin space. We argue that working directly with this representation not only avoids the construction and identification of the group, but also organizes and simplifies the resulting symmetry constraints on allowed responses. The presence or absence of magnetic compensation, piezomagnetism, spin and charge transport, the Edelstein effect, and momentum-space spin textures becomes an ordinary problem in the representation theory of space groups. The conditions reduce to overlaps between the three exterior powers of the defining representation and multipole representations of the point group. Several physically distinct responses then reduce to the same condition: a $p$-wave spin texture and the time-even Edelstein effect are allowed together, as are piezomagnetism and a $d$-wave spin texture in compensated order. The wave-vector content of the exterior powers gives a hierarchy of selection rules: depending on the power, a uniform response requires one, two, or three ordering wave vectors to sum to a reciprocal lattice vector. A non-relativistic anomalous Hall effect in compensated order at zero wave vector requires a defining representation built from three one-dimensional irreducible representations, a purely odd-parity spin texture requires a pair of nonzero ordering wave vectors that cancel, and coplanar order at nonzero wave vector in the interior of the Brillouin zone is always a $p$-wave magnet. We illustrate the approach with collinear, coplanar and non-coplanar magnets, and discuss extensions to magnetic space groups, connections to Landau theories of collinear order, and the characterization of odd-parity magnets.

authors.name: Jeffrey G. Rau

papers.title: Origin and photoluminescence of a shallow hydrogen-related donor in silicon
papers.summary: Paramagnetic color centers in silicon are being investigated recently for use in quantum technologies. While the origin of most of the prominent photoluminescence (PL) lines are well understood, that is not the case for those connected to hydrogen, even though it is almost always present in silicon, e.g., shallow hydrogen-related donors (SHDs), but their atomic structure remains elusive. Recent experiments suggested connection between the SHDs and the so-called X and the B$_i$ (or X$_i$) PL-lines. An SHD, termed the MT2 center, was tentatively assigned to a bistable, negative-U defect, arising due to the interaction of hydrogen with the self-interstitial complex I$_4$. Using high-level density functional theory calculations, we investigate the interaction of hydrogen with self-interstitial complexes In. A shallow effective-mass-theory donor arises when hydrogen attacks a Si-Si bond in I$_n$, inserting itself as a bond-center interstitial (I$_n$H$_{BC}$) in an exothermic reaction. We demonstrate this in the case of a single self-interstitial and of a complex of four. The latter I$_\mathrm{4}$H$_\mathrm{BC}$ complex shows electronic, spin and PL properties remarkably close to MT2. We find that hydrogen in the presence of I$_4$ follows the same behavior as in pristine silicon, i.e., it is a negative-U bistable defect, only detectable under illumination. In the I$_4$H$_{BC}$ complex, H can hop via photo-assisted mechanism between equivalent BC sites of the I$_4$ complex, leading to a motional averaged tetragonal symmetry as experimentally observed for MT2. The zero-phonon line is distinct from the X-line (attributed to the bare I$_4$ complex), and falls well into the range of the X$_i$ lines. Our results identify the I$_4$H complex as a prototype for a class of SHDs, inferring that similar SHDs may arise, with the X$_i$ lines as their PL fingerprints, when H attacks I$_n$ clusters.

authors.name: Miaomiao Han, Peter Deak, Bing Huang, Adam Gali

papers.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
papers.summary: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. The charge transition level is found at VBM$+$0.08~eV, conclusively ruling out the previously proposed association with the B3 EPR center and its correlated deep donor level. Most significantly, we identify a metastable spin-1 triplet excited state separated from the singlet by $\sim$1.6~meV, consistent with the NL51 EPR signal. The $D_{2d}$ symmetry of the defect suppresses intersystem crossing and phosphorescence by first-order spin--orbit coupling, implying an exceptionally long spin--lattice relaxation time. Combined with a spectrally resolvable zero-field splitting and near-infrared emission, the triplet state of the I$_4$ complex constitutes a viable spin quantum memory intrinsic to silicon.

authors.name: Miaomiao Han, Song Li, Gerg\H{o} Thiering, Thomas Frauenheim, Peter De\'ak, Bing Huang, Adam Gali

papers.title: Ambient-pressure superconductivity in bulk single crystals of La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{10}$
papers.summary: Superconductivity in the Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelates has so far been confined either to multilayer compounds under high pressure or to square-planar infinite-layer-type films stabilized by epitaxial strain. Here, we report the high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) growth of bulk single crystals of the quadruple-layer RP nickelate La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{13}$ ($n=4$) and reproduce the quintuple-layer La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{16}$ ($n=5$) synthesis, phases previously accessible only as thin films. Topotactic reduction of La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{13}$ single crystals with CaH$_2$ yields the square-planar La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{10}$, which we show to be a bulk, ambient-pressure superconductor with $T_\mathrm{c}^\mathrm{onset}\approx18.7$\,K, a shielding fraction above 60\%, and a specific-heat jump that confirms a bulk pairing transition. In transport, all crystals show an anomaly near 90~K reminiscent of a density-wave like transition, which may arise from a partially gapped Fermi surface or from the non-superconducting volume fraction. The upper critical field shows a small anisotropy, $\gamma \approx 2.4$, which remains finite as $T \to T_c$, indicating three-dimensional superconductivity with substantial coupling between the four-layer blocks. These results identify the square-planar nickelates $R_{n+1}$Ni$_n$O$_{2n+2}$ as a bulk platform in which the layer number alone tunes the nickel valence into the superconducting regime, without chemical substitution, pressure, or epitaxial constraint.

authors.name: R. Zhang, P. Reiss, A. Krajewska, M. Isobe, H. Takagi, P. Puphal

papers.title: Two Unconventional Hall Effects in the Kagome Magnet TmMn4Cr$_2$Sn$_6$
papers.summary: We identify two Hall anomalies in the kagome magnet TmMn$_4$Cr$_2$Sn$_6$. We propose that the high-field anomaly reflects a discontinuous spin reorientation and differing sublattice contributions to Hall transport and magnetization. At low fields, Hall hysteresis persists despite negligible magnetic hysteresis, suggesting a chirality-related contribution, although its microscopic origin remains unresolved. These contrasting regimes show how magnetic transitions can mimic unconventional Hall signals and highlight the limits of magnetization-based Hall decomposition.

authors.name: Mohamed El Gazzah, Fehmi Sami Yasin, Bishal Thapa, Sk Jamaluddin, Daniel Lu, Abhijeet Nayak, Resham Babu Regmi, Mary Katherine Carroll, Igor I. Mazin, Nirmal J. Ghimire

papers.title: Topological Hybridization Gaps from Molecular Orbitals Coupled to Dirac Fermions
papers.summary: A magnetically gapped topological-insulator surface carries a half-quantized Hall response. We show that hybridizing the surface Dirac fermions with a flat band of chiral orbitals adds an integer to it: spin-momentum locking forces the hybridization to wind around the band-crossing ring, opening a topological gap. For orbitals with total angular momentum $j$, rotational symmetry fixes the surface Hall conductivity to $je^2/h$, with the sign set by the Dirac branch crossed and independent of the sign of the Dirac mass. The result survives crystal-field quenching of the orbital moment, with the winding then set by interference between hybridization pathways. First-principles calculations for a monolayer of nitric oxide adsorbed on Bi$_2$Se$_3$ predict a $\sim 20$ meV hybridization gap and an intrinsic surface Hall conductivity of $\frac{3}{2}e^2/h$, identifying molecular orbital angular momentum as a handle on surface topology.

authors.name: Juli\'an Castro, Jorge I. Facio, Ver\'onica Vildosola

papers.title: Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
papers.summary: At strong repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto states without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments on the square lattice and, where possible, any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on $N\geq2$ sites, $\mu_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$ for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $\mu_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count $P_{\rm same}$ (four hops move at most three particles). For uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$, $\mu_4=A+\alpha P_{\rm same}$ in closed form: the slope $\alpha=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$ is set by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles, the intercept, via hard-core bosons, by edge, edge-pair and 4-cycle counts. With arbitrary Peierls phases, $\mu_4$ is a spin-independent baseline plus a coefficient times $\sum_C\cos\Theta_C$ over 4-cycle Wilson phases. (3) At finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Exchange loops carry the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, $\alpha\cos\Phi_\square$ on $L\times L$ tori, $L\neq4$, while the doublon hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $\pi$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows up to $O((2\lambda)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the closed form in (2) without phases, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moments and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.

authors.name: D. Souza

papers.title: Frame Based Inelasticity for Fracture in Anisotropic Media
papers.summary: A field theory is presented for predicting damage and fracture in brittle materials. Four concepts are used: a new nonlocal deformation gradient for dynamic stress analysis in anisotropic media, a new type of phase field coming from a constitutive law, the evolution of material displacement from Newton's second law, and a new incorporation of scaled strength surfaces into constitutive laws for predicting dynamic and quasi-static fracture patterns. The elastic softening is governed by the strain dynamics through the constitutive law and in this way we provide the two way coupling between strain and fracture. Simulations validating the approach for both dynamic and quasi-static fracture analysis are compared to experimental results and other simulation methods. The model is capable of predicting material strength in titania and the competition between strength and energy in soda lime glass and titana and captures dynamic crack branching in soda lime glass and concrete.

authors.name: Robert Lipton, Prakash K. C.

papers.title: Electrostatic and Quantum Transport Engineering of Multilayer Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions for Improved TER and RA Trade off
papers.summary: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for non-volatile memory and neuromorphic computing, but achieving a high tunnel electroresistance ratio (TER) with a low resistance-area (RA) product remains challenging. In this work, TiN/Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ (HZO)-based FTJs containing zero to three TiO$_2$ and IGZO-based quantum wells (QWs) are analyzed using the Miller ferroelectric (FE) polarization model integrated with the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism to examine the effects of QW material and thickness on polarization and transport. TiO$_2$-based structures exhibit higher polarization and TER than IGZO-based structures. At a read bias of 0.1 V, the uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structure, with 1-nm-thick QW and insulating layer (IL) layers, gives a TER of $2.71\times10^{10}\%$ and an RA product of $5\times10^4~\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2$, compared with $5.95\times10^7\%$ and $2\times10^5~\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2$, respectively, for IGZO. Both uniform and non-uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structures exhibit resonant tunneling (RT) and negative differential resistance (NDR) associated with QW-confined states. Increasing the first QW thickness to 1.38 nm, while keeping the second QW and both IL layers at 1 nm, shifts the confined-state energies and modifies resonant transport. The selected non-uniform structure achieves a TER of $2.95\times10^{11}\%$ and an RA product of $1.25\times10^3~\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2$ at a read bias of 0.1 V. Elastic scattering changes the amplitude and width of QW resonant-transmission peaks, with a stronger effect on the low resistance state (LRS) than on the high resistance state (HRS). These results show that QW material and thickness optimization can improve the TER--RA trade-off, while electrode screening and elastic scattering further influence polarization-dependent transport in multilayer FTJs.

authors.name: Balram Khattar, Manish Anand, Abhishek Sharma

papers.title: Generalized Critical-State Analysis of Local Field Screening in High-Pressure Yttrium Polyhydride
papers.summary: We resolve the long-standing controversy over the interpretation of magnetic-flux expulsion in high-pressure superhydrides by measuring the local magnetic field adjacent to yttrium polyhydride at 171 GPa and 4.1 K with a $^{57}$Fe M\"ossbauer sensor. Nuclear forward scattering tracks the local induction $B_{\rm sensor}(B_a)$, which nearly merges with the normal-state line near 1.5 T. Rather than assuming a constant-current Bean state, we solve the critical-state problem for the actual thin-disk geometry using the Shantsev--Clem--Sanchez method and compare generalized field-dependent critical-state models. Both the Kim and exponential laws reproduce the measured virgin branch, whereas the constant-$J_c$ Bean model fails. The corresponding zero-field critical-current densities, $(4.38\pm1.48)\times10^{11}$ and $(2.45\pm0.22)\times10^{11}$ A/m$^2$, respectively, are consistent in order of magnitude with transport estimates for granular YH$_6$. These results establish that the observed flux expulsion is a pinned critical state, not the equilibrium Meissner effect, and demonstrate a general methodology for probing local superconductivity under extreme conditions.

authors.name: A. G. Gavriliuk, I. A. Troyan, A. A. Mironovich, A. G. Ivanova, H. -K. Mao, V. V. Struzhkin

papers.title: Fitting the topology of synthetic particle systems with a novel graph representation
papers.summary: The shape and arrangement of particles in a material determine its macroscopic properties. The generation of synthetic data with varying particle structure, often represented as 3D voxel images, combined with simulation of macroscopic properties reveals structure-property relations. Most particle generation models focus on single-particle characteristics like shape and size. We aim at fitting the topology of the particle system using tools from persistent homology. However, the large size of the required 3D image data makes existing methods computationally infeasible. We bridge this gap by introducing a novel graph representation of particle systems and transferring the computation of persistent homology from the image domain to the graph domain. This yields a postprocessing method for synthetic images of particle systems, that is independent of the underlying generation method and improves topological and geometrical agreement with real particle systems while preserving morphological characteristics such as the particle size distribution.

authors.name: Martin Alexander Memmesheimer, Claudia Redenbach

papers.title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
papers.summary: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/\beta$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $\beta=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.

authors.name: Paul Bourgade, Pierre Le Doussal, Gregory Schehr

papers.title: Max-Cut on Token Graphs
papers.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. We prove that $m(F_k(G))\geq\binom{n-2}{k-1}m(G)$, and that this bound is tight up to a multiplicative factor of $1+O(k/n)$; in the case when $k=c \cdot n$ for some constant $0 0$.

authors.name: Jos\'e Angel Alejandro-Soto, Paulo T. Araujo, Ruy Fabila-Monroy, Sergio Gerardo G\'omez-Galicia, Mohamed Hibat-Allah, Md Moshiur Rahman Raj, Mahmud Ashraf Shamim, Ana Laura Trujillo-Negrete

papers.title: Bird-Call Recognition Across Distance: Acoustic Degradation and BirdNET Performance
papers.summary: As bird calls weaken with distance, their recordings lose spectral detail. We examine how species recognition varies with distance using controlled playback of ten-second excerpts from 20 bird species at seven distances from 1 to 48 ft. An STM32-based recording system acquires and stores the audio, which is subsequently analyzed on a computer using acoustic measurements and BirdNET. Across four metadata configurations, mean-aggregated top-1 accuracy is 95--100% through 24 ft, 90--95% at 36 ft, and 80--90% at 48 ft, with 20 recordings evaluated per configuration at each distance. Across the screened recordings, the median upper spectral edge is below its 1-ft reference at every evaluated distance from 4 to 36 ft, indicating an overall reduction in upper-frequency content with distance. These results show that recognition remains high through 24 ft despite measurable spectral degradation, followed by greater and configuration-dependent losses at longer distances.

authors.name: Hasmik Gharibyan, Bhaskar Krishnamachari

papers.title: Efficient Conversational Multi-Talker ASR with Predicted Speaker-Agnostic Activity Streams
papers.summary: Multi-talker automatic speech recognition (ASR) can be performed by conditioning a single-speaker recognizer on frame-level speaker activity. However, this approach requires a complete diarization pass to obtain the conditioning signals and one ASR pass per speaker, making both the frontend and recognition costs dependent on the number of speakers. We reduce these costs by using Heuristic Error Assignment Training (HEAT) to merge the activities of an arbitrary number of speakers into two speaker-agnostic streams. Conditioning on these streams limits recognition to two ASR passes regardless of the number of participants. Through an analysis of the resulting encoder representations, we show that under a stream-assignment heuristic suited to conversational speech, the recognizer represents a stream target much as it does a speaker target. Because the streams do not encode persistent speaker identities, we further replace the conventional sliding-window diarization and clustering frontend with a model that predicts both activity streams directly from the audio in a single pass. A combination of arrival-order and permutation-invariant training objectives over the two-stream powerset labels prevents the predictor from collapsing to identical streams. We also investigate post-hoc speaker attribution by matching decoded utterances to speaker activities within their assigned streams. Experiments on corpora with diverse conversational dynamics demonstrate a favorable efficiency--accuracy tradeoff. On AMI and ICSI, two-stream conditioning is respectively 44\% and 87\% faster than per-speaker conditioning using the same diarization frontend, with less than 2\% relative WER degradation. Direct activity prediction increases these speedups to 79\% and 132\%, with relative WER degradations of 10\% and 21\%, respectively.

authors.name: Xiluo He, Magdalena Rybicka, Laureano Moro-Velazquez, Jes\'us Villalba, Thomas Thebaud, Najim Dehak

papers.title: Connectivity-Constrained Linear System Realization: Feasibility and Realizable Sets
papers.summary: In this paper, we first study the problem of finding a state-space realization of a given transfer function that adheres to a given connectivity pattern (i.e., support). While variants of this problem have been studied in distributed and structured control, existing work typically focuses on connectivity patterns relating to some networked plant. In contrast, we are interested in arbitrary connectivity patterns, which are relevant to modeling problems in sensorimotor neuroscience. We show that this problem is equivalent to solving a system of multivariate polynomial equations, and can be solved exactly without relaxation or approximation. We then study the reverse problem: given a connectivity pattern, what transfer functions have a state-space realization that adheres to this pattern? In other words, what transfer functions can this pattern realize? A surprising finding is that any given pattern can realize nearly all transfer functions, or very few transfer functions. We provide rigorous results and algorithms for both problems, leveraging technical machinery from algebraic geometry. The efficacy of our approach is demonstrated in examples at the end of the paper.

authors.name: Yaozhi Du (Lisa), Jing Shuang (Lisa), Li

papers.title: $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ Grid-Forming Control in DC Microgrids
papers.summary: The growing share of DC-based generation, storage and loads has increased interest in DC microgrids. As a result, DC-bus voltage regulation and stability have become active research topics, with considerable effort directed at improving the transient performance of conventional droop control. Although numerous variants of droop algorithms have been proposed, many rely on increasingly complex control structures with multiple tuning parameters and measurements, thereby increasing the commissioning burden. Moreover, stable interaction with the surrounding microgrid is not guaranteed by design. To address these issues, this paper develops a passivity-constrained $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ synthesis method for the DC-bus voltage controller. The proposed $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ controller emulates the desired grid-forming behavior of the converter by minimizing the $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ error norm between device-level performance indices and their desired values, while additionally enforcing passivity during the optimization. The novel $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ control scheme is benchmarked in the frequency domain against representative droop-based and virtual-DC-machine algorithms from the literature, while experiments on a four-converter DC microgrid corroborate the frequency-domain analysis and validate the practical applicability of the algorithm.

authors.name: Jovan Krajacic, Ognjen Stanojev, Mario Schweizer, Gabriela Hug

papers.title: On Pareto-Optimal Estimation-Information Limits-Achieving Distributions for Integrated Sensing and Communications
papers.summary: ISAC systems enable simultaneous data transmission and environmental sensing using a common waveform. Characterizing their fundamental estimation-information performance limits is of core interest in information theory. In this paper, the achievable data rate for communications and the Miller-Chang-type CRB on sensing distortion are adopted as ISAC performance metrics, both of which are functionals of the ISAC waveform distribution. Our aim is to characterize the optimal input distributions across the entire CRB-rate Pareto boundary, corresponding to different sensing-communication tradeoff preferences. Three types of power constraint on input waveform are considered, namely, i) general power (GP), ii) maximum amplitude (MA), and iii) constant modulus (CM) constraints. Under these constraints, Pareto-optimal input distributions are shown to exhibit a common structural property: the directional component is uniformly distributed over the complex unit sphere; the power distribution is discrete (excluding the communication-optimal point under GP, where it follows a Gamma distribution induced by Gaussian inputs). We further investigate and characterize their Pareto-optimal sensing-communication preference dependent support structures. Finally, numerical algorithms are developed under GP and MA to trace their Pareto boundaries and determine corresponding optimal power distributions based on their respective support characteristics. From both analytical and numerical results, we conclude sensing prefers deterministic power while communication benefits from a richer distribution of power levels, thereby revealing the sensing-communication waveform uncertainty tradeoff in the fundamental power domain.

authors.name: Zi-Jie Wang

papers.title: Mode Recommendation and Dynamic Routing Guidance for Improved Trip Quality in Mixed Traffic Networks
papers.summary: Urban mixed traffic networks provide diverse mobility options, yet conventional routing guidance with fixed travel modes leaves the benefits of coordinating travel modes and route planning largely unexploited. This paper proposes an integrated mode recommendation and dynamic routing guidance framework for urban mixed traffic networks comprising private vehicles, autonomous vehicles, and buses. We formulate a dynamic trip index (DTX) that incorporates mode-specific travel time, monetary cost, and convenience, enabling consistent evaluation of trip quality across travel modes. Using this measure, we develop a mode recommendation method that selects feasible autonomous vehicle or bus services based on predicted DTX for travelers without private vehicles, while preserving service capacity for travelers with known demand. We integrate this method with dynamic routing guidance for private and autonomous vehicles to improve the average trip quality of all travelers. Simulation studies involving $1{,}500$ travelers on a real-world road network in Shanghai, China, show that the proposed framework increases the mean realized DTX by $13.01\%$ compared with dynamic routing guidance alone and by $19.68\%$ compared with fixed travel modes with preplanned routes, highlighting the value of mode flexibility in improving trip quality beyond route adaptation.

authors.name: Jin Zhang, Andreas A. Malikopoulos, Ting Bai

papers.title: Particle picking with an earth mover's seminorm
papers.summary: Particle picking is a key step in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy. It is a challenging task where tomographic projections of proteins and other macromolecules are identified in extremely noisy images. In this work, we introduce a particle picker based on a seminorm defined in terms of a fast wavelet approximation to the earth mover's distance. Our picker is template-free, self-supervised and does not require any prior knowledge of the molecules of interest other than their approximate size. We test it on three public datasets and show that it achieves state-of-the-art reconstructions.

authors.name: Dvir Moshe, Amit Moscovich, Amit Singer, Ayelet Heimowitz

papers.title: Which Data-Center Load Models Can Be Trusted? An Evidence-Graded Review of Dynamic Modeling and Validation for Large Computational Loads
papers.summary: Grid operators now require dynamic models of data centers and other large computational loads, and new ride-through rules assume that these models predict how facilities respond to disturbances. This review asks what evidence supports that assumption. We coded 160 documents, screened from 1,424 de-duplicated database and seed records plus 65 added documents, by the strongest reference object each presents, from grid-side records to simulation only. Across 19 field-evidence entries, 15 requirement documents from three continents and nine model classes, we find two comparisons of a standard library model with measured data-center events: with default parameters the model failed both, and refitting it to each event separately reduced the error but was never tested on an unseen event. Among the sources reviewed, we found no successful held-out validation of a frozen, facility-specific data-center model against an independent measured disturbance, and 25 of the 33 model-phenomenon combinations with any evidence involve no electrical measurement. The features that distinguish the new rules (memory of repeated dips, recovery within 0.5-3 s, proportional power reduction during the sag, overvoltage response) are those current phasor models cannot represent or have never been tested against. In the operator procedures examined, simulations and model-to-model benchmarks are accepted as evidence of model fidelity, unlike the measured validation required of generators, and proposed mitigations have mostly been evaluated on unvalidated facility models. We propose context-of-use gates that separate calibration from validation, release labels for model claims, a minimum validation protocol with acceptance criteria, and a research agenda.

authors.name: Dileep Cheerla

papers.title: Hybrid-Field Interference Suppression for Low-Complexity Uplink Channel Estimation
papers.summary: Uplink channel estimation can be severely degraded by hybrid-field interference, where strong near-field intra-site interference is coupled with far-field inter-site interference. Although a joint near-/far-field dictionary can capture this interference structure, it requires dense angle--distance matching that may incur high complexity and performance degradation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid-field interference suppression framework for uplink channel estimation. First, we formulate a hybrid-field interference model and analyze its sparse reconstruction. Then, to avoid exhaustive near-field dictionary matching, we propose a low-complexity interference-parameter estimation method based on the angle--domain diffusion pattern of the dominant interference. Using the estimated parameters, the proposed parametric interference-nulling orthogonal matching pursuit (PIN-OMP) algorithm suppresses the dominant interference components and reconstructs the desired uplink channel from the interference-suppressed observation. Furthermore, a physical critical-distance bound is derived to characterize the feasible distance-inversion region, and a conditional hybrid Cram'er--Rao bound (HCRB) is established to quantify the desired channel reconstruction limit under a reconstructed interference basis. Finally, numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

authors.name: Zihan Zhou, Li Chen, Ang Chen, Weidong Wang, Changsheng You, Yunfei Chen

papers.title: ECG-LabWAS: A Laboratory-Wide Association Study Using a Fine-Tuned Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Foundation Model
papers.summary: Laboratory testing guides clinical diagnosis but requires blood sampling and processing. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is fast and noninvasive and may carry information about laboratory abnormalities, yet most AI-ECG models target one test at a time using 12-lead recordings. We conducted an exploratory ECG laboratory-wide association study (ECG-LabWAS), fine-tuning an ECG foundation model pretrained on 10.8 million ECGs to screen 50 laboratory tests from single-lead waveforms alone. The model was developed in an emergency-department cohort (MC-MED; 31,826 patients) and applied unchanged to an independent hospital cohort (MIMIC-IV; 115,921 patients). Of 89 abnormality directions (low or high values of each test), 33 met the same screening criteria in both cohorts. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the two cohorts were 0.841 and 0.838 for elevated NT-proBNP, 0.769 and 0.740 for elevated cardiac troponin, 0.755 and 0.731 for elevated creatinine, and 0.713 and 0.710 for low potassium. Discrimination changed little when the ECG--laboratory matching window was widened from $\pm$1 to $\pm$24 hours. Model predictions reproduced the co-occurrence of observed abnormalities but were about twice as tightly coupled, largely along one shared component consistent with overall illness severity; low potassium, elevated NT-proBNP and troponin, and markers of renal function retained discrimination beyond that of correlated tests. In exploratory analyses, ECG-assisted versions of the modified Glasgow Prognostic Score and the systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria were associated with in-hospital and one-year mortality. These results identify which laboratory abnormalities warrant analyte-specific study with single-lead ECG.

authors.name: Wenhui Liu, Yujie Xiao, Gongzheng Tang, Jianwei Chen, Jun Li, Guangkun Nie, Deyun Zhang, Qinghao Zhao, Shenda Hong

papers.title: Strong Functional Observability and Strong Functional Detectability: Applications to Functional Observer Design for Systems with Unknown Inputs
papers.summary: This paper investigates strong functional observability, strong functional detectability, and strong$^*$ functional detectability for continuous-time linear systems with unknown inputs in both the state and measurement equations. Extending Kratz's finite algebraic approach \cite{26}, zero-output trajectories are characterized through the projected kernel of a finite matrix, without differentiating the unknown inputs. This characterization yields a necessary and sufficient rank condition for strong functional observability. For strong functional detectability, a frequency-dependent rank criterion involving only the original system matrices is derived, along with an equivalent finite test based on reduced zero-output dynamics. Strong$^*$ functional detectability is then characterized by an additional algebraic rank condition, and its relationship with the existence of stable functional observers is examined. A constructive observer design procedure based on constrained Sylvester equations is also developed. Particular cases and a numerical process example illustrate the theoretical results.

authors.name: M. Darouach

papers.title: PepDeTech: Anonymous Occupancy Monitoring on a Battery-Powered 2.3k-Zone dToF LiDAR Node with On-Chip Processing and Bluetooth LE Reporting
papers.summary: As populations grow, society is increasingly required to shift towards systems of shared resources, which allow space, energy and time to be optimised. Facilitating this transition depends on data: how many people are present, when and where. From such information, schedules can be organised more efficiently and resources allocated where they matter. At the same time, privacy concerns and energy consumption limit deployment: cameras are frequently unacceptable, while simpler sensors miss people and cannot provide the full picture. This paper presents PepDeTech, a compact, battery-powered occupancy node that combines a 54 x 42-zone direct Time-of-Flight (dToF) Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) (VL53L9CX) with a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) System on Chip (SoC). Three deterministic algorithms, background subtraction, motion history and a track lifecycle, run on-chip and count the people simultaneously, providing real-time occupancy monitoring. No trained model is involved, and setup takes less than a minute. Over three scenarios, background subtraction reaches a per-frame +-1-person accuracy of 83.6 % (mean absolute error (MAE) 0.70 persons), tested with up to five people present. At a 30 s interval the node draws only 3.1 mW, lasting 60 d on a 1200 mA h cell. Several weeks of deployment on a single charge make the node usable as a survey instrument for facility management: a room can be characterised for a measurement campaign without cabling, network provisioning or a camera, and the resulting occupancy record is what ventilation, lighting, cleaning and space-allocation decisions are argued from, ultimately resulting in more efficient resource allocation.

authors.name: Victor Luder, F\'elicien Ndozi, Michele Magno

papers.title: Learned Score-Based Turbo Message Passing for Compressive Image Recovery
papers.summary: Score-based generative models have been incorpo-rated into message passing algorithms for compressive image recovery, providing a prior for the denoising module in message passing. Score-based generative models assume the input signal to be a clean signal perturbed by independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Gaussian noise. Yet, this assumption often fails during message passing, leading to slow convergence and limited reconstruction quality. In this letter, we propose the learned score-based turbo message passing (LSTMP) algorithm to overcome this limitation. By employing a deep unfolding framework, LSTMP unrolls the iterative process into a neural network, enabling the denoiser to adapt to complicated noise distributions inherent in the iterative updates. Furthermore, by treating the denoiser as an iterative solver, we incorporate the likelihood information of compressed measurements into the neural network of the denoiser, resembling the message passing between linear and nonlinear modules in STMP. Experiments on the FFHQ dataset show that LSTMP achieves convergence in no more than three iterations while delivering high-ffdelity re-constructions, signiffcantly outperforming the existing baselines.

authors.name: Peihang Li, Hao Jiang, Xiaojun Yuan

papers.title: Network Traffic Dynamics in Urban Low-Altitude Air Transport with Projected-Space Macroscopic Fundamental Diagrams
papers.summary: The growth of Low-Altitude Air Transport (LAAT) systems calls for effective macroscopic modeling tools to manage dense drone traffic. The Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram (MFD) offers a promising framework for this purpose, but its conventional formulations do not directly account for the three-dimensional interactions and path deviations that characterize drone operations. To address this challenge, we introduce a projected-space framework that represents drone motion using projected speed and shortest origin-destination (OD) distances, eliminating the dependence on realized trip lengths that are unknown at trip generation. Under suitable assumptions, we prove the steady-state exactness of the projected-space accumulation-based model and establish deterministic finite-window error bounds for the trip-based estimator. The projected-space accumulation-based formulation is further extended to heterogeneous multi-class systems to accommodate different drone characteristics and operational priorities. Microscopic simulations validate the projected-space formulations under stationary and transient traffic conditions, including hysteresis. Moreover, simulations involving heterogeneous priority classes demonstrate that mixed-priority operations can improve network outflow under the investigated scenarios. These findings establish a theoretical foundation for projected-space macroscopic modeling of LAAT systems and support its application to real-time traffic estimation and future airspace management and control.

authors.name: Ran Chen, Can Chen, Nikolas Geroliminis

papers.title: Active Learning of Flows from Curve Observations using Gaussian Processes
papers.summary: The active learning of real control systems requires informative roll-outs of controls. In this paper, we present a local optimization algorithm that finds the trajectory that most reduces uncertainty about the flow of a control system modeled by a Gaussian process. Therefore, we derive an approximation scheme for the posterior kernel of the Gaussian process after observing it on an entire continuous-time trajectory and establish a Pontryagin-type necessary condition for the optimizer. As the flow is unknown, the actual trajectory can deviate from the planned trajectory. We propose a trajectory planner that searches for the most informative control within a maximal allowed deviation horizon instead of a fixed time horizon. We show by trajectory-wise time rescaling that the underlying optimal control problem is equivalent to a fixed end time optimal control problem. Finally, we study both the fixed end time planner and the fixed maximum deviation planner in a numerical example and compare them with benchmarks.

authors.name: Konrad Reichel, Sandra Hirche

papers.title: Linear Quadratic Control With Event-Based Control Actions: Performance Beyond Periodic Control
papers.summary: This paper investigates linear quadratic (LQ) control for discrete-time stochastic systems to balance control performance and actuation rate. In our framework, the control input is sparse in time, and the actuation timings are determined in an event-based manner. We examine two types of problems: A sparsity-promoting regularization problem and a hard-constraint problem with a prescribed average actuation rate. Due to the combinatorial nature of these problems, finding optimal solutions is generally hard. Inspired by rollout algorithms in the context of dynamic programming, we develop a rollout-based approach to obtain tractable suboptimal policies. We show closed-loop stability and establish theoretical performance guarantees with respect to classical periodic control. Moreover, under additional conditions, we quantify the performance improvement over periodic control and prove that this improvement is strictly positive. A numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in balancing control performance and actuation rate.

authors.name: Shumpei Nishida, Kunihisa Okano

papers.title: Incentive-based Fleet Rebalancing in Vehicle-Sharing Systems via Equilibrium-Constrained Optimal Control
papers.summary: We propose an incentive-based fleet rebalancing scheme for vehicle-sharing systems that uses fare discounts to steer users toward alternative pick-up locations. The discounts solve an optimal control problem that trades off users leaving the service against incentive costs over a day of operation. Users' responses to incentives are modeled as a Nash equilibrium of logit models coupled through shared vehicle-availability constraints, which makes the control problem a mathematical program with nested equilibrium constraints. We develop a first-order algorithm that backpropagates through the equilibria via nonsmooth implicit differentiation and enjoys convergence guarantees. In a case study that uses Helsinki bike-sharing data, our scheme reduces the number of leaving users by up to 99% relative to no incentives, and outperforms heuristic policies while using up to 52% less incentive.

authors.name: Daniel Tihanyi, Giuseppe Belgioioso

papers.title: From Pilots to Position: Experimental Near-Field Localization for ISAC
papers.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless systems to reuse communication signals for environmental sensing, potentially reducing the need for dedicated sensing resources. However, the achievable localization accuracy of communication-centric waveforms under practical hardware constraints remains an important challenge. In this paper, we experimentally investigate near-field target localization using OFDM pilot signals in a distributed communication system. We consider both coherent and noncoherent localization approaches, exploiting multistatic propagation delays and time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) information extracted from pilot-based channel estimates. A hardware setup comprising two transmitters and four receivers was developed and configured to operate at 3.4 GHz with 198 MHz occupied bandwidth to evaluate localization performance under realistic propagation and synchronization conditions. Experimental results across 16 static target positions demonstrate mean localization errors of 19.8 cm and 18.8 cm for coherent backprojection and noncoherent delay-TDOA fusion, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of occupied bandwidth on localization accuracy of the two proposed algorithms. These findings provide experimental insights into the capabilities and practical limitations of OFDM pilot-based sensing, supporting resource-efficient localization in future ISAC systems.

authors.name: Yunxin Li, Emiel Vanspranghels, Jialun Kou, Georgios Mystriotis, Achiel Colpaert, Rodney Martinez Alonso, Sofie Pollin

papers.title: Planar Formation Control with Minimal Sensing and No Common Orientation: An Almost-Global Result
papers.summary: Formation control based on geometric constraints often requires either rigid interaction graphs or a common orientation reference. This paper investigates whether a prescribed planar formation can instead be achieved using only $N-1$ pairwise interactions while preserving global rotational freedom. To this end, a guiding-vector-field-inspired framework is developed in which each selected distance relation is represented by a parameterized circular manifold and the remaining geometric freedom is coordinated through relative virtual phases, based on which, a distributed controller is then constructed.
